records.name: Rajeev Shukla
records.qn_text:
(a) whether it is a fact that Government of Sri Lanka informed Government of India that V. Prabhakaran, Chief of LTTE and his son have been killed in an encounter with Sri Lankan army and that LTTE agitation has come to an end;

(b) if so, the details thereof;

(c) whether Government has taken up this issue of safety and welfare of Tamils in Sri Lanka;

(d) if so, the details thereof; and

(e) if not, the reasons therefor?
records.ans_text:
THE MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF EXTERNAL AFFAIRS

(SMT PRENEET KAUR)

(a) to (b) In a telephonic conversation on 18th May, 2009, Sri Lankan President, H.E. Mahinda Rajapaksa informed then External Affairs Minister Shri Pranab Mukherjee that the LTTE leader Velupillai Prabhakaran was dead and armed resistance by LTTE had come to an end.

(c) to (e) The Government has emphasized to the Sri Lankan Government that it must focus on the issues of relief, rehabilitation and resettlement of the internally displaced Tamil population. The National Security Advisor Shri M K Narayanan and Foreign Secretary Shri Shivshankar Menon visited Colombo on May 20-21, 2009. The Sri Lankan Government conveyed to them their plan to resettle most of the displaced persons in their original homes within 180 days. This assurance was reiterated during the visit of a high-level Sri Lankan delegation led by Hon`ble Basil Rajapaksa, Senior Adviser to the Sri Lankan President, on June 24, 2009.

The Government has committed to provide all possible assistance for facilitating the rapid rehabilitation and resettlement of the Tamil population. Prime Minister has announced Rs. 500 crores for the relief and rehabilitation of the internally displaced persons in Sri Lanka.

records.name: T. Subbarami Reddy
records.qn_text:
(a) whether attacks against Indian students in Australia continue unabated in spite of assurance given that action would be taken by Australian Government ;

(b) if so, whether Australian Government has admitted that some attacks were racist ;

(c) If so, whether in spite of responding positively, no serious action has been taken by the Australian Government on our request ;

(d) the total students affected so far and whether there are reports of racial attacks in Canada also ;

(e) the latest position in this regard ; and

(f) whether Australia has agreed to take steps against culprits who attacked Indians ?
records.ans_text:
MINISTER OF OVERSEAS INDIAN AFFAIRS

(SHRI VAYALAR RAVI)

(a): Some incidents of attacks on Indian students are still being reported.

(b): In Victoria, where most of the recent attacks have taken place, Premier John Brumby announced during Question Time in the State Parliament on 02 June 2009 that his Government condemned racially motivated crimes in the strongest possible terms and will do everything in its power to track down the perpetrators of these cowardly acts and bring them to justice as well. He also announced that his Government proposes to amend the Sentencing Act to enable judges to take into account hatred for or prejudice against a particular group of people while sentencing persons found guilty.

(c): It has been conveyed by the Australian Government, that it has taken/is taking a series of steps to check such attacks.

(d) & (e) Total number of confirmed cases of attacks on Indians including students since 23 May 2009 is 81. There has been no report of attacks on Indian students in Canada.

(f): Yes Sir. In some cases arrests have been made and charges laid against the offenders. It has been impressed upon the Australian authorities that it should be ensured that police takes swift and stern action on such complaints.

records.name: Rajeev Shukla
records.qn_text:
(a) whether Nigeria has urged Oil and Natural Gas Corporation Ltd. (ONGC) to honour promises to fulfil its 6 billion dollor commitment of investment in infrastructure of the African nation as part of the deal by which it was awarded an oil block in November, 2006;

(b) is so, whether ONGC has agreed to implement the promise made to Nigeria in this regard;

(c) whether Nigeria has also invited Reliance Industries Ltd (RIL), Gas Authority of India Ltd. (GAIL) to set up petro-chemical plant; and

(d) if so, to what extent India has agreed to help and assist both Nigeria and Qatar setting up petroleum plants which will benefit India by obtaining oil from these countries?
records.ans_text:
MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF PETROLEUM & NATURAL GAS (SHRI DINSHA PATEL)

(a) & (b): No, Sir. Oil & Natural Gas Corporation Limited (ONGC) has no agreement with Nigerian Authorities. However, a Memorandum of Understanding (MOU) was entered between ONGC Mittal Energy Ltd. (OMEL) {a Joint Venture of ONGC Videsh Ltd (OVL). and Mittal Investments Sarl} and the Ministry of Petroleum Resources of the Federal Republic of Nigeria which envisages an investment of US$6 billion in Nigeria on infrastructure Projects. prorated according to average production realized by OMEL from the two blocks it has been awarded in Nigeria.

(c) & (d): GAIL (India) Limited (GAIL) has not received any formal invitation from Government of Nigeria for setting up Petro Chemical Plant. In so far as Reliance Industries Limited (RIL) is concerned, this Ministry has no information. Setting up of petroleum plants depends on commercial consideration techno-economic feasibility studies carried out by companies.

records.name: Rajeev Shukla
records.min_name: CONSUMER AFFAIRS, FOOD AND PUBLIC DISTRIBUTION
records.qn_text:
(a) whether with an increased uncertainty in the domestic market and weakening international market, edible oil importers are now reluctant to enter into new contracts for the imports as prices have fallen considerably by 20-28 per cent in the last one month after the duty cut announced by Government;

(b) whether Government has brought down import duties on crude palm oil to 20 per cent from 45 per cent and refined palm oil and RBD palmolein to 27.5 per cent from 52.5 per cent; and

(c) if so, the steps Government propose to take to import oil so that shortage is met?
records.ans_text:
MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF AGRICULTURE AND MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF CONSUMER AFFAIRS, FOOD & PUBLIC DISTRIBUTION

(DR. AKHILESH PRASAD SINGH)

(a): As on 16.02.2009, the wholesale domestic prices of soyabean oil, mustard oil, groundnut oil and sunflower oil have declined by 4.77%, 12.60%, 11.86% and 8.91% respectively during the last one month, whereas the international prices of crude palm oil and soyabean oil have increased by 8.91% and 4.48% respectively during the same period. There has been an increase of about 19% in import of edible oils during January, 2009 as compared to previous month i.e. December, 2008.

(b): W.e.f. 1.4.2008, custom duty on crude palm oil has been reduced to 0% whereas custom duty on both refined palm oil and RBD palmolein had been reduced to 7.5%.

(c): In order to maintain uninterrupted supply of edible oils at affordable price to consumers, certain measures like downward revisions in the import duty on crude and refined edible oils, ban on export of major edible oils and introduction of a Scheme for distribution of subsidized edible oils through State Governments have been taken by the Government from time to time.

records.name: Rajeev Shukla
records.qn_text:
(a) whether according to US study India faces threat of Mumbai re-run and would continue to face a serious jihadi threat from Pakistan based terrorist groups and India is not likely to reduce threat in the near future;

(b) whether studies indentifies operational and tactical features of attack, evaluates the response of the Indian security forces and analyses the implications for India, Pakistan and USA;

(c) if so, the other main points of the report; and

(d) whether Pakistan activities against India after Mumbai attack continues in the same manner and steps India has taken or proposes to take?
records.ans_text:
THE MINISTER OF EXTERNAL AFFAIRS

(SHRI PRANAB MUKHERJEE)

(a) Yes. According to a study titled “Terrorists Can Think Strategically: Lessons Learned From the Mumbai Attacks’’ undertaken by the Rand Corporation, a US based think tank, India is vulnerable to jihadi terrorist threat from Pakistan based terrorist groups.

(b) Yes.

(c) The other main points of the study are that
(i) terrorists will continue to focus on soft targets, including hotels and public surface transportation that offer high body counts and have iconic value;
(ii)the Taliban, Al-Qaida, Laskar-e-Taiba and other terrorist groups find sanctuary in Pakistan’s tribal areas and some of them have historically drawn on support from the Pakistani Government;
(iii) it does not rule out a Mumbai type attack in the US and asserts that new outfits have signed on to Al Qaeda’s ideology of global terror and
(iv) the fact that Mumbai attackers were able to paralyse a large city and commanded the attention of the world media for nearly three days would encourage similar operations in future.

(d) Government is committed to taking all necessary steps to safeguard the security of its citizens and its territory.

records.qtitle: RAPID ACTION UNITS OF NSG IN STATES .
records.name: Rajeev Shukla
records.qn_text:
(a) whether Centre has cleared a plan to urgently deploy rapid action units of National Security Guard in six or seven States including Mumbai until the State units are created;

(b) if so, whether Government proposes to utilize personnel of commandos units of the three armed forces in the States;

(c) whether Prime Minister has also emphasized need to step up security;

(d) if so, whether any strategy has been developed to tackle terrorism as India has paid heavy price for its inaction; and

(e) the extent Government is hopeful of meeting the situation of terrorism in the country?
records.ans_text:
MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF HOME AFFAIRS

(SHRI SRIPRAKASH JAISWAL)

(a): The Government has decided in principle to set up NSG hubs in the Metropolitan cities of Chennai, Kolkata, Hyderabad and Mumbai for swift deployment of the force in any emergent crisis situations.

(b): Yes, Sir.

(c): Yes, Sir.

(d) & (e): The Government remains firmly committed to counter the challenges posed by terrorism, and a multi-pronged strategy is being pursued towards this end, in close conjunction with the State Governments. This, inter alia, includes, measures to check infiltration from across the borders through intensive patrolling, border fencing and flood lighting, etc; strengthening the arrangements for coastal security through intensified vigilance and patrolling, both on the shores and in the waters, by the State Police, Coast Guard and the Navy; strengthening and streamlining of the arrangements for gathering analysis and sharing of real time intelligence between the agencies and with/among States, and coordinated action thereon; assistance to the State Governments for upgradation and modernization of the State Police Forces; raising of India Reserve Battalions, with additional assistance for raising 2 Coys per Bn. As Commando Units; strengthening the legal framework for dealing with terrorist offences; and various initiatives for cooperation with other countries at the bilateral and multi-lateral levels to deal with the challenges posed by terrorism, etc. in the context of strengthening the legal frame-work, the Unlawful Activities (Prevention) Amendment Act, 2008, the National Investigation Agency Act, 2008 and the CISF (Amendment) Ordinance, 2009 have been enacted/issued recently. In addition, notifications have also been issued whereunder the Government/NSG can requisition civil aircraft in the event of emergency to ensure speedy movement. Measures to strengthen the internal security/counter terrorism apparatus are being reviewed regularly, and further steps as required would be taken on a continuing basis.

records.qtitle: ROLE OF PUBLIC AND PRIVATE SECTORS IN POWER GENERATION AND DISTRIBUTION .
records.name: Rajeev Shukla
records.qn_text:
(a) whether, emphasizing the increased role for the public sector in power generation and the private sector in the distribution business, he has decided to strengthen technological and managerial expertise of Public Sector Undertakings (PSUs) in power sector and synergize their roles, to complement generation capacity building efforts;

(b) if so, what are the main suggestions made to the PSUs in the power sector;

(c) how many of these suggestions have been considered by those PSUs; and

(d) to what extent the power generation targets would be achieved during the Eleventh Five Year Plan?
records.ans_text:
THE MINISTER OF POWER

(SHRI SUSHILKUMAR SHINDE)

(a) to (d) : A Statement is laid on the Table of the House.


STATEMENT
STATEMENT REFERRED TO IN REPLY TO PARTS (a) TO (d) OF STARRED QUESTION NO. 283 TO BE ANSWERED IN THE RAJYA SABHA ON 22.12.2008 REGARDING ROLE OF PUBLIC AND PRIVATE SECTORS IN POWER GENERATION AND DISTRIBUTION.

(a) to (c) : The Ministry of Power places emphasis on capacity building in power sector. With growing competition and restructuring of the sector, the focus is on reorienting and upgrading managerial approach and improving work efficiency through structured skills upgradation and improvement programme.
The changes caused due to technological advances and upgradation are tackled through multi pronged strategy in the three major areas in the Power Sector i.e. Generation, Transmission and Distribution. The major initiatives taken are as follows:
I. Cadre Development:
i. Developing the cadre at induction level through institutionalizing career development programmes like B. Tech in Power through the National Power Training Institute (NPTI) for developing engineers specifically for the power sector.
In addition, a distance learning Advanced Certificate programme in Power Distribution Management has been initiated by Ministry of Power through the Indira Gandhi National Open University (IGNOU) to provide an overall perspective on power distribution. The programme commenced in 2007 and has covered more than 1500 participants. A six months Post Graduate Diploma is also offered by NPTI in Transmission and Distribution.
ii. Building a skilled manpower pool to cover new trades as well as upgrading the skills to cater to technological advances has been initiated by the Ministry of Power through `Adopt an ITI` Scheme wherein the power developers and utilities are encouraged to adopt ITIs near the project areas. Some of the Utilities that have adopted/built ITIs include NTPC 25 Nos., NHPC 6 Nos., DVC 8 Nos. and Tata Power 4 Nos.
iii. Ministry of Power in collaboration with IGNOU has recently launched a distance learning programme for Technicians in the Sector, delivered through multi media of print (course books), teleconferencing and practicals. The programme will help the Technicians to upgrade their skills and provide them opportunity in career growth as certificate awarded by IGNOU will be equivalent to that of ITI. It will also open new career stream for young students at entrance level to pursue the programme with a ready placement potential.
iv. To upgrade managerial skills and reorient the approach towards sectoral changes, a Post Graduate Energy Management programme has been institutionalized by the Ministry of Power through the Management Development Institute. The programme focuses on developing future leaders with particular emphasis on implementation of enactments relating to power distribution.
II. Induction level/Refresher Programmes:

(i) All utilities in the Central Sector have devised structured programmes catering to various levels. While in generation, NTPC, NHPC, THDC, SJVNL and NEEPCO have inhouse facilities along with institutional arrangements with other training institutes to cater to their training needs. The coverage during 2006-07 to 2008-09 (to date) is: NTPC about 61,000, NHPC about 26,000, THDC about 2,800, SJVNL about 2,950 and NEEPCO about 1,835 trainees respectively.

(ii) In Transmission, Power Grid Corporation of India Ltd (PGCIL) has adequate training structure to implement various programmes. The coverage during 2006-07 to 2007-08 is more than 8000 persons.

(iii) In Distribution, the Ministry of Power has institutionalized a structured distribution related project, called the Distribution Reforms Upgrade Management (DRUM) Programme. The programme was initiated in 2005 with targeted coverage of 20,000 participants. More than 25,000 participants have already been covered and an institutional network of 20 Institutions established covering all regions of the country. The programme primarily encompasses short term programmes covering the core technical and management theme, relevant to distribution business operation. Technological advances have also been addressed through programmes delivered by manufacturers on Metering technology and Distribution system equipment to enable direct interface between manufacturers and users. The overall coverage through the Distribution Reform Upgrade Management programme is as under: 




		2004-05	2005-06	2006-07	2007-08	2008-09	Overall
DRUM 		319	3,812	6,460	7,831	6,979	25,401


(iv) The NPTI, a national level training institute under Ministry of Power has covered more than 32,000 participants during the year 2006-07 to 2008-09 to date.

(d) : The Planning Commission had set a capacity addition target of 78,700 MW for the 11th Five Year Plan comprising 15,627 MW Hydro, 59,693 MW Thermal and 3,380 MW from Nuclear. The capacity realizable with close monitoring, as estimated by the Central Electricity Authority during 11th Plan period, however, is 79,790 MW, comprising 15,507 MW from Hydro, 60,903 MW from Thermal and 3,380 MW from Nuclear. A capacity of 11,322 MW has already been commissioned during 11th Plan Period up to 30.11.2008.

records.qtitle: ENHANCEMENT OF FINANCIAL GRANT FOR MID DAY MEAL SCHEME .
records.name: Rajeev Shukla
records.qn_text:
(a) whether the issue of price rise has created more problems for the Ministry, after the Public Accounts Committee suggesting to enhance financial grant for Mid-day Meal Scheme under Sarva Shiksha Abhiyan, in view of rising price index;

(b) whether one of its five recommendations pertains to national programme of Nutritional Support to Primary Education scheme, popularly known as Mid-day Meal Scheme;

(c) if so, what are other main recommendations made and to what extent these have been implemented; and

(d) to what extent it has helped in improving programmes of Sarva Shiksha Abhiyan? ANSWER
records.ans_text:
MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF HUMAN RESOURCE DEVELOPMENT

(SHRI M.A.A. FATMI)

(a): At the time of extension of Mid-Day Meal Scheme to the upper primary stage, a decision to link the cost of cooking to Inflation Adjusted Index

(Consumer Price Index) and assess cooking cost, both for primary and upper primary, every two years beginning 2008-09, was taken. Accordingly, with effect from 1.4.2008, the Central share of cooking cost was raised from Rs.1.50 to Rs.1.58 per child per working day for primary and from Rs.2.00 to Rs.2.10 per child per school working day for upper primary. In case of North-Eastern (NER) States, including Sikkim, the Central share of cooking cast has been raised from Rs.1.80 to Rs.1.89 per child per school day at primary stage and from Rs.2.30 to Rs.2.42 per child per school working day at upper primary stage. Some States/UTs are spending more than their minimum mandatory contribution for betterment of mid-day meal which is 20 paisa per child per school day for NER States including Sikkim and 50 paisa per child per school day in case of other States/UTs.

(b) to (d):Of the four recommendations, one relates to Mid-Day Meal Scheme and three to Sarva Shiksha Abhiyan

(SSA). Public Accounts Committee (PAC) in their 66th Report (where out of 4 paras, 3 relate to SSA) has not made any recommendation relating to price rise in relation to this programme. Implementation of SSA Programme since 2000-01 has seen bringing of all eligible children in the age group of 6-14 years into the fold of elementary education except for 45 lakhs out-of-school children who represent children of ‘difficult to reach category’.

records.name: Rajeev Shukla
records.qn_text:
(a) whether Planning Commission is preparing a strategic plan for investment in infrastructure projects and has been placed before the Prime Minister;

(b) if so, the main points mentioned in the report;

(c) Whether Government has considered it; and

(d) its main features and by what time it is likely to be implemented?
records.ans_text:
MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF PLANNING AND MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF PARLIAMENTARY AFFAIRS

(SHRI V. NARAYANASAMY)

(a) to (d): The strategy for infrastructure development in the Eleventh Plan reflects the dominant role of the public sector in building infrastructure. However, it also recognises that total resources required to meet the deficit in infrastructure exceed the capacity of the public sector. It is, therefore, necessary to attract private investment through appropriate forms of public private partnerships (PPPs) to meet the overall investment requirement. The strategy for the Eleventh Plan thus, also encourages private sector participation directly as well as through various forms of PPPs where desirable and feasible. The projected investment in infrastructure during the Eleventh Plan is about Rs. 20,56,150 crore. This includes public investment of about Rs. 14,36,559 crore and private investment of about Rs. 6,19,591 crore.

records.name: Rajeev Shukla
records.qn_text:
(a) whether some political parties have written to the Prime Minister with reference to its policies on modernisation of Kolkata and 35 other non-metro airports in the country;

(b) if so, whether some of the parties have questioned Government`s decision in this regard;

(c) if so, what are the main reasons put forward for reversing policy of modernisation of Kolkata and other 35 non-metro airports in the country; and

(d) what is the final decision taken and whether Government has agreed to modernise these airports also ?
records.ans_text:
MINISTER OF STATE (INDEPENDENT CHARGE) OF THE MINISTRY OF CIVIL AVIATION
(SHRI PRAFUL PATEL)

(a), (b), (c) & (d) A Statement is laid on the Table of the House.
Statement in reply to parts (a), (b), (c) & (d) of the Rajya Sabha Starred () Question No. 214 for 16.12.2008 regarding `Modernisation of Kolkata airport`. (a), (b), (c) & (d): Yes, some Hon`ble Members of Parliament have expressed concern over delay in the process of modernisation of Kolkata and 35 non-metro airports. The Government have, accordingly approved the project of modernisation of Kolkata Airport at an estimated cost of Rs.1942.51 crores for implementation by AAI. The work has been awarded on 6.10.2008 and is likely to be completed in 30 months. As per guidelines issued by COI, 35 non-metro airports, namely Amritsar, Agra, Agatti, Ahmedabad, Aurangabad, Bhopal, Bhubaneshwar, Chandigarh, Dehradun, Indore, Jaipur, Jammu, Khajuraho, Lucknow, Madurai, Mangalore, Nagpur, Pune, Ranchi, Trichy, Trivandrum, Udaipur, Varanasi, Visakhapatnam, Agartala, Coimbatore, Dimapur, Goa, Guwahati, Imphal, Patna, Port Blair, Raipur, Rajkot and Vadodara are being developed. The Terminal Building and Air Side infrastructure at these 35 non-metro airports are being developed by AAI in a time bound manner for completion by end March 2010. The City Side Development of select 24 Non-Metro airports is to be done through public- private partnership route. The modernisation and expansion of Kolkata airport and 35 non-metro airports is underway as planned.

records.name: Rajeev Shukla
records.qn_text:
(a) whether Governments top level Committee, e on financial sector reforms has pointed out that the Reserve Bank: of India (RBI) must cut interests quickly when inflation eases up;

(b) if so, whether according to the Chairman of the Committee, it is necessary as RBI raises rates when inflation is expected to exceed the objectives because growth exceeds the economy`s potential;

(c) if so, what are the other main points suggested by the panel;

(d) to what extent these suggestions have been accepted; and

(e) to what extent the RBI has agreed to cut rates once the Inflation is eased?
records.ans_text:
THE MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF FINANCE

(SHRI PAWAN KUMAR BANSAL)

(a) and (b): The High Level Committee on Financial Sector Reforms chaired by Prof. Raghuram G. Rajan in its report has stated as follows :- `The RBI should formally have a single objective to stay close to a low inflation number, or within a range, in the medium term and move steadily to a. single instrument, the short term interest rate (repo and reverse repo) to achieve it. The RBI should be .as willing to cut rates when inflation is expected to fall below the objective so that the policy revives growth, as it is to raise rate when inflation, is expected to exceed the objective because growth exceeds the economy`s potential. It is in thi.s way that the RBI can best support the Objectives of growth and stability. `

(Source: Chapter 1, page 5 of the aforesaid Report)

(c): The Recommendations of the Commitee span over the areas of the macro-economic framework, broadening access to finance, levelling the playing field, creating more efficient markets, a growth-friendly regulatory environment and a robust for credit.

(d): The recommendations need to be examined before any action can be taken by the Government thereon.

(e): In the recent past, with the easing of inflationary pressures combined with tightening of liquidity following the global financial crisis, the RBI has reduced the CRR and Repo Rates in several stages,

records.name: T. Subbarami Reddy
records.qn_text:
(a) whether Government is giving top priority to exploit hydel potential in India, as hydel power is cheaper than the nuclear energy;

(b) whether Government proposes to implement a 40 MW hydro electric project on river Beas;

(c) whether Government has decided to give priority to power sector during the Eleventh Five Year Plan;

(d) if so, what concrete measures and steps Government is considering to take to improve the hydel power projects; and

(e) by when all the power projects, that are being presently set up, would be completed and what would be the total power generation (in MWs) after completion of these projects?
records.ans_text:
THE MINISTER OF POWER

( SHRI SUSHILKUMAR SHINDE )



(a) to (e) : A Statement is laid on the Table of the House.


STATEMENT
STATEMENT REFERRED TO IN REPLY TO PARTS (a) TO (e) OF STARRED QUESTION NO. 194 TO BE ANSWERED IN THE RAJYA SABHA ON 15.12.2008 REGARDING HYDEL POWER GENERATION.

(a) : Yes, Sir. The Government is giving priority to exploit hydro power development in India.

(b) : Dhaula Sidh Hydro Electric Project (40 MW) in Himachal Pradesh on river Beas is under development by M/s Satluj Jal Vidyut Nigam Ltd. for which agreement with the Govt. of Himachal Pradesh was signed on 27.10.2008.

(c) : Yes, Sir. The Planning Commission has approved a capacity addition of 78,700 MW in the 11th Plan as against the total capacity addition of 21,180 MW in the 10th Plan. The proposed capacity addition of 78,700 MW in the 11th Plan includes 36,874 MW in Central Sector, 26,783 MW in State Sector and 15,043 MW in Private Sector.

(d) : In order to give a fillip to hydro power development, the Government has approved the New Hydro Policy, 2008. This policy seeks to create a level playing field for private sector projects vis-à-vis public sector projects. It also offers some additional benefits to project affected families over and above the National Rehabilitation and Resettlement Policy

(NRRP), 2007. The Government has taken several further steps to achieve 11th Plan hydro capacity programme, viz:-
- Only those projects have been included in the capacity addition programme of 11th Plan which had all the statutory clearances required for execution of a project. Through rigorous monitoring, it had been ensured that orders for main works were placed in a timely manner.
- The monitoring mechanism has been strengthened to achieve targets by designating a nodal officer for each project, both at the conception stage as well as during execution. The nodal officers keep track of and facilitate resolution of problems which may delay the project by escalating the issue to appropriate levels for immediate resolution. In addition, regular review meetings are being organized in the Ministry of Power.
- The Government has also constituted a Task Force under the Chairmanship of Chairperson, CEA for the development of Model Contract Documents for accelerated development of hydel power projects. The responsibility of the Task Force is to recommend a set of Model Contract Documents which can be adopted uniformly by hydro project developers for early completion of projects. This would minimize contractual problems so as to avoid delays during project execution.
- The Government has constituted a sub-Committee of the Standing Group of Power Ministers called the `Task Force on Hydro Power Development`, to look into all issues relating to the development of hydro power, including issues of rehabilitation and resettlement of project affected persons, under the Chairmanship of Hon`ble Minister of Power. It also comprises various other Ministers from Central / State Governments and also representatives from CPSUs /CEA/ CWC etc.
- A National Power Projects Monitoring Panel has also been formed comprising various experts from different fields of engineering. The responsibility of this panel is to visit various on-going projects and to point out the shortcomings, if any, for early completion of the project.

(e) : The capacity addition during the 11th Plan is likely to increase significantly i.e. 78,700 MW, against the capacity addition of merely 21,180 MW, during the 10th Plan out of which the share of hydro power was 7,886 MW. A statement indicating the summary of capacity addition proposed during 11th Plan is at Annex-I. A statement indicating the hydro power projects proposed for likely benefits during 11th Plan is at Annex-II.

records.name: Rajeev Shukla
records.qn_text:
(a) Whether, even after 15 months of National Pharma Policy being referred to a Group of Ministers (GoM), Price control issue failed to get resolved and has landed in a legal tangle;

(b) if so, whether GoM has sought clarification on a Supreme Court order of March,2003 and its implications;

(c) if so, whether in the GoM meeting held in April,2008, no decision was taken on pharma policy, primarily on account of span of price control on drugs which has been interpreted as per Supreme Court Order;-

(d) if so, the steps Government proposes to take; and

(e) by when a final decision in this regard is likely to be taken?
records.ans_text:
THE MINISTER OF CHEMICALS AND FERTILIZERS AND MINISTER OF STEEL

(SHRI RAM VILAS PASWAN)

(a) to (e): A Statement is laid on the Table of the House.

STATEMENT REFERRED IN REPLY TO PARTS (a) to (e) OF THE RAJYA SABHA STARRED QUESTION NO.169 FOR ANSWER ON 12.12.2008 REGARDING NATIONAL PHARMA POLICY

(a) The Draft National Pharmaceuticals Policy was submitted before the Cabinet for its approval. The Cabinet considered the Policy in its meeting held on 11-1-2007 and decided that the matter may, in the first instance, be considered by a Group of Ministers (GOM). GOM has since been constituted and has held four meetings so far on 10.4.2007, 12.9.2007, 30.1.2008 and 30.4.2008. GOM is yet to make its recommendations to the Cabinet.

(b) & (c) Yes, Sir. In its 4th meeting held on 30.4.2008, the GOM has asked the Department that a reference may be made to the Department of Legal Affairs about interpretation /implications of Supreme Court`s Order dated 10.3.2003. In its 4 meeting itself held on 30.4.2008, the GOM among many other issues also discussed the issue of span of price control on drugs interpreted as per Supreme Court Order. The Group of Ministers (GOM) discussed the Supreme Court`s Order dated 10-3-2003 and it was felt that for better clarity, the opinion of Department of Legal Affairs may be solicited in this matter. The Department has obtained the opinion of Department of Legal Affairs and the same has been forwarded to the GOM for its consideration.

(d) & (e) The Department has constantly been making efforts to seek the decision of the GOM for early finalization of the Pharma Policy. Since, the final decision on the issue of Pharma Policy can only be taken after GOM takes a decision in this regard, this Department is not in a position to comment upon the likely timeframe for finalization of the policy.

records.qn_text:
(a) whether he has written to the Indian Ports Association to prepare a comprehensive information system on land management pattern in major ports of the country:

records.ans_text:
MINISTER OF SHIPPING, ROAD TRANSPORT AND HIGHWAYS

(SHRI T.R. BAALU)

(a) & (b): The Union Ministry for Shipping has requested Indian Ports Association (IPA) to evaluate the online system of land management of Tuticorin Port Trust. The Tuticorin Port Trust has recently introduced an online system to monitor and handle its land in order to bring transparency which includes digitization of all plots of land with its status and classification, automatic generation of alert message and online request for processing. The Indian Ports Association has been asked to evaluate this online system and make necessary study, if it is workable, so that it could be implemented in all major Port Trusts.

(c): Improvement/modernization of ports is a continuous process where various projects are taken up by the individual ports based on their requirement and forecast. The Department of Shipping has formulated a National Maritime Development Programme (NMDP) for modernization of the Port sector to facilitate enhanced private investment, improve service quality and promote competitiveness. Under the NMDP, 276 projects have been identified in the Port sector for implementation in the Major Ports which are to be taken up in a period from 2004-05 to 2011-12. These projects cover the entire gamut of activities in the Port sector which include berth development, deepening of channel, procurement of equipment and port craft, rail/ road connectivity and other associated work. Till date 36 projects of the port sector with total cost of Rs. 3930 crores have been completed under NMDP.

(d) & (e): No, Sir.

records.qtitle: STEPS TO RESOLVE TEXTILE INDUSTRY CRISIS .
records.name: Rajeev Shukla
records.qn_text:
(a) whether his Ministry has assured and announced that the textile sector will take right steps at the right time to resolve the textile industry crisis;

(b) if so, whether Government has decided to pay special attention to textile this year to solve the problems being faced by the sector by holding consultations with the Prime Minister;

(c) if so, the main decisions taken by Ministry to help and assist textile industry to meet the crisis;

(d) whether any special scheme of assistance has been announced by his Ministry; and

(e) if so, the details thereof?
records.ans_text:
THE MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF TEXTILES

(SHRI E.V.K.S. ELANGOVAN)

(a) to (e): Yes, Sir. Government has announced several relief measures to support the textile industry from time to time, which has been representing that textile exports have been affected by the global recession. Steps taken by Government to help and improve textiles industry include the following:

(i) The Technology Upgradation Fund Scheme (TUFS) was launched to facilitate the modernisation and upgradation of the textile industry both in the organised and unorganized sector. The Scheme has been further fine tuned to promote the rapid investments in the targeted sub-sectors of the textile industry. The cost of machinery has been further brought down by reducing the customs duty on imports.

(ii) To provide the textile industry with world-class infrastructure facilities for setting up their textile units, meeting international environmental and social standards, a Public-Private Partnership (PPP) based Scheme known as the “Scheme for Integrated Textile Park (SITP)” has been introduced in August 2005.

(iii) In 2004-05 Budget, the entire textile sector, except for man-made fibre and filament yarn was provided optional exemption from excise duty. In 2005-06 Budget, Central Value-added Tax (CENVAT) on Polyester Filament Yarn has been reduced from 24% to 16%. These modifications in fiscal levies aim at attracting more investments for modernization of textile sector.

(iv) To facilitate import of state of the art machinery to make our products internationally competitive in post quota regime, in 2005-06 Budget, the customs duty on textile machinery has been brought down to 10% except for 23 machinery appearing in List 49, which attracts Basic Customs Duty (BCD) of 15%. The concessional duty of 5% continues to be at 5% on most of the machinery items.

(v) Government has launched the Debt Restructuring Scheme w.e.f. Sept., 2003 with the principal objective to permit banks to lend to the textile sector at 8-9% rate of interest.

(vi) Government has allowed 100% Foreign Direct Investment in the textile sector under automatic route.

(vii) Government has de-reserved the readymade garments, hosiery and knitwear from SSI sector so that large-scale investments may be encouraged in these sectors.

(viii) National Institute of Fashion Technology (NIFT) has been set up to provide the leadership role in sensitizing the Industry to the concept of value addition by inducting trained professionals to manage the industry. This has resulted in an increased demand for trained professionals in various sectors servicing the industry.

(ix) A series of relief measures to textiles exporters such as enhanced DEPB & Duty drawback rates, reduced ECGC premium, subvention on credit rates, refund of service tax paid by exporters on various services etc.;

(x) Apparel Export Promotion Council (AEPC) has established Apparel Training Design Centres (ATDCs) throughout the country to cope with the requirement of skilled / semi-skilled manpower for the textile industry.

records.qtitle: SHARING OF INFORMATION ON TERROR CASES .
records.name: Rajeev Shukla
records.qn_text:
(a) whether India and Pakistan have decided to share information on terror cases;

(b) if so, whether he, recently had a telephonic conversation with his Pakistani counterpart to seek revival of the bilateral dialogue;

(c) whether during his visit, both Governments have agreed to fight terror together;

(d) if so, whether any agreement in this regard has been worked out;

(e) if so, the details thereof; and

(f) to what extent both the countries have drawn up a plan of joint action against terrorism?
records.ans_text:
THE MINISTER OF EXTERNAL AFFAIRS

(SHRI PRANAB MUKHERJEE)

(a) to (f) A statement is placed on the Table of the House.

STATEMENT REFERRED TO IN REPLY TO PARTS (A) TO (F) OF RAJYA SABHA STARRED QUESTION NO. 82 REGARDING ‘SHARING OF INFORMATION ON TERROR CASES’ FOR ANSWER ON 23.10.2008

We have regularly raised our concerns related to terrorism in Foreign Secretary and the Home Secretary level talks in the four rounds of the Composite Dialogue with Pakistan as also at Ministerial and Head of Government level meetings. A Joint Anti Terror Mechanism was established in November 2006 by India and Pakistan to identify and implement counter-terrorism initiatives and investigations. Three meetings of the Joint Anti Terror Mechanism have been held in March 2007, October 2007 and June 2008.

Issues related to terrorism in the recent past including the suicide bomb attack outside our Embassy in Kabul on 7th July, 2008 has vitiated the atmosphere between India and Pakistan and brought the Composite Dialogue process itself under stress.

The Foreign Minister of Pakistan had telephoned the External Affairs Minister on 20th July 2008 to condemn the attack on Indian Embassy in Kabul. During the conversation, EAM expressed our concerns to the Foreign Minister on this issue and stated that a conducive atmosphere has to be created for further progress in the Composite Dialogue.

Prime Minister met the Prime Minister of Pakistan in Colombo on 2nd August 2008 and frankly expressed his concerns about events which have had an impact on the relationship and on the prospects of the dialogue, namely, the attack on our Embassy in Kabul, the violations of ceasefire and the infiltration across the Line of Control. Both Prime Ministers expressed the determination to overcome these events and Prime Minister Gilani said that he would conduct an independent investigation on the attack on Indian Embassy in Kabul. During the meeting of the Prime Minister with the President of Pakistan in New York on 24th September 2008, it was decided that a special meeting of Joint Anti Terror Mechanism would be held in the month of October 2008 to discuss issues of mutual concern including the attack on the Indian Embassy in Kabul.

India expects Pakistan to fully implement its commitment of 6th January 2004 not to allow territory under its control to be used to support terrorism in any manner and in particular, act on the information which has been provided to it on terrorism related cases in meetings of the Composite Dialogue and of the Joint Anti Terror Mechanism.

records.name: T. Subbarami Reddy
records.qn_text:
(a) whether the Supreme Court, in the month of April, 2008, while dealing with issue of 27 per cent OBC reservation in higher education, did not lose sight of the importance of primary education arid felt that a lot needs to be done to universalize tile fundamental right to education;

(b) if so, whether in the judgment, stress has been given on primary and secondary education so that proper foundation, for higher education can be effectively laid;

(c) what other main points were made in the judgment; and

(d) what steps Government proposes to take in order to fulfil the constitutional obligation of providing compulsory education to the children of 6 to 14 years?
records.ans_text:
MINISTER OF HUMAN RESOURCE DEVELOPMENT

(SHRI ARJUN SINGH)

(a) to (d): A statement is 1aid on the Table of the House.

STATEMENT REFERRED TO IN REPLY TO PARTS (a) To (d) OF THE RAJYA SABHA STARRED QUESTION NO,35 FOR 20.10.2008 ASKED BY DR. T. SUBBARAMI REDDY AND SHRI RAJEEV SHUKLA, HONOURABLE MEMBERS OF PARLIAMENT, REGARDING IMPORTANCE OF PRIMARY EDUCATION

(a): Yes, Sir. The Supreme Court while disposing of the Writ Petition No. 265 of 2006 and a bunch of related Writ Petitions challenging the vires of Article 15(5) of the Constitution and the Central Educational Institutions (Reservation in Admission) Act, 2006, has emphasised that imparting of good quality education to all children aged six to fourteen years and regular attendance in school is necessary in order to ensure total compliance of Article 21A of the Constitution. In para 473(f) as reported in SCC 2008(5) SCALE I, the Apex Court has inter-alia observed that `Parliament should set a deadline; by which time free and compulsory education will have reached every child. This must be done within six months`.

(b): Yes, Sir. In Para 332(8) of the judgment referred to in part (a) above, the Apex Court has also observed that:
`Stress has to be on primary and secondary education so that proper foundation for higher education can be effectively laid`.

(c): The summary of the judgment in W.P No.265 of 2006 pronounced on 10.4.2008 and as read out in the court is as follows:
i) The 93rd Amendment Act does not violate the basic structure in so far as it relates to aided educational institutions. As far as private unaided educational institutions are concerned, 4 out of 5 Judges have left the question open while Justice Bhandari held that it was violative of the basic structure.
ii) The 2006 Act is constitutionally valid subject to exclusion of `Creamy Layer.`

(iii) The quantum of 27% reservation for OBCs is not illegal.

(iv) The CEI Act, 2006 is not illegal merely because time limit has not been ` prescribed for reservation.

(v) There should be a review of the lists of SEBCs every 5 years.`

(d): A legislative proposal on Right of Children to Free and Compulsory Education is under consideration of the Government.

records.qtitle: USE OF COOKING GAS BY MOTOR VEHICLES .
records.name: Rajeev Shukla
records.qn_text:
(a) whether Government is aware of many people including taxi service operators using cooking gas for running motor vehicles in the country;

(b) if so, the details thereof; and

(c) the steps taken by Government to control this?
records.ans_text:
MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF PETROLEUM AND NATURAL GAS (SHRI DINSHA PATEL)

(a) & (b): The possibility of misuse of the domestic LPG cylinders in motor vehicles cannot be ruled out due to the wide gap between the retail price of LPG for domestic use and market price for auto LPG.
During the last three years and April-December, 2007, 6997 motorists were caught by the Road Transport Authorities for which assistance was provided by the Oil Marketing Companies.

(c) : In order to stop misuse of domestic LPG cylinders, the Government has enacted “Liquefied Petroleum Gas (Regulation of Supply and Distribution) Order, 2000”; Liquefied Petroleum Gas (Regulation of Use in Motor Vehicles) Order,2001 and formulated “Marketing Discipline Guidelines, 2001” which provides for penal action against LPG distributors indulging in misuse of LPG.
Whenever OMCs receive complaints, these are investigated and if the complaint is established, suitable action is taken against the LPG distributor(s) in

accordance with the provisions of the MDG. MDG provides for following action against the distributor:-
- Fine of Rs. 20,000 plus the price of LPG diverted at commercial rates for 1st offence.
- Fine of Rs. 50,000 plus the price of LPG diverted at commercial rates for 2nd offence.
- Termination of the distributorship for 3rd offence.
In addition to the action taken by the OMCs, State Governments are empowered under the LPG (Regulation of Supply & Distribution) Order, 2000 promulgated under the Essential Commodities Act, 1955 to take action against misuse of domestic LPG. Similarly, the Weights and Measures Departments of the States / UTs initiate legal action against those LPG distributors found supplying under-weight LPG cylinders. The State Governments have been alerted from time to time to take steps against the misuse of domestic cylinders for unauthorized usage.
Government have issued advertisements cautioning the public that use of domestic LPG for non-domestic purposes is illegal, dangerous and against national interest. Through these advertisements, cooperation of the general public has also been sought to report any irregularity / malpractice to the OMCs.
The officials of OMCs carry out random checks at distributors godowns, delivery points, as well as en-route to ensure that no misuse takes place. The distributors of OMCs are under strict instructions to check the weight of cylinders at their godowns before delivery, and only cylinders with the specified weight are to be delivered to the customers. The distributors have also been instructed to ensure that the seals are verified & shown to the customers at the time of delivery. In case any under-weight cylinder is received by the customer, such cylinders are replaced with a fresh refill cylinder without any charges levied by the OMCs.

records.qtitle: PROBLEM OF LONG QUEUES AT DELHI AIRPORT .
records.name: Rajeev Shukla
records.qn_text:
(a) the interim measures taken by Government to deal with the claustrophobic conditions prompted by construction work going on at the New Delhi airport; and

(b) the proposed measures to deal with the long queues and rush at the airport entrance and immigration counters that cause troubles to domestic as well as international passengers?
records.ans_text:
MINISTER OF STATE (INDEPENDENT CHARGE) OF THE MINISTRY OF CIVIL AVIATION ( SHRI PRAFUL PATEL )

(a) & (b) Following steps have been taken to facilitate passengers and avoid rush and long queues during the ongoing upgradation and modernization works at the terminals of IGI airport:
(i) Space for passenger movement and smooth operation has been increased by relocating Airline offices outside the International Terminal building;
(ii)Modernisation activities have been rescheduled to implement them in a phased manner to minimise inconvenience to passengers;
(iii) New flight information display boards have been installed to facilitate passengers.
(iv) An agency has been deployed at the international terminal to guide the passengers to respective check-in counters,
(v) Security check gates have been increased from 8 to 14. Number of immigration counters on the departure side is being increased from 28 to 44 and further to 52. On arrival side, the immigration counters are being increased from 28 to 48.
(vi) Hand-baggage x-ray machines at international terminal have been increased from 8 to 12 which would further go upto 16 by June 2008. The check-in counters would increase from 78 to 100 by June 2008.

records.name: Rajeev Shukla
records.qn_text:
(a) whether Government have any policy for providing low cost housing finance to people from economically weaker sections;

(b) if so, the details thereof; and

(c) if not, the reasons therefor?
records.ans_text:
MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF HOUSING & URBAN POVERTY ALLEVIATION


( KUMARI SELJA )


(a)to(c): A Statement is laid on the Table of the Sabha.
STATEMENT
STATEMENT REFERRED TO IN REPLY TO RAJYA SABHA STARRED QUESTION NO. 604 FOR 17.5.2007 REGARDING PROVIDING LOW COST HOUSING FINANCE

(a)to(c): Yes, Sir. The Government has a policy supported by specialised institutions for providing low cost housing finance to the Economically Weaker Sections (EWS) of society. The Housing and Urban Development Corporation Ltd., (HUDCO), owned 100 per cent by the Government, has been providing concessional housing finance to EWS beneficiaries for more than three decades. Keeping in view the limited paying capacity of EWS beneficiaries, HUDCO has a repayment period up to 20 years. Currently financial assistance is extended to the EWS category at 9.5% (floating rate) of interest with a maximum limit of 90% of the project cost. Further, HUDCO`s current rate of interest for Special Categories of EWS Housing schemes related to Scheduled Castes/Scheduled Tribes, Widows, single women above 35 years of age, Physically Handicapped and beneficiaries located in areas affected by natural calamities is 9% (floating). In this manner, HUDCO is playing a significant role in providing low cost housing finance to economically weaker sections of society.
The Government in the budget for 2007-08 has announced an Interest Subsidy Scheme for urban areas which provides an interest subsidy to beneficiaries belonging to the Economically Weaker Sections (EWS) of society with a family income upto Rs.3,300/- per month and Low Income Group (LIG) beneficiaries (with a family income ranging between Rs,3,301 to Rs.7,300/- per month). The Interest Subsidy Scheme is meant for providing housing to the urban poor.

records.name: Rajeev Shukla
records.qn_text:

records.ans_text:

(SHRI ASHWANI KUMAR)

(b) to (d): Under the liberalized economic framework manufacturing of cement is exempt from industrial licensing. The Government is encouraging capacity-addition in the private sector by providing an investor friendly environment.

records.name: Abdul Wahab
records.qn_text:
(a) whether it is a fact that the country produces nearly eleven per cent of all the world`s vegetables and fifteen per cent of all fruits, yet its share in global exports of vegetables is only 1.7 per cent and in fruits, a meager 0.5 per cent only;

(b) if so, what are the major factors which are undermining out country`s potential for reaching super markets around the globe; and

(c) the steps taken by Government to boost horticulture export?
records.ans_text:
MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF AGRICULTURE

(SHRI KANTI LAL BHURIA)

(a): As per production database of the Food and Agriculture Organization (FAO) for the year 2005, India`s share in global production of vegetables and fruits was about 9.2% and 10.47% respectively and the share in global export of vegetables and fruits was about 3.72% and 0.36% respectively.

(b): The major factors undermining India`s potential for exports are: - 



1.	Unorganized export sector. 

2.	Lack of standards for farm & orchard maintenance including presence of pest and disease. 

3.	Lack of packaging standards. 

4.	Lack of market information.  

5.	Poor harvest infrastructure.
6.	Lack of proper cold chain and logistics facilities. 

7	Various non-tariff barriers imposed by importing countries, particularly, the developed 
	countries. 

8.	Lack of awareness among farmers about producing good quality and safe produce. 

9.	Lack of trained Horticulture manpower.
10.	High transport costs.


(c):	 The steps taken by Government to boost horticulture exports are:-


1.	Training programmes for improvement in quality of produce and developed pre-harvest and 
	post harvest protocols for export of grapes, mangoes, litchis, oranges, apples, Kinnows etc. 


2.	Export standards for 34 fruits and vegetables to EU have been prepared and notified under the 
	Agmark Act.


3.	Schemes for registration/ recognition of Pack houses/ processing units have been introduced 
	for fresh fruits and vegetables particularly mangoes and grapes, meat, poultry, dairy, 
	floriculture, peanuts, rice and cereal sectors. 


4.	A Scheme for grant of license to use certification mark ` Quality Produce of India` is in 
	operation for the processing/export.

  

5.	 Promoting commercial research for benefit of processors/exporters under its scheme for 
Research & Development through     various organizations under ICAR/CSIR system and 
Agriculture Universities. Creation of awareness among the farmers regarding orchard 
practices for qualitative production has been undertaken.


6.	Further the Department of Commerce   through APEDA is implementing the concept of Agri 
Export zones (AEZ) which aims at overall development of the supply and value chain of the 
identified commodities in a contiguous geographical region, having export potential, in 
collaboration with the State and Central Government agencies. 


7    The Government of India promotes agro-exports directly and through Commodity Boards, 
Export Promotion Councils and Commodity Associations.  In order to boost export of agro 
products, the Government, provides various incentives for infrastructure development, quality 
control, market development and promotion, packaging, publicity, information dissemination 
etc. besides providing assistance to exporters for conducting publicity campaigns, market 
surveys, sending delegations abroad, participating in international trade fairs, inviting 
potential buyers etc.  Further, initiatives include awareness amongst farmers about the latest 
techniques of farming through mass media support to agriculture   through Doordarshan. In 
order to disseminate information on improved production technologies amongst the farmers, 
block demonstrations and Integrated Pest Management (IPM) demonstrations are organized 
through State Department of Agriculture and Frontline Demonstrations through Indian 
Council of Agricultural Research.


8.    The Government has introduced a number of initiatives and interventions for enhancement of 
production and productivity of agricultural products, which inter-alia include Integrated 
Schemes under National Horticulture Mission for integrated Development of Horticulture, 
and Micro-irrigation.

records.qtitle: PERMISSION TO DRIVE UPTO TARMAC OF AIRPORTS .

records.name: Rajeev Shukla
records.qn_text:
(a) whether Government propose to start Mumbai-Delhi Industrial Corridor with the help of Japanese Government to be patterned on the lines of the Tokyo-Osaka Industrial belt;

(b) whether any detailed project has been finalized;

(c) if so, which states and cities, the corridor would cover;

(d) what is the overall investment outlay, involved in the project and which Industries would form part of the development;

(e) whether such industrial corridors are placed in the regions of Andhra Pradesh and West Bengal;

(f) if so, the details thereof; and (g) if not, the reasons therefor?
records.ans_text:
THE MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF COMMERCE & INDUSTRY

(SHRI ASHWANI KUMAR)

(a) to (d): A Memorandum of Understanding was signed on December 13, 2006 during the visit of Prime Minister of India to Japan for cooperating in establishment of the ‘Delhi Mumbai Industrial Corridor’ (DMIC). M/s IL&FS has been engaged by Department of Industrial Policy & Promotion to prepare the concept paper for the project. The concept paper, after discussions with the Japanese Government is being aimed to be finalized by July 2007. The detailed project will be finalized thereafter. The overall investment outlay cannot be estimated at this stage. The Corridor is likely to pass through the States of NCT of Delhi, Haryana, UP, Rajasthan, Gujarat and Maharashtra. The objective of the project is to delineate areas along the alignment of the Dedicated Freight Corridor between Delhi and Mumbai to provide good quality connectivity and other infrastructure like investment hubs comprising of industrial parks and estates, SEZs, agro-processing zones etc.

(e) to (g): The proposed Delhi-Mumbai Industrial Corridor does not cover the regions of Andhra Pradesh and West Bengal.

records.name: KARNENDU BHATTACHARJEE
records.qn_text:
(a) whether Government have decided to upgrade the status of 13 medical institutions and to set up six new medical institutions of the level of AIIMS;

(b) if so, the details and location of these institutions and hospitals; and

(c) the estimated cost thereof?
records.ans_text:
THE MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF HEALTH & FAMILY WELFARE

(SMT. PANABAKA LAKSHMI)

(a) to (c): Under Pradhan Mantri Swasthya Suraksha Yojana (PMSSY), it has been decided to set up six new AIIMS like institutions, each in the States of Bihar (Patna), Chattisgarh (Raipur), Madhya Pradesh (Bhopal), Orissa (Bhubaneshwar), Rajasthan (Jodhpur) and Uttaranchal (Rishikesh). The estimated cost for setting up each institute is Rs 332 Crores based on CPWD plinth area rates.

Under PMSSY, it has also been decided to strengthen 13 existing Medical College Institutions in terms of infrastructure and equipments. List of Institutions being upgraded is annexed. An outlay of Rs.120 crores has been approved for upgradation of each medical college institution. Out of this, the Government of India is investing Rs. 100 Crores for each institution and the State Government’s share is Rs 20 Crores and subsequent recurring, maintenance and manpower costs. In respect of SVIMS, Tirupati, the TTD trust is bearing half of the cost ie. Rs 60 Crores, and the GOI share is only Rs 60 Crores. Likewise, in respect of IMS (BHU) Varanasi, which is a GOI institution, Rs 20 Crores is being provided by Ministry of Human Resource Development.
Annexure 


Upgradation of 13 medical institutes under PMSSY


	The following 13 medical institutes have already been identified for 
upgradation under PMSSY.


1. Govt. Medical College, Jammu (J&K)


2. Govt. Medical College, Srinagar (J&K)


3. Kolkatta Medical College, Kolkatta (W.B.)
