records.name: Rajeev Shukla
records.qn_text:
(a) whether Government have a programme to create a 3D video surveillance database of New Delhi;

(b) if so, the details of the programme and estimated date of its completion;

(c) the benefits of the programme;

(d) whether such programme will be implemented in other major cities in the country; and

(e) if so, the details thereof?
records.ans_text:
MINISTER OF SCIENCE AND TECHNOLOGY AND MINISTER OF EARTH SCIENCES

(KAPIL SIBAL)



(a) & (b): No, Sir. However, under Department of Science and Technology (DST), a research project was initiated in collaboration with the Russian Academy of Sciences for creating a 3-D Global Information System (GIS) database/ video surveillance for City Zone –I in Delhi on pilot basis to demonstrate the technology. The Technology is still at the stage of testing and validation. Other parts of the Delhi are not being covered by DST.

(c) The 3D GIS Database/ surveillance system has a number of applications like change detection, urban planning and disaster management etc.

(d) & (e): Being a pilot project, no such programme is contemplated for any other major city at this stage.

records.name: Vijay Mallya
records.qn_text:
(a) whether according to the Planning Commission’s estimate the country is facing a crunch of trained healthcare personnel;

(b) if so, what is the total requirement and availability of healthcare personnel including doctors in the Indian System of Medicines and the percentage of availability thereon;

(c) what are the reasons for the short availability of healthcare personnel, particularly in rural areas; and

(d) what steps are proposed to be taken to provide full complement of healthcare personnel across the country?
records.ans_text:
THE MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF HEALTH & FAMILY WELFARE

(SMT. PANABAKA LAKSHMI)

(a) & (b) Yes, Sir. According to approach Paper for the 11th Five Year Plan, at present our health care system suffers from a severe shortage of trained personnel. Across States 6-30% posts of doctors remain vacant.
As per the exercise undertaken by the Confederation of Indian Industries in collaboration with Planning Commission the potential employment in health sector in 2010 has been assessed as 2602440 as against 1250000 in 2004 indicting a potential addition of 13.5 lakhs personnel.

(c ) The reasons for short availability are varied and include inter-alia.
> Delays in recruitment > Inappropriate personnel policy > Lack of basic amenities and incentives for working in the rural areas.

(d) Under NRHM, an additional ANM is being provided to all Sub centres functioning in the country as per 2001 census to supplement the existing staff. A number of steps have been taken by various State Governments to ensure services of doctors in rural areas such as:
> Compulsory rural area posting for admission to post-graduate courses and as a pre-requisite for promotion, foreign assignment or training abroad. > Compulsory rotation of doctors on completion of prescribed tenure as per classification of locations. > Contractual appointment of doctors. > Option to forgo non-practicing allowance and undertake practice without compromising on assigned duties, as per the service rules, offering incentive in form of allowance etc.
A Task Force under NRHM has also made recommendations for supplementing health care personnel in rural areas.

records.qtitle: POLIO SPREAD DUE TO INADEQUATE VACCINE .
records.name: Rajeev Shukla
records.qn_text:
(a) whether Government are aware of a recent finding by international experts stating that polio cases continue to be reported in India because the vaccine used in India is not targeting the specific polio strain prevalent in India;

(b) if so, whether in light of this finding, Government would propose to change the vaccine used in polio vaccination drives across India; and

(c) if so, the details of any other steps taken by Government to prevent the spread of polio virus in the country?
records.ans_text:
THE MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF HEALTH & FAMILY WELFARE

(SMT. PANABAKA LAKSHMI)

(a) &(b): In a recent publication in the journal Science, it is stated that the vaccine used in most of the world and in India over last 20 years ( the trivalent polio vaccine) which includes all strains (type-1, type-2 and type-3) may have somewhat lower effectiveness in some areas in India.
The Government was aware of the situation. Once the type-2 virus was eliminated and type- 3 was restricted to small area, based on the advice of India Expert Advisory Group (IEAG) a monovalent Oral Polio Vaccine which has improved effectiveness against the type-I virus is now being used.

( c ) In order to prevent spread of polio virus following actions are being taken: 
 

(i) Conducted consistent high quality supplementary immunization 
rounds in January, February, April, May, June, July, September and November, 
2006 and planed national immunization rounds in the month of January and 
February, 2007.


(ii) Social mobilization activities are being intensified by  involving 
the local influencers, community and religious leaders to improve community 
participation and acceptance  of polio vaccine.

records.qtitle: SUPPLY OF POTABLE WATER BY MUNICIPALITIES
records.name: Rajeev Shukla
records.qn_text:
(a) whether Government are aware of high contamination rate of potable water supplied by municipalities to homes across the cities in India;

(b) if so, whether Government have taken or propose to take any action to ensure that water supplied to homes by municipalities is free from contamination;

(c) if so, the details thereof; and

(d) if not, the reasons therefor?
records.ans_text:
MINISTER OF URBAN DEVELOPMENT

( SHRI S. JAIPAL REDDY )


(a)to(d): A Statement is laid on the Table of the Sabha.
STATEMENT
STATEMENT REFERRED TO IN REPLY TO RAJYA SABHA STARRED QUESTION NO.335 FOR 14.12.2006 REGARDING SUPPLY OF POTABLE WATER BY MUNICIPALITIES.

(a): `Drinking Water Supply in urban areas` is a State subject. It is the responsibility of State Governments/Urban Local Bodies to provide safe drinking water to population living in urban areas, in accordance with the Water Quality Guidelines indicated in the Manual on Water Supply & Treatment published by Central Public Health & Environmental Engineering Organisation (CPHEEO), technical wing of Ministry of Urban Development, Government of India. State Governments/ULBs should undertake water quality testing/ monitoring test to make it fit for human consumption before supplying it to consumers. Data regarding high contamination rate of potable water supplied by municipalities to homes across cities in India is not maintained by Government of India.

(b)to(d): To ensure that water supplied by municipalities is free from contamination, this Ministry has published the following Manuals for guidance:-

(i) Manual on Water Supply & Treatment;

(ii) Manual on Operation & Maintenance of Water Supply System. The guidelines laid down in aforesaid Manuals are to be complied with by municipalities. The provision covers various technical, operational and managerial aspects including quality parameters of drinking water, monitoring and surveillance for proper operation and maintenance of water supply system for supplying safe drinking water to consumers.

records.qtitle: REGULARIZATION OF UNAUTHORIZED COLONIES IN DELHI.
records.name: Rajeev Shukla
records.qn_text:
(a) whether Government have a proposal to regularize a large number of unauthorized residential colonies in New Delhi; and

(b) if so, the details of the proposal and the tentative date of its implementation?
records.ans_text:
THE MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF URBAN DEVELOPMENT

( SHRI AJAY MAKEN )

(a)&(b): The Union Government had prepared guidelines for regularization of unauthorized colonies in 2001. These guidelines were revised in 2004. The GNCTD has again requested for revision of certain provisions of the revised guidelines. Inter-departmental consultation has been undertaken in this regard by the Union Government.
As per Delhi High Court directions dated 29.9.2004 in CWP No.8487/2003 - Punjabi Bagh Cooperative Housing Society Vs MCD & Ors., the Government of National Capital Territory (GNCTD) had invited applications from Societies/Associations of unauthorized colonies existing as on 31.3.2002, seeking regularization and received 1432 applications. Further, 107 applications have been received by GNCTD in response to a later advertisement inviting applications. GNCTD has informed that verification on site of these applications has been taken up through different agencies.
In view of the legal and administrative issues involved, no time frame has been fixed.

records.name: Rajeev Shukla
records.qn_text:
(a) whether it is a fact that out of approximately 66,000 km. of highways in India, only 6000 km. highways have four lanes;

(b) whether Government are of the view that given a high growth rate of interest vehicular traffic, even four-laned highways will prove to be insufficient to handle traffic in near future; and

(c) if so, the details of any schemes by Government to widen the remaining length of highways into four-lanes or six-lanes alongwith estimated date of completion of these schemes?
records.ans_text:
THE MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF SHIPPING, ROAD TRANSPORT AND HIGHWAYS

(SHRI K.H. MUNIYAPPA)



(a) There are about 66,590 kilometers length of National Highways in the country and out of which about 7699 kilometers length is of four-lane and above standard.


(b) and (c ) The development of National Highways including widening to 4/6 lane standard is a continuous process and depends upon the traffic , its growth, inter-se priority and availability of funds. Accordingly, the Government has taken up several projects for improvement of National Highways including four laning, six laning and construction of expressways under the various schemes as National Highways Development Project (NHDP), Special Accelerated Road Development Programme in North East region

(SARDP-NE) and under the Annual Programme of the Department of Road Transport and Highways. The details of such approved projects are given below. These are in addition to 4/6 laning of National Highways under the ongoing NHDP Phase I and Phase II.

records.qtitle: COORDINATION BETWEEN POLICE AND INTELLIGENCE AGENCIES .
records.name: Rajeev Shukla
records.qn_text:
(a) whether Government have taken any steps in the recent months to increase coordination and to streamline the flow of information between intelligence agencies and State police departments;

(b) if so, the details thereof; and

(c) if not, the reasons therefor?
records.ans_text:
MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF HOME AFFAIRS

(SHRI SRIPRAKASH JAISWAL)

(a) to (c): For streamlining intelligence effort, Multi Agency Centre (MAC) has been functioning at Delhi and Subsidiary Multi Agency Centres (SMACs) in various States comprising representatives of various security, law enforcement and intelligence agencies. Joint Task Force on Intelligence (JTFI) has also been coordinating the efforts of intelligence agencies at the Centre and in the States. Financial Intelligence Unit(FIU) has also become operational to facilitate intelligence relating to money laundering.

records.qtitle: US ASSISTANCE IN CIVIL AVIATION SECTOR .
records.name: Rajeev Shukla
records.qn_text:
(a) Whether the Federal Aviation Authority of the United States and the Ministry signed a Memorandum of Agreement paving the way for technical assistance from US on a host of aviation related matters;

(b) if so, what are the other main features of the agreement;

(c) whether MoA is an umbrella agreement and would have many subordinate agreements as and when signed with different agencies; and

(d) if so, to what extent the agreement will be helpful to boost aviation management?
records.ans_text:
MINISTER OF STATE (INDEPENDENT CHARGE) OF THE MINISTRY OF CIVIL AVIATION ( SHRI PRAFUL PATEL )

(a): Yes, Sir,

(b), (c) and (d): This MoA creates enabling provisions to sign agreements for technical and managerial expertise in civil aviation sector in the following areas:


(i) Providing technical and managerial expertise in developing, improving and operation of civil aviation infrastructure, standards, procedures, policies, training and equipment.
(ii) Co-operation in a range of aviation safety areas.
(iii) Providing training for civil aviation personnel.
(iv) Inspection and calibration of our civil aviation equipment and air navigation facility.
(v) Assistance in aircraft certification in India.
(vi) Assistance in the field of Helicopter Operational Safety initiative.

records.name: Rajeev Shukla
records.qn_text:
(a) whether attention of Government has been brought to a recent report published in the print media regarding trafficking of women and children in the country, sponsored by National Human Rights Commission, which has pointed that India is slowly turning into a centre for child-sex tourists;

(b) whether Government are also aware that the problem is more acute in India’s popular tourist destinations including Goa and Kerala;

(c) if so, whether Government have taken any steps to prevent children from sexual abuse in these tourist circuits;

(d) if so, the details thereof; and

(e) if not, the reasons therefor?
records.ans_text:
MINISTER OF STATE (INDEPENDENT CHARGE) FOR WOMEN AND CHILD DEVELOPMENT (SHRIMATI RENUKA CHOWDHURY)

(a)&(b) As per the Report of Action research on Trafficking in Women and Children, August 2004 sponsored by National Human Rights Commission, child sex tourism is prevalent in India and also in the States of Goa and Kerala.

(c)&(d) the Immoral Traffic (Prevention) Act, 1956 (ITPA) supplemented by the Indian Penal Code prohibits trafficking in human beings including children for purpose of prostitution and lays down severe penalties for traffickers. The ITPA is now being further amended providing for more stringent punishment for trafficking in persons including children. The Ministry of Women and Child Development conducts advocacy, awareness generation, sensitization programmes for prevention of child trafficking. The Central Advisory Committee on combating Child Prostitution headed by Secretary, Ministry of Women and Child Development, Government of India reviews the State’s activities in combating trafficking and prostitution every quarter. The Ministry of Women and Child Development also runs Swadhar shelter Homes which provide shelter, food, clothing, emotional support, counseling, rehabilitation and other facilities to sex workers including children.

(e) Does not arise.

records.name: Rajeev Shukla
records.qn_text:
(a) whether it is a fact that a recent analysis by Supreme Court has revealed that approximately 30 lakh minor cases of bounced cheques and traffic offences are pending in lower courts, many of them for years;

(b) if so, whether Government are planning any action to dispose of these cases quickly by imposition of penalties or otherwise; and

(c) if so, the details thereof?.
records.ans_text:
MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF LAW AND JUSTICE

(SHRI K. VENKATAPATHY)

(a) to (c) As per information furnished by the Supreme Court of India, 17,19,569 cases under Section 131 of the Negotiable Instruments Act and 22,45,879 Traffic Challan Cases pending in the courts of Judicial Magistrates First Class/Metropolitan Magistrates and Chief Judicial Magistrates. Quick disposal of such cases is within the domain of the judiciary. With a view to expeditiously disposing petty cases in the courts, the Conference of Chief Ministers and Chief Justices held on 11.3.2006 made the following resolution which has been forwarded to the State Governments for appropriate action:
` ;Cases involving petty offences including traffic and municipal challans be transferred to the courts of Special Metropolitan Magistrates / Special Judicial Magistrates.`

records.qtitle: FRESH APPROVALS FOR FIELD TRIALS OF GM CROPS
records.name: Rajeev Shukla
records.qn_text:
(a) the Government’s response following a Hon’ble Supreme Court directive barring it from issuing fresh approvals of field trials of Genetically Modified (GM) crops;

(b) whether Government propose to direct independent enquiry into the long term economic viability of GM crops in the Indian environment;

(c) If so, the details thereof; and

(d) If not, the reasons therefor?
records.ans_text:
MINISTER OF ENVIRONMENT AND FORESTS (SHRI A. RAJA)

(a) to (d) A Statement is laid on the Table of the House.
STATEMENT REFFERED TO IN THE REPLY TO PARTS (a) TO (d) OF THE RAJYA SABHA STARRED QUESTION NO. 246 BY SHRI RAJEEV SHUKLA REGARDING “FRESH APPROVALS FOR FIELD TRIALS OF GM CROPS” DUE FOR REPLY ON 8.12.2006.

(a) The Government of India has not approved any fresh field trials on transgenic crops, after the Supreme Court direction dated 22.9.2006 However, field trials for transgenic mustard developed by University of Delhi South Campus, New Delhi have been permitted as per Hon’ble Supreme Court order dated 13.10.2006 passed on an appeal filed by Delhi University.

(b) to (d) There is no proposal to direct independent inquiry into the long term economic viability of GM crops in the Indian environment.
As per the prevailing statutory rules, procedures and guidelines under the Rules for the Manufacture, Use/Import/Export and Storage of Hazardous Micro Organisms/ Genetically Engineered Organisms or Cells, 1989 notified under the Environmental (Protection) Act, 1986, the safety, efficacy, agronomic advantage and economic viability of the introduced trait in GM crops are assessed on a case to case basis by the regulatory agencies prior to according environmental release of the product. No prior determination that GM crops in general or a specific GM crop in particular, is, or is not viable in Indian conditions is scientifically defensible. The evidence has to be generated, and evaluated in each case in the Indian context, through properly defined Protocols.

records.name: Rajeev Shukla
records.qn_text:
(a) the total number of cases of RDX seizures made by Indian security forces during the preceding year, and the total quantity of RDX thus recovered;

(b) whether it is a fact that a majority of RDX thus seized is being smuggled into country, because a majority of airports in India lack suitable equipment to scan and detect RDX; and

(c) if so, what steps Government propose to take to prevent inbound smuggling of RDX at all entry points of the country?
records.ans_text:
MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF HOME AFFAIRS

(SHRI SRIPRAKASH JAISWAL)

(a): As per information available with this Ministry, 1021 Kgs. (Approx.) of RDX were seized by Police and security forces in different parts of the country in 2005, while in 2006 (till October), 724 Kgs.(Approx.) of RDX were seized.

(b): There are no inputs to suggest that the RDX so seized were smuggled into the country through the Airports.

(c): The necessary steps have been taken to enhance surveillance and physical security and scanning of baggage at the Airports. The security of a large number of Airports is now looked after by CISF. The Government has also initiated several measures to prevent smuggling of arms, ammunition and explosives from across the borders, which inter-alia include i) ongoing fencing of Eastern and Western borders, ii) deployment of border guarding forces, iii) strengthening of intelligence capacity along the borders, iv) periodic sensitization of Border Guarding Forces and the State governments particularly in the border states, v) strengthening of coastal security, etc.

records.name: Rajeev Shukla
records.qn_text:
(a) whether Government have any proposal to divide the electricity consumption in the country into peak and off-peak hours, with electricity costing cheaper during the off- peak hours; and

(b) if so, the details thereof?
records.ans_text:
THE MINISTER OF POWER

( SHRI SUSHILKUMAR SHINDE )


(a) & (b) : A Statement is laid on the Table of the House.
STATEMENT
STATEMENT REFERRED TO IN REPLY TO PARTS (a) & (b) OF STARRED QUESTION NO. 180 TO BE ANSWERED IN THE RAJYA SABHA ON 04.12.2006 REGARDING DIFFERENTIAL TARIFF FOR ELECTRICITY.


(a) & (b): The National Electricity Policy seeks to encourage reduction of the difference between electrical power demand during peak periods and off-peak periods in order to reduce the requirements for capacity additions. It states that differential tariff structure for peak and off peak supply and metering arrangements (Time of Day metering) would be conducive to load management objectives. TOD meters for large consumers with a minimum load of one MVA are sought to encourage in the first instance.
The Tariff Policy requires the State Electricity Regulatory Commissions to introduce two-part tariffs featuring separate fixed and variable charges and time differentiated tariff on priority for large consumers (consumers with demand exceeding 1 MW) within one year. This would also help in flattening the peak and implementing various energy conservation measures.
Wherever such differential tariff is introduced, it would naturally involve higher tariffs during peaking hours and lower tariffs during off-peak hours.

records.name: Rajeev Shukla
records.qn_text:
(a) whether Government are aware of the acute shortage of trained computer professionals in the country against the demands of a rapidly growing IT industry;

(b) if so, whether Government has a proposal to open or facilitate opening technical institutes focused on IT industry, to train large number of people for employment in the IT industry;

(c) if so, the details thereof; and

(d) if not, the reasons therefor?
records.ans_text:
MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF HUMAN RESOURCE DEVELOPMENT

(SMT. D. PURANDESWARI)

(a) to (d): As per the information submitted by the All India Council for Technical Education (AICTE), with the anticipated annual growth rate of 15% in admissions in Engineering Colleges the availability of manpower for IT jobs in terms of numbers may not be an issue. However, enhancing the employability of available manpower may be the issue. Depending on the availability of funds during the 11th Five Year Plan, new technical Institutions focused on IT would be opened.

records.qtitle: PREVENTION OF BIRD FLU AMONG THE HUMAN BEINGS .
records.name: Rajeev Shukla
records.qn_text:
(a) whether Government have any contingency plan ready to prevent the reoccurrence of bird flu virus in the human population in the country in the coming months;

(b) if so, the details thereof; and

(c) if not, the reasons therefor?
records.ans_text:
THE MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF HEALTH & FAMILY WELFARE

(SMT. PANABAKA LAKSHMI)


(a) Yes, Sir.

(b) & (c) Ministry of Health and Family Welfare, Government of India has a contingency plan to manage human cases of Avian Influenza. The plan includes active surveillance, preventive public health measures, clinical management, stockpiling of specific drugs, personal protective equipments and IEC activities.
This plan was operationalized during the outbreak of Avian Flue among poultry in Nundurbar and Jalgaon districts of Maharasthra, Surat District of Gujarat and Burhanpur district of Madhya Pradesh in February-April, 2006. Due to the coordinated action no human case of avian influenza was reported. This contingency plan would hold good for any reoccurrence of bird flu in human population in the country.

records.name: Rajeev Shukla
records.qn_text:
(a) whether it is a fact that the fertilizer subsidy burden on Government have touched a whopping Rs.32,840 crores against the budgeted Rs.18,752 crores during the current fiscal;

(b) if so, whether Government propose to take any action to limit the subsidy expenditure; and

(c) If so, the details thereof?
records.ans_text:
THE MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF CHEMICALS AND FERTILIZERS AND MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF PARLIAMENTARY AFFAIRS.

(SHRI B.K.HANDIQUE)

(a) The requirement of funds for subsidy on sale of fertilizers during 2006-07 is estimated at Rs.27039.00 crore and in addition, there was a carry-over liability from the previous year of Rs.5913.94 crore increasing the total requirement to Rs.32952.94 crores in the current year. Department of Fertilizers has till now received Rs.18752.91 crore for payment of subsidy in the current year.

(b) & (c). The increase in subsidy expenditure is due to the increase in consumption of fertilizers within the country coupled with the increase in cost of fertilizer due to increase in raw material cost in the international market. The Department is making efforts to encourage the Indian industry to set up Joint Ventures in raw material resource rich countries to ensure sustained availability of inputs and finished fertilizers in the country at reasonable prices. It is expected that Indian investment in fertilizer sector abroad and will ensure long-term supplies of raw materials/finished fertilizers to the country as also help in stabilizing the volatility of the prices in the international market. The New Pricing Scheme for Urea units in the country also lays emphasis on maximizing indigenous production with energy efficiency and competitiveness at global standards. This will also help in controlling subsidy expenditure.

records.qtitle: CREATION OF OFFICE OF A TELECOM OMBUDSMAN .
records.name: Rajeev Shukla
records.qn_text:
(a) whether Government have any proposal to formulate the office of a telecom Ombudsman to resolve telecom subscribers` problems;

(b) if so, the details thereof; and

(c) the estimated time-frame by which the office of the Ombudsman would be made functional?
records.ans_text:
THE MINISTER OF COMMUNICATIONS AND INFORMATION TECHNOLOGY

(SHRI DAYANIDHI MARAN)

(a) to (c) A Statement is laid on the Table of the House.

STATEMENT TO BE LAID ON THE TABLE OF THE RAJYA SABHA IN RESPECT OF PARTS (a) TO (c) OF RAJYA SABHA STARRED QUESTION NO. 124 FOR 30TH NOVEMBER, 2006 REGARDING CREATION OF OFFICE OF A TELECOM OMBUDSMAN.


(a) & (b) No, Sir. Telecom Regulatory Authority of India had recommended setting up of office of Ombudsman. However, Government after careful consideration have decided that this was not a feasible proposition. Instead various Service Providers were asked on 22nd September, 2005, to set up a consumer redressal mechanism at following levels:- 




(i)	Call Centre level 

(ii)	An Appellate Authority within service provider`s organization


Further, all Service Providers were asked to publicise about their redressal mechanism
on regular basis through various advertising means or through telephone bills sent to
their subscribers.


(c)	Does not arise in view of (a) & (b) above.

records.qtitle: REDUCTION IN TRANSACTION COSTS FOR EXPORTS .
records.name: Rajeev Shukla
records.qn_text:
(a) whether it is a fact that Indian exporters have to incur huge transaction costs to transport their products in foreign markets, compared to exporters from other countries;

(b) if so, whether Government have taken any steps to reduce the transaction costs and to simplify the procedures, in order to make our exporters more competitive;

(c) if so, the details thereof; and

(d) if not, the reasons therefor?
records.ans_text:
MINISTER OF COMMERCE AND INDUSTRY

( SHRI KAMAL NATH )


(a) to (d) Indian exporters may have to incur higher transaction costs as compared to other developed countries.
Government has taken several steps to reduce the transaction costs and to simplify the procedures. It is a continuous and ongoing exercise. To make the Export Promotion schemes user friendly, major simplification of procedures has been introduced. To that end, a single application form covering all Export Promotion Schemes has been introduced, thereby enabling filing of applications on EDI mode. This has significantly reduced filing of multiple documents. Online exchange of data with the Department of Customs, remittance of application fees through EFT are some of the other steps which have already been taken to reduce transaction costs.

records.name: Rajeev Shukla
records.qn_text:
(a) the details of the greenfield airports currently under construction in the country alongwith the estimated dates of beginning of their operations; and

(b) the details of greenfield airport projects currently in the process of approval?
records.ans_text:
MINISTER OF STATE (INDEPENDENT CHARGE) OF THE MINISTRY OF CIVIL AVIATION ( SHRI PRAFUL PATEL )
(a): Two greenfield airports namely Hyderabad International Airport and Bangalore International Airport are under construction. Both these Airports are expected to start their operation by April 2008.
(b): Proposals from State Governments for greenfield airports at Pekyong in Sikkim, Chiethu near Kohima in Nagaland, Chakan II, (Rajguru Nagar) near Pune & Navi Mumbai in Maharashtra, Kannur in Kerala and Itanagar in Arunachal Pradesh have been received.`In-principle` approval has been given for a new airport at Mopa in Goa. The other proposals are at different stages of consideration.

records.qtitle: DROP OUT RATE OF GIRL STUDENTS
records.name: Rajeev Shukla
records.qn_text:
(a) whether it is a fact that number of girl students who drop out of schools at all levels is uniformly and significantly higher than that of boy student,,;;

(b) whether Government have any scheme underway that seeks to rectify this anomaly;

(c) if so, the details thereof; and

(d) if not, the reasons therefor ?
records.ans_text:
MINISTER OF HUMAN RESOURCE DEVELOPMENT

(SHRI ARJUN SINGH)

(a) to (d) : A statement is laid on the Table of the Sabha. STATEMENT
STATEMENT REFERRED TO IN REPLY TO PARTS (a) to (d) OF THE RAJYA SABHA STARRED QUESTION N0. 63 FOR ANSWER ON 27.11.2006 ASKED BY SHRI RAJEEV SHUKLA REGARDING ` DROP-OUT OF GIRL STUDENTS `

(a): In 2003-04, the drop-out rates for` girl students in the country as a whole at the primary stage (Classes I-V), at elementary stage (Classes I-VIII) and Secondary stage (Classes I-X) were 28.6%, 52.9% and 64.9% respectively . At the primary stage, the drop-out rate for girls was lower than that of boys, whereas for elementary and secondary stages, they were higher than that of boys.

(b),(c) & (d): Under Sarva Shiksha Abhiyan, a multi-pronged approach has been adopted for reducing drop-out rates. One set of interventions relates to strengthening of primary and upper primary schools and improving the quality of education through improvement in school infrastructure, recruitment of additional teachers, annual school grants, regular training of teachers, introduction of good and innovative teaching practices that make class rooms more joyful and attractive regular academic support to teachers, etc. On the other hand, several interventions aim at improving the demand for schooling through community mobilization, special interventions for enrolment and retention of vulnerable groups of children including girls and children of weaker sections. Measures are also being undertaken to strengthen the accountability of the school system towards parents and the community. The Mid-Day Meal Scheme that: provides a cooked meal to all children of Government and Government-aided primary schools, Education Guarantee Scheme (EGS) Centers and Alternative & Innovative Education (AIE) centers, also has the potential for promoting school enrolment and participation.

Free textbooks are provided to all girls and all SC & ST students up to the elementary stage. Under the National Programme for Education of Girls of the Elementary Level (NPEGEL), additional resources are provided to 3164 educationally backward blocks for interventions of community mobilization, bridge courses for out-of-school girls, strengthening of model cluster schools, gender sensitization of teachers etc. to promote retention of girls in primary and upper primary schools. 1000 Kasturba Gandhi Balika Vidyalayas (KGBV) which are residential schools for girls at upper primary level, particularly for girls from disadvantaged sections of society, have been approved in the current year besides 1180 KGBVs sanctioned earlier in educationally backward blocks of the country.
As per a new Scholarship scheme introduced by Central Board of Secondary Education (CBSE) from the academic session 2006-07, a girl who is the only child of her parent, and who secures 60% or more marks in class X examination for the year 2006 onwards under C3SE system, would be given a scholarship of Rs.500 per month for studying in classes XI and X]II in a CBSE affiliated school which charges tuition fee of not more than Rs. 1000 per month.
All Kendriya Vidyalayas provide fee waiver to single girl children
from classes VI to XII. In Jawahar Navodaya Vidyalayas, one third of the seats are reserved for girls.

records.qtitle: TECHNOLOGY TRANSFER FROM US FOR F PLANES .
records.name: Rajeev Shukla

(a) whether Government have any proposal to initiate requisite technology transfers from US-based suppliers, to enable F-16 fighter planes to be built in the country by Hindustan Aeronautics Limited; and

(b) if so, the details thereof?
records.ans_text:
(RAO INDERJIT SINGH) MINISTER OF STATE FOR DEFENCE PRODUCTION


(a) No, Sir.

(b) Does not arise.

records.name: Rajeev Shukla
records.qn_text:
(a) whether Government are aware of news reports stating that many airlines force their pilots to fly for longer hours, thus endangering the security of air passengers;

(b) if so, the details of any action contemplated or taken in this regard;

(c) whether the international system of upper-limit of maximum flying hours for commercial pilots exists in India; and

(d) if so, the details thereof?
records.ans_text:
MINISTER OF STATE (INDEPENDENT CHARGE) OF THE MINISTRY OF CIVIL AVIATION ( SHRI PRAFUL PATEL )

(a):- Directorate General of Civil Aviation (DGCA) have not received any such representation or complaint from the Pilots.

(b):- Does not arise.

(c) and (d):- Flight Duty time and Flight Time Limitation for Flight Crew have been specified by DGCA in their Aeronautical Information Circular (AIC) 28/1992 in accordance with international practices. It also contains the duration of rest period and number of landings etc. for all types of operations. All operators are required to follow these guidelines.

records.qtitle: INSTITUTIONAL BIAS AGAINST HIV POSITIVE PEOPLE .
records.name: Rajeev Shukla
records.qn_text:
(a) whether Government are aware about several cases of institutional bias against HIV positive people in the country, including instances of Government schools and offices preventing HIV people from studying and working there;

(b) if so, whether Government propose to take any action in this regard; and

(c) if so, the details thereof; and

(d) if not, the reasons therefore?
records.ans_text:
THE MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF HEALTH & FAMILY WELFARE

(SMT. PANABAKA LAKSHMI)

(a) Yes, Sir.

(b) to (d) The Government support non-discrimination of people living with HIV/AIDS in schools and at workplace. The policy laid down is that no mandatory HIV testing should be imposed as pre-condition for providing employment (except Armed Forces) school education or for providing health care. Guidelines have been issued to all State AIDS Control Societies to ensure that there is no discrimination to HIV positive patients attending government hospitals in the State for treatment purposes.

(SHRI MANI SHANKAR AIYAR)


(a) to (d): A statement is laid on the table of the House.


STATEMENT REFERED TO IN REPLY TO PARTS (a) to (d) OF THE RAJYA SABHA STARRED QUESTION NO. 313 ASKED BY SHRI RAJEEV SHUKLA REGARDING INDIA`S BID FOR 2014 ASIAN GAMES

records.qtitle: EVACUATION STRATEGY FOR INDIAN CITIZENS ABROAD
records.name: Rajeev Shukla
records.qn_text:
(a) the total number of Indian citizens living in various war-prone and crisis-ridden areas of the world;

(c) if so, the salient features thereof; and

(d) if not, the reasons therefor?
records.ans_text:
THE MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF EXTERNAL AFFAIRS

(SHRI ANAND SHARMA)

(a) The number of Indians living in war-prone and crisis-ridden areas of the world is around 18000.

(b) & (c) As per Government instructions, Indian Missions in countries with sizeable Indian population are required to prepare a contingency plan to facilitate the evacuation of Indian nationals from the country concerned in the event of a war/crisis. The contingency plan is vetted by the Ministry of External Affairs and activated in consultation with other concerned Ministries/agencies of the government whenever large scale evacuation of Indian nationals is undertaken; the Indian nationals are evacuated to either a safe neighbouring country or to India depending on the situation in the region and other factors.

(d) Does not arise.

records.qtitle: WORKING CONDITIONS IN SCIENTIFIC RESEARCH ESTABLISHMENTS .
records.name: Rajeev Shukla
records.qn_text:
(a) whether it is a fact that lack of good research facilities and poor working conditions including low salaries in the country`s major scientific research establishments is the major reason for fewer students opting for science courses at the college level this year;

(b) if so, the details of any corrective action Government plans to take in this regard; and

(c) the details of steps taken by Government to improve the work environment at our scientific research establishments?
records.ans_text:
MINISTER OF SCIENCE AND TECHNOLOGY AND MINISTER OF EARTH SCIENCES

(KAPIL SIBAL)

(a) to (c): No Sir. The students` choice to take admission in various science courses is driven by other avenues available in the country. This is a cyclical phenomenon and is in response to the available employment opportunities in various other sectors. The Government have taken various corrective measures like enhanced research infrastructure in the universities for better training of students, adoption of new syllabi to match the global changes, special schemes for attracting students to science streams, etc. The salary of a scientist employed in a Government funded institute cannot be comparable to that in private funded organizations in the country.
Science is driven by individual passion and commitment and not necessarily by monetary benefits. However, a reasonable minimum level of good research facilities and better working conditions and associated perquisites will greatly improve the present situation. The Government has doubled the funding for science and technology in the 10th Plan and the same will be further enhanced in 11th Plan.

records.name: Rajeev Shukla
records.qn_text:
(a) whether it is a fact that Government have approved a project for strengthening of western grid in the country;

(b) if so, the details of the project and the estimated date of its completion; and

(c) the details of the benefits accruing to Maharashtra following the project`s completion?
records.ans_text:
THE MINISTER OF POWER

( SHRI SUSHILKUMAR SHINDE )


(a) to (c) : Yes, Sir. Investment approval has been issued for `Western Region System Strengthening Scheme-II` of Power Grid Corporation of India Limited (PGCIL) on 24th July, 2006. The estimated cost of the project is Rs. 5221.23 Crore. The Scheme is scheduled to be implemented within 48 months from the date of investment approval. The project will facilitate drawal of power from other regions and its dispersal to various load centres of Western Region, including Maharashtra. It will also improve the reliability of the Western Region Grid.

records.qtitle: FREQUENT TRAVELLER SCHEMES ON SHATABDI TRAINS .

records.ans_text:
MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF RAILWAYS

(SHRI R.VELU)

(a) & (b): With a view to improve the patronisation of higher classes, where occupancy level is relatively low as compared to that in Sleeper class and 3-AC classes, a Scheme of Frequent Travellers (SOFT) has been launched in the month of February, 2006, which is applicable to 1st AC, 2AC and AC Chair Car Classes. A Frequent Traveller will get a complimentary train trip after certain numbers of reward points are accumulated.

records.qtitle: PANCHAYATI RAJ YUVA SHAKTI KHEL KOOD ABHIYAN .

THE MINISTER OF PANCHAYATI RAJ AND YOUTH AFFAIRS & SPORTS

(SHRI MANI SHANKAR AIYAR)

records.qtitle: CONTINGENCY PLAN FOR CRUDE OIL PRICES
records.name: Rajeev Shukla
records.qn_text:

(b) if so, whether Government have a contingency plan to minimize the effect of surging oil prices;

(c) if so, the details thereof; and

(d) if not, the reasons therefor ?
records.ans_text:
MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF PETROLEUM AND NATURAL GAS (SHRI DINSHA PATEL)

(a): From the Energy Information Administration (EIA) reports and the latest Organization of Petroleum Exporting Countries (OPEC) statements, it appears that international oil prices are expected to continue to remain high and even increase ha the near future, given the geopolitical pressures particularly in the Middle East region.

(b)to(d): In the context of unprecedented rise in international oil prices, the Government has taken a number of steps to protect the interest of common man. These include :- 

	Policy of Equitable burden sharing mnongst three stakeholders namely, 
Government, PSU oil companies and the consmners.
Of the burden ofRs.73,500 crores, only 12% passed on to the consumers.
Prices of kerosene and LPG have not been increased. Only small increase has 
been made in price of petrol and diesel.
	Central taxes both, excise duty mad customs duty on kerosene and LPG have 
been completely removed and   `Nil`.
	Customs duty on petrol and diesel reduced to 7.5% fi:om 20% when 
Government came to power.
	LPG placed under declared goods restricting the states to charging just 
4% sales tax.
	Navaratna companies, have been made financially viable so they can, 
continue to serve the `commonman`.

records.name: Rajeev Shukla
records.qn_text:

(SMT. PANABAKA LAKSHMI)

(b) Kits for diagnosis of HIV are being procured and supplied to states as commodity assistance. Nearly 60 lakh kits are being procured during 2006-07. These are made available at Integrated Counselling and Testing Centres, Antenatal Clinics, Blood Banks etc., for testing of HIV free of cost.

records.qtitle: COMPREHENSIVE TRAUMA CARE ON NATIONAL HIGHWAYS .
records.name: Rajeev Shukla
records.qn_text:
(a) whether it is a fact that Government are planning to introduce comprehensive trauma-care system for victims of road accidents on National Highways across India;

(b) if so, the details of the proposal; and

(c) by when the proposed system would be implemented?
records.ans_text:
THE MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF SHIPPING, ROAD TRANSPORT AND HIGHWAYS

(SHRI K.H. MUNIYAPPA)

(a)to(c) Provision of assistance in case of road accident is basically the responsibility of the State Governments. The Ministry of Health & Family Welfare provides assistance to the States/ Union Territories (UTs) under the scheme of ‘Assistance for Capacity Building’ for upgradation of emergency services/trauma care facilities in hospitals including those located near the National Highways for the purpose of treatment of accident victims. This Ministry also provides ambulance to States/UTs to evacuate victims of accident to the nearest medical centre under National Highways Accident Relief Service Scheme (NHARSS). In addition, National Highways Authority of India deploys an ambulance at an average interval of 50 kms under their Operation and Maintenance Contracts/Build operates Transfer agreements on the completed stretches of National Highways entrusted to them.

records.qtitle: LOW COST LOANS FOR RURAL HOUSING .
records.name: Rajeev Shukla
records.qn_text:
(a) the total number of rural households living in mud (Kutcha) homes in India;

(b) whether Government has any scheme to extend low-cost housing loans in rural areas to promote conversion of these mud homes to brick and mortar (pucca) homes;

(c) if so, the details thereof; and

(d) if not, the reasons therefor?
records.ans_text:
MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF RURAL DEVELOPMENT

(SHRIMATI SURYAKANTA PATIL)

(a) According to the information made available by 2001 Census, 11.651 million households are living in unserviceable temporary houses in rural areas.

(b) to (d) Under Indira Awaas Yojana (IAY), the Ministry of Rural Development is providing financial assistance amounting to Rs. 25,000/- per unit in plain areas and Rs. 27,500/- in hilly/difficult areas, to the BPL rural poor for construction of a new dwelling unit or for replacement of an existing unserviceable temporary house. However, the District Rural Development Agencies (DRDAs) can utilize up to 20% of the total funds available under IAY, for up gradation of existing unserviceable temporary house or under Credit-cum-Subsidy Scheme for construction of a house with credit from banks/financial institutions. Rural households having an annual income of upto Rs. 32,000/- can avail of the facility under Credit-cum-Subsidy Scheme. Ceiling of subsidy under the scheme is Rs. 12,500/- per household and the balance amount has to be arranged by way of loan not exceeding Rs. 50,000/- in each case from banks/financial institutions.

records.qtitle: PROMOTION OF HIGHER USE OF ETHANOL .
records.name: Rajeev Shukla
records.qn_text:
(a) Whether Government have any proposal to promote addition of a large percentage of ethanol in petrol to substantially reduce retail market prices of petrol in view of the facts that bio fuel like ethanol is suitable for use as petrol-mix by motor vehicles and that ethanol`s production price is a fraction of petrol`s retail price;

(b) If so, the details thereof; and

(c) If not, the reasons therefor?
records.ans_text:
Minister of State in the MINISTRY OF PETROLEUM & NATURAL GAS

(SHRI DINSHA PATEL)

(a) to (c): With a view to reducing dependence on imported oil by way of encouraging use of indigenous sources of energy and to provide a supportive role to the sugarcane farmers, the Ministry of Petroleum & Natural Gas (MoP&NG) had introduced the scheme of mandatorily supplying 5% ethanol blended petrol in major sugar producing states and contiguous union territories w.e.f. 1.1.2003. However, the programme could be implemented only in a staggered manner because ethanol was not available in a consistent manner and at reasonable prices. MoP&NG issued an amending Notification dated 27.10.2004 making sale of EBP mandatory in 10 States and 3 UTs if the price of sourcing indigenous ethanol for supply of ethanol-blended petrol is comparable to the price of indigenous ethanol for alternative uses; the delivery price of ethanol at the locations is comparable to the import parity price of petrol at that location; and the indigenous ethanol industry is able to maintain uninterrupted supply of ethanol for ethanol-blended petrol programme at such prices. As regards procurement price of ethanol, the Public Sector Oil Marketing Companies (OMCs) have been procuring ethanol through public tenders. While the delivered price of petrol and ethanol at mixing depots would vary from location to location and from time to time, it is not correct to state that ethanol price may be a fraction of petrol price. In fact the availability of ethanol at reasonable prices has been one of the constraints in smooth implementation of the programme so far.

records.name: Rajeev Shukla
records.qn_text:
(a) whether Government are working on a proposal to appoint tax ombudsmen throughout the country to resolve taxpayers disputes or grievances against the Income Tax Department;

(b) if so, the details of the proposal; and

(c) the proposed date of implementation of the said proposal?
records.ans_text:
MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF FINANCF

(SHRI S.S. PALANIMANICKAM)

(a), (b) & (c): Yes sir. The Department has introduced the Income Tax Ombudsman Guidelines, 2006 with effect from 1st January 2006, with the objective of resolution of complaints relating to public grievances against the Income-Tax Department, and to facilitate the satisfaction or settlement of such complaints. The Guidelines envisage appointment of 12 Income Tax Ombudsmen at New Delhi, Mumbai, Chennai, Kolkata, Bangalore, Hyderabad, Ahmedabad, Pune, Kanpur, Chandigarh, Bhopal and Kochi. The Income Tax Ombudsmen at New Delhi and Kolkata have already been appointed.

records.qtitle: UNICEF REPORT ON EDUCATION IN BIHAR .
records.name: Rajeev Shukla
records.qn_text:
(a) whether the attention of Government has been drawn to a UNICEF report captioned `State of the world`s children, 2006` wherein it has been mentioned that the biggest problem with Bihar has been non- utilization of Central funds and 31 lakh children have never gone to school in the State;

(b) whether Government have studied the report; and

(c) the follow-up action taken by Government in this regard?
records.ans_text:
MINISTER OF HUMAN RESOURCE DEVELOPMENT

(SHRI ARJUN SINGH)

(a) to (c): The UNICEF report captioned `State of the World`s children 2006` is an annual publication commenting on status of the World`s children, particularly with respect to the internationally notified Millennium Development Goals. It give data on respective countries. Government of India is addressing the educational requirements of children in the 6-14 years age group through several Centrally sponsored programmes like the Sarva Shiksha Abhiyan and the Mid Day Meal Scheme.

records.name: Rajeev Shukla
records.qn_text:
(a) whether it is a fact that almost one-fourth of 800,000 cases awaiting disposal in Allahabad High Court have been pending for more than ten years,

(b) if so, the details thereof;

(c) the total number of cases pending for more than 10 years in all High Courts of the country;

(d) whether any steps are contemplated for fast track disposal of these cases; and

(e) if so, the details thereof?.
records.ans_text:
MINISTER OF STATE INTHE MINISTRY OF LAW AND JUSTICE

(SHRI K. VENKATAPATHY)

(a)&(b) Yes, Sir. Out of a total 10,53,794 cases pending as on 31.3.2006, which includes 7,75,583 main cases and 278211 miscellaneous cases, 342135 cases are pending for more than 10 years.

(c). A Statement is enclosed.

(d) & (e) Expeditious disposal of cases in the courts is a matter which concerns the judiciary. Government has, however, taken a number of measures that include timely filling up of the vacancies in the High Courts, review of the judge strength etc.

records.name: Rajeev Shukla
records.qn_text:
(a) whether Government are aware of newspaper reports to the effect that UGC affiliated universities and institutes axe facing a severe shortage of quality faculty as more and more academicians are lured by higher-paying private sector institutes;

(b) if so, the details of Government’s action to arrest the trend;

(c) whether Government will also consider hiking salaries of highly skilled faculty in courses like biotechnology and computer sciences, to prevent them from taking professional jobs in the private sector;

(d) if so, the details thereof; and

(e) if not, the reasons therefor?
records.ans_text:
MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF HUMAN RESOURCE DEVELOPMENT

(SHRI M.A.A. FATMI)

(a) to (e): The Higher Education Institute are appointing faculty as per minimum qualifications laid down by the University Grants Commission. The pay scales of teachers are based on norms of the Government.

records.name: Rajeev Shukla
records.qn_text:
(a) by when Government propose to launch direct rail link to Srinagar from Jammu;

(b) whether Government apprehends any security threats to the Jammu- Srinagar rail link in view of large number of sensitive bridges and tunnels involved in the link; and

(c) if so, the details of any proposal to minimize the security risks as above?
records.ans_text:
MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF RAILWAYS

(SHRI R.VELU )


(a): Railways have planned to launch direct rail link to Srinagar from
Jammu by 2008-09.

(b) & (c): Yes, Sir. To minimize security risk, deployment of security along
the section, at tunnels, bridges and at station buildings round the clock has
been planned.

records.qtitle: STUDY ON WEAKNESSES IN HEALTH DELIVERY SYSTEMS IN STATES .
records.name: Rajeev Shukla
records.qn_text:
(a) whether Government have set up a group of experts to study the population profile of the States of Bihar, Uttar Pradesh, Rajasthan, Madhya Pradesh and Orissa to identify weaknesses in the health delivery systems to suggest measures that would be taken to improve the health and demographic status of the States; and

(b) if so, the details thereof?
records.ans_text:
THE MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF HEALTH & FAMILY WELFARE

(SMT. PANABAKA LAKSHMI)

(a) & (b) :Yes, sir. In the first meeting of the reconstituted National Commission on Population (NCP) which was held on 23rd July 2005 under the chairmanship of Hon’ble Prime Ministers, it was decided to set up five groups of experts for studying the population profile of the States of Bihar, Uttar Pradesh, Rajasthan, Madhya Pradesh and Orissa to identify weaknesses in the health delivery systems and to suggest measures that would be taken to improve the health and demographic status of the States. Accordingly, five expert groups have been set up by the Government on 29.9.2005 and each expert group has completed two rounds of meetings for the purpose.

records.qtitle: SHORTAGE OF NURSES DUE TO MIGRATION .
records.name: Rajeev Shukla
records.qn_text:
(a) whether it is a fact that India’s public health system is facing a crunch of trained nurses as scores of US-based hospitals have recruited a large number of Indian nurses;

(b) if so, whether Government have any proposal to arrest the trend; and

(c) if so, the details thereof?
records.ans_text:
THE MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF HEALTH & FAMILY WELFARE

(SMT. PANABAKA LAKSHMI)

(a) to (c) There are 1312 General Nursing and Midwifery, 580 B.Sc.(Nursing) and 77 M.Sc. (Nursing) Institutions functioning in the country with a capacity about 40,000 per year and as such there is no shortage of trained nurses.

records.qtitle: SCREENING OF INDIAN FILMS IN PAKISTAN .
records.name: Rajeev Shukla
records.qn_text:
(a) whether Government of Pakistan has banned the transmission of some Indian T.V. channels in that country;

(b) if so, the details thereof.

(c) whether Pakistan has allowed the screening of some of the Indian feature films in their country; and

(d) if so, the names of such films and the terms and conditions imposed by Pakistan for screening these Indian films?
records.ans_text:
THE MINISTER OF INFORMATION & BROADCASTING AND PARLIAMENTARY AFFAIRS (SHRI P.R. DASMUNSI)

(a) to (d): A statement is laid on the Table of the House.
STATEMENT AS REFERRED TO IN REPLY TO PARTS (a) TO (d) OF RAJYA SABHA STARRED QUESTION NO. 71 FOR ANSWER ON 27.7.2006

(a) & (b) : Yes, Sir. Pakistan has banned the transmission of Indian TV channels in Pakistan. The ban on Indian news channels is strictly enforced, in particular.

(c) & (d): The Pakistan Film Censor Board recently permitted public screening in Pakistan of the Indian films “Taj Mahal” and “Mughal-e-Azam”. This was stated to be a one time exception. Financial proceeds from the screenings were stated to be utilised for the victims of the earthquake of 8th October 2005.

records.name: Rajeev Shukla
records.qn_text:
(a) whether it is a fact that BSNL`s not offering sufficient points of Interconnect (PoIs) to private mobile operators leading to high level of congestion and poor quality service for mobile telephones across India;

(b) if so, whether Government propose to take any action to resolve the problem; and

(c) if so, the details thereof?
records.ans_text:
THE MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF COMMUNICATIONS AND INFORMATION TECHNOLOGY (DR. SHAKEEL AHMAD)

(a) Congestion in the mobile telephony happens due to the problems within the network of the private mobile operators in addition to shortage of capacity at the points of interconnection among networks of telecom service providers including BSNL. Congestion is one of the reasons for poor quality of service from mobile phones. BSNL provides interconnection based on technical feasibility and as per the time frame provided in the interconnection agreement between BSNL and Private Operators.

(b) & (c) Interconnection provisioning is a continuous process. The Government has asked Bharat Sanchar Nigam Limited and the private telecom operators to take various steps which inter-alia include holding of regular review meetings, streamlining of the procedure for provisioning of PoIs in time bound manner, to provide forecast for demand of PoIs in advance to enable BSNL to plan necessary equipment where feasible so as to reduce the cases of technical non-feasible.

records.name: Rajeev Shukla
records.qn_text:
:

(a) Whether it is a fact that Planning Commission has accepted a recommendation to raise India`s nuclear energy capacity to 100,000 MW in 25 years; and

(b) if so, the details of the proposal?
records.ans_text:
THE MINISTER OF STATE IN THE PRIME MINISTER`S OFFICE

(SHRI PRITHVIRAJ CHAVAN) :

(a) The Planning Commission had constituted an expert committee to formulate & an integrated energy policy for the country. The expert committee in its draft

(b) report has suggested the possibility of reaching a nuclear power capacity of 48000 MWe to 63000 MWe in the next 25 years or so, by a mix of indigenous Pressurised Heavy Water Reactors, Fast Breeder Reactors and Light Water Reactors based on imports and is contingent on availability of fuel/reactors through international cooperation in nuclear field.

records.qtitle: SHORTFALL IN COLLECTION OF EDUCATION CESS .
records.name: Rajeev Shukla
records.qn_text:
(a) whether it is a fact that the revenue receipts from the two per cent education cess in the first eight months of current fiscal at Rs. 2,400 crore have been only a third of the budgeted yearly estimates of Rs. 6,975 crore;

(b) whether Government are of the view that such drastic shortfall will have a negative impact on successful conduct of elementary and other education programmes like ‘Sarva Shiksha Abhiyaan’ ;

(c) if so, the details of any action contemplated to redress the shortfall of money; and

(d) if not, the reasons therefor?”
records.ans_text:
FINANCE MINISTER (SHRI P. CHIDAMBARAM)

(a) to (d) : A statement is laid on the Table of the House.
STATEMENT REFERRED TO IN REPLY TO PARTS (a), (b), (c) and (d) OF RAJYA SABHA STARRED QUESTION NO.550 DUE FOR ANSWER ON 23-5-2006

(a): In the current fiscal, eight months have not yet been completed. However, during the last fiscal, so far as indirect taxes are concerned, Rs.2600.30 crore have been collected in the first eight months against the Budget Estimates (BE) of Rs.3572 crore which is 72.8% of the BE (of indirect taxes), much higher than the pro-rata target. Insofar as direct taxes are concerned, the information is not yet available for the last fiscal 2005-06. However, in the fiscal 2004-05, the education cess collected in respect of direct taxes was Rs.1804.51 crore (where as Rs.2514.22 crore was collected in respect of indirect taxes in 2004-05).

(b) to (d): No, Sir. Prarambhik Shiksha Kosh (PSK) has been shown as a separate line item in the Budget of 2006-07. Budget 2005-06 assumes Rs.6,975 crore as estimated receipts through “education cess”. The allocation made in BE 2005-06 for Sarva Shiksha Abhiyan (SSA) and Mid-day-Meal (MDM) scheme was Rs.11,145.26 crore which was enhanced to Rs. 11,156.01 crore in revised estimates of the fiscal 2005-06. The above allocations are irrespective of the fact whether revenue budgeted through education cess is actually realized or not.
In the current year also an amount of Rs.8,746 crore has been assumed as receipts through education cess, out of which Rs. 5831 crore has been allocated to SSA and Rs.2915 crore to MDM. As against this, the expenditure provided for these two flagship programmes namely SSA and MDM at Rs.16,348 crore which is about twice the receipts that are being estimated to be received through “education cess” during the year. The total outlay for Sarva Shiksha Abhiyan and Mid-Day Meal Scheme has been augmented considerably in the Year 2006-07 as compared to the Budgetary allocations provided for these programmes/schemes during 2005-06.

records.qtitle: AUCTION OF OIL AND GAS BLOCKS .
records.name: Rajeev Shukla
records.qn_text:
(a) whether Government propose to auction a large number of new oil and natural gas exploration blocks over the next two years

(b) if so, the details thereof; and

(c) the total estimated yield of crude oil and gas respectively from these blocks?
records.ans_text:
MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF PETROLEUM & NATURAL GAS

(SHRI DINSHA PATEL)


(a) to (c):- With a view to attract private investment including foreign investment for exploration and exploitation of Hydrocarbon resources in the 26 sedimentary basins of the country covering onland and offshore areas, the Government has been inviting bids from private companies on a regular basis since, 1991. To give further impetus to the exploration efforts, the Government has formulated the New exploration Licensing Policy ( NELP) which provides equal opportunities and a level playing field to foreign companies and Indian companies, both Public Sector Undertakings ( PSUs) and private companies to bid for exploration acreages, offered by the Government from time to time. Exploration activities including identification and offer of blocks through NELP is a continuous and ongoing process. The Government of India, on 23rd February, 2006, has offered 55 blocks comprising of 24 deep water, 6 shallow water and 25 onshore blocks under the sixth round of New Exploration Licensing Policy (NELP-VI). The bid closing date for these blocks is 15th September, 2006. These are exploration blocks where exploration of oil and gas is proposed to be carried out. The exploration period for these blocks is 7-8 years. Being exploration blocks, oil and gas reserves have to be established through exploration, hence any estimation of reserves would be pre-mature.

records.name: Rajeev Shukla
records.qn_text:
(a) whether it is a fact that budgetary allocation for adult education has been reduced to Rs.214 crore this year`, as against Rs.263 crore in last year`s revised estimates;

(b) if so, whether Government are of the view that targets in respect of adult education have been achieved and therefore lesser budgetary allocation is required;

(c) if not, the reasons for reduction in allocation; and

(d) the performance details of various schemes run by Government in the field of adult education?
records.ans_text:
MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF HUMAN RESOURCE DEVELOPMENT

(SMT. D. PURANDESWARI)

(a) to (d): A statement is laid on the Table of the House.

Statement referred to in reply to parts (a) to (d) of the Rajya Sabha Starred Question No.527 for 22.5.2006 regarding Budgetary allocation for adult education asked by Shri Rajeev Shukla, MP

(a): The budgetary provision for adult education during 2006-07 is Rs.214.97 crores both for Plan and Non Plan (excluding North East region) as against Revised Estimates of Rs.262.97 crores for 2005-06. The provision is inclusive of allocation for various schemes of adult education as also the budgetary support for Directorate of Adult Education etc.

(b) & (c): The goal of the National Literacy Mission is to achieve 75% literacy by 2007 in the age group of 7 years and above. The Universalisation of Elementary Education and eradication of adult illiteracy form the two-pronged strategy for improving the literacy rate of the country. The budgetary provision of Elementary Education has been increased from Rs. 12,241.76 crores in 2005-06 to Rs. 16,892.50 crores in 2006-07. The increased allocation under Elementary Education would to an extent supplement the efforts of NLM in achieving its targets.

(d): The .achievements under various schemes of Adult Education are as under:-
(i) Literacy Campaigns: 597 districts in the country have been covered under Total Literacy C, ampaigns for imparting basic literacy to the adult illiterates and 487 districts have been covered under Post Literacy Programme for the reinforcement of literacy skills of neo-literates. So far, 1203.49 lakh persons are reported to have been made literate under various programmes. Female Literacy Prograrnmes were taken up in those districts of Uttar Pradesh, Bihar, Jharkhand and Orissa, which had female literacy below 30%. In addition, 150 districts, which had the lowest literacy rates in the country, have been identified for launching a special literacy drive.

(ii) Continuing Education Programme: 311 districts have been covered under C.ontinuing Education Programme for providing opportunities for lifelong learning to the neo-literates and other sections of the community through 2,12,032 Continuing Education Centres.


(iii) Support to Non-Governmental Organizations: 25 State Resource Centres have been set up for providing academic and technical resource support to adult education programmes.

(iv) Jan ShikshanSansthans: 172 Jan Shikshan Sansthans have been sanctioned for providing training in vocational courses to the neo-literates and unskilled and unemployed youth.

records.name: Rajeev Shukla
records.qn_text:
(a) whether Government have any proposal for establishment of a Trans-Asia power grid, to transfer surplus power from Central Asian countries to India;

(b) if so, the details thereof;

(c) whether Government consider such a project to be feasible; and

(d) if so, the details of any decision taken so far in this regard?
records.ans_text:
THE MINISTER OF POWER

( SHRI SUSHILKUMAR SHINDE )

(a) : No, Sir. There is no such proposal with the Government.

(b) : Does not arise.

(c) & (d) : In the absence of specific proposals the feasibility of such a project cannot be assessed.

records.qtitle: . CONNECTING THE DISTRICT COURTS WITH PRISONS THROUGH VIDEO CONFERENCING.
records.name: Rajeev Shukla
records.qn_text:
(a) whether it is a fact that several district courts across the country have been connected to district prisons through video conferencing, for questioning of prisoners;

(b) if so, the details thereof and the status of implementation of the programme under which the said video links are being set up;

(c) whether the new system will do away with the practice of prisoners being transported to courts` premises for routine questioning and other matters ; and

(d) if not, the reasons therefor?
records.ans_text:
MINISTER FOR STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF LAW & JUSTICE

( SHRI K. VENKATAPATHY)

(a) to (d) : No programme with Central financial assistance, for providing video links for connecting the district courts to the district prisons in the States, is under implementation for questioning of prisioners. f

records.name: Rajeev Shukla
records.qn_text:
(a) whether Government have taken a decision to launch the scheme of hospital ratings in the country;

(b) if so, the details of the scheme along with the parameters on which the hospitals are being rated;

(c) whether the scheme will be made compulsory for all hospitals; and

(d) if not, the reasons therefor?
records.ans_text:
THE MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF HEALTH & FAMILY WELFARE

(SMT. PANABAKA LAKSHMI)


(a) to (d) : There are various mechanisms by which quality of services and care provided by hospitals and other health care institutions can be assessed. Some of these are Accreditation, Certification and Rating. Concerned health institutions obtain these quality benchmarks depending on their own requirement and the requirement of clients they serve. Government of India is of the view that Accreditation etc. is to be purely a voluntary process and, therefore, should be left to independent specialist agencies outside the Government set up. There can also be more than one agency that could undertake such accreditation, certification or rating. Such agencies will fix their own standards. The Quality Council of India, which is an autonomous body under the Ministry of Commerce and Industry, has set up a National Accreditation Board of Hospital (NABH).
The purpose of accreditation/rating is to assure the patients about the quality of services available in the accredited hospital.

records.qtitle: ENCOURAGEMENT OF HIGH INCOME INDUSTRIES IN RURAL INDIA
records.name: Rajeev Shukla
records.qn_text:
(a): whether Government have taken any strategic steps to encourage high-income rural industries of wine, textiles, tourism and handicrafts in rural areas across the country;

(b): if so, the details thereof; and

(c): if not, the reasons therefor? (SHRI MAHABIR PRASAD)
records.ans_text:
MINISTER OF SMALL SCALE INDUSTRIES & AGRO AND RURAL INDUSTRIES

(a)&(b): The Government in the Ministry of Agro and Rural Industries implements the Rural Employment Generation Programme

(REGP) through the Khadi and Village Industries Commission (KVIC) for promotion of village industries and generation of productive employment in the rural areas, including town with population up to 20,000. Similarly, the Government in the Ministry of Tourism implements the Scheme of Destination Development for creation of infrastructure in rural areas with potential for tourism, with the objective of showcasing rural life, art, culture and heritage at rural locations having core competency in crafts, handlooms, textiles, culture, etc. Further, the Government in the Ministry of Textiles implements a number of schemes, viz., Deen Dayal Upadhaya Hatkargha Protsahan Yojana in the handlooms sector, Babasaheb Ambedkar Hastshilpa Vikas Yojana in the handicrafts sector, etc., throughout the country, in both urban and rural areas, for the development and promotion of these sectors.

(c): Does not arise.

records.name: Rajeev Shukla
records.qn_text:
(a) whether it is a fact that Government have announced its decision to install sophisticated equipment for automatic toll calculation and deduction for the upcoming toll roads ;

(b) if so, the details of the proposal along with the total cost to be incurred in this regard; and

(c) the estimated financial benefits likely to accrue from installation of the said equipment?
records.ans_text:
THE MINISTER OF SHIPPING, ROAD TRANSPORT AND HIGHWAYS

(SHRI T. R. BAALU)


(a) to (c) A Statement is laid on the Table of the House.
STATEMENT REFERRED TO IN REPLY TO PART (a) TO (c) OF RAJYA SABHA STARRED QUESTION NO. 489 FOR ANSWER ON 18TH MAY, 2006 ASKED BY SHRI RAJEEV SHUKLA REGARDING AUTOMATIC TOLL PLAZAS.

(a) and (b) It has been decided to install Modern Toll Collection Systems at 14 important toll plaza locations between Delhi-Mumbai, Panipat-Jalandhar and Delhi-Agra sections as a pilot project for which tenders have been invited.
Following subsystems form part of the integrated Modern Toll Collection Systems: 

>	Automatic Vehicle Counter cum Classifier (AVCC)
>	Automatic Boom Barrier
>	ETC (Electronic Toll Collection)
>	Contactless Smart Card Systems
>	User Fare Display Unit
>	Lane Controller
>	Barcode reader
>	Close Circuit Television System
>	Traffic Light System
>	Over Head Lane Signs
>	Intercom System


The approximate cost of implementation of Modern Toll Collection Systems at each 
Toll Plaza location would be Rs. 3 crores.


(c)	The following financial benefits are expected to accrue from implementing Electronic 
Toll Collection Systems:


(i)	Better Revenue collection  

(ii)	Improvement in  transparency of financial transactions 

(iii)	Better  user convenience with facility for non-stop payment and time savings 

(iv)	Reduction in vehicular emission and environmental improvement   

(v)	Reduction in  toll plaza operating costs 

(vi)	Enhancement in  audit control on fee collection  by centralizing user accounts

records.name: Rajeev Shukla
records.qn_text:
(a) whether it is a fact that National Commission for Minorities has submitted its report to Government over the recent Aligarh riots;

(b) if so, whether it is a fact that the NCM in its report has incriminated the State Government for its inept handling of the situation;

(c) if so, the relevant details thereof;

(d) whether Government have taken any action on the basis of the report; and

(e) if so, the details thereof?
records.ans_text:
MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF HOME AFFAIRS

(SHRI SRIPRAKASH JAISWAL)

(a): Yes, Sir.

(b): The Report draws attention to the fact that the incident happened due to some administrative lapse on the part of the State Government as well as total failure of district administration.

(c): The Report has highlighted that the guidelines given in Prime Minister`s 15 point programme were not observed and recommends constitution of a balanced police force in the State with proportionate representation of all communities including minority communities and a time-bound enquiry into the Aligarh incidents by a sitting Judge of a High Court.

(d) & (e): A copy of the Report has been sent by the commission to the State Government of Uttar Pradesh, who are primarily concerned with it, and the State Government is taking appropriate action in the matter.

records.name: Rajeev Shukla
records.qn_text:
(a) whether it is a fact that in view of steep fall in onion prices, Government are considering for increasing the export quantity of onions to neighbouring States; and

(b) if so, the details of any action taken in this regard?
records.ans_text:
THE MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF COMMERCE AND INDUSTRY

(SHRI JAIRAM RAMESH )


(a) & (b) To check the sliding prices of onion and to sustain the production levels by providing adequate price realization to the farmers, National Agricultural Cooperative Marketing Federation of India Ltd. has started procuring onion w.e.f. 17 April 2006 from Lasalgaon and Pimpalgaon in Maharashtra. Onions so procured, would be exported to Sri Lanka, Singapore, Malaysia, Dubai, Saudi Arabia and Mauritius. For this, proper marketing strategy would be adopted by National Agricultural Cooperative Marketing Federation of India Ltd. which includes grading, reliability, quality and pricing of onions.

records.name: Rajeev Shukla
records.qn_text:
(a) whether Government are aware that a large scale corruption and irregularities in potable water distribution in most cities across the country;

(b) whether it is a fact that poor management of water distribution system is leading to a huge amount of wastage of water;

(c) if so, the details in this regard; and

(d) the details of action taken or proposed to be taken by Government to improve the water distribution across the country?
records.ans_text:
THE MINISTER OF WATER RESOURCES

(PROF. SAIF-UD-DIN SOZ)

(a) The Ministry of Urban Development have reported that no complaint has been received by them from any of the State Government/ Urban Local Bodies (ULB) regarding large scale corruption and irregularities in distribution of potable water in cities across the country.

(b) & (c) As per report on study titled “Status of Water supply and Sanitation and Solid Waste Management in Urban areas” conducted by National Institute of Urban Affairs, New Delhi under the sponsorship of Ministry of Urban Development, the unaccounted for water (UFW) mainly in Indian cities is of the order of 40-50%, while acceptable value according to Central Public Health Engineering and Environment Organisation’s norms is 15%.

(d) The Ministry of Urban Development have launched a new programme namely, “Jawaharlal Nehru National Urban Renewal Mission” (JNNURM) with an aim to encourage reforms and fast track planned development of identified cities. The focus is to be on efficiency in urban infrastructure (water supply) service delivery mechanism, community participation and accountability of ULBs. The JNNURM envisages various mandatory and obligatory reform measures. One of the mandatory reforms to be carried out by the ULBs is “Levy of reasonable user charges by ULB/Parastatals with the objective that full cost of operation and maintenance or recurring cost is collected within next seven years. However, cities/towns in North East and other special category States may recover atleast 50% of operation and maintenance charges initially. These cities/towns should graduate to full O&M cost recovery in a phased manner”.

records.qtitle: INCREASE IN DEARNESS RELIEF TO PENSIONERS
records.name: Rajeev Shukla
records.qn_text:
(a) whether Government are aware that the order s issued by the Department of Pension for increase in dearness relief to pensioners from time to time do not reach branches of the Public Sector Banks disbursing pensions for months together thereby causing unnecessary delay in the disbursement of additional relief to the pensioners; and

(b) if so, what procedure is being followed for the purpose and what steps are contemplated to ensure that the relevant orders reach all the concerned branches within a week of their issue through internet and fax or other expeditious means ?
records.ans_text:
THE MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF FINANCE

(SHRI PAWAN KUMAR BANSAL)

(a) & (b) :- Department of Pension and Pensioners` Welfare, Government of India sends a copy of each notification regarding revision in dearness relief to Central Government Pensioners/Family Pensioners to all heads of pension disbursing banks. The banks, in turn, circulate the notification to their pension disbursing branches. The notification is also forwarded by the Government to Indian Banks` Association (IBA), which ensures its wide publicity through advertisements in leading Hindi, English and major regional language newspapers. The details of notification are also made available at the websites of IBA and Ministry of Personnel, Public Grievances and Pension, for access by individual banks/branches and pensioners.

records.qtitle: STUDY ON NEW AIRPORT AT MUMBAI .
records.name: Rajeev Shukla
records.qn_text:
to answer to Unstarred Question 1365 given in the Rajya Sabha on 6th December, 2005 and state:

(CIDCO) and Airports Authority of India (AAI) has since been completed; and

records.ans_text:
MINISTER OF STATE (INDEPENDENT CHARGE) OF THE MINISTRY OF CIVIL AVIATION ( SHRI PRAFUL PATEL )
(a):- No, Sir. (b):- The study is likely to be completed by July, 2006.

records.name: Rajeev Shukla
records.qn_text:
(a) whether it is a fact that several American biotech companies have expressed their keenness to off-shore their research and development work to India; and

(b) if so, the details of the proposals received in this regard?
records.ans_text:
Minister of Science & Technology and minister of ocean development


(KAPIL SIBAL)

P.T.O.


STATEMENT IN RESPECT OF RAJYA SABHA STARRED QUESTION NO.427 TO BE ANSWERED ON 15.05.2006 REGARDING RESEARCH AND DEVELOPMENT WORK.
