records.qtitle: SPREADING LITERACY AMONG THE RURAL MASSES BY NATIONAL LEGAL LITERACY MISSION.
records.name: Rajeev Shukla
records.qn_text:
(a) the details of the States where Project-Combat will be launched by the National Legal Literacy Mission in protecting the rights of Dalits, disadvantaged women and girl child;

(b) what would be the role of the law students participating in the project to help the underprivileged; and

(c) whether budget allocation has been made by the Union Government to spread legal awareness in the remote rural areas?
records.ans_text:
MINISTER OF LAW AND JUSTICE (SHRI H.R. BHARDWAJ)

(a) As a part of the initiative of the National Legal Literacy Mission, the National Legal Services Authority has launched the Project Combat for protecting the Dalits and Disadvantaged, Women in Religious places and Tourismin the States of Kamataka, Andhra Pradesh, Maharashtra, Goa, Tamil Nadu and Orissa. The object is Sensitization and Effective Implementation of Prevention of Devdasi and other related Legislations Pertaining to Organized and Commercial Sexual Exploitation of Women and Girl Child. The said Project is proposed to be implemented soon in allStates and Union Territories.

(b) The role of law students would be to generate awareness on the protection of rights of such vulnerable groups to save them from degeneration of their 1 mental health, socio-economic crises leading to the threat to their basic ?! survival. The law students will be associated and involved in the activities of State Legal Services Authorities/District Legal Services Authorities.

(c) There is no separate provision of the funds made for jhe purpose Of spreading legal awareness programme in remote rural areas. However, the funds allocated by the Government are utilized for implementation of legal aid programmes and schemes which also include the spreading of legal awareness programme in the remote rural areas, framed under the Legal Services Authorities Act, 1987.

records.qtitle: NTMENT OF NON ACADEMICS TO UNIVERSITY BODIES
records.name: Rajeev Shukla
records.qn_text:
(a) whether it has come to the notice of Government that Government of Karnataka has decided to nominate politicians to Syndicates and Academic Councils of the Universities;

(b) whether it is ethical or useful to send non-academics to university bodies; and (6 whether his Ministry would intervene and advise the State Governments to reconsider their stand and nominate only educationists of eminence to university bodies?
records.ans_text:
MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF HUMAN RESOURCE DEVELOPMENT

(SHRI M.A.A. FATMI)

(a) to (c): State Universities are established under the respective Acts of State Legislatures. These Universities are competent to appoint members in their Syndicates and Academic Councils on the advise of the concerned State Governments as per the provisions of their respective Acts/Statues etc. The Central Government does not interfere in the administrative matters of the State Universities.

records.qtitle: ASSISTANCE TO MAHARASHTRA FOR COMPENSATING FALL IN ONION PRICES .
records.name: Rajeev Shukla
records.qn_text:
(a) whether the Central Government propose to provide any sort of assistance to help farmers of Maharashtra who are facing financial loss due to fall in onion prices; and

(b) if so, the details thereof?
records.ans_text:
MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF AGRICULTURE

(SHRI KANTI LAL BHURIA)

(a)&(b): The Government of India implements Market Intervention Scheme at specific request of State Government in event of fall in prices due to glut in market. The losses, if any, are shared on 50:50 basis between the Central and State Government.

records.qtitle: (clubbed) MEASURES FOR PREVENTION OF SUICIDES BY FARMERS .
records.name: Ram Jethmalani
records.qn_text:
(a) whether with a view to focus permanent measures to prevent suicides by farmers, he had convened a meeting in the recent past with the Chief Ministers of those States where farmers under the pressure of debt had committed suicides during the last years;

(b) if so, the names of those States whose Chief Ministers attended the said meeting;

(c) whether some Chief Ministers of those States where farmers had committed suicides did not attend the meeting;

(d) if so, the names of those States;

(e) the outcome of the meeting; and

(f) whether Government propose to provide any special package for these States?
records.ans_text:
MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF AGRICULTURE

(SHRI KANTI LAL BHURIA)

(a): Yes, Sir.

(b): Andhra Pradesh & Maharashtra.

(c): Yes, Sir.

(d): Karnataka & Kerala.

(e)&(f): Based on the suggestions/feedback received in this meeting, a relief package is under preparation for the districts worst affected by the incidence of suicide by farmers in the States.

records.qtitle: SUICIDES BY POULTRY FARMERS OF MAHARASHTRA .
records.name: Rajeev Shukla
records.qn_text:
(a) the number of farmers committed suicides in various States since January, 2006, State-wise;

(b) whether it is a fact that some poultry farmers in Maharashtra have also committed suicides after running up major debts because of tumbling poultry prices caused by bird flue; and

(c) if so, the details thereof?
records.ans_text:
THE MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF AGRICULTURE

(SHRI TASLIMUDDIN)

(a): As per the reports received from the State Governments, there has been no information of poultry farmers committing suicide since January 2006. However, as per report of the Andhra Pradesh Poultry Federation, four poultry farmers have committed suicide during March-May 2006.

(b): No, Sir.

(c): Question does not arise.

records.name: Rajeev Shukla
records.qn_text:
(a) whether Jawaharlal Nehru Stadium in New Delhi is likely to be connected with Metro rail before the Commonwealth Games, 2010; and

(b) if so, the steps taken by Government in this regard?
records.ans_text:
THE MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF URBAN DEVELOPMENT

( SHRI AJAY MAKEN )


(a)&(b): The stations nearest to the Jawaharlal Nehru Stadium as per the alignment already approved for the Phase II of the Delhi Metro are Jorbagh and INA which will be connected before the Commonwealth games. Connectivity to the stadium from these points will be available through other modes.

records.qtitle: ACTIVITIES UNDER JNNURM IN MAHARASHTRA NO. RAJEEV SHUKLA
records.name: Rajeev Shukla
records.qn_text:
(a) the details and current status of various activities currently underway under the Jawaharlal Nehru National Urban Renewal Mission in the State of Maharashtra;

(b) whether it is a fact that the Government has approved city development plans involving outlay of funds from JNNURM for Pune and Nagpur; and

(c) if so, the details of the funds outlay proposed in this regard?
records.ans_text:
THE MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF URBAN DEVELOPMENT

( SHRI AJAY MAKEN )


(a): City Development Plans have been received in respect of Greater Mumbai, Nagpur, Nanded and Pune. 23 project proposals have been received, out of which the city of Nagpur has been sanctioned 5 projects and a sum of Rs.22.19 crore has been released towards first installment of Central Share.

(b): Yes, Sir.

(c): No State-wise or city-wise allocation of funds are made under JNNURM. The Central Government`s financial assistance varies from project to project depending upon the scope of the project.

records.name: Rajeev Shukla
records.qn_text:
(a) whether it is a fact that the representatives from seven Asian countries including India had earlier discussed setting up of a Trans-Asian Railway Link between India and Vietnam, passing through other countries including Thailand, Cambodia and Myanmar;

(b) if so, the details of the outcome of the discussions;

(c) the details of any other proposal to set up an international railway line;

(d) If no such proposal exists, whether Government would consider setting up such a railway link; and

(e) if not, the reasons therefor?
records.ans_text:
THE MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF EXTERNAL AFFAIRS

(SHRI E. AHMED)

(a) The 3rd Ministerial meeting of the Mekong-Ganga Cooperation (MGC) initiative held in Phnom Penh, Cambodia on June 20, 2003 discussed the possibility of a rail link from Delhi to Hanoi. The member countries of MGC are India, Myanmar, Thailand, Lao PDR, Cambodia and Vietnam.

(b) It was agreed to study the feasibility of the rail link and to identify missing links. As a first step, a feasibility study has been conducted for an India-Myanmar rail link.

(c) The United Nations Economic Commission for Asia and Far East (ECAFE) initiated a Trans-Asian Railway project for providing a continuous rail link between Singapore and Turkey, via Southeast Asia, Bangladesh, India, Pakistan and Islamic Republic of Iran in 1960. Work on this project has subsequently been undertaken by the United Nations Economic and Social Commission for Asia and the Pacific (UN-ESCAP) which replaced ECAFE in 1974.

(d) Not applicable.

(e) Does not arise.

records.name: Rajeev Shukla
records.qn_text:
(a) whether Government have initiated any exercise to examine the issue of granting full Statehood to Delhi; and

(b) if so, the status of the proposal?
records.ans_text:
MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF HOME AFFAIRS

( SHRI MANIKRAO HODLYA GAVIT )

(a) & (b): Yes, Sir. The proposal to grant statehood to Delhi has been referred for in-depth examination to an Inter-Ministerial Committee of officials, which includes a representative of the Government of NCT of Delhi.

records.qtitle: (clubbed) STRENGTHENING OF SPECIAL TASK FORCE DEALING WITH NAXALISM .
records.name: SHOBHANA BHARTIA
records.qn_text:
(a) whether the review meeting of the coordination centre on Naxalism was held in April, 2006 to discuss strengthening of the special task force both in terms of manpower and response time and extreme violence in 13 States, high profile attacks, detaining of train in Jharkhand, blasting truck in Chhattisgarh and jail break in Orissa;

(b) whether the PM also called a meeting of 13 Naxal affected States on the 13th April, 2006; and

(c) if so, what were the main decisions taken to check the Naxal menace in those States?
records.ans_text:
MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF HOME AFFAIRS

( SHRI SRIPRAKASH JAISWAL )

(a) to (c): A statement is laid on the Table of the House.

Statement referred to in reply to Rajya Sabha Starred Question No. 375 for 10.5.2006 regarding “Strengthening of special task force dealing with Naxalism”.


(a) & (b): The 2nd meeting of the Standing Committee of the Chief Ministers of the naxal affected States and the Coordination Centre meeting were held in New Delhi on 13.4.2006 and 31.3.2006, respectively to comprehensively review the naxal situation in the affected states and consider appropriate strategies and measures to deal with the problem.


(c): The main decisions of the above meetings are annexed.
ANNEXURE

MAJOR DECISIONS OF THE 2ND MEETING OF THE STANDING COMMITTEE OF THE CHIEF MINISTERS OF NAXAL AFFECTED STATES AND 20TH MEETING OF THE COORDINATION CENTRE: 



(i)         The States will prepare/revise and implement comprehensive 
but realistic action plans at the State and district levels with short-term and 
long-term approaches and strategies to combat the naxalite menace 
simultaneously on political, security and development fronts.






(ii)        The States will strengthen and improve ground level 
policing and initiate action to fill up vacancies particularly in the police 
stations in the naxal affected areas on utmost priority and such police 
stations will be fortified in a time bound manner by utilizing funds under the 
Police Modernization (PM) Scheme.






(iii)       The State Governments and RPF will take steps to put in 
place effective coordination on ground between RPF, GRP, local police and 
intelligence agencies to ensure protection and safety of railway passengers, 
trains and other railway infrastructure.






(iv)       The States will consider and take steps to constitute Joint 
Task Forces of neighbouring States to enhance the effectiveness of intelligence 
driven inter-State joint operations against naxalites and their infrastructure.









(v)        The States will give higher priority and focused attention 
on socio-economic development in the naxal affected areas through convergence 
of existing developmental schemes and fund missing links, if any, in these 
schemes by utilizing funds under BDI etc.






(vi)       The States will take immediate policy and operational 
measures for speedy and effective implementation of land reforms, putting in 
place a progressive and forward looking rehabilitation and resettlement policy 
for displaced tribals, ensuring meaningful implementation of PESA 
withdrawing/compounding of minor forest offences and allowing debt waiver in 
the naxal affected areas. 





(vii)      The States will post young and committed officers in both 
civil and police administration with a stable tenure in naxal affected 
districts to effectively address security and development issues in these 
areas.





(viii)      The Central Government will continue to provide all 
possible help to the States on both security and development fronts to enable 
them to successfully meet the challenge posed by naxalism.

records.qtitle: PRODUCTIVITY AND COMPETITIVENESS OF WORK FORCE IN PSUS .
records.name: Rajeev Shukla
records.qn_text:
(a) whether Government have any long-term plan to improve productivity and competitiveness of workforce in public sector manufacturing industries ;

(b) if so, the details thereof; and

(c) if not, the reasons therefore?
records.ans_text:
MINISTER OF LABOUR AND EMPLOYMENT

(SHRI K. CHANDRASEKHAR RAO)

(a) & (b) The Central Public Sector Enterprises (CPSEs) make their own Human Resource Development (HRD) plans. The CPSEs are expected to improve produvtivity and competitiveness of worforce. The Government has introduced several measures like Performance Related Payment Plan, organization of Executive Development Programmes in association with several reputed Management Organizations and foreign training. Further, the system of Memorandum of Understanding (MOU) is also introduced in the CPSEs in which adequate weightage is given on improvement in production and efficiency by CPSE.

(c) : Does not arise.

records.name: ABU ASIM AZMI
records.qn_text:
(a) whether the Indian Air Force pilots want to leave the Government job of the Air Force;

(b) if so, the number of such pilots and other designations, if any;

(c) the main reasons which are forcing the pilots to resign and how Government are not meeting their requirements;

(d) how leaving of these pilots shall have an adverse effect on the working of Indian Air Force; and

(e) how Government shall meet the shortage of pilots?
records.ans_text:
MINISTER OF DEFENCE

(SHRI PRANAB MUKHERJEE)


(a) No, Sir.

(b) & (c): Do not arise.

(d) & (e): The requests for acceptance of premature retirement/resignation from the pilots are considered as per the government instructions. The majority of pilots released from service had completed their useful tenure as pilots. Thus their exits do not affect the operational status of the squadrons.
The improvement in the job profile of the IAF pilots is a continuous process keeping in view the job specific requirements and operational necessity. The vacancies in the forces including those arising due to premature retirement/resignation are filled up as per normal procedure.

records.qtitle: QUALITY OF FRUITS AND VEGETABLES SUPPLIED THROUGH MOTHER DAIRY OUTLETS .
records.name: Rajeev Shukla
records.qn_text:
(a) whether the quality of vegetables and fruits particularly onions and potatoes suplied through the Mother Dairy outlets in Delhi is inferior;

(b) whether any check is exercised by the senior officers of his Ministry on the officials of the organization responsible for procurement;

(c) if so, at what level and whether any irregularities/corruption in the procurement have come to the light; and

(d) if so, the details thereof and the action taken to ensure reasonable good quality of vegetables and fruits at reasonable prices are made available through Mother Dairy outlets in the State?
records.ans_text:
THE MINISTER OF AGRICULTURE

(SHRI SHARAD PAWAR)

(a) to (d): A statement is laid on the Table of the House.
STATEMENT REFERRED TO IN REPLY TO PARTS (a) TO (d) OF THE RAJYA SABHA STARRED QUESTION NO.343 TO BE ANSWERED ON 17TH MARCH, 2006.

(a): No, Sir. Fruit and Vegetable Unit (A Unit of Mother Dairy Foods Processing Limited) is an ISO:9001:2000 Certified Company. Strict control is excercised on the quality of fruit and vegetables supplied through the outlets of the company. However, at the time of shortage of onions in Delhi during Setpember, 2005, Fruit and Vegetrable Unit of Mother Dairy Foods Processing Limited sold onions procured by Government of National Capital Territory of Delhi in order to make onions available at more reasonable prices to consumers. There were some press reports at that time on this issue alleging that smaller variety of onions was being sold at higher prices by Fruit and Vegetable Unit`s outlets. This was investigated by Fruit and Vegetable Unit of Mother Dairy Foods Processing Limited and found to be incorrect.


(b)to(d): No, Sir. The senior officers of the level of General Manager and Head (Procurement) of Fruit and Vegetable unit of the Mother Dairy Foods Processing Limited exercise checks on the officials responsible for procurement. No irregularities/corruption in the procurement of fruits and vegetables has been reported by the Mother Dairy Foods Processing Limited.

records.qtitle: (clubbed) APPROVAL OF AYURVEDA FORMULATIONS AND MEDICINES .
records.name: Vijay Mallya
records.qn_text:
(a) whether it is a fact that Ayurveda formulations and medicines are proposed to be covered by a system of approval by the Drug Controller General of India;

(b) if so, how many such Ayurvedic formulations have been identified for such approvals and the progress made in this direction;

(c) whether it is proposed to cover other traditional systems of medicines such as Unani, Siddha and Homoeopathy; and

THE MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF HEALTH & FAMILY WELFARE

(a) to (d) Manufacturing licenses in respect of Ayurveda, Siddha, Unani medicines are issued by State Drug Licensing Authorities notified by the State Governments under Rule 152 of the Drugs & Cosmetics Rules, 1945. There is a proposal for setting up of a Central Drug Authority in pursuance of the recommendations of the Mashelkar Committee to deal with all regulatory aspects relating to drugs including Indian Systems of Medicine.

records.name: Rajeev Shukla
records.qn_text:
(a) whether Government have plans to increase the Minimum Support Price for wheat to Rs.700 per quintal; and

records.ans_text:
MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF AGRICULTURE

(SHRI KANTI LAL BHURIA)

(MSP) for wheat to Rs.700 per quintal. The MSP of Rs.650 per quintal of wheat has been fixed for the rabi crops of 2005-06 to be marketed in 2006-07.

records.qtitle: NEW OIL AND GAS BLOCKS FOR EXPLORATION .
records.name: Rajeev Shukla
records.qn_text:
(a) whether it is a fact that Government have offered 55 oil and gas blocks under the sixth round of bidding;

(b) if so, the details of the proposals along with the total estimates of oil and gas reserves;

(c) what percentage of India’s oil and gas requirements will be met by domestic production once these blocks start production; and

(d) by when production from these block is expected to start?
records.ans_text:
MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF PETROLEUM & NATURAL GAS

(SHRI DINSHA PATEL)

(a) to (d):- Yes, Sir. The Government of India, on 23rd February, 2006, has offered 55 blocks comprising of 24 deep water, 6 shallow water and 25 onshore blocks under the sixth round of New Exploration Licensing Policy (NELP-VI). The bid closing date for these blocks is 15th September, 2006. These are exploration blocks where exploration of oil and gas is proposed to be carried out. The exploration period for any of these blocks is 7-8 years. The estimated gas reserve and likely production will depend on the size of the discovery, if any, after exploration. Hence, no estimate of reserves and production can be made at this stage.

records.name: Rajeev Shukla
records.qn_text:
(a): whether Government are aware of recent RBI report stating that increasing incidences of SSIs declaring themselves sick is a reason for slowing growth of flow of bank credit to the sector;

(b): whether Government are of the view that the trend may lead to drying up of a major source of financial assistance to the SSIs in the country; and

(c): whether any plans have been formulated or steps being taken to increase and promote the credit and loan sources for development of SSI sector in India? ANSWER (SHRI MAHABIR PRASAD)
records.ans_text:
MINISTER OF SMALL SCALE INDUSTRIES & AGRO AND RURAL INDUSTRIES

(a)to(c): A statement is placed on the Table of the House.
STATEMENT REFERRED TO IN REPLY TO PARTS (a) TO (c) OF RAJYA SABHA STARRED QUESTION NO. 318 FOR ANSWER ON 13.03.2006 RAISED BY SHRI RAJEEV SHUKLA.

(a): According to information received from the Reserve Bank of India (RBI), it has not brought out any report recently which mentions that incidences of small scale industries (SSIs) declaring themselves sick is increasing or the credit flow to this sector from banks is slowing down. On the contrary, according to the information provided by the RBI, the number of sick SSIs has declined from 1,67,980 as at the end of March 2003 to 1,38,041 as the end of March 2005. During the same period, the loans from the public sector banks outstanding against the SSI has gone up from Rs. 52,988 crore to Rs. 67,634 crore.

(b)&(c): In view of the declining trend in sickness and increasing trend in flow of credit to the SSI as stated in reply to part (a) above, there is no question of the bank finance to the SSI drying up. On the contrary, the `Policy Package for Stepping up Credit to Small and Medium Enterprises (SMEs)` as announced by the Central Government on 10th August, 2005 envisages a minimum of 20 per cent year-on-year growth in credit to the SME sector, leading to doubling of the loan outstanding in a period of 5 years. Based on this Policy Package, the RBI has already issued detailed guidelines to the public sector banks on 19th August, 2005. This Package also includes some other measures to increase quantum of credit to SMEs (including SSI), such as
(i) public sector banks to follow a transparent rating system with cost of credit linked to the credit rating of the enterprise,
(ii) commercial banks to make concerted efforts to provide credit cover on an average to at least 5 new tiny, small and medium enterprises at each of their semi-urban/urban branches per year,
(iii) special dispensation under the Credit Guarantee Scheme for all (a) loans upto Rs. 2 lakh, (b) eligible women entrepreneurs and (c) eligible borrowers located in the North Eastern region (including Sikkim) and Jammu and Kashmir,
(iv) adoption of cluster-based approach by banks for SME financing, etc.

records.name: Rajeev Shukla
records.qn_text:
(a) whether Government have long term plan to launch high- speed trains on major national routes to thwart competition from low-fare airlines;

(b) if so, the details and status of implementation thereof;

(c) whether work is in progress on other major railway tracks for introduction of high-speed trains running at 150 km per hour, after launch of such trains on Delhi-Agra routes;

(d) if so, the details thereof, route-wise? ANSWER
records.ans_text:
MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF RAILWAYS


(SHRI R. VELU )


(a) to (d): There is no long term plan for running of High Speed trains. However, Indian Railways has already introduced a passenger train running at a speed of 150 kilo metre per hour on Delhi-Agra section. The Integrated Railway Modernisation Plan contemplates introduction of 150 km per hour passenger trains on Delhi-Patna-Howrah section and Delhi-Chennai section. It is also proposed to introduce a 150 km per hour passenger train between Delhi and Lucknow.

records.qtitle: DIETARY SUPPLEMENTS AND MEDICAL DEVICES UNDER DRUGS AND COSMETICS ACT .
records.name: Rajeev Shukla
records.qn_text:
(a) whether Government have received any suggestionS to bring dietary supplementS and medical devices under the purview of the Drugs and Cosmetics Act, for effective monitoring of their quality and prices;

(b) if so, the details of any action taken by Government in this regard?
records.ans_text:
THE MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF HEALTH & FAMILY WELFARE

(SMT. PANABAKA LAKSHMI)

(a) & (b) The report of the Expert Committee on Comprehensive Examination of Drug Regulatory Issues, including the Problem of Spurious Drugs (Mashelkar Committee), had recommended that there is need to have separate regulation defining dietary supplements, laying criteria of permissible limit of ingredients and a procedure of evaluation of safety and efficacy, information to consumers and provision related to their advertisements. It was also recommended that these products should be regulated under PFA or any other emergent mechanism/infrastructure. Products that claim or are intended to diagnose, cure, prevent or treat a disease are to be classified as drugs as is the current rule. (para 7.11 to 7.1.19 of the said report) Central Committee on food standards (CCFS) has recommended that productS marketed as dietary supplements belonging to certain specified categories need to be considered under Drugs and Cosmetics Rules.
As regards medical devices, the suggestion of Mashelkar Committee was to specifically define them under Section 3 of the Drugs and Cosmetics Act and to create a specific medical devices division for their regulation. The Committee has also recommended for an appropriate regulatory mechanism to be set up under Central Drug Authority for certification, quality assurance and post marketing surveillance of imported as well as locally made medical devices. A Committee under DDG(M) has been to go into these recommendations and suggest appropriate legislation. In the mean time 10 sterile medical devices which are of critical nature, have been notified. By the Government under Section 3(b)
(iv) of the Drugs and Cosmetics Act in order to ensure appropriate regulation over their import and manufacture.

records.qtitle: USA INTEREST IN CHANDRAYAN I MISSION .
records.name: Rajeev Shukla
records.qn_text:
(a) the progress made in India`s space mission to the moon during the last two years, along with its status as on date;

(b) whether it is a fact that United States of America has expressed its interest in placing its own payload aboard first Indian spacecraft to moon, Chandrayan-I; and

(c) if so, Government`s response to the same?
records.ans_text:
MINISTER OF STATE IN THE PRIME MINISTER`S OFFICE (SHRI PRITHVIRAJ CHAVAN):

(a) Considerable progress is made under Chandrayaan-1 in the last two years. Spacecraft configuration as well as selection of core payloads from India and announcement of opportunity payloads from abroad have been finalised. The Preliminary Design Reviews of Chandrayaan-1 spacecraft and payload systems have been completed. The development of the spacecraft & scientific instruments and establishment of deep space network are progressing satisfactorily. Chandrayaan-1 is planned for launch in 2007-08 onboard India`s PSLV.

(b) Yes, Sir.

(c) After a scientific-merit based selection process, two US payloads have been accepted to be included in Chandrayaan-1 mission.

records.name: Rajeev Shukla
records.qn_text:
(a) whether it is a fact that the completion of Parichha Power Project in Jhansi of Uttar Pradesh is behind its deadline because of differences between different stakeholders;

(b) if so, the details thereof;

(c) whether Government plan to take any action to resolve the matter and ensure speedy completion of the project; and

(d) if so, the details thereof?
records.ans_text:
THE MINISTER OF POWER

( SHRI SUSHILKUMAR SHINDE )

(a) & (b) : Parichha Thermal Power Project Extension (2x210 MW) in Jhansi district of Uttar Pradesh was under construction by Uttar Pradesh Rajya Vidyut Nigam Limited. The original commissioning schedule of the project was envisaged as April, 2005 for Unit 3 and August, 2005 for Unit 4 respectively. The work on the project came to stand still during December, 2003 due to non release of payment to Bharat Heavy Electricals Limited (BHEL) by the Power Finance Corporation (PFC) due to non furnishing of Government warranty/guarantee by Government of Uttar Pradesh.

(c) & (d) : The matter was taken up with the Government of Uttar Pradesh by the Government of India for furnishing the requisite warranty/guarantee to PFC so that funds are released to BHEL and the work restarted. After the follow up the funds were released to BHEL in March, 2004 and the work restarted after about 13 months. The revised commissioning schedule of the project was envisaged as March, 2006 and September, 2006 for Unit 3 & 4. The work on the project is in the final stages of completion. The Unit 3 is likely to be commissioned during March, 2006 and Unit 4 in September, 2006 as per the revised schedule.

records.qtitle: COMPUTERISATION OF POLICE STATIONS BY NCRB .
records.name: Rajeev Shukla
records.qn_text:
(a) the details and the status of computerisation of police stations across the country undertaken by National Crime Research Bureau;

records.name: Rajeev Shukla
records.qn_text:
(a) whether Government are aware of a recent admission by Indian Navy Chief in a recent news report that incidents of piracy, terrorism and smuggling of illegal goods are happening through coastline of India, and that such instances are difficult to detect;

(b) if so, whether Government propose any action to curtail or stop piracy and smuggling through its coastline;

(c) if so, the details thereof; and

(d) if not, the reasons therefor?
records.ans_text:
MINISTER OF DEFENCE

(SHRI PRANAB MUKHERJEE)


(a) to (d): A Statement is attached.

STATEMENT IN RESPECT OF PARTS (a) TO (d) OF RAJYA SABHA UNSTARRED QUESTION NO. 1688 FOR 8.3.2006 REGARDING SMUGGLING THROUGH COASTLINE OF INDIA.

The Government is not aware of any such admission having been made recently by the Chief of the Naval Staff. The Indian Navy and the Indian Coast Guard undertake surveillance and patrolling in coordination with other Government agencies like the Customs and the State police to check piracy, smuggling, illegal immigration and illegal fishing in Indian territorial waters. A scheme has also been formulated for patrolling in the sea close to the coast. The scheme envisages setting up of new coastal police stations and to strengthen the existing coastal police stations in the coastal States and Union Territories. This will supplement the efforts of the Indian Navy and the Coast Guard.

records.qtitle: BENEFITS TO FARMERS FROM RISING MARKET PRICES .
records.name: Rajeev Shukla
records.qn_text:
(a) whether it is a fact that farmers are not benefiting from rising market prices of wheat as the middlemen are raking all the profits;

(b) whether Government have a plan to ensure that farmers get adequate benefit from higher market prices of their crops;

(c) if so, the details thereof; and

(d) if not, the reasons therefor?
records.ans_text:
MINISTER OF AGRICULTURE

(SHRI SHARAD PAWAR)

(a) to (d): A statement is laid on the Table of the House.
STATEMENT IN RESPECT OF PARTS (a) TO (d) OF RAJYA SABHA STARRED QUESTION NO. 181 FOR 03/03/2006 REGARDING BENEFITS TO FARMERS FROM RISING MARKET PRICES.


(a) to (d): Marketing of wheat along with other notified commodities is regulated under the Agricultural Produce Marketing Regulation Act (APMC Act). The whole geographical area in the State is divided asmarket area wherein markets are managed by the Market Committees. As a consequence of such a regulation, the farmer is restricted from entering into direct contract with any bulk buyer, as the produce is required to be canalized through regulated markets. The monopoly of the regulated market has enabled the intermediaries operating therein to take a disproportionate share of the price paid by the consumer. As per the available information, the producer`s share in the consumer`s price in major wheat producing States varied between 71.1% to 85.72%. The balance is accounted for by charges such as mandi charges, sales tax, weighing charges, palledari, brokerage, transport cost and market margins.
Government has taken several steps to ensure that the farmers get adequate benefit from the higher market price for their crops. These are as follows:- 


(i)	This Ministry is proactively encouraging the State Governments to 
promote new competitive 

markets in private and cooperative sectors and allow direct marketing and 
contract farming 

programmes by suitably amending APMC Act.  This is with the objective of 
promoting fair 

competition, so that the farmers can gain from the options available, and take 
their produce to the centres that offer the best prices/services including 
regulated markets.



(ii)	This Ministry is implementing a capital investment subsidy scheme 
titled `Construction of Rural Godowns` w.e.f. 01.04.2001, to provide the 
farming community with facilities for scientific 

storage so that wastage and produce deterioration are avoided and also to 
enable it to meet its 

credit requirement without being compelled to sell the produce at a time when 
the prices are low.  

The scheme has been made farmer friendly by allowing subsidy for smaller 
godowns of 50 MT 

size in general and of 25 MT in hilly areas.  Five lakh tonnes capacity to be 
created is reserved for small farmers.  Till 31.12.2005, 10932 storage projects 
having a capacity of 158.68 lakh tonne have been sanctioned under the scheme by 
providing a subsidy of Rs.279.91 crore.



(iii)	Government has permitted futures trading in wheat at the commodity 
exchange to enable farmer to disover prices of traded commodities including 
wheat well in advance of the crop season thus enabling them to decide when to 
sell his produce.



(iv)	In addition, to ensure payment of remunerative prices to the 
farmers, the Government announces Minimum Support Prices (MSPs) for major 
crops.  The price support mechanism enables the 

farmers to sell their produce at remunerative prices, whenever the market 
prices tend to fall below the MSP level.

records.name: Rajeev Shukla
records.qn_text:
(a) whether it is a fact that Government are planning to introduce Mass Rapid Transit System (MRTS) like Delhi metro in other cities;

(b) if so, whether Government are working on a policy in this behalf;

(c) if so, the details thereof; and

(d) the details of any proposal to secure funds for development of MRTS in cities across India?
records.ans_text:
THE MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF URBAN DEVELOPMENT

( SHRI AJAY MAKEN )

(a): Urban Transport being a State subject, proposals for MRTS in individual cities originate from the respective State Governments.

(b)&(c): The draft National Urban Transport Policy recommends that all million plus cities should plan for mass transit systems using any of the proven technologies. It also offers Central Government financial support by way of equity or one time viability gap funding.

(d): There is no specific proposal aimed at securing funds for the development of MRTS in cities across India. Individual project authorities are expected to secure funding from various sources such as private participation, loans from financial institutions, multi-lateral/bi-lateral agencies, property development, etc.

(c) the response of the Japanese delegation to Government`s proposal?

( SHRI KAMAL NATH )

records.qtitle: SCHEME OF FUND FOR REGENERATION OF TRADITIONAL INDUSTRIES
records.name: Rajeev Shukla
records.qn_text:
(a): the status of implementation of `Scheme of Fund for Regeneration of Traditional Industries (SFURTI) as approved by Government last year;

(b): whether work has begun on development of any of the proposed hundred clusters (25 Khadi, 50 village industries and 25 Coir clusters) under the scheme; and

(c): if so, the details thereof? ANSWER (SHRI MAHABIR PRASAD)
records.ans_text:
MINISTER OF SMALL SCALE INDUSTRIES & AGRO AND RURAL INDUSTRIES



(a)to(c): The Central Government has approved the Scheme of Fund for Regeneration of Traditional Industries (SFURTI). This Scheme envisages the development of 100 clusters in the khadi, coir and village industries sector over five years beginning 2005-06. All State Governments/Union Territory Administrations have been asked to send their proposals.
50 proposals (25 in the khadi sector, 9 in the village industry sector and 16 in the coir sector) have so far been received by the Government in the Ministry of Agro and Rural Industries for consideration under the scheme.

e:

(b) if so, the status of the dialogue and response from the States, so far; and

(c) the other steps being taken to popularize the use of fair price shops?
records.ans_text:
MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF AGRICULTURE AND MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF CONSUMER AFFAIRS, FOOD & PUBLIC DISTRIBUTION

(DR. AKHILESH PRASAD SINGH)

(a),(b)&(c): At present the Central Government makes available wheat, rice, sugar and K. Oil under the Public Distribution System to the State Government for distribution through the Fair Price Shops (FPS). In order to increase the viability of FPSs, under the System, the State Governments have been advised to allow the FPSs, to deal with other items of daily consumption/use also. Some States have already allowed sale of such items through the FPSs. For LPG/Kerosene, Ministry of Petroleum and Natural Gas has not agreed with the proposal as it is not a practical proposition to put domestic LPG in FPS as LPG is not a rationed good. records.name: Rajeev Shukla
records.qn_text:
(a) whether it is a fact that growth in foodgrain production in the country has shown consistently a downward trend over the last decade;

(b) whether Government are aware of a report by International Food Policy Research Institute, which predicted that by 2020, India`s foodgrain production will not be enough to feed its own population, forcing the country to import foodgrains;

(c) if so, whether Government have formulated any long-term policy to reverse the current trend and increase foodgrain productivity in the country;

(d) if so, the details thereof; and

(e) if not, the reasons therefor?
records.ans_text:
MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF AGRICULTURE

(SHRI KANTI LAL BHURIA)

(a): The foodgrain production in the country shows an upward trend albeit with year to year fluctuations. The total production of foodgrains in 1995-96 was 180.42 million tonnes which increased over the years to `reach 213.46 million` tonnes` in 2003-04. In 2004-05 `as `per` the 4th advance estimates the production of foodgrains was 204.61 million tonnes.

(b): The International Food Policy Research Institute (IFPRI) in its report titled `2020 Global Food Outlook` mentioned that India would shift from near self-sufficiency under the baseline scenario (Scenario prevailing in and around 1997) to imports of 30 million (tonnes of cereals).

(c) to (e): As per National Agriculture Policy, special efforts are made to raise the productivity and production of crops to meet the increasing demand for food generated by demographic pressures and raw materials for expanding agro-based industries. A regionally differentiated strategy is pursued, taking into account the agronomic, climatic and environmental conditions to realize the full growth potential of every region. Special attention is also given to development of new crop varieties, particularly of food crops, with higher nutritional value through adoption of bio-technology particularly, genetic modification, while addressing bio-safety concerns.

records.name: Rajeev Shukla
records.qn_text:
(a) whether it is a fact that fencing on India`s border with Bangladesh is currently being undertaken;

(b) if so, the details of the project and its status so far;

(c) whether Government have received any objections to fencing from the Government of Bangladesh;

(d) if so, the details thereof; and

(e) the steps taken by Government to resolve the objections?
records.ans_text:
MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF HOME AFFAIRS

(SHRI S. REGUPATHY)

(a) & (b): Yes, Sir. The Government of India has sanctioned construction of 3286 Kms. of fence along Indo-Bangladesh border. Out of this 2129 Kms. has been erected till 31st January, 2006

(c) to (e): The Bangladesh Rifles has been objecting construction of border fence within 150 yards of the international border on the plea that construction of fence is a defensive structure. Secondly, it violates provisions of Joint Indo-Bangladesh Guidelines for Border Authorities- 1975. The Government of India has been trying persistently to convince Bangladesh Government that the erection of border fence does not violate the Joint Indo-Bangladesh Guidelines for Border Authorrities-1975 as the border fence is mutually beneficial for both the countries in curbing trans-border crimes.

records.name: Rajeev Shukla

records.qtitle: IMPROVEMENT IN EFFICIENCY OF ATC EMPLOYEES .

records.ans_text:
MINISTER OF STATE (INDEPENDENT CHARGE) OF THE MINISTRY OF CIVIL AVIATION ( SHRI PRAFUL PATEL )
(a) Yes, Sir. (b) No, Sir. Standard guidelines as prescribed by International Civil Aviation Organisation (ICAO) are followed by ATC officers. (c) and (d) Yes, Sir. Steps taken by Airports Authority of India (AAI) for improving efficiency of ATC officers inter-alia include regular Refresher Training, upgradation of ATC system and Ground infrastructure particularly at major airports and exposure of ATC officers at times to advanced ATC systems available in other countries.

records.qtitle: PROPOSAL FOR LINKING OF SMALL RIVERS AND CANALS .
records.name: Rajeev Shukla
records.qn_text:
(a) whether Government are planning to create smaller links between rivers and canals to resolve irregularities of water distribution; and

(b) if so, the details of the proposal along with its status so far?
records.ans_text:
THE MINISTER OF WATER RESOURCES

(PROF. SAIF-UD-DIN SOZ)

(a) & (b) The Ministry of Water Resources (MOWR) and Central Water Commission (CWC) formulated a National Perspective Plan (NPP) for Water Resources Development in 1980 envisaging interbasin transfer of water from surplus basins to deficit ones. NPP comprises of two components,viz
(i) Himalayan rivers development component and
(ii) Peninsular rivers development component. National Water Development Agency (NWDA) was set up in 1982 as a registered Society under MOWR to carry out detailed studies for NPP. NWDA, based on water balance and other studies, identified 30 links (14 under Himalayan and 16 under Peninsular) for preparation of feasibility reports (FR). FRs of 16 (2 Himalayan and 14 Peninsular) links have been completed by NWDA. Irrigation is a State subject and as per present policy, irrigation projects are planned, investigated, formulated, implemented and funded by the State governments out of their own resources and as per their own priorities. Therefore, the works to resolve irregularities of water distribution are carried out by State Governments and the Central Government does not contemplate smaller links between rivers and canals.

records.qtitle: VACANT POSTS OF JUDGES IN HIGH COURTS .
records.name: Rajeev Shukla
records.qn_text:
(a) the total number of vacancies in the High Courts as on date;

(b) the steps being taken to fill up the vacancies;

(c) whether any proposal exists to increase the strength of judges in any of the High Courts; and

(d) if so, the details thereof alongwith the action taken so far?
records.ans_text:
MINISTER OF LAW AND JUSTICE (SHRI H. R. BHARDWAJ)

(a), (b), (c) & (d) A statement is laid on the Table of the House.
Statement referred to in reply to parts (a), (b), (c) & (d) of the Rajya Sabha Starred Question No. 34 for answer on 20.2.2006.
Against the sanctioned strength Of 675 Judges in 21 High Courts, 553 Judges were in position as on 15.2.2006, leaving 122 vacancies to be filled up.2. Filling up of vacancies in the High Courts is a continuous consultative process among the constitutional authorities. While every effort is made to fill up the existing vacancies expeditiously, vacancies`do keep arising on account of retirements, resignation or elevation of Judges.

3. After the Supreme Court Judgment of October 6, 1993 in the Supreme Court Advocates-on-Record & Ant. Vs. Union of India, read with the Advisory Opinion of October 28, i998, the entire process of initiation of proposal for appointment of a Judge of a High Court lies with the Chief Justice of that High Court. Government has been periodically reminding the Chief Justices of the High Courts and the Chief Ministers of the States to initiate proposals for filling up all vacant posts of judges in the High Courts as also those which will be falling vacant during the next six months.

4. The judge strength of the High Courts is reviewed every three years. For review of Judge strength, the average institution and the pendency of main cases during the last five years is considered by taking into account the national average or the average rate of disposal of main cases per Judge per year in that ttigh Court, whichever is higher. If the disposal per Judge in the concerned High Court is below even the national average then instead of increasing the strength, the concerned High Court is required to take steps for improvement in the rate of disposal of cases. If the average disposal of concerned High Court is above the national average then increase in Judge strength is accordingly considered. The strength of Additional Judges is` reviewed only if there is an increase in the arrears of the pending cases during the last 5 years and the disposal per Judge is above the national average. The last review was undertaken in the year 2003 when 94 new posts were recommended. As an interim review, 4 posts of Judges were approved for the Bombay High Court in 2005, making the total for increase of 98 posts. The next review is due in 2006 for which the High Courts have been requested to furnish data.

(a) whether it is a fart that Government have requested Planning Commission for more resources to fund higher education;

records.name: Rajeev Shukla
records.qn_text:
(a) whether Government are working on a plan to reduce vast inequalities in healthcare delivery system across different regions and socio-economic groups in India;

(b) if so, the details thereof;

(c) whether Government have also finalized its policy on soliciting private sector involvement for advancing healthcare facilities across all regions; and

(d) if so, the details thereof ?
records.ans_text:
THE MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF HEALTH & FAMILY WELFARE

( SMT. PANABAKA LAKSHMI)

(a) & (b) The National Health Policy, 2002 has given over riding importance to ensuring more equitable access to health services across the country. As health is a State subject, the policy has emphasised that the State Governments would need to design specific schemes wherever required, to suit the health needs of their region.
The Government of India is implementing National Health Programmes for control of major communicable and non communicable diseases like Malaria, TB, Leprosy, AIDS, blindness, cancer and mental health which cover the entire country. With a view to removing regional imbalances and availability of tertiary health facilities, six AIIMS like institutions are to be set up in the under served areas of the country and several institutions are to be upgraded to that level. Recently the Government has launched a National Rural Health Mission to provide accessible, affordable, accountable, effective and reliable primary health care especially to the poor and vulnerable sections of the population. It has as its key components provision of a female health activist in each village in select states a village health plan prepared through a local team headed by the Health and Sanitation committee of the Panchayat; strengthening of the rural hospital for effective curative care and made measurable and accountable to the community through Indian Public Health Standards (IPHS); and integration of vertical Health and Family Welfare Programmes and Funds for optimal utilization of funds and infrastructure and strengthening delivery of primary health care.

(c) & (d) The National Health Policy, 2002 welcomes the participation of the private sector in all the areas of health activities - Primary, Secondary and Tertiary - with suitable regulatory mechanisms. The private sector increasingly is participating in the delivery of health care particularly in National Programmes like TB, Blindness, HIV/AIDS, amongst others. The Central Government Health Scheme (CGHS) also engages some private hospitals for providing treatment to the CGHS beneficiaries. Health is a State subject. Public Private Partnership is also an important strategy under NRHM.

( c ) It has been suggested to the Canadian Government that a Joint Indo-Canadian Centre for Nanotechnology may be set up in India. records.qtitle: MODIFICATIONS IN DATA COLLECTED THROUGH TIN .
records.name: Rajeev Shukla
records.qn_text:
(a) whether Government have been able to make any significant use of the wealth of information being collected through Tax Information Network (TIN);

(b) if so, the details thereof;

records.ans_text:
MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF FINANCE

(SHRI S.S. PALANIMANICKAM)

(a)and(b) The Tax Information Network (TIN) is a repository of important tax related information coming from various sources which is being used by the Income-tax Department for widening and deepening the tax direct tax base of the country. Information coming from electronic TDS returns is being used for identification of non-filers of TDS returns and for matching tax deducted at sources with the tax deposited in Government account. The information coming in from Online Tax Accounting Systems (OLTAS) is being used for monitoring tax collections. The information coming in from the Annual Information Returns (AIR) is about specified high value financial transactions for identifying non-filet, for selection of cases for scrutiny and for deepening the tax base.

(c) No Sir.

(d) Not applicable in view of reply to (c) above.

records.qtitle: SHIFTING BUSINESS PROCESS OF REGISTRAR OF COMPANIES TO E GOVERNANCE MODE QUESTION .
records.name: Rajeev Shukla
records.qn_text:

(b) if so, the details of the proposals alongwith status of its implementation?
records.ans_text:
THE MINISTER OF COMPANY AFFAIRS

(SHRI PREM CHAND GUPTA)

(a) Yes, Sir.

(b) The Ministry of Company Affairs (MCA) has launched an ambitious e-Governance and modernization programme called `MCA21 e-Governance Project` on 01.03.2005. The Project aims at transforming MCA into a paperless, modern, service-oriented, quality conscious and customer centric organization, envisages shifting entire business process of Registrar of Companies to e-governance mode. After implementation, all services, such as registration of new companies, filing of annual returns and balance sheets, filing of event based documents and also viewing of documents etc. will be available to public online through Internet.
The Project envisages: 


- Digitisation of legacy data of Companies and Annual Returns & Balance Sheets 
of two years running into approx. 6.0 crore pages.


- Setting-up of facilitation centers at 53 locations throughout the country.  
These are known as Physical Front Offices (PFOs) and will remain operational 
for a period of three years.


	As per plan, the Project is to be implemented within a period of 60 weeks 
starting 1.3.2005. The Project implementation will start as pilots from  mid 
January in phases leading to nation-wide rollout by the end of April, 2006. The 
implementation is going ahead as per schedule.

records.name: Rajeev Shukla
records.qn_text:
(a) whether it is a fact that crop harvesting losses in India are as huge as Rs.65,000 crores per year;

(b) if so, the reasons therefor; and

(c) the details of steps being contemplated by Government to control and minimize harvesting losses of such a magnitude?
records.ans_text:
MINISTER OF AGRICULTURE

(SHRI SHARAD PAWAR)

(a)&(b): In a study conducted by the Directorate of Marketing & Inspection post harvest losses at producers` level have been estimated to be varying from 1.79 to 7.14 per cent for foodgrains and pulses and from 16.35 to 30.00 per cent in the case of fruits and vegetables. The wastage depends on nature of produce, its shelf life, mode of transportation, packaging, processing, distance from the market, availability of infrastructure facilities like rural godowns and cold storage etc.

(c): The Government has taken the following step to reduce post-harvest losses in the country.
Indian Council of Agricultural Research has been developing new techniques/systems to minimize the losses in agricultural produce in the country through the Central Institute of Post Harvest Engineering & Technology, Ludhiana and the all India Coordinated Research Project on Post Harvest Technology. The All India Coordinated Research Project on Post Harvest Technology has 33 co-operative centres located throughout the country to develop regionally differentiated post harvest technology packages for crop, livestock product and fisheries produce in terms of reducing post harvest losses, aiding value to the main produce and by-products.
National Horticulture Board, an autonomous body under this Ministry is implementing programmes to reduce post harvest losses by providing investment subsidy on the capital cost of infrastructure projects for post-harvest handling, processing and marketing of horticulture produce. The rate of subsidy is 20 percent of the project cost with a maximum limit of Rs.25 lakh per project.

The Department is also implementing schemes for construction/modernization of Cold Storage and Rural godowns in the country with a view to provide scientific storage facilities to farmers. Under these schemes, subsidy is provided @ 25% of capital cost of the storage project in general and @ 33.33 percent in case of North Eastern States, hilly areas and Scheduled Castes/Scheduled Tribes entrepreneurs. The scheme of Construction of Rural Godown has recently been revised to restrict subsidy on the storage projects for individual, companies and corporations @ 15 percent of the project cost.

records.name: Rajeev Shukla
records.qn_text:
(a) whether it is a fact that Government are planning to institutionalize arbitration by involving top members of bar and bench;

(b) if so, the details thereof;

(c) whether Government believe this action would speed up the arbitration process;

(d) if so, the reasons therefor; and

(e) the details of the other steps being contemplated by Government to speed up arbitration?
records.ans_text:
MINISTER OF LAW AND JUSTICE

(SHRI H.R. BHARDWAJ)

(a) & (b): Yes, Sir. The Departmental Related Parliamentary Standing Committee on Personnel, Public Grievances, Law & Justice which examined the Arbitration and Conciliation (Amendment) Bill, 2003 introduced in Rajya Sabha on 22na December, 2003 in its Ninth Report presented to Rajya Sabha on 4th August, 2005 recommended a legislation incorporating provisions relating to institutionalised arbitration. The Committee felt that intitutionalised arbitration would end the alleged unethical practice followed by some institutions as at present. This will also bring in accountability of arbitrators and committed people to conclude the arbitration proceedings in a time bound manner failing which there could be penalty for delay in settlement of disputes.

(c), (d) & (e): Yes, Sir. Institutionalised arbitration will bring in fully dedicated panel of lawyers and arbitrators devoting full time for arbitration proceedings. It will also considerably reduce delay in settlement of disputes occurring at present due to availability of arbitrators and arbitration lawyers only on a part time basis. The Government considers that mediation, conciliation, fast tract courts, lok adalats, etc, would also pave way for early resolution of disputes besides institutionalised arbitration proceedings.

(b) : The Government on 22.09.2005 has approved the implementation of Phase `A` of the Special Accelerated Road Development Programme (SARDP) for the North-Eastern region and the preparation of Detailed Project Reports (DPRs) for Phase `B` of the Programme. Under Phase `A` of the programme, 1310 km of roads at an estimated cost of Rs.4618 crore has been taken up ~b:r improvement. :-

MINISTER OF STATE FOR COMMUNICATIONS AND INFORMATION TECHNOLOGY(DR. SHAKEEL AHMAD)

records.qtitle: INFILTRATION ACROSS THE BORDER IN J K .

records.ans_text:
MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF HOME AFFAIRS

( SHRI SRIPRAKASH JAISWAL )

(a): As per the report of the State Government of Jammu and Kashmir, infiltration across the border in the State increased in May 2005 as compared to the previous months of this year. Level of infiltration declined in the month of June but it increased again in July. However, overall level of terrorist infiltration in the State has come down significantly this year till July 31, as compared to the corresponding period last year.

(b): Details are given below:- 


2005	Estimated no. of Infiltrators 
May	43
June	21
July	67
	

(c):   The Government, jointly with the State Government, have 
adopted a multi-pronged approach, to contain cross-border infiltration in Jammu 
and Kashmir, which includes, inter-alia, strengthening of border management and 
multi-tiered and multi-modal deployment along International Border/Line of 
Control and near the ever changing infiltration routes, construction of border 
fencing, improved technology, weapons and equipment for security forces, 
improved intelligence and operational coordination and synergising intelligence 
flow to check infiltration and pro-active action against the terrorists within 
the State. The counter infiltration efforts are reviewed periodically at 
various levels in the State Government (including the two Unified Headquarters 
headed by the Chief Minister of Jammu and Kashmir) and in the Central 
Government.

records.name: Rajeev Shukla
records.qn_text:
(a) whether as per the recent NCAER report over half of Kerosene supplied to PDS is pilfered and used in petrol and diesel adulteration;

(b) whether it is also a fact that the over 75 percent of Kerosene users in rural areas use it for lighting purposes;

(c) the total cost of India’s Kerosene imports for each of the last three years;

(d) the steps, if any, contemplated by Government to check pilferage and misuse of Kerosene; and

(e) the steps, if any, contemplated by Government to promote use of LPG in rural households?
records.ans_text:
MINISTER OF PETROLEUM & NATURAL GAS & PANCHAYATI RAJ

(SHRI MANI SHANKAR AIYAR)

(a) & (b): The Government have commissioned the first-ever detailed study of Kerosene demand in the country, through the National Council of Applied Economic Research (NCAER) in December 2004. They have submitted their interim report in June 2005. While, the interim report does not indicate the extent of pilferage of PDS kerosene, the final report is likely to attempt an estimate the diversion of PDS kerosene for unintended usage. As per the interim report, nearly 73% of households in rural areas use kerosene for lighting purposes.

(c) : The total cost of kerosene imported during 2002-03, 2003-04 and 2004-05 was about Rs.808 crore, Rs.890 crore and Rs.429 crore respectively.


(d) : In order to check pilferage and misuse of kerosene and to ensure that highly subsidized kerosene supplied under the Public Distribution Network (PDS) reaches the targeted consumers, the Government have developed an innovative scheme for the marketing of PDS kerosene called “ Jan Kerosene Pariyojana”. The scheme would be initially implemented as a pilot project w.e.f.

2.10.2005 covering about 10% of the blocks in the country. Based on the experience of the pilot project and its evaluation by an independent agency, the scheme would be further extended to cover all the blocks in the country.

(e) : In order to promote use of LPG in rural households, Government have directed Oil Marketing Companies (OMCs) to concentrate on setting up more distributorships in rural areas and also to adopt innovative methods such as sale through rural mobile vehicles, setting up community kitchens, and sale of small size 5 kg. Cylinders for low income group customers.

records.qtitle: REFUSAL BY BANKS TO ACCEPT FRINGE BENEFITS TAX .

records.ans_text:
MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF FINANCE

(SHRI S.S. PALANIMANICKAM)

(a),(b)&(c): - On complaints made to the Reserve Bank of India by the Central Board of Direct Taxes (CBDT) that certain branches of Banks are not accepting the payment of fringe benefits tax as the bank`s software has not been modified, Reserve Bank of India vide its letter dated 14th July,2005 had advised all agency banks to take remedial action and ensure that their authorized branches accept the above tax from customers without fail. In order to provide some more time to the taxpayers to familiarize themselves with the practices and procedures of payment of fringe benefits tax, the Central Board of Direct Taxes has decided that interest shall not be charged if the first installment of advance fringe benefit tax is paid on or before 31Ausgust, 2005.

records.qtitle: INTRODUCTION OF ADVANCED PASSENGER INFORMATION SYSTEM .
records.name: Rajeev Shukla

(b) if so, the details thereof, including the airports where this system will function, and the expenses to be incurred;

( SHRI SRIPRAKASH JAISWAL )

(a): Yes, Sir.

(b): A notification amending the Foreigners Order, 1948 was issued on 07.03.2005 to implement Advance Passenger Information System (APIS) from 01.10.2005 making it obligatory on the pilot of the aircraft/master of the vessel coming to India to provide prescribed information electronically about passengers on board to the immigration authorities in India within 15 minutes of taking off/leaving from the port outside India. APIS will function at all international airports in India. Expenses on communication and processing of the information will be born by the airlines and Central Government respectively.

(c) APIS will facilitate faster immigration clearance without compromising security.

records.qtitle: EFFECT OF CECA WITH SINGAPORE ON INDIAN PRIVATE BANKS .

(SHRI E.V.K.S. ELANGOVAN )

(a) to (c): Under the recently approved India-Singapore Comprehensive Economic Cooperation Agreement (CECA), Singapore Banks are permitted to invest in private sector banks in India through the FDI route subject to the following conditions :-

- Banks will have to follow the one mode of presence criteria laid down by RBI.  
Under this criteria, foreign banks can have a presence in the Indian markets 
through one of these forms ; (a) branches (b) not more than one wholly owned 
subsidiaries (c) Joint ventures.

records.qtitle: NEW AIRPORTS FOR LOW COST AIRLINES .
records.name: Rajeev Shukla
records.qn_text:
(a) the details of all Greenfield airport projects being planned by Government, alongwith the latest status and projected dates of completion;

(b) whether Government will consider additional new Greenfield airports exclusively for the use of low-cost airlines;

(c) whether it is a fact that Government are ruling relaxation of norms to allow new airports to come up in both New Delhi and Mumbai; and

(d) if so, the details thereof?
records.ans_text:
MINISTER OF STATE(INDEPENDENT CHARGE) OF THE MINISTRY OF CIVIL AVIATION ( SHRI PRAFUL PATEL )
(a),(b),(c) & (d) : At present two Greenfield airport projects, one at Devanahalli near Bangalore and the other at Shamshabad near Hyderabad, are in progress. Government of India has already entered into Concession Agreements with the project companies of these Greenfield airports. The project company for Devanahalli airport, Bangalore International Airport Limited(BIAL), has already executed the relevant project agreements and the Financial Close has been achieved by it on 23rd June, 2005. As per the Concession Agreement entered by Government of India with BIAL, the new airport at Devanahalli is required to be completed within 33 months from the date of Financial Close. The project agreements for Shamshabad Hyderabad airport are in different stages of execution. The project Company for this airport i.e. Hyderabad International Airport Limited(HIAL) is required to complete this project within 36 months from the date of financial close, as per the Concesssion Agreement entered by Government of India with HIAL. Financial Close is expected to be achieved by September, 2005. Government has also given in principle approval for construction of new greenfield airports at MOPA in Goa for which the State Government has got a Technical Feasibility Report prepared. There are also plans for construction of greenfield airports at Navi Mumbai, Chakan near Pune, Ludhiana in Punjab, Kannur in Kerala, Pakyong in Sikkim, Kohima in Nagaland which are in preliminary stages. At present, there is no proposal for second airport at New Delhi.

records.name: Rajeev Shukla
records.qn_text:
(a) whether it is a fact that civil courts in lower Judiciary combined with High Courts and Supreme Court are the only constitutional institutions to observe summer and winter vacations;

(b) whether it is also a fact that hundreds of thousands of court cases are pending and that theirnumber shows no signs of abating;

(c) whether in view of

(a) and

(b) above, Government would consider to put an end to the colonial practice of courts observing summer vacations; and

(d) if so, the details thereof and if not, the reasons therefor?
records.ans_text:
MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF LAW & JUSTICE

(SHRI K.VENKATAPATHY)

(a) to (d); The working days in the Supreme Court and High Courts are regulated by the rules framed by the respective Courts, According to available information, the Supreme Court of India works for 222 days in a year; all High Courts in the country normally have 210 working days in a year and the number of working days of the District/Subordinate Courts are regulated by the concerned High Court.
The question of curtailing/discontinuing the vacations in the Courts has been considered in the past, but it has not been found feasible or advisable to do so because of the taxing nature of work of the Judiciary and the Bar. The Department of Justice in July 2001 had invited the views of the High .Courts regarding the number of working days in the High Courts and the curtailment of their vacations. Replies were received from 14 High Courts. The High Court of Uttaranchal increased the number of its working days in a year from 210 to 224 and the High Court of Karnataka from 210 to 214. Jharkhand High Court had no objection to increase the number of working days. Other High Courts had not favoured increase in the number of their working days in a year.
In view of the urgent need of the hour to reduce the huge pendencies prevailing in the High Courts, this Department addressed to all the High Courts, requesting them to fix the period of vacations in such a way that the number of working days of High Courts generally do not fall below 222 days in a year.
Various other steps have been taken by the Government to expedite disposal of cases, these include periodically monitoring the pendency position in courts, grouping of cases involving common question of law, constitution of specialized benches, timely filling up the vacancies of judges, increasing the judge strength, organizing Lok Adalats at regular intervals, encouraging alternative modes of disputes resolution like negotiation, mediation and arbitration and setting up of special tribunals like Central Administrative Tribunals, State Administrative Tribunals, Income Tax Appellate Tribunals, Family Courts, Labour Courts etc,

records.name: Rajeev Shukla
records.qn_text:
(a) whether any specific policy exists regarding facilities to be provided to pregnant working women in Government and private sector organizations;

(b) if so, the details thereof;

(c) whether any specific policy exists to enumerate facilities to nursing working mothers in the above organizations; and

(d) if so, the details thereof?
records.ans_text:
THE MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF HEALTH & FAMILY WELFARE

( SMT. PANABAKA LAKSHMI)

(a) to (d): Several laws have been enacted to secure reasonable working conditions for women workers and to prevent their exploitation. Special provisions have been made under various labour laws to provide facilities to pregnant working women. Under the Maternity Benefit Act, 1961, maternity benefits are to be provided on completion of 80 days working. No work of arduous nature, long hours of standing likely to interfere with pregnancy/normal development of foetus which may cause miscarriage or is likely to affect health. On production of medical certificate, advance maternity benefit as per law is to be allowed. Rs.250 as Medical bonus to be given when no prenatal confinement and post-natal care is provided free of charge.
The insured women covered under ESI Act are provided medical care by way of Pre-natal Care (ante-natal care including immunisation & prophylaxes against iron deficiency anaemia). Natal care (all services related to delivery of child) and Post-Natal Care (regular check-ups, counselling for family welfare and immunisation of child) and maternity benefits by way of cash benefits for all days on which she does not work for remuneration during a period of 12 weeks for confinement, 6 weeks in case of miscarriage and additional one month in case of sickness arising out of pregnancy, confinement, pre-mature birth of child or miscarriage or medical termination of pregnancy as per provisions of Section 56 & 50 of ESI Act, 1948 and Regulations thereof. No separate specific policy for Nursing working mothers is available in ESI Act, 1948.
Under the Plantation Labour Act, 1951, women workers are provided time off for feeding children.
Under the Building and Other Construction Workers (Regulation of Employment and Conditions of Service) Act, 1996, provisions for maternity benefit to female beneficiaries of the Welfare Fund have been made.

(c) if so, the details thereof?

THE MINISTER OF POWER

( SHRI P.M. SAYEED )

(a) : Energy shortage in the country during the summer months (April – July, 2005) is anticipated to be of the order of 4% of the total energy requirement of the country as compared to 6% during the same period last year.

(b) & (c) : The following measures are being taken to augment availability of power in the country during ensuing summer months:

(i) Export of power from surplus regions to deficit regions.

(ii) Load management:-Imposition of statutory power cuts/restriction and load shedding by State Government/Power Utilities from time to time depending upon the availability of power.

(iii) Coordinated operation and maintenance of hydro/thermal/nuclear gas turbine power station in the regional power system to optimally utilize the existing generation capacity.

(iv) Installation of shunt capacitors to improve voltage profiles of regional grids.

(v) Import of coal to bridge the gap between demand and availability of domestic coal and consequently enhance generation from coal based power stations.

records.name: Rajeev Shukla
records.qn_text:
(a)

(a) whether Government feel a need for regulating stem-cell research in India;

(b)

(b) if so, the details of any legislation being considered in this behalf; and

(c)

(c) if not, the reasons therefor?
records.ans_text:
MINISTER OF STATE (INDEPENDENT CHARGE) OF THE MINISTRY OF SCIENCE & TECHNOLOGY AND MINISTER OF STATE (INDEPENDENT CHARGE) OF THE DEPARTMENT OF OCEAN DEVELOPMENT

(SHRI KAPIL SIBAL)

(a), (b) &(c) Yes Sir,
National Bioethics Committee set up by the Department of Biotechnology(DBT) with the approval of Hon`ble Minister of Science and Technology, in its sixth meeting recommended promotion of stem cell research in the country in view of its vast potential and its clinical use. There are no special legal or ethical problems in respect to stem cells, derived from adults, bone marrows or foetal cord blood. However, in respect to embryonic stem cells the Government does not allow generation of embryos for the sole purpose of obtaining stem cells. Only surplus or spare or supernumerary embryos can be used with the permission of couples from registered Assisted Reproductive Technique (ART) clinics.
The Indian Council of Medical Research (ICMR), Ministry of Health and Family Welfare was requested by the Drugs Controller General of India (DCGI) to prepare appropriate guidelines to help in regulation of stem cell research and its application. Accordingly, a drafting committee provided brief guidelines for regulatory aspects of stem cell research to DCGI. These draft guidelines have been put on the website of the ICMR. The guidelines suggested constituting a multidisciplinary National Apex Committee (NAC) to monitor stem cell research activities in the country. It was also emphasized that newer technology should be thoroughly examined before approving any research. It was further suggested that this committee should examine all proposals involving stem cells of any source. Centres involved in stem cell research should be registered with the committee. Currently in the absence of a National Committee, an Expert Committee has been constituted to monitor and review stem cell research activities under ICMR.
The issues regarding legislation and ethical issues involved in stem cell research are being discussed by a joint working group of ICMR and DBT.

records.name: Rajeev Shukla
records.qn_text:
(a) whether Government are planning to establish a Tsunami early warning system in the Indian Ocean;

(b) if so, whether the system would be set up with other countries touched by the oceans;

(c) its financial implications and in what way it is going to be obtained; and

(d) by when the system is likely to be started and the time by which it would be completed?
records.ans_text:
MINISTER OF STATE (INDEPENDENT CHARGE) OF THE MINISTRY OF SCIENCE & TECHNOLOGY AND MINISTER OF STATE (INDEPENDENT CHARGE) OF THE DEPARTMENT OF OCEAN DEVELOPMENT

(SHRI KAPIL SIBAL)

(a) Yes, Sir. It is proposed to set up a `tsunami and storm surges warning system` in the country with the following components: Strengthening of the existing seismological network to identify in near real time occurrence of a tsunamigenic earthquake. Installation of tsunami warning sensors close to the ocean bottom at appropriate locales in the Indian Ocean, with real time connectivity. Tide gauge and data buoys networking. Modeling of the inundation scenarios for the entire coast. = The establishment of a centre for collection of the information,.`analysis and generating Tsunami and Storm Surge advisories

(b) No, Sir. After such a system is in place and warning systems are made near real time then networking with countries in the Indian Ocean who might require prior information in case of a Tsunami would be done for exchange of information for their benefit and mutual benefit.

(c) & (d): The system would cost about Rs.125 crores. India will bear this cost. The work has been initiated. Different components would be achieved with passage of time and the system will be fully operational by September 2007.

records.name: Rajeev Shukla
records.qn_text:
(a) whether growing clout of Maoist in Nepal is a threat to India`s security; [b] whether Government hold the view that the Maoists in Nepal have links with Naxalite insurgents in many Indian states; and

(c) the steps Government are taking to protect India`s interest from these insurgent movement?
records.ans_text:
THE MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF EXTERNAL AFFAIRS

(SHRI E. AHAMED)

(a) Yes, Sir.

(b) Yes, Sir.

(c) Government of India has provided assistance as required by Government of Nepal in dealing with the challenges posed by the Maoist insurgency. Sashastra Seema Bal (SSB) has been deployed along the India-Nepal border to strengthen security in the border areas. A network of Institutional dialogue mechanisms with the Government of Nepal has been evolved to discuss cross-border security issues.

records.name: Rajeev Shukla
records.qn_text:
(a) whether it is a fact that Government encourage the use of CNG as an environment-friendly fuel in passenger and commercial vehicles;

(b) if so, whether Government are planning any steps to promote its usage by facilitating supply and distribution of CNG in major cities of the country; and

(c) if so, the details thereof?
records.ans_text:
MINISTER OF PETROLEUM & NATURAL GAS & PANCHAYATI RAJ

(SHRI MANI SHANKAR AIYAR)

(a) to (c): A statement is laid on the Table of the House.

STATEMENT REFERRED TO IN REPLY TO PARTS (a) TO (c) OF THE RAJYA SABHA STARRED QUESTION NO.286 BY SHRI RAJEEV SHUKLA TO BE ANSWERED ON 21ST DECEMBER, 2004 REGARDING PROMOTION OF USE OF CNG

(a) to (c) Yes, Sir. Government is encouraging the use of CNG as an environment- friendly fuel in cities with high levels of pollution. At present, there are 228 CNG stations in operation in the country, as per the details given in the Annexe. Further, Indraprastha Gas Limited (IGL), in the adjoining areas of Delhi, namely, NOIDA, Faridabad and Gurgaon, and Mahanagar Gas Limited (MGL) in the adjoining areas of Mumbai, namely, Mira-Bhayander, Thane city, Vashi, New Bombay, Kalyan-Dombiwali etc., are proposing to expand their CNG network. CNG, as an auto fuel, will be introduced in a phased manner in different polluted cities of the country, subject to availability of natural gas and gas transmission infrastructure.
In order to cover more areas under the CNG network, GAIL (India) Limited (GAIL) have formed Joint Ventures for implementing city gas distribution projects with Hindustan Petroleum Corporation Limited (HPCL) for Andhra Pradesh, and with Bharat Petroleum Corporation Limited (BPCL) for Kanpur and Pune. In addition, GAIL has signed an MoU with the Indian Oil Corporation Limited (IOCL) for the formation of a Joint Venture to implement City Gas Projects in Agra, Lucknow and Bareilly.
