records.qtitle: POLICY ON DUTY ON IMPORT OF ANTIQUES .
records.name: Rajeev Shukla
records.qn_text:
(a) whether it is a fact that no Government policy or guidelines exist today with regard to duty and tax free import of antiques, relics and items of national treasure, which belonged to India in first place and were exported there after;

(b) if so, whether there is any proposal to be put in place for such a policy;

(c) If so, the details thereof; and

(d) If not, the reasons therefore?
records.ans_text:
MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF FINANCE (SHRI S.S.PALANIMANICKAM)

(a), (b) and (c) Under the present government policy, antiques and works of art imported for exhibition in a public museum or in a national institute are fully exempt from customs duties. As regards relics and items of national treasure, there is no specific exemption at present. However, if such items qualify to be treated as antiques, they will also be eligible for exemption subject to condition specified above.

(d) Does not arise in view of (a), (b) and (c) above.

records.name: Rajeev Shukla
records.qn_text:
(a) whether it is a fact that there is no mechanism to ensure that unreserved tickets issued to passengers for a train matches the number of seats available in that train;

(b) if so, whether such a mechanism is possible;

(c) if not, whether Government are planning to put such mechanism in place; and

(d) if so, the details thereof ?
records.ans_text:
MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF RAILWAYS

(SHRI R.VELU)

(a) & (b): Unreserved tickets are issued for a particular destination and are valid for travel for the entire day on the date of journey. Unreserved tickets are not issued for a particular train and thus, it is not possible to link it to the carrying capacity of a train.

(c) & (d): No, Sir.

records.name: Rajeev Shukla
records.qn_text:
(a) whether it is a fact that air pollution levels in major cities including metros in India are above levels that are regarded as safe;

(b) whether it is also a fact that pollution levels in many major cities have been increasing over the last five years;

(c) if so, change in pollution level figures for five years for ten most polluted cities in India; and

(d) the steps Government propose to take to bring back the air pollution levels within safe thresholds in the worst-affected cities?
records.ans_text:
MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF ENVIRONMENT AND FORESTS

(SHRI NAMO NARAIN MEENA)

(a)&(b) A decreasing trend has been observed in the Sulphur-dioxide (SO²) levels in residential areas of many major cities. The trend in annual average concentration of Nitrogen-dioxide (NO2) is fluctuating in most of the cities and levels of Respirable Suspended Particulate Matter (RSPM) are usually higher than the stipulated standards mainly due to natural dusty conditions.

(c) Based on the ambient air quality monitored under the National Ambient Air Quality Programme (NAAQM), Central Pollution Control Board, in coordination with the State Pollution Control Boards, has identified top ten cities on the basis of RSPM levels observed in the residential areas during 2003 ( a list enclosed.) A similar trend of air pollution is observed (n these ten c/ties as that of ma)or cities stated above.

(d) The Government has taken various steps to check air pollution levels within safe thresholds in the worst affected cities, which include - 
	Notification of general and source specific emission standards.
-	Enforcement of auto exhaust emission standards for new vehicles at
	manufacturing stage.
-	Improved fuel quality.
	Use of beneficiated coal in the thermal power stations.
	Regular monitoring for compliance of environmental standards in 17
	categories of industries. Legal action is taken in case of defaulting units.
-	A road map up to 2010 has been developed to control vehicular
	pollution for both the new and in-use vehicles.
	New emission norms for in-use vehicles have been introduced from
	October, 2004.

records.qtitle: (clubbed) OFFER OF FBI S HELP TO INDIA .
records.name: Vijay Mallya
records.qn_text:
(a) whether it is a fact that US Ambassador has recently offered the assistance of Federal Bureau of Investigation to investigate the serial blasts in the North Eastern States;

(b) if so, the details thereof;

(c) whether any such offer has been received from any European countries also;

(d) if so, the details thereof;

(e) whether Government are aware that the Government of United States of America have circulated a document earlier which seeks to alienate the North Eastern Region from the country; and

(f) whether Government have taken a view of this offer of assistance keeping in view the security of the country?
records.ans_text:
THE MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF EXTERNAL AFFAIRS

(SHRI E. AHAMED)

(a) Yes, Sir.

(b) The offer of assistance was received by Ministry of Home Affairs in the form of a letter dated October 4, 2004 written by Ambassador of USA.

(c) No, Sir

(d) Does not arise.

(e) No, Sir

(f) Government`s position is that cooperative efforts in the field of counter-terrorism would be discussed within the existing framework of cooperation for such matters.

records.name: Rajeev Shukla
records.qn_text:
(a) whether a proposal from an American Company ‘Unocal” to lay a pipeline from Turkmenistan to India via Afghanistan and Pakistan is under consideration of Government;

(b) if so, the details of the proposal;

(c) if not, whether there are any other proposals under consideration of Government;

(d) whether Government have analyzed the security and economic aspects of the proposal in view of the possible interruption in the supplies through possible militant activities along the supply line; and

(e) if so, the details thereof?
records.ans_text:
MINISTER OF PETROLEUM & NATURAL GAS & PANCHAYATI RAJ

(SHRI MANI SHANKAR AIYAR)

(a): No, Sir.

(b): Does not arise.

(c): No, Sir. There is at present no specific proposal under consideration for gas imports from Turkmenistan to India via Afghanistan and Pakistan.

(d) and (e): As and when any proposal for the supply of gas from Turkmenistan to India via Afghanistan and Pakistan is taken up, all security and economic aspects will be thoroughly examined.

records.name: Rajeev Shukla
records.qn_text:
(a) Whether Government are aware of the reports in the media on differences of opinion between the Reserve Bank of India and his Ministry in the matter of utilization of part of foreign exchange reserves for development of infrastructure ;

(b) Whether in view of the larger requirement of funds for the purpose, how do Government propose to raise funds, particularly since RBI is not in favour of utilizing the forex reserves for the purpose;

(c) Whether regulatory agencies are being contemplated to be set up in the Planning Commission to make infrastructure funding by the private sector more attractive; and

(d) If so, the details thereof?
records.ans_text:
MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF FINANCE

(Shri S.S. Palanimanickam)
a): India`s total foreign exchange reserves are now more than US$128 billion. Any decision to utilise a part of these reserves for funding domestic projects requires a careful assessment, inter alia, of the impact of such a measure on the fiscal situation, money supply, exchange rate, domestic interest rates, reserve adequacy and inflation. An informed debate on the feasibility of such an utilisation is currently on.

(b): The latest Union Budget (2004-05) has underlined enhancing investment - both public and private - in industry, as a thrust area, and has reiterated the commitment to remove inadequacies in infrastructural facilities. Specific measures aiming to enhance investment like increasing foreign direct investment

(FDI) ceiling in civil aviation, and setting up an Investment Commission for inviting domestic and foreign businesses to invest in India, have already been taken.

(c) : No, Sir.

(d) : Does not arise.

records.name: Vijay Mallya
records.qn_text:
(a) whether it is a fact that the National Commission to review the working of the Constitution had recommended that a National Judicial Commission be set up so that there is wider public participation and transparency;

(b) whether Government have examined the recommendation and if so, the action taken in this regard;

(c) in view of the complaints on the functioning of the judicial particularly at the higher levels, which can be looked into by such a National Judicial Commission, why there has been so much delay in appointing the Commission; and

(d) the time frame to set up the Commission?
records.ans_text:
MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF LAW AND JUSTICE

( SHRI K. VENKATAPATHY )

(a)&(b) Yes, Sir. The Constitution(Ninety Eighth Amendment) Bill, 2003 was introduced in the Lok Sabha on 9.5.2003 for setting up of a National Judicial Commission. The Bill has, however, lapsed due to dissolution of the last Lok Sabha in May, 2004.

(c)&(d) The Chief Justice of India and the Chief Justice of a High Court have the competence to receive complaints against the conduct of the Judge of his Court and when he receives any, he would look into it whether the allegations deserve to be closely looked into. There is no proposal for setting up of National Judicial Commission.

records.name: Vijay Mallya
records.qn_text:
(a) the number of farmers who committed suicide in Karnataka since 1998;

(b) the measures taken by Government to prevent such deaths and the number of families paid compensation and the amount of compensation, so paid;

(c) the special incentives announced by Hon`ble Prime Minister for the farmers of Andhra Pradesh and when the same incentives would be extended to farmers of Karnataka; and if not, the reasons therefor; and

(d) whether Government have announced any fresh package for the welfare of farmers?
records.ans_text:
MINISTER OF AGRICULTURE

(SHRI SHARAD PAWAR)

(a) to (d): A statement is laid on the Table of the House. STATEMENT IN RESPECT OF PARTS (a) TO (d) OF RAJYA SABHA STARRED QUESTION NO. 148 FOR 10/12/2004 REGARDING SUICIDE BY FARMERS IN KARNATAKA.


(a): According to information received from the Government of Karnataka the number of farmers who have committed suicide in the State since 1998 is as follows:- 
S.No.	Year	Figures of State Crime Records Bureau	Figures of 
Agriculture Department 

1.	1998-99	2039	 

2.	1999-2000	2379	- 

3.	2000-01	2630	 

4.	2001-02	2505	  

5.	2002-03	2340	
6.	2003-04		708


(b):  The State Government  has announced a series  of measures for the farming community to tide 
over the situation.  With a view to providing relief to the farmers and for revival of agricultural 
operations, Government of Karnataka announced a relief package comprising the following: -


?	Waiver of interest on co-operative short-term loans for Rabi-2002.  No penal interest 
on short-term agricultural loans by cooperatives in future.  Rebate on current interest 
for long-term loans to the farmers at the rate of 5.5% to be reimbursed by the 
Government provided the farmers pay the remaining interest on 9%. 


?	To write off outstanding loan and interest on failed wells.


?	Full waiver of the outstanding dues to the State Electricity Board from the farmers as 
on 31.3.2001 in respect of irrigation pump sets.


?	Supply of seeds to small and marginal farmers at 50% subsidy in drought affected 
regions.


?	Minimum Support Price operations for Soya bean, Maize and Sunflower by the     
Agricultural Marketing Department in collaboration with NAFED.


 
?	Educating farmers with the help of Psychologists and Social scientists about the ill 
effects of suicide and inculcate among them the confidence to stand up to any 
adversity.


?	Encouragement to farmers to take up alternate crop in places where rainfall has failed 
and drought resistant varieties of crop can be grown.


?	Implementation of Rashtriya Krishi Bima Yojana in the State from 2000-01 and 
admissible compensation till Kharif 2003 paid.


?	Raitha Samparka Kendras to act as focal points to receive representations and 
complaints from farmers.




A sum of Rs. 204 lakhs have so far been sanctioned   @ Rs. 1,00,000 for each 
family in respect of farmers who committed suicide during 2003-04.   A sum of
 Rs. 36 lakhs has also been sanctioned and paid to the families of farmers who
 committed suicide during the current financial year i.e. 2004-05.


(c):  The Prime Minister  visited  a  few villages in Andhra Pradesh on
 1st  July, 2004 and directed among other things, that livelihood cover should
 be provided to one person from each of the suicide affected families there 
through collaborative action between the Government and the banks.  He also
announced an assistance of Rs. 50,000 from the PM`s National Relief Fund
  (PMNRF) to the families of persons who committed suicide.


(d) 	In order to mitigate the distressing situation of farmers due to
 the problem of indebtness, the Government of India on 18.6.2004 has announced
 a special package for providing credit related relief 
to the farmers.   Following are the highlights of this announcement: -


?	Total flow of agricultural credit which is estimated at Rs.80,000 crore
 in 2003-04 is to 
be enhanced to about Rs.1,05,000 crore in 2004-05 representing a 30 per cent
 increase over the flow of credit in the previous year.


?	In order to provide credit to tenant farmers and oral lessees, NABARD to
 facilitate formation and financing of self-help groups of tenant farmers and
 oral lessees.  This exploratory/pilot effort is expected to bring nearly a
 lakh of tenant farmers, oral lessees and sharecroppers within the banking
 fold.


?	Scales of finance to be reviewed to meet the realistic credit needs of
 farmers, especially capital-intensive agricultural operations. 


?	Debt restructuring to be done by commercial banks, RRBs and cooperatives 
in accordance with the new guidelines to be laid down by RBI/NABARD.


NABARD have issued directions to all State level cooperative institutions for
 fixation of realistic scales of finance to meet the credit requirements of the
 farmers for raising crops.    Debt restructuring will be done by the 
commercial banks, RRBs and cooperatives in accordance with the new guidelines
 as in the following: -
Farmers in distress – Debts of farmers in districts declared as calamity-
affected by the State Government concerned will be rescheduled/restructured.
  Interest outstanding in the accounts of such borrowers will be clubbed with
 the principal outstanding on March 31, 2004, and the amount thus arrived at 
shall be repayable over a period of five years, at current interest rates,
 including an initial moratorium of two years.Farmers in arrears – Loans and
 advances outstanding as on 31st March, 2004 may be rescheduled into a term
 loan repayable over a period of three to five years at the current rates of
 interest.  Interest outstanding      as   on 31st March, 2004     may     be
     collected        upfront.     In      case     of  term 
loans and previous rescheduled loan where the existing repayment schedule is
 longer than 3 to 5 years the overdue part of the principal shall only be
 rescheduled.  The remaining part of the loan shall have originally contracted
 schedule of repayment. 
OTS for small and marginal farmers – Loans outstanding of the identified
 farmers whose accounts have been categorized,   as   NPAs   as   on 31.3.2001
 would be covered under the scheme.   Eligible farmers  should  apply   to
   bank   in  writing requesting for such  settlement.     For accounts declared  


as NPAs as on 31.3.2001, the settlement amount will be the balance outstanding 
in the loan account as on 31.3.2001.  As regards interest accrued in the
 account after 31.3.2001, banks will decide upon the amount of compromise to be
 offered in each individual case subject to the condition that the
amount of compromise will not exceed the interest accrued in the account 
between 31st March, 2001 and date of settlement.  


The Reserve Bank of India has also issued standing guidelines to banks for
 providing relief to the farmers in areas affected by natural calamities.
   These guidelines envisage inter-alia:


?	Conversion/ rescheduling of loans in the event of natural calamity for
 periods ranging from 3 to 9 years depending upon the successive crop failure/
 intensity of damage of crops. 


?	Grant of fresh crop loans to affected farmers.


?	Conversion of principal as well as interest due on the existing short
 term loans to medium term loans. 


?	Grant of consumption loans. 


?	Not to compound interest in respect of loans converted / rescheduled etc. 


?	Not to charge penal interest in respect of current dues in default.

forest clearances, infrastructure facilities

etc.


(v)     setting up of an Empowered Committee in  the 
administrative  Ministries   for  review  of 
departmentally executed projects;


(vi)    inter-ministerial coordination for resolving 
unresolved problems;


(vii)   setting  up  of Standing Committees  in  the 
Ministries/Departments to fix responsibility 
for time and cost overruns;


(viii)  appointment  of  nodal  officers  for   each 
project with continuity of tenure; and


(ix)    issue  of  guidelines  on  standard  bidding 
documents for adoption.

records.name: Vijay Mallya
records.qn_text:
(a) whether it is a fact that functioning of Member of Parliament Local Area Development Scheme (MPLADS) has not been satisfactory;

(b) whether any study by any Parliamentary Committee has been undertaken to assess the extent and the reasons for unsatisfactory implementation of the scheme;

(c) if so, the States which are affected; and

(d) what action Government propose to rectify this situation?
records.ans_text:
MINISTER OF STATE (INDEPENDENT CHARGE), MINISTRY OF STATISTICS AND PROGRAMME IMPLEMENTATION

(SHRI OSCAR FERNANDES)

(a) No, Sir, MPLADS implementation is generally satisfactory.

(b)and(c) No Sir. There was no Parliamentary Committee exclusively to assess the extent and the reasons for unsatisfactory implementation of MPLADS. Lok Sabha and Rajya Sabha MPLADS Committees have visited some States.

(d) Reports received from the MPLADS Committees are acted upon and necessary advice are issued to the State Governments and District Authorities.

records.name: Rajeev Shukla
records.qn_text:
(a) whether Government have received any proposals from major international telecom companies for setting up of manufacturing facilities in India;

(b) if so, the details of Government`s decision in this regard; and

(c) the details of any incentives proposed by Government to promote such investments in manufacturing?
records.ans_text:
THE MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF COMMUNICATIONS AND INFORMATION TECHNOLOGY (DR. SHAKEEL AHMAD)

(a) & (b): The fast growing telecom service sector in India has drawn attention of major international telecom companies for setting up of manufacturing facilities in India. As per the policy, no Government approval is required for setting up of manufacturing unit for the telecom sector.

(c) Some of the international telecom companies have given their recommendations for extending fiscal incentives and removal of certain impediments for the accelerated growth. However, the Government has already provided a number of incentives to promote investment in telecom manufacturing sector. Some of the incentive are:- 
 

(i)	100% Foreign Direct Investment is allowed in this sector under automatic route through Reserve Bank of India (RBI).  A technical know-how fee of 
US  $ 2 million and royalty at the rate of 5% for the domestic sales and at the rate of 8% for the export are also allowed under automatic route.


(ii)	Electronic Hardware Technology Park Scheme had been modified to boost indigenous telecom manufacturing industry.


(iii)	The telecom service operators have been allowed to issue Form `C` under Central Sales Tax enabling telecom manufacturing industry to avail concessional sales tax benefits.

records.qtitle: (clubbed)  NAXALITES RISE AND MENACE IN KARNATAKA .
records.name: Vijay Mallya
records.qn_text:
(a) whether Government are aware about rise in Naxalite activities in Karnataka in Chikmagalur and Mangalore districts, spread over Western Ghats area;

(b) if so, what are the steps taken to prevent naxalite activities;

(c) whether the living of Tribal people in those areas is being disturbed and dislocated; and

(d) what are the steps taken by the State Government to rehabilitate these Tribals?
records.ans_text:
MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF HOME AFFAIRS

(SHRI SRIPRAKASH JAISWAL)

(a) to (d): A Statement is laid on the Table of the House.
STATEMENT REFERRED TO IN REPLY TO RAJYA SABHA STARRED QUESTION NO. 111 FOR 8.12.2004 REGARDING NAXALITES RISE AND MENACE IN KARNATAKA.



(a) & (b): The CPML-PW and its front bodies are spreading their activities on the issue of eviction of tribals from the Kudremukh National Park in Malenadu region, comprising the districts of Chikmagulur, Shimoga, Udupi, Dakshina Kannada, Hassan and Kodagu.


The Central Government has adopted a multi-pronged strategy to tackle the problem of naxalism which includes (a) having a peace dialogue by the affected States, wherever feasible, with naxal groups willing to abjure violence, (b) moderanisation and strengthening of the State Police forces, long term deployment of Para Military forces, intensified intelligence based well-coordinated anti-naxalite operations, (c) focused attention on integrated development of the affected areas and (d) removal of socio-cultural alienation of people, gearing up of public grievances redressal system and creation of Local Resistance Groups.


The Government of Karnataka is alive to the problem of naxlites spreading their activities to some parts of the State and has initiated suitable counter measures.



(c) & (d): The issue of dislocation and rehabilitation of the tribals has been taken up by the State Government which is also in touch with the Ministry of Forest and Environment and the Ministry of Tribal Affairs.

records.name: Rajeev Shukla
records.qn_text:
(a) whether Government are aware of a recent report that declining water table may result in no ground water in major States like Delhi, in as few as 15 years;

(b) which are the top five worst performing States in terms of decline of their water table; and

(c) what steps are being planned and taken by Government to remedy the current situation?
records.ans_text:
THE MINISTER OF WATER RESOURCES

(SHRI PRIYA RANJAN DASMUNSI)

(a) to (c) A Statement is laid on the Table of the House.
STATEMENT REFERRED TO IN REPLY OF PARTS (a) TO (c) OF RAJYA SABHA STARRED QUESTION NO.96 FOR REPLY ON 07.12.2004 REGARDING DECLINE IN WATER TABLE

(a) As per the studies carried out by Central Ground Water Board (CGWB), under the Ministry of Water Resources, the fresh water zones in some areas of Delhi will become unavailable for exploitation within the next decade if the present rate of exploitation of ground water continues. The worst affected areas of Delhi are South West and South districts, which have been notified by the Central Ground Water Authority (CGWA) for control and regulation of ground water development. In South West district where a lens of 10 to 30 meter potable water floats over brackish water, the annual domestic draft is as high as 134 MCM (Million Cubic Meter) and the ground water levels are declining at the rate of 0.93 meter/year. In South district, the maximum depth of water level has reached 59 meter and annual decline of ground water level is about 0.7 meter with domestic draft of about 82.6 MCM.

(b) The top five worst affected States in terms of decline of water table and over-exploitation of ground water resources are Punjab, Delhi, Rajasthan, Tamil Nadu and Haryana.

(c) Water being a State subject, it is primarily the responsibility of the concerned State Governments to take steps to remedy the situation. Central Government has initiated/planned following measures to check over-exploitation and augmentation of ground water:- 
 

(i)  Circulation of a Model Bill in the year 1970 which was re-
circulated in 1992 and again in 1996 to all the States/Union
Territories to enable them to enact suitable legislation for
regulation and control of ground water development. 

(ii) Constitution of Central Ground Water Authority under the
Environment (Protection) Act, 1986 for regulation and control of
ground water management and development. The CGWA has notified
11 critical areas, including South and South West districts of
Delhi, on consideration of over-exploitation of ground water
resources. Further, the CGWA has also notified 32 over-exploited
areas in the country for registration of ground water
structures. 

(iii)     In 673 over-exploited and 425 dark/critical areas in
the country, State Pollution Control Boards and Ministry of
Environment & Forests obtain No Objection Certificate (NOC) from
CGWA for any new industry/projects. A pre-condition for any
permission is the mandatory adoption of rain water harvesting
system by the industry/project for ground water recharge. 

(iv) On similar lines, other developmental projects located in
Coastal Regulation Zone obtain NOC from CGWA as pre-requisite
for environment clearance. 

(v)  The CGWA has issued directions to Group Housing Societies,
Institutes, Hotels, Industries, Farm Houses etc., in the
notified areas of Delhi, Faridabad, Gurgaon and Ghaziabad to
adopt rain water harvesting system. 

(vi) Implementation of a Central Sector Scheme for Study of
Recharge to Ground Water in the country during the VIII & IX
Five Year Plans. 

(vii)     The CGWB has proposed a Centrally Sponsored Scheme at
an estimated cost of Rs. 175 crores for Artificial Recharge to
Groundwater and Rainwater Harvesting during the remaining part
of the X Five Year Plan. 

(viii)     Circulation  of Manual/Guidelines on  Artificial
Recharge of Ground Water to the States/Union Territories to
enable them to formulate area specific artificial recharge
schemes to check the declining trend of ground water levels. 

(ix) Central Ministries/Departments of Railways, Defence, Posts,
Telecommunications, Central Public Works Department and National
Highways Authority of India have been requested to provide roof
top rain water harvesting structures in the buildings under
their control. 

(x)  States/UTs have been requested to provide water harvesting
structures in buildings under their administrative control. 

(xi) All the States/Union Territories have been requested for
advising the local bodies in their respective States/Union
Territories to allow rebate in property tax to persons, who
adopt roof top rainwater harvesting in their premises. 

(xii)      The  Ministry  of  Urban Development  &  Poverty
Alleviation has amended Building Bye-laws, 1983, making
provision for water harvesting through storing of water run-off
including rain water in all new buildings on plots of 100 square
meters and above in Delhi mandatory. 

(xiii)    CGWB has provided technical guidance on rain water
harvesting to around 1800 agencies, including State Government
agencies, educational institutions, private entrepreneurs and
individuals. 

(xiv)      Launching  of a website on Roof Top  Rain  Water
Harvesting (www.cgwbindia.com) to make aware and educate the
public about various techniques of harvesting rainwater and
store it for future use. 

(xv) Organisation of mass awareness programmes and training
courses on rainwater harvesting and artificial recharge of
ground water. 

(xvi)     Water conservation campaign has been launched keeping
in view the various target groups like youth and children,
women, farmers and villagers, policy and opinion makers.
Publicity through print media, telecasting of spots on the
television, broadcasting messages on radio, holding of seminars,
workshops, conferences etc., have been undertaken for the
purpose.

records.name: Rajeev Shukla
records.qn_text:
(a) Whether it is a fact that the recently implemented Tax Information Network has enhanced tax receipts in mere four-five months of its existence;

(b) if so, the details thereof; and

(c) what is the estimate for increase in tax receipts for the complete fiscal?
records.ans_text:
MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF FINANCE

(SHRI S.S. PALANIMANICKAM)

(a), (b) & (c) Tax Information Network (TIN) has been set up as a repository of tax related information received by the Income Tax Department from various sources :in order to enhance tax compliance. These include information on tax payment coming from banks and on tax deducted at source from returns filed by tax deductors. From F.Y. 2005-06 onwards, information will also flow into TIN on tax collection at source and on certain high value transactions coming from prescribed persons. It is, however, not possible to specifically co-relate the increase in tax receipts with the implementation of Tax Information Network.

records.name: Vijay Mallya
records.qn_text:
(a) whether it is a fact that Government have set up the National Manufacturing and Competitiveness Council to advise Government on measures to restructure Public Sector Enterprises and on disinvestments;

(b) whether the Investment Commission and Board for Reconstruction of Public Sector Enterprises proposed earlier in the Budget 2004-05 are being set up;

(c) if so, whether it would not result in overlapping of functions of these institutions; and

(d) whether any decision has been taken in this regard and if so, the details thereof?
records.ans_text:
Minister of State in the Ministry of Finance ( Shri S.S. Palanimanickam)

(a) Yes, Sir. The Government has set up an autonomous National Manufacturing and Competitiveness Council under the administrative control of the Department of Industrial Policy & Promotion. However, the mandate of this Council is not to advise the Government on measures to restructure Public Sector Enterprises and/or on disinvestment, but to advise it on industrial and sector specific initiatives required for enhancing competitiveness of Indian industry in areas like research and development, entrepreneurship promotion, infrastructure enhancing facilities, trade and fiscal policies and employment generation.

(b) Yes, Sir. The Cabinet Committee on Economic Affairs has approved the setting up of an Investment Commission and the Board for Reconstruction of Public Sector Enterprises (BRPSE).

( c ) & (d) The functions of the three institutions are not likely to overlap as each of them have distinct terms of reference. While the National Manufacturing and Competitiveness Council has been constituted to advise the Government on industrial and sector specific initiatives required for enhancing competitiveness of Indian industry, the BRPSE is expected to advise the Government on ways and means for strengthening Public Sector Enterprises and to critically examine the proposals for revival, rehabilitation and reconstruction of sick or loss making Public Sector Enterprises. On the other hand, the mandate of the Investment Commission would be to make recommendations to the Government on both policy and procedures to facilitate greater foreign direct investment flows in India and to encourage investment in sectors where there is dire need for investment but adequate investment has not flowed so far.

records.name: Rajeev Shukla
records.qn_text:
(a) whether Government are aware that the state of airports outside major cities is far from satisfactory;

(b) if so, whether there are any plans by Government to improve those airports and the facilities thereof; and

(c) if so, the details thereof?
records.ans_text:
MINISTER OF STATE(INDEPENDENT CHARGE) OF THE MINISTRY OF CIVIL AVIATION ( SHRI PRAFUL PATEL )
(a), (b) & (c) : The improvement and upgradation of airports located outside major cities is a continuous process and taken up in phased manner on felt-need basis.
Airports Authority of India (AAI) has proposed to modernize twenty five (25) Non-Metro airports in phases with focus on airside and cityside development. In the first phase, approximately 10 airports would be taken up and the remaining in the second phase. Airports Authority of India (AAI) has decided to upgrade these airports to world class standards through the process of modernisation. AAI is in the process of appointing Indian Financial Consultant (IFC) and Global Technical Advisor (GTA) who will assist AAI in conducting techno-economic feasibility study of identified airport to evolve an appropriate model based on viability of the project.

records.name: Rajeev Shukla
records.qn_text:
(a) whether airlines in India have decided to increase air fares and if so, the details thereof;

(b) whether the air fares in India are three times more than elsewhere in the world and if so, the reasons therefor;

(c) whether Air Turbine Fuel is more expensive here as 80 per cent excise tax coupled with state sales tax ranging from 4 per cent to 9 per cent is imposed on it and if so, the reasons therefor; and

(d) whether Government propose to look into the matter and bring parity in fares with airlines of other countries?
records.ans_text:
MINISTER OF STATE(INDEPENDENT CHARGE) OF THE MINISTRY OF CIVIL AVIATION ( SHRI PRAFUL PATEL )
(a),(b) & (d): Government does not regulate the air fares and airlines are free to determine the same in accordance with their commercial judgement and market forces. (c) The prices of Aviation Turbine Fuel (ATF) before sales tax in India is higher by 25 to 35% compared to the average international prices. The taxation structure on ATF uplifted for domestic operation is 8% excise duty plus Sales Tax levied by State Governments ranging from 4% to 36%, average rate being 25% at present.

(b) if so, the details thereof and reasons therefor; and

Periodic meetings are held by the Department of Commerce with the State Governments/promoters of the SEZs to expedite the projects.

records.name: Rajeev Shukla
records.qn_text:
(a) whether there is a sports strategy and plan in place in view of the coming 2010 Commonwealth Games in New Delhi;

(b) if so, the details thereof; and

(c) if not, the reasons therefor?
records.ans_text:
MINISTER OF YOUTH AFFAIRS AND SPORTS

(SHRI SUNIL DUTT)

(a) to (c): A statement is laid on the Table of the House.

STATEMENT REFERRED TO IN REPLY TO PARTS (a) TO (c) OF THE RAJYA SABHA STARRED QUESTION NO.4 FOR 1.12.2004 REGARDING STRATEGY FOR COMMONWEALTH GAMES, 2010 ASKED BY SHRI RAJEEV SHUKLA


(a) to (c) : A multi-pronged strategy for preparation and conduct of the Commonwealth Games, 2010 includes upgradation of existing and creation of new infrastructure, providing facilities to Indian sportspersons for participation and setting up of Organizational structure for conduct of the Games. A review of existing infrastructure in the city of Delhi in context of Commonwealth Games 2010 has been undertaken. The review shows that the existing infrastructure with Sports Authority of India (SAI), Delhi Development Authority (DDA), New Delhi Municipal Corporation (NDMC) and Municipal Corporation of Delhi (MCD) with major upgradation and renovation could be used for most of the disciplines covered under the Commonwealth Games. A Task Force on SAI infrastructure has been set up by the Ministry with representatives from Ministry, CPWD & SAI. However, one indoor and one outdoor stadium as well as Squash Court would need to be constructed. In addition, a Commonwealth Games Village is also proposed to be constructed off Nizamuddin Bridge.
Specific efforts by way of providing specialized training and exposure under Indian and foreign coaches with scientific inputs are being made for the sports persons who are expected to excel in their respective disciplines in the Commonwealth and Asian Games, 2006 & Olympic Games, 2008 and to prepare them for participation in Commonwealth Games, 2010.
For coordinating the work relating to the organization and conduct of the Commonwealth Games, 2010, Government has constituted a Core Group of Ministers under the Chairmanship of Minister, Human Resource Development, Government of India.

records.name: Rajeev Shukla
records.qn_text:
(a) whether the recent ASSOCHAM Report saying that the cost of free electricity given to farmers by different State Boards is Rs.20,000 crore over last five years is true; and

(b) if so, how does the Government propose to recover the loss thereof?
records.ans_text:
THE MINISTER OF POWER

( SHRI P.M. SAYEED )


(a) : According to a press release of Associated Chambers of Commerce and Industries of India (ASSOCHAM), the power tariff subsidy granted to the agriculture sector has eroded the revenues of State Electricity Board to the extent of around Rs.20,000 crores in the last five years. Basis of this assessment is not available in this communication.

(b) : The Electricity Act, 2003 provides that the State Electricity Regulatory Commissions (SERCs) have the powers to fix tariff for sale of electricity to consumers taking into account the revenue requirement of distribution licensees. Section 65 of the Act provides that if the State Government requires the grant of any subsidy to any consumer or class of consumers in the tariff determined by the SERCs, the State Government shall pay to the concerned utility/licensees the full amount required to compensate the grant of subsidy. Thus, the matter of providing subsidy in tariff to a class of consumers is exclusively in the domain of the State Government.

records.name: Rajeev Shukla
records.qn_text:
(a) whether Doordarshan has decided to boost revenue by getting back some of its outstanding dues from the well known producers who owe it; and

(b) if so, the dues involved and the follow up action Government have taken to recover it?
records.ans_text:
THE MINISTER OF INFORMATION & BROADCASTING AND CULTURE

(SHRI S. JAIPAL REDDY)


(a) & (b): A statement is laid on the Table of the House.




STATEMENT REFERRED TO IN REPLY TO PARTS (a) & (b) OF RAJYA SABHA STARRED QUESTION NO. 396 FOR ANSWER ON 23.08.2004

(a) & (b): Prasar Bharati has informed that as on 16.08.2004 Doordarshan has outstanding dues amounting to Rs. 213.57 crore against various producers, marketing and advertising agencies. This figure does not include interest charges. The Prasar Bharati has taken following steps for recovery of dues: 
 

1.	The accreditation rule has been revised for the agencies and now the 
marketing agencies have to submit a bank guarantee for Rs. 25,00,000/-  

(Rupees Twenty Five Lakhs only) which was earlier for Rs. 3,00,000/- 

(Rupees Three Lakh only).
	 

2.	To secure Doordarshan`s revenue and to cover the credit period the bank 
guarantee amount for running serials has been enhanced to eight weeks of the 
telecast fee instead of six weeks.  In the case of high value events, 100% bank 
guarantee of the minimum assured revenue is taken. 


3.	Outstanding are monitored on monthly basis and regular reminders are sent to 
the agencies for the clearance of the outstanding dues.  Advance notices are 
being issued 15 days before the due date reminding the parties to pay their 
dues on due date. 


4.	No fresh programme/extension of programmes is being allowed to any 
defaulting agency/producer.  In order to ensure this, the status of the dues as 
on date is intimated to the department that allots/extends sponsored 
programmes. 

  

5.	Defaulting agencies are allowed to run their programmes only on advance 
payment of telecast fee.


6.	Agencies having outstanding have been asked to follow a payment plan to 
wipe off the arrears within a defined time frame.  Producers/agencies 
following a repayment plan are not allowed the normal credit period of sixty 
days.  


7	To recover the outstanding against the defaulting agencies, legal action has 
been initiated against several agencies.

records.name: Rajeev Shukla
records.qn_text:
(a) whether the recommendations of various Committees including Prakash Narain Committee on Railway accidents have Since been considered and action taken on them; and

(b) if so, the details thereof ?
records.ans_text:
MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF RAILWAYS

( SHRI R. VELU )

(a) & (b): A statement is attached.
STATEMENT REFERREDTO IN REPLY TO PARTS (a) & (b) OF UNSTARRED QUESTION NO. 1916 BY SHRI RAJEEV SHUKLA TO BE ANSWERED IN RAJYA SABHA ON 20-08-2004 REGARDING COMMITTEES ON RAILWAY ACCIDENTS.

(a) & (b): Between 1960 and 1980, three High Powered Committees viz. Railway Accidents Committee-1962 (Kunzru Committee), Railway Accidents Inquiry Committee - 1968 (Wanchoo Committee) and Railway :Accidents Enquiry Committee-1978 (Sikri Committee) went into the entire gamut of Railway working and suggested measures for improving the Railway Safety. Action for implementation of the accepted recommendations of these Committees was taken. Thereafter, Railway Safety Review Committee i.e RSRC (Kharma Committee) had been set up in 1998 to, inter alia review the position of accidents on the Indian Railways and to review the implementation of the recommendations made by the earlier Committees and to make their own recommendations. The Railway Safety Review Committee made a total of 278 recommendations in both the parts of its report. Of the 242 recommendations, which have been accepted fully or partially, 92 have already been implemented. Other accepted recommendations are at various stages of implementation depending upon the availability of resources. There was no Prakash Narain Committee on railway accidents. However, a National Transportation Safety Board had been set up in 1987 under the Cabinet Secretariat, with the main objective of bringing about improvements in safety in different transport sectors like Railways, Civil Aviation, Road Transport etc. This Board was wound up with effect from 1st April, 1990. Shri Prakash Narain was the Chairman of National Transportation Safety Board. After-winding up the National Transportation Safety Board some recommendations pertaining to Railways were communicated to the Ministry of Railways on which action as warranted was taken.

records.qtitle: (clubbed) FOREIGN POLICY WITH REGARD TO EAST
records.name: Vijay Mallya
records.qn_text:
(a) whether Government would consider evolution of a foreign policy for the East which will benefit the Eastern and North-Eastern States of the country;

(b) whether free trade among the Eastern Neighbouring Countries with India would be considered;

(c) whether any discussions have been held with the neighbouring countries in the East; and

(d) if so, the details thereof?
records.ans_text:
THE MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF EXTERNAL AFFAIRS

(SHRI E. AHAMED)

(a) to (d) Yes, Sir. Government has been taking into account the need to benefit the Eastern and North-Eastern states in pursuing foreign policy goals with neighbouring countries in the East bilaterally as well as multilaterally through the regional grouping, Bay of Bengal Initiative for Multi-Sectoral Technical and Economic Cooperation (BIMSTEC) consisting of India, Bangladesh, Bhutan, Myanmar, Nepal, Sri Lanka and Thailand.
The BIMSTEC Framework Agreement on Free Trade Area signed in October 2003 envisages FTA in goods, investment and services. For trade in services and investments, the negotiations shall commence in 2005 and are expected to be completed by 2007.
Bilaterally India already has a free trade regime with both Nepal and Bhutan. A framework FTA was signed with Thailand in October 2003 and an `Early Harvest Package` of 82 items will commence on September 1, 2004. India and Bangladesh are also exploring the possibility of signing an FTA on which two rounds of discussions have already been held. An agreement has been reached with China in June 2003 to set up a Joint Study Group composed of officials and economists to examine the potential complementarities between the two countries in expanded trade and economic cooperation, as well as the feasibility of an FTA between India and China.

records.name: Vijay Mallya
records.qn_text:
(a) whether it is a fact that he had led a delegation of Members of Parliament to the Eleventh Session of United Nations Conference on Trade and Development at Sao Paulo in Brazil recently;

(b) if so, the stand taken by Government on farm subsidies by the United States;

(c) whether the delegation had impressed upon the need for preferential treatment for developing countries; and

(d) if so, the details of the outcome of the conference and how far the same has been beneficial to the country?
records.ans_text:
MINISTER OF COMMERCE AND INDUSTRY

( SHRI KAMAL NATH )


(a) Yes, Sir.

(b) Farm subsidies by United States was not specifically on the agenda of UNCTAD XI Conference. However, the need for elimination of all export subsidies by developed countries was emphasized by us in our discussions. The negotiated text adopted by the Conference emphasized, among other things, the need for reductions of, with a view to phasing out, all forms of export subsidies, and substantial reductions in trade-distorting domestic support.

(c) Yes, Sir.

(d) A Statement is laid on the Table of the House.
STATEMENT REFERRED TO IN REPLY TO PART (d) OF THE RAJYA SABHA STARRED QUESTION NO 289 FOR 16th AUGUST 2004 REGARDING UNCTAD MEETING AT SAO PAULO

India along with other developing countries group known as G-77 and China, were successful in highlighting the concerns of developing countries under the multilateral trading system. India also participated in a G-20 meeting, along with countries such as Brazil, China, South Africa, Argentina etc., which was held in parallel to the UNCTAD deliberations. The main theme of the G-20 discussions was the need for preferential treatment for developing countries especially in the agricultural sector, in the on-going negotiations of the WTO. The developing countries succeeded in pointing out that the central issue of globalization should be development. It was also acknowledged that there is a need for policy space and policy flexibility for the development strategies of national Governments. It was decided that UNCTAD, which has provided an invaluable forum for advancing the inter-relationship between trade and development, from both the national and international perspective, across the three pillars of its mandate: independent policy analysis, technical assistance and consensus building, should continue its work and provide necessary inputs to the developing countries.

(b) to (e) Since 1981, the Government of Kamataka has been of the view that a Bench of the Kamataka high Court be established at Hubli-Dharwad. However, successive Chief Justices of the High Court have not so far endorsed the proposal. It is the policy of the Government of India that both the State Government and the High Court consider the matter from all angles and arrive at a consensus. As no complete proposal has been received from the Government of Karnataka, in consultation with the Chief Justice of Karnataka High Court, for establishing a Bench of the High Court in North Karnataka, it has not been possible for the Central Government to take a decision in the matter.

(d) whether any. study has. been prepared on. the costs and benefits of nuclear power expansion in the country; and

records.ans_text:
THE MINISTER OF STATE IN THE PRIME MINISTER`S OFFICE

(SHRI PRITHVIRAJ CHAVAN)

(a) to (e) A Statement is laid on the Table of the House.

DEPARTMENT OF ATOMIC ENERGY
STATEMENT REFERRED TO IN REPLY TO RAJYA SABHASTARRED Q.NO.258 FOR ANSWER ON 22/7/2004 BY DR. VIJAY MALLYA AND SHRI RAJEEV SHUKLA REGARDING NUCLEAR ENERGY.

(a) Government is considering all fuel options for meeting the increasing demands of energy of the country. Nuclear power is one such option.

(b) During the year 2003-04 the electricity generated from nuclear power was 17,861 Million Units (MUs). This is about 3.2% of the electricity generated by the utilities in the country.

(c) Yes, Sir. Government has approved setting up of nine nuclear power reactors, which are at various stages of construction. The completion cost of these projects is around Rs.29,500 crores.

(d) Yes, Sir. A Study on `Long term cost-effectiveness of nuclear energy` was carried out by NPCIL in 1998-99. This study has now been updated in June 2004 based on current inputs.

(e) The study evaluated generation cost of electricity produced by nuclear power vis-a-vis Thermal Power, as base load central generating stations. Factors such as cost of ~the project, financing cost, cost of fuels along with its transportation etc. were considered. The study suggests that the electricity from nuclear power at distances of about 800 kms from coal pit heads is a long term cost effective option.

records.name: Vijay Mallya
records.qn_text:
(a) whether Government are aware that only two per cent of the vegetables in the country are being processed at present as against 15-40 per cent in other countries;

(b) whether there is any proposal to reduce excise duty on processed foods to boost the demand for the products in the country;

(c) whether Government are contemplating to provide a supporting network of infrastructure of roads, electricity, transport and cold storage, etc. to the processed food sector; and

(d) if so, the steps being contemplated to organize the food processing industry on a modern and scientific basis to ensure quality and cost efficiency in the industry? ANSWER
records.ans_text:
THE MINISTER OF STATE OF THE MINISTRY OF FOOD PROCESSING INDUSTRIES

(SHRI SUBODH KANT SAHAI)



(a) to (d): A statement is laid on the table of the House.




Statement referred to in reply to Parts (a) to (d) of Rajya Sabha Starred Question No. 178 for 16th July, 2004 regarding processing of fruits & vegetables.


(a) & (b): Level of processing of fruits & vegetables is presently a little over 2% as against higher level of processing in certain other countries. Processed products of fruits & vegetables are already exempted from payment of excise duty. For promotion of upcoming agro processing units, the Government has announced on 8th July, 2004 in Parliament to allow under Income Tax Act, a deduction of 100% of profit for five years and 25% of profits for the next five years in case of new agro processing industries set up to process, preserve and package fruits & vegetables. Present excise duty of 16% on dairy machinery has been fully waived. Excise duty on meat, poultry and fish products has been reduced from 16% to 8%. Excise duty on food grade hexane used in edible oil has been reduced from 32% to 16%.

(c) & (d): In order to ensure better market orientation and make food processing units more cost-competitive, financial assistance @ 25% for general and 33.33% for difficult areas subject to maximum of Rs. 4.00 crore is sanctioned for establishment of food parks which provide common facilities such as uninterrupted power supply, water supply, cold storage/ice plant, warehousing facilities, affluent treatment plant, quality control and analytical laboratories, training/conference facilities etc. Financial assistance is also provided for establishment, modernization and expansion of food processing units @ 25% and 33.33% of costs of plant and machinery and technical civil works subject to a maximum of Rs. 50 lakhs and Rs. 75 lakhs in general and difficult areas respectively. For improvement of food quality/safety, financial assistance is provided to units/organizations to enable them to adopt bar coding practices, implement HACCP/ISO standards, set up quality control lab, codex cell, etc. Keeping in view the new approach and fresh thinking towards agro processing, the Government has planed to act vigorously as a catalyst agent to promote power arrangement and other networking facilities in food parks.

records.name: Vijay Mallya
records.qn_text:
(a) whether it is a fact that a Member of Planning Commission studied the problems faced by the Small Scale Industrial Sector;

(b) if so, what are the recommendations and what is Government`s approach towards these recommendations; and

(c) whether Government are ready to implement the recommendations, in order to address the problems of the Small Scale Industries?
records.ans_text:
MINISTER OF STATE FOR SMALL SCALE INDUSTRIES AND DEVELOPMENT OF NORTH-EASTERN REGION (SHRI TAPAN SIKDAR)

(a): Yes, Sir. Government had set up a Study Group under the Chairmanship of Dr. S. P. Gupta, Member Planning Commission to study the problems faced by the Small Scale Industries (SSI) Sector and make recommendations thereon.

(b) & (c): The recommendations of the Study Group inter-alia included a single comprehensive law for SSIs, continuation of policy of reservation with periodic reviews in the context of the changing economic scenario, easier access to credit, marketing support, technological upgradation, improved infrastructure etc. to enable the sector to face the challenges of globalization of economy and international competition. Government considered the recommendations and announced a Comprehensive Policy Package on 30th August 2000 to strengthen the SSI sector and enhance its competitiveness both domestically and globally, which included all major recommendations of the Study Group. The implementation of the package has gone a long way in addressing the concerns of the SSI Sector.

records.qtitle: ADDITIONAL AMBASSADOR LEVEL OFFICIAL AT INDIAN EMBASSY IN USA .
records.name: Rajeev Shukla
records.qn_text:
(a) whether in addition to the Indian Ambassador in USA, another official of the same rank is operating in USA:

(b) if so, what specific role has been assigned to him particularly in regard to NRIs and Persons of Indian Origin (PIOs) in the USA: and

(c) the details of the action already taken and proposed to be taken by him in this regard?
records.ans_text:
THE MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF EXTERNAL AFFAIRS (SHRI VINOD KHANNA)

a) There is only one official designated as the Ambassador of India to USA. However, two officers are designated in the rank of `Ambassador` for functional reasons, which includes Permanent Representative of India to UN, New York, and Special Adviser to the Permanent Mission of India and Ambassador-at-Large to NRIs/PIOs based in New York.

b) The Government of India appointed Ambassador-at-Large (AAL) for Non-Resident Indians(NRIs) and Persons of Indian Origin (PIOs), with the aim to strategically promote better coordination within the NRI/PIO community as well as economic cooperation, investment and commerce by NRIs/PIOs with India and other countries.

c) The mandate of Ambassador-at-Large for NRIs & PIOs is global and not limited to USA. Action taken and to be taken by his office, inter-alia include:-

(i) Visits to the countries with large diaspora presence to establish contact and network with various Indian organizations.

(ii) Preparation of reports giving suggestions/proposals/ recommendations and organization of meetings and workshops covering youth and students, enhancement of India`s image in the ethnic media, inter-religious meet, Indo-Caribbean leadership forum and youth and diaspora students etc. A number of workshops in these areas are in the offing.

(iii) Functioning of a Grievances and Complaints Cell which attends to more than 1000 queries per month from all over the globe pertaining to diaspora issues, seeking information and Consular complaints.

(iv) Managing a website which provides NRI/PIO related information and about the services provided by AAL`s office.

(v) Organization of a Public Meeting for the Prime Minister with Indo-American community in September, 2003. More than 4000 participated in the meeting.

(vi) Promotion of Pravasi Bharatiya Divas (PBD)-2003 and PBD-2004 for large scale diaspora participation.

(vii) Providing support and interaction base to visiting VIPs, Members of Parliament, State and Central Ministers with the NRI segment in socio-cultural, investment and other areas.

records.qtitle: (clubbed) INDIA FOR NEW ALLIANCES WITH ASEAN AND OTHER COUNTRIES
records.name: Vijay Mallya
records.qn_text:
(a) whether in view of the failure of the WTO Ministerial Conference at Cancun and the threat issued by the US of bypassing WTO for bilateral trading arrangements, Government are contemplating to forge new alliances with ASEAN and other countries such as China, South Korea, Japan etc.;

(c) the details of steps taken in this regard?
records.ans_text:
THE MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF COMMERCE AND INDUSTRY

records.name: Rajeev Shukla
records.qn_text:
(a) the nature of assistance provided to Indian workers in foreign countries once they are in distress; and

records.ans_text:
MINISTER OF STATE FOR LABOUR AND PARLIAMENTARY AFFAIRS

(SHRI SANTOSH GANGWAR)

(a): Indian workers in distress abroad are provided temporary relief for meeting their financial needs in times of extreme difficulty. They are also assisted in their repatriation. Additionally, some Indian Missions/Posts abroad, particularly in the Gulf region, also operate Labour Welfare Funds with the assistance of the Indian community to cater to the needs of distressed workers.

(b): Such data is not maintained.

records.name: ABRAR AHMED
records.qn_text:
(a) whether the workload of postmen have been drastically reduced with the introduction of e-mail and FAX services;

(b) whether any survey has been done in this regard; and

(c) if so, the details thereof?
records.ans_text:
THE MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF COMMUNICATIONS AND INFORMATION TECHNOLOGY (SHRI SU. THIRUNAVUKKARASAR)

(a) The workload of Postmen has not come down drastically because of introduction of e-Mail and FAX services. The workload of existing postmen staff has increased in many offices due to expansion of delivery areas. In addition, the postmen staff are undertaking additional work like picking up of articles for booking from customers` premises for customers` conveniences.

(b) & (c): No survey as such has been conducted to find out the impact of introduction of e-Mail and FAX services on workload of postmen staff.

records.qtitle: (clubbed) FRESH INFUSION OF CAPITAL INTO LIC

(b) whether it is also a fact that the LIC is in urgent need of infusion of fresh capital to maintain its solvency, and if so, how much;

(c) whether Government propose to restructure the Corporation to face the competition from the private insurance companies; and

(d) if so, what are the details thereof?
records.ans_text:
MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF FINANCE SHRI ANANDRAO V. ADSUL

(a) The Life Insurance Corporation of India (LIC) continue to maintain its predominate position even after the sector was opened for private players. As on 31.3.2003, the overall share of LIC in terms of the number of new policies procured stands at 96.70% whereas all the private life insurance companies put together have only 3.30% of market share.

(b): No, Sir.

(c): No, Sir.

(d): Does not arise.

records.name: Rajeev Shukla
records.qn_text:
(a) whether upgradation of major metro airports in India to world class standards was one of the mandates given by the Task Force on Infrastructure, set up by the Prime Minister in 1998; and

(b) if so, the details of progress made by the Ministry of Civil Aviation from 1998 till date in this respect?
records.ans_text:
MINISTER OF STATE OF THE MINISTRY OF CIVIL AVIATION ( SHRI RAJIV PRATAP RUDY )
(a):- Yes Sir. (b):- The Task Force on Infrastructure on 9.12.1998 recommended that airports at Delhi, Mumbai and Bangalore be corporatised. Based on this recommendation, Government of India in January, 1999 decided to corporatise the airports at Delhi, Mumbai, Chennai and Kolkota, besides construction of Greenfield Airports at Bangalore. Considering the complexitites involved in corporatisation, the Task Force on 3.6.1999 approved the leasing route. Government of India in Janurary, 2000 approved restructuring of airports of Airports Authority of India through long term leasing route as and when found suitable. The airports at Delhi, Mumbai, Kolkota and Chennai were taken up for this exercise at the first instance. The Financial Consultant and Legal Consultant for restructuring exercise were appointed in March, 2000 and March, 2001 respectively. An Inter-Ministerial Group(IMG) was constituted to advise and monitor the entire exercise. The IMG met periodically to discuss and deliberate on various strategic issues. Pre-Investment Meets were held in New Delhi and London in April, 2002 to formally introduce the long term lease process. The Meet was attended by many Airport Operators, Financial Companies etc. An Amendment Bill was introduced in the Parliament on 30.11.2000 for incorporating and enabling provision in the Airports Authority of India (AAI) Act, 1994 providing for leasing of airports. The Bill was referred to the Department Related Standing Committee on Transport, Tourism and Culture. The Committee tabled its report on 21.11.2002. As per the recommendations of the Committee, a comprehensive Airports Authority of India (Amendment) Bill, 2003 was introduced in the Parliament. The Bill was passed by Lok Sabha and Rajya Sabha on 9.5.2003 and 28.7.2003 respectively. Meanwhile, the restructuring through Joint Venture route was also considered. The Hon`ble Finance Minister, in Budget Speech 2003-04 has inter-alia announced that in addition to the existing initiatives for leasing of major airports, the Delhi and Mumbai airports will be taken up for modernisation to international standards through formation of two Joint Venture companies. Steps have been taken for incorporation of two separate companies for Delhi and Mumbai airports. The transaction structure is being finalised in consultation with Ministry of Finance.

records.qtitle: NEW CONVENTION AND EXHIBITION CENTRE AT MUMBAI .
records.name: Rajeev Shukla
records.qn_text:
(a) whether during the 68th Board meeting of Airports Authority of India, held on 14th July, 2003, it was decided to form a Public Limited Company for setting up of International level Convention and Exhibition Centre at Mumbai Airport; and

(b) if so, the details and the justification thereof?
records.ans_text:
MINISTER OF STATE OF THE MINISTRY OF CIVIL AVIATION ( SHRI RAJIV PRATAP RUDY )
(a) :- Yes, Sir. (b) :- An International Convention Centre is proposed to be set up at Mumbai by a Joint Venture Company with participation by five star hoteliers of Mumbai and Airports Authority of India. The proposal is in the context of the announcement in the Budget Speech for the year 2003-04 wherein the Government propose to provide a major thrust to infrastructure through innovative funding mechanisms. The comprehensive initiative will inter-alia include two global standard international convention centres.

records.name: Rajkumar Dhoot
records.qn_text:
(a) whether it is a fact that Government propose to launch an unmanned spaceship to moon;

(b) if so, the purpose and the cost involved in this venture; and

(c) what is the urgency for such a venture when a lot of developmental activities are held up for want of funds and what public interest and removal of poverty are going to be served by such a venture?
records.ans_text:
MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF PLANNING, MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF STATISTICS AND PROGRAMME IMPLEMENTATION, MINISTER OF STATE IN THE DEPARTMENT OF ATOMIC ENERGY, MINISTER OF STATE IN THE DEPARTMENT OF SPACE AND MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF COMMERCE AND INDUSTRY (ADDITIONAL CHARGE) (SHRI S.B. MOOKHERJEE):

(a) In consonance with the mandate of Indian Space Research Organisation for research in space sciences and based on the interest of the scientific community, an unmanned spacecraft mission around moon has been planned.

(b) The main purpose of the mission is to study the hitherto unexplored aspects of the moon and to expand the horizon of our scientific knowledge and also to upgrade our technological capability. The cost of the mission is presently estimated to be Rs.386.00 crores.

(c) Such a deep space mission would throw-up challenges to our vision and scientific knowledge and upgrade our technological capabilities. Moon can be the outpost for further planetary exploration. The technological up-gradation involved in this mission would provide several spin-offs in the areas of mineral prospecting, power generation, communication systems, etc.

records.name: Rajeev Shukla
records.qn_text:
(a) whether it is a fact that Prime Minister met Heads of Germany, China and Russia during his visit abroad during May-June this year;

(b) If so, the details of the subject matters discussed and their response thereto; and

(c) what has been their stand on the cross border terrorism by Pakistan and the Kashmir issue?
records.ans_text:
THE MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF EXTERNAL AFFAIRS
(SHRI DIGVIJAY SINGH)


(a) Prime Minister had bilateral meetings with Mr. Gerhard Schroedar, German Chancellor on 28th May, 2003, in Berlin, Mr. Vladimir Putin, President of the Russian Federation on 30 May, 2003 in St. Petersburg and with Mr. Hu Jintao, President of the People`s Republic of China on May 31, 2003 in St. Petersburg;

(b) During his visit to Germany, PM held wide ranging discussions with the German leadership on bilateral relations and on regional and international issues of mutual interest.




In his meeting with President Putin, Prime Minister discussed issues of bilateral, regional and international interest. The two leaders agreed that in accordance with the strategic partnership between the two countries, the extensive consultations between them should be continued. President Putin reiterated Russia`s commitment to further deepen defence relations with India. The two leaders agreed that there should a UN role in Iraq.
In the meeting with President Jintao, Prime Minister`s then forthcoming visit to China, global peace, stability, bilateral relations, situation in Iraq, role of the UN and PM`s initiative with respect to Pakistan were discussed. Both leaders agreed that China and India shouldered major responsibility for promoting world peace and stability, authority of the UN needed to be further strengthened and our Missions to UN should stay in touch regarding this and on Iraq. President Hu expressed confidence that PM`s visit to China would promote constructive and cooperative partnership. PM underlined the need for developing bilateral relations based on the Panchsheel and mutual sensitivity to each other`s concerns to resolve our differences.

(c) His interlocutors in Germany were sensitized to our concerns on the need for an immediate cessation of cross-border terrorism. There was unanimous appreciation for Prime Minister`s peace initiative.
Russia has repeatedly stated that cross-border terrorism should be ended and that the Kashmir issue should be settled bilaterally between India and Pakistan in accordance with the Simla Agreement and the Lahore Declaration.
Chinese President complimented and congratulated the Prime Minister of India on his peace initiative with respect to Pakistan. He said that the Chinese government supported any initiative to ease the situation and hoped that India and Pakistan would resolve their differences through dialogue and by peaceful means to make the situation in South Asia peaceful.

records.qtitle: U.S. EFFORTS TO STOP CROSS BORDER TERRORISM IN INDIA .
records.name: Rajeev Shukla
records.qn_text:
(a) whether it is a fact that USA President took up the issue of cross border terrorism with Pakistan President Pervez Musharraf during June, 2003;

(b) if so, the details thereof; and

(c) whether Government are satisfied with the outcome of the USA efforts and optimistic of positive response from Pakistan?
records.ans_text:
THE MINISTER OF STATE R IN THE MINISTRY OF EXTERNAL AFFAIRS

(SHRI DIGVIJAY SINGH)

(a) & (b) Yes. The United States has repeatedly stated that it continues to press President Musharraf to end infiltration and take action on terrorist camps. At the joint press briefing after his Camp David summit with President Musharraf on 24 June 2003, President Bush stated, ` we discussed the need to address extremism and cross-border infiltration`. A senior U.S. official also stated at a press briefing on 24 June 2003, `we expect and what we think Musharraf needs to commit to and we think he has committed to is a hundred percent effort at trying to stop cross-border incidents`.

(c) Government has noted statements by the United States in this regard. Cross-border infiltration and terrorist attacks in Jammu and Kashmir continue.

records.name: Rajeev Shukla
records.qn_text:

(b) if so, the reasons therefor; and

(c) whether there is no scope for diversification or expansion of SAIL to absorb the surplus staff?
records.ans_text:
MINISTER OF STATE (SHRI BRAJA KISHORE TRIPATHY) IN THE MINISTRY OF STEEL

(a)&(b): Based on a study, the size of Steel Authority of India Limited`s manpower was found to be in excess of its requirement which affected its competitiveness and hence profitability. Accordingly, SAIL drew up a programme in the year 2000 for a phased reduction in its manpower. During 2003-2004, 10,000 employees are sought to be reduced through a Voluntary Retirement Scheme as well as superannuation and other separations.

(c) No such scope exists.

records.qtitle: (clubbed) FINANCIAL IRREGULARITIES IN CSIR AND DBT .
records.name: Vijay Mallya
records.qn_text:
(a) whether the Audit Report for the year 2003 by the Comptroller and Auditor General of India has brought out several financial and other irregularities in the functioning of organizations such as CSIR and Department of Bio-technology ;

(b) if so, the details thereof ;

(c) whether Government have already taken action or propose to take action to rectify the situation ; and

(d) whether any responsibility has been fixed/proposed to be fixed on the persons found guilty of indulging in financial and other irregularities ?
records.ans_text:
MINISTER OF STATE FOR SCIENCE AND TECHNOLOGY

(BACHI SINGH RAWAT)

(a)&(b) In the case of CSIR & DBT the CAG report for the year 2003 has brought out some cases of non-achievements of objectives, unfruitful expenditure, delay in project monitoring & delays in technology transfer, non receipt of technology fee etc.

(c)&(d) The issues raised in the CAG report have been addressed by CSIR & DBT. In the case of CSIR the same were conveyed through the mechanism of the action taken notes. These in turn are being monitored, by the CAG. DBT, in addition, has also highlighted the fact that in scientific departments 100% achievement of the objectives is difficult to predict at the project sanction stage.

records.name: Rajeev Shukla
records.qn_text:
(a) whether it is a fact that the avenues for employment are shrinking and the number of unemployed and semi-employed persons are soaring over the years;

(b) the generation of employment opportunities planned in different categories during the period 2003-04 and 2004-05;

(c) what has been and what is likely to be the impact of cut in jobs in Government PSUs, divestment in PSUs and closure of industrial units in creating new job opportunities; and

(d) whether Government have set any target to provide employment to every eligible citizen of the country?
records.ans_text:
MINISTER OF LABOUR

(SHRI SAHIB SINGH VERMA)

a) to d) A Statement is laid on the Table of the House.
STATEMENT REFERRED TO IN REPLY TO THE RAJYA SABHA STARRED QUESTION NO.268 BY SHRI RAJEEV SHUKLA AND SHRI RAJKUMAR DHOOT REGARDING UNEMPLOYMENT PROBLEM FOR REPLY ON 7.8.2003.

Estimates of employment and unemployment are obtained through quinquennial labour force surveys conducted by National Sample Survey Organistion. Last such survey was conducted during 1999-2000. As per these surveys, estimated employment in the country on usual status basis has gone up from approximately 374 million in 1993-94 to 397 million in 1999-2000. Number of unemployed during 1993-94 and 1999-2000 was approximately 75 lakh and 90 lakh respectively. The Special Group headed by Dr. S.P.Gupta, Member, Planning Commission has recommended strategy and programmes which have been considered while formulating the 10th Plan, for targeting creation of 50 million employment opportunities (10 million per year) during the 10th Plan period (2002-2007). It identified the activities where there is a major potential of large new job opportunities as in agriculture, including social forestry, animal husbandry, fishing, horticulture and related areas and small and medium industries, construction, tourism, information technology, financial sector, education and health. The special Group has felt that with the target of achieving 10 million jobs per year, it will be possible to achieve near full employment situation by the end of 2012. Organised Sector constitutes about 7% of the total employment in the country. Loss of jobs, if any ,in Public Sector Undertakings (PSU`s), disinvested PSU`s and industrial units, may not have any significant effect on total employment in the country.

(b) if so, the details thereof; and

(c) whether Government propose to set up a Committee to consider this problem?
records.ans_text:
MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF URBAN DEVELOPMENT & POVERTY ALLEVIATION

( SHRI PON RADHAKRISHNAN )

(a)&(b): DDA has reported that the surrender of some flats may be a consequence of free market conditions in housing sectors and the growth of satellite cities in the National Capital Region, which have resulted in providing wider options to the allottees. (c) if so, the details thereof?
records.ans_text:

(SHRI SHRIPAD YESSO NAIK)

records.qtitle: (clubbed) SIMPLIFYING PROCEDURE FOR ISSUE OF PASSPORTS .
records.name: ABRAR AHMED
records.qn_text:
(a) whether it is a fact that police verification of applicants is one of the major reasons causing delay in the issuing of passports to them in a stipulated period: and

records.ans_text:

records.name: SHABANA AZMI
records.qn_text:
(a) whether UNESCO, which was initially optimistic about India`s claims of total literacy by decade-end, has now started expressing reservations;

(b) if so, whether a recent report of the UN body says universal elementary education may elude the country even around 2015, five years after the Government`s deadline;

(c) if so, what were the main reasons put forward by them; and

(d) what steps Government propose to take to see that India achieves literacy target by 2015?
records.ans_text:
THE MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF HUMAN RESOURCE DEVELOPMENT

(DR. SANJAY PASWAN)

(a) to (c) UNESCO has brought out a EFA Global Monitoring Report, 2002 in which India has been shown at serious risk of missing the EFA goals of Universal Primary Education and Total Literacy by 2015. The conclusions drawn in this Report are based on data available to UNESCO on the parameters of net enrolment ratio in primary schools, gender parity as per gross enrolment ratio in primary schools and the percentage of adult literacy. The data used by UNESCO for these parameters were either outdated or not available to UNESCO as far as India is concerned. Further, initiatives taken in the recent years like launch of Sarva Shiksha Abhiyan and restructuring of literacy programmes have not been taken into account for arriving at the conclusions.

(b) The initiatives of the Government for achieving the literacy target include:-
1) The Sarva Shiksha Abhiyan (SSA) to achieve universalization of elementary education.
The objectives of SSA are: 
-   All  children  in  school, Education Guarantee  Centre,
Alternate School, `Back-to-School` camp by 2003


-   All children complete five years of primary schooling by
2007


-   All children complete eight years of elementary schooling
by 2010


-   Focus on elementary education of satisfactory quality with
emphasis on education for life


-   Bridge  all gender and social category gaps at primary
stage by 2007 and at elementary education level by 2010


-   Universal retention by 2010


2)  The  literacy schemes of the National Literacy Mission (NLM)
have  been  restructured to achieve continuity,  efficiency
and  convergence  in  the implementation  of  the  Literacy
Campaigns  and  expansion in the scope  of  the  Continuing
Education programme.


3) NLM aims to achieve a sustainable threshold level of 75%
literacy by 2007.
