-

(a) the names of nationalised banks which are without CMDs at present;

(b) whether a number of new CMDs are likely to be appointed in the near future; and

(c) if so, the procedure/ Criteria/ guidelines laid down for appointing new CMDs?
records.ans_text:
FINANCE MINISTER (SHRI JASWANT SINGH)

(a),(b) and (c):- A statement is placed on the Table of the House.

STATEMENT REFERRED TO PARTS (a), (b) &(c) of RAJYA SABHA STARRED QUESTION N0.25 FOR 22nd JULY. 2003 REGARDING BANKS WITHOUT CMDs BY SHRI RAJEEV SHUKLA AND DR. ABRAR AHMED

a) Currently the posts of Chairmen and Managing Director in Allahabad Bank and Bank of India are lying vacant.

b) The anticipated vacancies of Chairmen and Managing Director of Nationalised Banks upto 31.3.2004 are :-

I) CMD, Andhra Bank w.e.f. 1.11.2003
ii) CMD, Dena Bank w.e.f. 1.1.2004
iii) CMD, United Bank of India w.e.f. 1.3.2004

(c) Appointment of CMDs in the Nationalised Banks are made in accordance with the provisions of Section 9(3) of the Banking Companies (Acquisition and Transfer of Undertakings) Act 1970/1980. Government have, in addition, constituted an Appointments Board under the Chairmanship of Governor, Reserve Bank of India , Officials of Ministry of Finance and two outside experts to consider eligible candidates and to make appropriate recommendations. These recommendations of the Appointments Board are then considered by the Government for final approval. Appropriate criteria and procedure are laid down by the Appointments Board, from time to time. Copies of these criteria laid down in October, 2000, and in November, 2002 are enclosed at Annexures I and II respectively. 

ANNEXURE-I


RELEVANT EXTRACTS FROM THE MINUTES OF THE MEETING OF THE APPOINTMENTS BOARD HELP IN RBL 
NEW DELHI ON 11th  OCTOBER, 2000
Agenda Item No.2 Procedure for appointment of Whole time Directors in Public Sector Banks
The Appointments Board recognized the need for providing for a reasonable tenure for Whole 
Time Directors in public sector banks in order to ensure that the bank gets the benefit of 
continuity in leadership in an era of increasing competition along with a fair method of 
selection based on merit with due consideration to seniority, for maintaining the morale 
and motivation of employees. The issue of residual service for Chief Executive in an 
institution matters a lot, as a chief Executive with very short tenure implies lack of 
long-term commitment and vision and gaps in formulation and implementation of the long-term
policy for the organisation. It was also felt that the whole issue of Corporate Governance, 
which inter alia prescribes autonomy with accountability of the top management necessarily
demands a minimum reasonable tenure for Chief Executives, which will avoid uncertainty and 
ensure continuity of policy.
The Appointments Board also noted that the introduction of a procedure prescribing a minimum
tenure for appointment of whole time director will give rise to super-session of a few persons
with excellent record for the top position on ground of their residual service being less than 
the minimum prescribed. However, the situation of super-session of otherwise qualified and 
competent persons will emerge at any time, when a transition from merit-cum-seniority procedure
to tenure-oriented procedure is made. It was recognized that this may




create resentment among some persons and may impinge on building organisational teams at
higher levels.


The Appointments Board also recognized that the procedure for prescribing minimum tenure
for whole time directors in State Bank of India (SBI) keeping in view its special status, 
large size and trained and skilled manpower, may be somewhat different from the one which may 
be followed for the nationalised banks. Keeping in view the constraints of public sector 
character of these banks and the existing guidelines of Department of Personnel & Training,
the Appointments Board suggested that the following system may be followed by the Board while 
considering candidates for appointment as whole-time directors on the Boards of public sector
banks:-


a)   For Chairman & Managing Director of SBI - a minimum residual service of two years from 
the date the vacancy arises.


b)   For Managing Director of SBI - a minimum residual service of one year from the date the 
vacancy arises.


c)   For Chairman and Managing Director of Nationalised Banks - All persons with minimum 
residual service of two years as on 1st April of the financial year in which vacancy arises 
will be considered. However, it should be kept in view that the person who is recommended for
a particular nationalised bank should as far as feasible, have at least two years of service
in the concerned bank.


d)   For Executive Directors of Nationalised Banks - A minimum residual service of two years as
on Ist April of the concerned financial year shall be considered for the purpose of calling
people for interview.......`



Annexure-II


RELEVANT EXTRACTS FROM THE MINUTES OF THE MEETING OF THE APPOINTMENTS BOARD HELD IN RBI, 
NEW DELHI ON 25th NOVEMBER, 2002
`Agenda Item No.2 Appointment of CMDs of Nationalised Banks
The Board noted that the past practice has been to appoint CMDs from the existing Executive
Directors of nationalised banks based on seniority. The Board felt that the CMD being the 
head of the bank must be dynamic, possess leadership qualities and executive ability. The 
Board decided that a Committee comprising of Shri S. Narayan, Finance Secretary, Ms. Vineeta
Rai, Secretary (B&I), Dr. P. Kotaiah, Banking Expert and Prof. Abad Ahmed, Management Expert
may have interactions with the Executive Directors who have put in at least one year service 
as ED and with at least two years of service remaining as on 1st April, 2003 and recommend 
suitable names for appointment as CMDs for all the vacancies arising during the financial year 
1st April 2003 to 31st March, 2004. The Board further decided that the Government may separately
decide whether to confine selection of future vacancies to the existing Executive Director or
whether to widen the scope of selection by inviting applications from suitable professionals/
candidates through advertisement from the open market.   Government may consider granting a 
compensation package to be offered to an open market candidate in order to attract best 
available talent. It was noted that the past experience of attracting outside candidates for 
top public sector positions at present salary levels was not every encouraging.

records.qn_text:
(a) whether the National Commission on Population has suggested restrategising the policies and programmes relating to population stabilisation in the country; and

(b) if so, the details thereof?
records.ans_text:
MINISTER OF HEALTH AND FAMILY WELFARE AND PARLIAMENTARY AFFAIRS

(SMT. SUSHMA SWARAJ)

(a)&(b): A statement is laid on the Table of the House.
STATEMENT REFERRED TO IN REPLY TO RAJYA SABHA STARRED QUESTION NO. 8 FOR 21ST JULY, 2003 ......

(a)&(b): Yes, Sir. The implementation of the Family Welfare Programme was reviewed jointly by the Department of Family Welfare and the National Commission on Population in August, 2001. The present level of use of different types of contraceptives, the couple protection rate and the financial and physical achievements, the need for area-specific plans in the high fertility areas and the necessity for involving Panchayati Raj Institutions, NGOs and self-help groups in service delivery were also discussed. Other important areas were as follows:
Importance of meeting the unmet needs for contraception Registration of births, deaths and marriages to be considered for inclusion as a plan scheme. Extension of ICDS programme through the Anganwadi Workers in improving the nutritional status of pregnant women and children. Special focus on improvement in the implementation of Family Welfare Programs in the States of Uttar Pradesh, Bihar, Rajasthan and Madhya Pradesh, so as to reach the goals set out in the National Population Policy (NPP) 2000. Mechanisms to be evolved for public and private participation in order to fill in the infrastructure gaps to increase the outreach and the better utilisation of RCH and Family Planning services. Treating motivational and promotional measures in NPP, 2000, as the basis for promoting the small family norm. Need for decentralised planning and programme implementation .....

records.name: Rajeev Shukla
records.qn_text:
(a) whether it is a fact that Pure Science is losing popularity among students as a subject of higher education as opined by Prof. C.N.R. Rao in a recent newspaper article;

(b) if so, the main reasons for it; and

(c) what steps are being contemplated to encourage youth to take to Pure Science?
records.ans_text:
MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF HUMAN RESOURCE DEVELOPMENT

(DR. VALLABHBHAI KATHIRIA)

(a) to (c) : According to the information furnished by the University Grants Commission (UGC) there has been a slight decline in enrolment in Science subjects at undergraduate level. This is due to the fact that unlike in the past, now there are several options available for the youth to select courses from amongst job oriented professional and I.T degree courses. However, the data available with UGC shows slight increase in students enrolment in postgraduate courses in various subjects like Physics, Chemistry, Mathematics, Botany, Zoology. The UGC is promoting higher education/research in pure science by providing assistance to university departments/colleges under various schemes like Special Assistance Programme/Strengthening of Infrastructure in Science and Engineering/Technology, etc. Teachers are encourage to undertake projects (Major/Minor) in different areas. The UGC has initiated a scheme of National Lecturer as per which toppers in science subjects are eligible for lectureship.

records.name: Rajeev Shukla
records.qn_text:
(a) Whether it is a fact that the Portuguese legal authorities have told their Government that Abu Salem wanted in connection with 1993 Mumbai blasts can be deported to India;

(b) If so, how India is going to secure the return of Salem in the absence of an extradition treaty with Lisbon; and

(c) the details of the procedure to get around the legal requirements of an Extradition Treaty?
records.ans_text:
THE MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF EXTERNAL AFFAIRS

(SHRI VINOD KHANNA)


(a) Request for extradition of Abu Salem, who was arrested in Portugal in 2002 on the basis of an Interpol Red Corner Alert, is under consideration of the Portuguese authorities.


(b)&(c) Absence of Extradition Treaty does not bar consideration of an extradition request. In view of friendly relations with India, Portugal agreed to consider India`s request for extradition of Abu Salem under its domestic laws.

records.qtitle: REPORT OF TASK FORCE FOR WASTELAND WATERSHED DEVELOPMENT .

(b) if so, the main recommendations of the report?
records.ans_text:
MINISTER OF STATE FOR RURAL DEVELOPMENT (SHRI ANNASAHEB M.K, PATIL)

(a) & (b) No Task Force has been constituted for wastelands/watershed development in the Department of Land Resources, Ministry of Rural Development. records.name: ABRAR AHMED
records.qn_text:
(a) whether water contamination has led to high levels of lead, copper and zinc in vegetables grown and sold in Delhi and some other parts of the country;

(b) whether such vegetables are injurious to public health;

(c) the steps Government have taken to check the menace?
records.ans_text:
THE MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF HEALTH AND FAMILY WELFARE

(SHRI A. RAJA)

(a): A study was carried out at Delhi and Varanasi by Imperial College, London in partnership with
(i) Shrshti; Delhi University;
(ii) Banaras Hindu University, Varanasi;
(ii) Development Tracks, New Delhi and
(iv) Indian Agriculture Research Institute to assess the level of heavy metals in vegetables and to develop simple techniques, which could reduce heavy metal from these vegetables.
The studies revealed that vegetables crop are often grown in polluted and degraded environmental condition in the urban fringe zone and are subject to further pollution from vehicles and industries during marketing. The outcome of the studies in brief are as follows :-
`Fresh vegetables samples of cauliflower, okra, spinach were found to contain heavy metals higher than the permissible limits, as defined by PFA Act, 1954`.
A proportion of heavy metals in spinach samples were present on the surface of the leaves. After one washing 20 percent contamination is reduced and after second wash, it is reduced by approximately 50 percent.

(b) & (c): Regular intake of higher amount of metals in diet are injurious to health. There is a need to educate the farmers to adopt Good Agricultural Practices for production of crops including integrated pest management.
-

records.name: Rajeev Shukla
records.qn_text:
(a) what are the main reasons for continuous decline in India`s textile exports; and

(b) the steps taken by Government to boost its export ?
records.ans_text:
THE MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF TEXTILES SHRI BASANAGOUDA R. PATIL (YATNAL)

(a) The textile exports had recorded a growth of 10.1% in 1999-2000 and 14.6% in 2000-2001, but shown a negative growth of 11.0% in 2001-2002.
The major reason for negative growth of textile exports during the year 2001-02 were the reduced global demand triggered by the slowdown in the economies of some of our major trading partners like US, increasing polarization of world trade, formation of preferential trading blocks and stiff competition from low cost suppliers like Bangladesh, China, etc.
As per the available DGCIS export data, the textile exports during the period April-December 2002 have amounted to US$ 8849.4 million which when compared with the exports of US$ 7814.6 million during the corresponding period of 2001 show a growth of 13.2%. This indicates the downtrend in textile exports has been reversed and they are back on path of export growth.

(b) Government have been taking a number of measures to boost textile exports. Some of the important initiatives are:-

(i) The Government has de-reserved the woven segment of readymade garment from the SSI sector. It has also raised the SSI investment limit for knitted segment to Rs. 5 crores.

(ii) The Technology Upgradation Fund Scheme (TUFS) has been made operational from 1-4-1999 to facilitate the modernisation and upgradation of the sector.

(iii) Weaving, processing and garment machinery, which are covered under TUFS, have been extended the facility of accelerated depreciation at the rate of 50%. Cost of machinery has also been reduced through Fiscal Policy measures. This further encourages modernisation.

(iv) With a view to encouraging backward integration, the custom duty on shuttleless looms and other important textile machinery items has been brought down to 5%.

(v) National Institute for Fashion Technology (NIFT), its six branches and Apparel Training & Design Centres (ATDCs) are running various courses/programmes to meet skilled manpower requirements of textile industry especially apparel in the field of design, merchandising and marketing.

(vi) Facilities by way of eco-testing laboratories have been created to enable exporters to get the garments/textiles pre-tested for conforming to the requirements of importing countries.

(vii) The Government has launched a centrally sponsored scheme titled `Apparel Park for Export Scheme` for imparting focused thrust for setting up of apparel manufacturing units of international standards at potential growth centres and to give fillip to exports.

(viii) For upgrading infrastructure facilities at important textile centers, a scheme `Textile Centre Infrastructure Development Scheme (TCIDS) has been launched.

records.name: ABRAR AHMED
records.qn_text:
(a) whether the manpower and modernisation requirements of Delhi Police, as recommended by Bureau of Police Research and Development have been fully met; and

(b) if so, the details thereof?
records.ans_text:
MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF HOME AFFAIRS AND MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF PERSONNEL, PUBLIC GRIEVANCES AND PENSIONS (SHRI HARIN PATHAK)


(a ) & (b): The Government have identified the following areas which need to be strengthened on priority in the first phase of implementation of the recommendations made by the Bureau of Police Research & Development:

(a) Upgradation of training facilities;

(b) Computerization at Police Station level;

(c) Modernization of Delhi Traffic Police;

(d) Upgradation of communication network;

(e) Separation of crime investigation from law & order functions at Police Station level by creation of dedicated teams of investigating officers;

(f) Setting up of Metro Rail Police Station and a Police Post; and

(g) Miscellaneous proposals of modernization including modernization of weaponry.

records.name: Rajeev Shukla
records.qn_text:
(a) what is the present strength of Members of National Integration Council;

(b) when the last meeting of NIC was held;

(c) the reasons for not calling a single meeting of NIC by the present NDA Government; and

(d) by when Government propose to call a meeting of NIC?
records.ans_text:
MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF HOME AFFAIRS

(SHRI I.D. SWAMI)

(a)&(b): The last meeting of National Integration Council (NIC) was held on 23.11.1992. At that time there were 147 Members of the NIC.

(c)&(d): The reconstitution of NIC is under consideration of the Government at the moment and the meeting of NIC would be convened thereafter.

records.name: Rajeev Shukla
records.qn_text:
(a) the number of Co-operative Banks operating in the country without requisite licence from Reserve Bank of India as on date;

(b) whether the matter of such unauthorized banks has been taken with concerned State Governments; and

(c) if so, the details thereof?
records.ans_text:
(Minister of Finance & Company Affairs) (Shri Jaswant Singh) `(a), (b) & (c): A Statement is placed on the Table of the House.
Statement laid on the Table of the Rajya Sabha in reply to parts (a), (b) & (c) of Starred Question No. 557 for 29th April. 2003 tabled by Shri Rajeev Shukla and Dr. Abrar Ahmed regarding Co-operative Banks without licennce.

(a), (b) & (c): As reported by Reserve Bank of India (RBI) and National Bank for Agriculture & Rural Development (NABARD), at present there are 17 State Cooperative Banks (SCBs), 296 District Central Co-operative Banks (DCCBs) and 112 Urban Co-operative Banks (UCBs) are operating in the country without licence from Reserve Bank of India (RBI). Since Co-operative Banks were brought under the ambit of Banking Regulation Act 1949 from 1st March, 1966, these Banks are permitted to carry on banking business till a decision is taken on their licence applications by RBI. In respect of the Banks which are likely to comply with the licence norms in the near future/ RBI has considered it advisable to give time to do the needful. Apart from these, there are 58 co-operative societies (54 in Kerala, 1 in Assam and 3 in Manipur) carrying on banking business without licence from RBI, on the basis of registration given by Registrar of Co-operative Societies(RCS) of the respective states. In addition, there are entities, one in Orissaand the other one in Uttar Pradesh, carrying on banking business unauthorisedly. RBI has taken up the cases of unlicensed Banks with the respective State Governments. Some unlicensed Urban Co-operative Banks in Kerala have filed writ petition in the High Court of Kerala to quash the circular issued by the Registrar of Cooperative Societies of Kerala on 23rd January, 2003 to all joint Registrar of Co-operative Societies in the Districts and registered unlicensed Co-operative Urban Banks to stop any violation of Banking Regulation Act and to change their constitution to Urban Cooperative Societies by making necessary changes in their by-laws within two months. The Court issued an interim direction on 24th March, 2003 restraining the State of Kerala from taking any coercive steps for non-compliance of the circular dated 23rd January, 2003.

records.name: ABRAR AHMED
records.qn_text:
(a) whether Government have decided to develop important tourist destinations and circuits including ancient monuments, places of cultural importance and places of historical importance in consultations with State Governments/U.T. Administrations; and

records.name: Rajeev Shukla
records.qn_text:
(a) the number of Indians in Iraq and Kuwait at the outbreak of war on March 20, the number who have left for home and those still left behind;

(b) the steps Government are contemplating for the due return of the Indians to resume their jobs in the Gulf States from where they left for India since and prior to the outbreak of the war; and

(c) Government`s response to the media reports that not all, who left in the wake of war, may be welcome to return?
records.ans_text:
THE MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF EXTERNAL AFFAIRS

(SHRI VINOD KHANNA)

(a, b & c) There were approximately 3,50,000 Indians in Kuwait at the outbreak of war on 20 March. Kuwait airport has remained open to normal commercial flights throughout the duration of war. Air India and Indian Airlines carried 5705 passengers from Kuwait to India between 19-31 March, 2003. The Government of Kuwait has clarified that an expatriate can return to Kuwait within 6 months of his departure provided his residence visa remains valid. There were reportedly 19 Indian nationals in Iraq at the outbreak of the war, all of whom chose to stay on in Iraq. There are no reports of Indian nationals leaving other Gulf countries on account of outbreak of war.

records.name: ABRAR AHMED
records.qn_text:
(a) when the last evaluation of the Pradhan Mantri Rozgar Yojana was done and the results thereof; and

(b) the details of the rate of loan recovered under it? ANSWER ( SHRI SANGH PRIYA GAUTAM )
records.ans_text:
MINISTER OF STATE (INDEPENDENT CHARGE) IN THE MINISTRY OF AGRO AND RURAL INDUSTRIES



(a): The last evaluation of the Pradhan Mantri Rozgar Yojana

(PMRY) (second round) was done in the year 2000-01 by the Institute of Applied Manpower Research (IAMR), New Delhi. The study pertained to the programme years 1995-96; 1996-97 and 1997- 98. It covered 13 districts of 5 States namely; Assam, Andhra Pradesh, Manipur, Punjab and Rajasthan covering 16,397 beneficiaries. The important findings of the evaluation study

(second round) are enclosed as Annexure-I.


(b): As per the reports received from Reserve Bank of India, the recovery of loan overdues under the Prime Minister`s Rozgar Yojana

(PMRY) was 34.6 per cent for the year ended March, 2002.

MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF HOME AFFAIRS

(SHRI I.D. SWAMI)



(a), (b) & (c): A Statement is laid on the Table of the House.

STATEMENT REFERRED TO IN PARTS (a), (b) & (c) OF THE RAJYA SABHA STARRED QUESTION NO. 463 FOR 23RD APRIL, 2003

(a): Yes, Sir. These are part of the recommendations of the National Police Commission and the Padmanabhaiah Committee on Police Reforms set up by the Central Government which have been sent to the States for implementation.

records.name: Rajeev Shukla
records.qn_text:
(a) whether Sino-Indo relations were discussed at 5th Asian Security Conference at Delhi, late January;

(b) whether Defence Minister who spoke at the meet described China as having great potential for mutually beneficial economic relations with India;

(c) whether the meet saw hope of improving political relations with China despite the border dispute;

(d) what is the status of the border dispute and how Government hopes to settle it; and

(e) does the Government hope to push economic relations, putting the border dispute in the backburner?
records.ans_text:
MINISTER OF STATE IN THE (PROF. CHAMAN LAL GUPTA) MINISTRY OF DEFENCE

(a) to (e): The 5th Asian Security Conference on “Asian Security and China in the period 2000-2010” was organised by the Institute for Defence Studies and Analyses in New Delhi from 27th to 29th January, 2003. India-China relation was not per se included in the theme of discussions at the Conference. However, while delivering the concluding address there, Raksha Mantri had expressed optimism that India and China would arrive at consensus through continuous dialogue and accommodation of competing interests in the near future. He had also observed that China had made good progress on economic front in the last two decades and India might learn a lesson from them on this front.
Although contentious issues like the boundary problem between the two countries are to be settled, the economic relation between them has been showing an upswing.
As regards boundary dispute between India and China, the two sides have been discussing the boundary question based on the institutional framework provided by the two Agreements signed by them in 1993 and 1996 with the objective of seeking a mutually acceptable settlement of the issue.

records.name: Rajeev Shukla
records.qn_text:
(a) whether Tamil Nadu Government has protested against the Kerala Government’s reported proposal to build dams across some rivers flowing between the two States;

(b) whether the Central Government propose to consider a long- standing demand of nationalising the water resources in view of such disputes which have increased in the recent past; and

(c) if not, what other measures Government are contemplating to improve the situation?
records.ans_text:
THE MINISTER OF WATER RESOURCES (SHRI ARJUN CHARAN SETHI)

(a) to (c) A Statement is laid on the Table of the House. STATEMENT REFERED TO IN REPLY TO PARTS (a) to (c) OF THE STARRED QUESTION NO. 456 TO BE ANSWERED ON 22.4.2003 IN RAJYA SABHA REGARDING NATIONALISATION OF WATER RESOURCES

(a): In December, 2002, the State of Tamil Nadu has written to the Central Government regarding launching of a new scheme of constructing a weir across river Bhavani near Mukkali village to divert water to the west outside the Cauvery basin by the State of Kerala and requested Central Government to take up the matter with Government of Kerala and prevail upon it for not proceeding in any manner with the construction of the proposed weir. Subsequently, the State of Tamil Nadu has filed Petitions before the Cauvery Water Disputes Tribunal(CWDT) objecting to the undertaking of the construction of the scheme by the State of Kerala. The CWDT has on April 2, 2003 directed the State of Kerala that during the pendency of the proceeding before the CWDT, the State of Kerala shall not proceed further with the construction of the weir leading to trans basin diversion and shall maintain the status quo as it was existing on 7.2.2003.

(b) & (c): The mechanism for resolution of the Inter-State Water disputes exist in the form of Inter-State Water Disputes(ISWD) Act, 1956, enacted under Article 262 of the Constitution. The ISWD Act, 1956 has been amended on March 28, 2002 to provide for time-bound adjudication of the dispute by the Tribunals. Also as per the amended Act, the decision of the Tribunal after its publication in the Official Gazette shall have the same force as an Order or decree of the Supreme Court.

records.name: Rajeev Shukla
records.min_name: CONSUMER AFFAIRS, FOOD AND PUBLIC DISTRIBUTION
records.qn_text:
(a) whether it is a fact that about 50 lakh tonnes of wheat, valued at Rs. 3200 crores, is missing from the Food Corporation of India godowns in Punjab;

(b) if so, the details thereof;

(c) the results of the enquiry, if any, conducted into the missing stocks and the responsibility fixed, if any, and the follow up action thereon; and

(d) the details of the steps taken for proper upkeep of the inventories and movement of stocks from the FCI godowns to avoid recurrence of such incidents?
records.ans_text:
THE MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF CONSUMER AFFAIRS, FOOD AND PUBLIC DISTRIBUTION

( SHRI SUBHASH MAHARIA )

(a)&(b): No, Sir. However, the Managing Director, Food Corporation of India (FCI) had detected a discrepancy of about 50 lakh MTs in the stocks of wheat stored with the State Agencies in Punjab, as on 1st January, 2003, as reported by the Regional Office of FCI, Punjab.

(c)&(d): As per the information made available by the FCI, a Committee of officers of the FCI has visited Punjab and their investigations have revealed that the discrepancies arose due to deficiencies in the stock reporting system. The Government has already issued directions to the FCI to streamline the stock reporting system.

records.name: ABRAR AHMED
records.min_name: CONSUMER AFFAIRS, FOOD AND PUBLIC DISTRIBUTION
records.qn_text:
(a) whether in a recent swoop on errant bottled drinking water manufacturers, Government have cancelled the ISI quality mark licences of several plants; and

(b) if so, the details thereof; ANSWER
records.ans_text:
THE MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF CONSUMER AFFAIRS, FOOD & PUBLIC DISTRIBUTION

(SHRI V. SREENIVASA PRASAD)

(a) & (b): Recently while carrying out the surveillance activity, various discrepancies were observed in operation of licences in 24 units belonging to large and small scale and accordingly they were put under stop marking. Stop marking does not mean the cancellation of licence. Under stop marking condition, these firms were not authorized to put BIS mark on their product till permitted by BIS after verification of corrective actions taken by them.

records.qtitle: (clubbed)  TERMS OF REFERENCE OF REVIEW COMMITTEE ON POTA
records.name: R.P. GOENKA
records.qn_text:
(a) whether the proposed committee to review implementation of the Prevention of Terrorist Act, 2002, has been set up; and

(b) if so, the details thereof, including the personnel, terms of reference and time-frame fixed for giving findings and suggesting to check any misuse of various provisions of the POTA?
records.ans_text:
MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF HOME AFFAIRS AND MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF PERSONNEL, PUBLIC GRIEVANCES AND PENSIONS (SHRI HARIN PATHAK)

(a)&(b): The Central Government has constituted a Review Committee headed by Mr. Justice Arun B. Saharya (Retd.) Chief Justice of High Court of Punjab and Haryana, and Shri M.U. Rehman, IAS(Retd.), former Secretary to the Government of India, and Shri Arvind S. Inamdar, IPS(Retd.), former Adviser to the Governor of Uttar Pradesh, as its Members. The terms of reference of the Committee are as under:

(i) the Review Committee shall take a comprehensive view of the use of the said Act in various States and shall be empowered to entertain complaints or grievances with regard to enforcement of the said Act and accordingly, give its findings and suggestions for removing the shortcomings, if any, in the implementation of the said Act; and

(ii) the Review Committee shall suggest measures to ensure that the provisions of the said Act are invoked for combating terrorism only.
The Review Committee has been notified in the Gazette of India Extraordinary on 4.4.2003.

records.qtitle: RATE OF ENTERTAINMENT TAX FOR CINEMA HALLS .
records.name: Rajeev Shukla
records.qn_text:
(a) whether there has been a uniform rate of entertainment tax for cinema halls throughout the country; and

(b) if not, the efforts Government have made in this regard and the results thereof?
records.ans_text:
THE MINISTER OF STATE OF THE MINISTRY OF INFORMATION AND BROADCASTING (SHRI RAVI SHANKAR PRASAD)

(a) Entertainment Tax is a State subject and the rates vary from State to State.

(b) With the objective of all round development of film industry, State Governments were inter-alia requested to consider rationalising the rates of Entertainment Tax so that a uniform rate prevails in the country. However, no consensus was arrived at in the matter and during the 24th Conference of State and Union Territory Information Ministers held in New Delhi on 21.1.2001, it was decided to set up a Committee for Development of the Entertainment sector, to suggest the policy framework both at the Centre and in the States for realising the potential of the Entertainment Sector. As a result of the deliberations in this Committee, it has been decided to recommend that all State/Union Territory administrations fix a ceiling of 60% on entertainment tax. The recommendations of the Committee have been circulated to all States/Union Territory Administrations.
______

records.name: Rajeev Shukla
records.qn_text:
(a) the measures Government have taken to save the film industry from video piracy; and

(b) the results achieved so far?
records.ans_text:
THE MINISTER OF STATE OF THE MINISTRY OF INFORMATION & BROADCASTING

(SHRI RAVI SHANKAR PRASAD)


(a) & (b) The Copyright Act, 1957, which falls under the purview of the Ministry of Human Resource Development provides the legal basis for the subsistence of copyright in cinematograph films and music. The responsibility for dealing with offences under the Copyright Act rests with the police authorities of the State Governments and Union Territory Administrations. Copyright Enforcement cells have been set up in most States/UT Administrations headed by a senior police officer to deal with such offences.
The Copyright Act is amended from time to time to keep it in consonance with International Copyright Law.
The Ministry of Information and Broadcasting has taken several initiatives to mitigate piracy of films as follows:

(i) On the basis of a recommendation made by the Committee for Development of the Entertainment Sector, the Indian Institute of Mass Communication has been asked to formulate appropriate training modules for police officers to train them for anti-piracy work.;

(ii) To create an anti-piracy mind-set and to promote cooperation among stakeholders, this Ministry had brought film producers, multi-service operators and cable operators together, and they had jointly resolved not to exhibit films without valid permission from the copyright holders.

(iii) In an effort to check cable piracy, the Cable Television Networks Regulation Act has been amended in 2000, enabling the Government to prohibit a Cable operator from transmitting or re-transmitting any programme or channel for which he has not been granted a license by the Copyright holder.

(iv) A recommendation made by the Committee for Development of the Entertainment Sector, that a realistic ceiling level for entertainment tax to be imposed by the State Governments could be 60%, since high rate of entertainment tax facilitates piracy, has been communicated to all State Governments.

records.qtitle: TASK FORCE S RECOMMENDATIONS ON EMPLOYMENT OPPORTUNITIES .
records.name: Rajeev Shukla
records.qn_text:
(a) whether recommendations of the Task Force on employment opportunities has been examined by the Planning Commission;

(b) if so, the details thereof; and

(c) if not, the status thereof?
records.ans_text:
MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTERY OF STATISTICS & PROGRAMME IMPMENTATION, MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF PLANNING AND MINISTER OF STATE IN THE DEPARTMENTS OF ATOMIC ENERGY AND SPACE

(SHRI S.B. MOOKHERJEE)

(a): Yes, Sir.

(b): The Planning Commission constituted a `Special Group on Targeting 10 Million Employment Opportunities Per year` under the Chairmanship of Dr. S.P. Gupta, Member, Planning Commission vide Order No.P-12049/9/01-LEM/ERS dated

5.9.2001. The Special Group has examined the recommendations of the Task Force on Employment Opportunities in detail. The Special Group gave recommendations for generating additional employment in the Tenth Plan. It identified sectors/subsectors with employment potential like agriculture, including social forestry, animal husbandry, fishing, horticulture and related areas and small and medium industries, construction, tourism, information technology, financial sector, education and health.

(c): Does not arise.

records.qtitle: RETURN AND REHABILITATION OF KASHMIRI MIGRANTS
records.name: Rajeev Shukla
records.qn_text:
(a) whether any action plan for the return and rehabilitation of Kashmiri migrants have been prepared; and

(b) if so, the status of the plan?
records.ans_text:
MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF HOME AFFAIRS AND MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF PERSONNEL, PUBLIC GRIEVANCES AND PENSIONS (SHRI HARIN PATHAK)

(a ) & (b): A statement is laid on the Table of the House. STATEMENT REFERRED TO IN REPLY TO PARTS (A) AND (B) OF RAJYA SABHA STARRED QUESTION No. 302 ( POSITION NO.2) FOR REPLY ON MARCH 12, 2003.

(a) & (b): In order to enable safe and honourable return of migrants to their native places in the Valley, the then State Government of J&K had finalized an Action Plan involving a total amount of Rs. 2589.73 crores. The Union Government has agreed to reimburse costs borne by the State Government as per approved norms in the case of those Kashmiri migrants who actually return to the Valley. The Action Plan is to be implemented in phases which envisages return and rehabilitation of migrant families in areas where clusters of migrant houses are available and in villages/mohallas in the Kashmir Valley Districts with sizeable Kashmiri Pandit population and where security is already being provided. To begin with, 166 houses forming 15 clusters were identified in Srinagar and Badgam Districts, which are considered safe for the return of the owners of these houses. The list of these clusters was published in the newspapers and steps were taken to identify the families and find their willingness to return to their homes. About 50 families who were registered with the Relief organization, Jammu were contacted personally to give their consent for return to the Valley on the basis of the package announced by the Government. Interaction meetings with some of these families were also held but as reported by State Government, only two families (not belonging to the particular area) have agreed to return to the Valley so far.
The new State Government has indicated that it has identified the shrines in Mattan and Kheer Bhavani where the Kashmiri migrants displaced from these places could be settled temporarily by developing two model clusters containing temporary shelters for Kashmiri migrants, till such time they can repair their existing residential houses. Ministry of Finance has agreed to provide a grant of Rs. 10 crores to the State Government for the reconstruction/renovation of houses and shrines at Kheer Bhavani and Mattan.

records.name: Rajeev Shukla
records.qn_text:
(a) what is the criteria laid down for considering sites as World Heritage Sites; and

(b) the sites selected for the purpose for the year and progress made thereon?
records.ans_text:
MINISTER FOR TOURISM AND CULTURE (SHRI JAGMOHAN)

(a) The criteria are enclosed as per Annexure.

(b) Rock-cut shelters at Bhimbetka, District Raisen, Madhya Pradesh has been nominated for inclusion in the UNESCO World Heritage List for the year 2003.
The Bhimbetka Site has been evaluated in November 2002 by ICOMOS, an agency engaged by UNESCO. ANNEXURE
ANNEXURE REFERRED TO IN REPLY TO PART PART (a) TO THE RAJYA SBAHA UNSTARRED QUESTION NO.749 TO BE ANSWERED ON 25.2.2003
A monument, group of buildings or site which is nominated for inclusion in the World Heritage List will be considered to be of outstanding universal value for the purpose of the Convention when the Committee finds that it meets one or more of the following criteria and the test of authenticity. Each property nominated should therefore;

(a)
(i) represent a masterpiece of human creative genius; or

(ii) exhibit an important interchange of human values, over a span of time or within a cultural area of the world, on developments in architecture or technology, monumental arts, town-planning or landscape design; or

(iii) bear a unique or at least exceptional testimony to a cultural tradition or to a civilization which is living or which has disappeared; or

(iv) be an outstanding example of a type of building or architectural or technological ensemble or landscape which illustrates (a) significant stage(s) in human history; or

(v) be an outstanding example of a traditional human settlement or land-use which is representative of a culture (or cultures), especially when it has become vulnerable under the impact of irreversible change; or

(vi) be directly or tangibly associated with events or living traditions, with ideas, or with beliefs, with artistic and literary works of outstanding universal significance (the Committee considers that this criterion should justify inclusion in the List only in exceptional circumstances and in conjunction with other criteria cultural or natural); and

(b)
(i) meet the test of authenticity in design, material, workmanship or setting and in the case of cultural landscapes their distinctive character and components (the committee stressed that reconstruction is only acceptable if it is carried out on the basis of complete and detailed documentation on the original and to no extent on conjecture).

(ii) have adequate legal and/or contractual and /or traditional protection and management mechanisms to ensure the conservation of the nominated cultural properties or cultural landscapes. The existence of protective legislation at the national, provincial or municipal level and/or a well-established contractual or traditional protection as well as of adequate management and/or planning control mechanism is therefore essential and, as is clearly indicated in the following paragraph, must be stated clearly on the nomination form. Assurances of the effective implementation of these laws and/or contractual and/or traditional protection as well as of these management mechanisms are also expected. Furthermore, in order to preserve the integrity of cultural sites, particularly those open to large numbers of visitors, the State Party concerned should be able to provide evidence of suitable administrative arrangements to cover the management of the property, its conservation an! d its accessibility to the public.

records.name: Rajeev Shukla
records.qn_text:
(a) whether Government are aware that many drugs that are banned in several countries are freely available in India;

(b) if so, whether Government have made inquiries in this regard; and

(c) if so, the details thereof?
records.ans_text:
THE MINISTER OF CHEMICALS AND FERTILIZERS (SHRI SUKHDEV SINGH DHINDSA )

(a) to (c): A Statement is laid on the Table of the House.



STATEMENT REFERRED TO IN PARTS (a) to (c) OF RAJYA SABHA STARRED QUESTION NO.78 FOR ANSWER ON 21.2.2003.

(a), (b) and (c): Drugs withdrawn in some countries can continue to be used by other countries. The decision rests on various factors such as the disease pattern in a country, the varying reactions of certain ethnic groups in a given population to the drug and the availability of safer substitutes as well as the cost factor involved in the treatment of a particular disease. There is no system of global banning of drugs. There is an adequate mechanism to review the status of drugs in India as and when any serious adverse event is reported in international journals or WHO newsletters etc. 75 categories of drugs/drug formulations have so far been prohibited in the country.
The drug or formulations discontinued in developed countries are assessed by an expert committee in consultation with leading experts in given specializations. Based on their advice, the matter is placed before the Drug Technical Advisory Board (DTAB), a statutory body which comprises representatives from the medical profession, the State Drug Enforcement Authorities, experts, institutions, agencies that advise the government on technical issues related to the implementation of Drugs and Cosmetics Act, 1940 and rules there under.

records.name: ABRAR AHMED
records.qn_text:
(c) whether Government have recently started Water Management plans for villages involving Panchayats; and

(d) if so, the details thereof ?
records.ans_text:
MINISTER OF STATE FOR RURAL DEVELOPMENT (SHRI ANNASAHEB M.K.PATIL) i

(a) & (b) : Yes Sir, Hon`ble Prime Minister has launched a new initiative namely `Hariyali` on 27.1.2003. Under this initiative, all watershed development programmes (DPAP, DDP and IWDP) of the Department of Land Resources would be implemented through Panchyati Raj Institutions (PRI). The basic features of `Hariyali` are given below: Under this initiatve, the Gram Saabha would replace the Watershed Association and the Gram Panchyat would be execute the watershed project with technical support from the Block Panchayat who would act as the Project Implementing Agency (PAI) for all watershed projects in a particular Block. In case the Block/Zilla Panchyat has no technical staff to support the Gram Panchyats, suitable Government Line Department/Autonomous Agency may be identified for the purpose. Failing all these options, a reputed voluntary organization (NGO) of good operational/financial standing in the district with adequate technical expertise and experience may be identified to act as the PIA. At the present rates of allocation to the existing watershed programmes of the Department, an amount of Rs. 1000 crore would be available annually to support execution of watershed projects through the PRIs. Detailed Guidelines for operationalizing this new initiative are under preparation. The provision of this initiative applicable to all the new watershed development projects that would be sanctioned in future. The on-going watershed projects will continue to be implemented under the prevailing Guidelines.

records.name: Rajeev Shukla
records.qn_text:
(a) whether during his recent visit to India the Iranian President has made an offer of supply of gas to India;

(b) if so, the details thereof;

(c) whether it is a fact that the proposed supply line for the transfer of gas will pass through Pakistan;

(d) if so, what arrangements are proposed to be put in place to cover the security risk involved in a pipeline through Pakistan;

(e) whether the proposed offer also includes a new global corporate ownership of the pipeline; and

(f) if so, the details thereof and Government`s reaction thereto?
records.ans_text:
MINISTER OF PETROLEUM & NATURAL GAS (SHRI RAM NAIK)

(a) to (f): A statement is laid on the Table of the House.
STATEMENT REFERRED TO IN REPLY TO PARTS (a) to (f) OF THE RAJYA SABHA STARRED QUESTION NO. 18 BY SHRI RAJEEV SHUKLA AND SHRI MANOJ BHATTACHARYA TO BE ANSWERED ON 18TH FEBRUARY, 2003 REGARDING SUPPLY OF GAS FROM IRAN.



(a) & (b): During the recent visit of President of Iran to India a Memorandum of Understanding (MoU) has been signed between India and Iran for mutual cooperation in hydrocarbon sector including natural gas and LNG. As regards, import of natural gas from Iran, under bilateral cooperation, Indo-Iran Joint Committee constituted a Joint Technical Sub-Committee to assist it to explore all the options to import natural gas from Iran. The Joint Committee has decided to undertake an offshore feasibility study for laying of pipeline from Iran to India outside the Exclusive Economic Zone (EEZ) of Pakistan. GAIL (India) Limited (GAIL) from India and National Iranian Gas Export Company (NIGEC) from Iran have been nominated as nodal agencies for the pipeline project by the respective Governments. Accordingly, GAIL and NIGEC have jointly commissioned an offshore pipeline feasibility study for the pipeline from Iran to India. Decision to take up the project would depend on technical feasibility and economic viability of the project.

records.name: Rajeev Shukla
records.qn_text:

(b) if so, the details thereof?
records.ans_text:
MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF AGRICULTURE

(SHRI HUKUMDEO NARAYAN YADAV)

(a)&(b): Government has removed restrictions on farm sector for export of wheat & wheat products, grain and flour of barley, maize, bajra, ragi, jowar (excluding hybrid jowar grown as Kharif crop), butter; and on all types of pulses, lentils, grams and flour made therefrom with effect from March, 2002. Registration requirement for export of non-basmati rice and the requirement of export of pulses in package of 5 kg have also been removed.
Further, the restrictions on exports of cashew to Russia, groundnut oil in 5 kg. packs and above; and agricultural seeds except cashew, jute and onion, have also been lifted with effect from 31.03.2002. The registration requirement on export of butter and wheat & wheat products have also been removed with effect from 31.03.2002.

(d) if not, the reasons therefor; and

(e) by when the revised formula is likely to be finalised?
records.ans_text:
THE MINISTER OF STATE OF THE MINISTRY OF SMALL SCALE INDUSTRIES, MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF PERSONNEL, PUBLIC GRIEVANCES & PENSIONS, MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF PLANNING AND MINISTER OF STATE IN THE DEPARTMENTS OF ATOMIC ENERGY AND SPACE

(SHRIMATI VASUNDHARA RAJE)

(a) to (e): Since the States have sought a revision of the Gadgil Formula for allocation of Normal Central Assistance to States, Planning Commission has sought their views and suggestions have been received from various State Governments. However, there is wide divergence in the views amongst the States in this regard. In general, while the advanced States have sought higher weightage for performance, the less advanced States have sought higher weightage for backwardness. Hence, the full Planning Commission in its meeting held on 27th and 29th June, 2001 discussed, inter-alia, the issue of revision of Gadgil Formula and in view of the divergence of the views among the State Governments and the sensitivity of the issue, it was decided it would be necessary to discuss this further and evolve a consensus before alternatives are considered by the NDC.

MINISTER OF DEFENCE

STATEMENT IN RESPECT OF PARTS (a) TO (d) OF RAJYA SABHA UNSTARRED QUESTION NO. 2119 FOR 11.12.2002 REGARDING INDIAN PoWs IN PAKISTANI JAILS.

In response to the matter raised by the
Prime Minister at Agra Summit, the Government
of Pakistan, in September, 2001, intimated
that it had conducted an ‘exhaustive search’
and scrutiny of jail records throughout the
country to ascertain whether any Indian POW
from 1971 war was still held anywhere in
Pakistan. It added that fresh investigations
had once again confirmed the earlier results
that no Indian POW from 1971 war was held in
any jail in Pakistan.

Pakistan had offered to receive a
delegation of the families of POWs.
Government has had consultations with the
relatives’ Association of the POWs in this
regard. Suggestions put forth by the
Association are being considered viz-a-viz
Pakistani proposal as also the most opportune
time for taking the process further.

records.name: ABRAR AHMED
records.qn_text:
(a) the number of child labourers in the country;

(b) the various child labour abolition programmes undertaken by Government at present;

(c) whether Government propose to bring amendment in the Child Labour Prohibition of Regulation Act, 1986 to make it more purposeful; and

(d) if so, the details thereof?
records.ans_text:
MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF LABOUR

(SHRI ASHOK PRADHAN)


(a): Authentic information on child labour in the country is generated by the decennial census. According to the 1991 census, the number of working children in India was 11.28 million. The figures of the 2001 census have not yet been published.

(b): Government of India has taken steps for withdrawal and rehabilitation of child labour working in hazardous occupations to reduce the incidence of child labour in a particular district through the Scheme of National Child Labour Projects (NCLPs). Under the Scheme of NCLP, special schools have been set up in the child labour endemic districts with the provision for non-formal/formal education, vocational training, stipend, nutrition, health-care etc. So far, 100 NCLPs have been sanctioned in 13 child labour endemic districts for coverage of 2.11 lakh children. As per the information available, 1.45 lakh children (approx.) have already been mainstreamed into the formal school system.

(c) & (d): The Child Labour (Prohibition & Regulation) Act, 1986 prohibits employment of children in occupations and processes listed in the schedule to the Act and regulates it in all other employments.
The issue regarding amendment of the Child Labour (Prohibition & Regulation) Act, 1986 has been discussed in several fora including the Conference of the State Labour Ministers. Important suggestions made in the conference to make the Act more stringent include (a) making the offence a cognizable one; (b) making the penalties more stringent and deterrent; and (c) the responsibility as to the proof of age of a child being made that of the employer. Amendment of the Act is an ongoing process. As of now, no definite time frame can be indicated for amendment of the Child Labour (Prohibition & Regulation) Act, 1986.

records.name: Rajeev Shukla
records.qn_text:

(b) whether it is also a fact that they have threatened to launch a nation-wise satyagraha and jail bharo stir on the 8th January, 2003 followed by march to Parliament on the 26th February during the next Budget Session; and

(c) if so, what steps are being taken by Government to avoid this?
records.ans_text:
MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF LABOUR

(SHRI ASHOK PRADHAN)

(a) to (c): The Government has seen newspaper reports regarding the proposed agitation by the trade unions on January 8 and February 26, 2003. The trade unions have time and again raised the issue of adverse impact of economic reforms on labour. Review/updation of labour laws is an ongoing process for bringing them in tune with the emerging needs of the economy. The Government has already initiated the process of tripartite consultation and there is a continuing interaction with the social partners to bring about a consensus especially on the implementation of the recommendations of the Second National Commission on Labour.

records.name: ABRAR AHMED
records.qn_text:
(a) whether any action plan for the return and rehabilitation of Kashmiri migrants have been prepared by the Centre in consultation with State Government of Jammu and Kashmir; and

(b) if so, the details thereof?
records.ans_text:
MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF HOME AFFAIRS

( SHRI CH.VIDYASAGAR RAO)

(a) & (b): In October 2000, Government of Jammu and Kashmir submitted an Action Plan for the Return and Rehabilitation of Kashmiri migrants involving a total amount of Rs. 2589.73 crores to enable 52, 689 families of Kashmiri migrants comprising about 1.25 lakhs souls at present residing in Jammu, Delhi and other States/UTs to return to the Valley. The Action Plan envisages rehabilitation grant per family @ Rs. 1.50 lakhs; grant for repair of houses @ Rs. 1 lakh for houses intact and Rs. 3 lakhs for houses damaged; grant for household goods @ Rs. 0.50 lakhs and furniture @ Rs. 0.50 lakhs; interest free loan @ Rs. 1-2 lakhs per person; compensation for loss of income from agriculture upto Rs. 1.50 lakhs per family; interest free loan of Rs. 1.50 lakhs per family for investment in agricultural operations and sustenance of Rs. 2,000/- per month for one year.
The Action Plan is proposed to be implemented by State Government in phases, which envisages return and rehabilitation of migrant families in areas where clusters of migrant houses are available and in villages/mohallas in the Kashmir Valley Districts with sizeable Kashmiri Pandit population and where security is already provided. To begin with, 166 houses forming 15 clusters had been identified by the State Government in Srinagar and Badgam Districts, which are considered safe for the return of the owners of these houses. The list of these clusters was published in the newspapers and steps were taken to identify the families and find their willingness to return to their homes. About 50 families who were registered with the Relief organization, Jammu were contacted personally to give their consent for return to the Valley on the basis of the package announced by the Government. Interaction meetings with some of these families were also held but none of the families have agreed to return to the Valley so far.
``

records.name: ABRAR AHMED
records.qn_text:
(a) whether it is a fact that a large number of State Finance Corporations are very sick and burdened with a large amount of non-performing assets;

(b) if so, the details thereof; and

(c) in what manner Government proposes to rehabilitate the State Finance Corporations and deal with their large non-performing assets?
records.ans_text:
MINISTER OF FINANCE & COMPANY AFFAIRS (SHRI JASWANT SINGH)

(a} to (c): A Statement is placed on the Table of the House.

Statement placed on the Table of Rajya Sabha in reply to Starred Question No.201 for answer on 3rd December,2002 regarding `NPAs of State Finance Corporations`Tabled by Dr. Abrar Ahmed and Shri Rajeev Shukla. o

(a): Yes, Sir.

(b): Out of the 18 State Financial Corporations (SFCs) four, that is of, Delhi, Kerala, Rajasthan and West Bengal have a positive net worth as on 31st March, 2002. The net worth, however, of the remaining 14 SFCs stands fully eroded. The accumulated losses of all these SFCs, during 2001-02, aggregates to Rs.4,198 crores. NPAs of SFCs as a whole were 61% of the loans and advances, as at the end of March 2002. The amount involved is Rs.7076 crore. Standard Assets constitute only 39%.

(c): The SFCs Act was amended in 2000 for providing flexibility and functional autonomy to them. A Committee headed by Shri G.P.Gupta, the then CMD, IDBI looked into their functioning and submitted a report recommending, inter-alia, financial, operational and organizational restructuring of SFCs. The report of the Committee has been sent to various SFCs for taking immediate action on recommendations that do not involve any financial support, such as operational and organizational restructuring. SFCs being State entities, the State Governments are the principal stakeholders. They are thus expected to consider steps for improving the performance and recapitalisation of SFCs. In order to attract long term refinance from Financial Institutions, SFCs have to improve recovery of NPAs and reestablish their viability.

records.name: ABRAR AHMED
records.qn_text:
(a) whether Government have assessed the impact of various family planning measures adopted to control the population explosion in the country;

(b) if so, the details thereof;

(c) whether Government propose to introduce new methods adopted in foreign countries in the field of family planning; and

(d) if so, the details thereof?
records.ans_text:
MINISTER OF HEALTH AND FAMILY WELFARE

(SHRI SHATRUGHAN SINHA)

(a)to(d): A statement is laid on the table of the House.

STATEMENT REFERRED TO IN REPLY TO RAJYA SABHA STARRED QUESTION NO. 184 FOR 2.12.2002 .....
The measures adopted to control population by the Government have yielded favourable results. The Total Fertility Rate has come down from 6 in 1951 to 3.2 in 1999. The Birth Rate has come down from 40.8 in 1951 to 25.8 during the year 2000, as per the estimates of Sample Registration System(SRS), Registrar General of India. According to National Family Health Survey conducted in 1998-99, about 42% of the couples with two children and about 58% of couples with 3 children have adopted terminal methods of contraception. The child population (0-6 years) has come down from 18% in 1991 to 15% in 2001 census, showing decline in fertility rate.
Among the major States with more than 20 million population, the States of Kerala and Tamil Nadu have already achieved a replacement level of fertility of a TFR of 2.1, while the States of Andhra Pradesh, Gujarat, Karnataka, Maharashtra, Orissa, Punjab and West Bengal are having a TFR of 2.2 to 3.0 and are in the direction of replacement level of fertility. There are 4 States viz. Assam, Madhya Pradesh, Chattisgarh and Haryana which are having a TFR of 3.1 to 4.0, while the 4 States of Rajasthan, Uttar Pradesh, Bihar and Jharkhand have recorded a TFR of 4.1 to 4.7 as per the SRS, 1999.
Regarding the acceptance of terminal methods, the percentage of couples with two children have high acceptance in southern and western regions, being 60% in Tamilnadu, 72% in Andhra Pradesh, 50% in Maharashtra and 60% in Karnataka, while in Northern States, the acceptance is on the lower side in the States of U.P. (11%) & Bihar (18%). Similarly the percentage of couples with 3 children accepting terminal methods ranges between 65% to 85% in southern and western States, while in northern States of Uttar Pradesh, Bihar, the range is between 24 to 31% as per NFHS 1998-99.
The proportion of Child population aged 0 to 6 years also follows a similar pattern. Tamilnadu has the lowest child population of 11% and Bihar with the highest of 20% as per census 2001.
As regards introduction of new methods of family planning in the current financial year, the Government has introduced an advanced version of Intra Uterine Device Cu.T 380 A, which remains effective for ten years. Emergency Contraceptive Pills, which is hormonal contraceptive that can be used to prevent pregnancy following an unprotected act of sexual intercourse within the past 72 hours, is also included in the programme. In addition, research work is being carried out for injectible contraceptive CYCLOFEM, injection on male contraceptive (RISUG) and praneem as microbicidal and contraceptive. .....

records.name: ABRAR AHMED
records.qn_text:
(a) whether it is a fact that cleanliness , maintenance and upkeep of rail coaches are not upto the mark, causing inconvenience to the rail passengers; and

(b) if so , the steps taken by Government to improve the situation ?
records.ans_text:
MINISTER OF RAILWAYS (SHRI NITISH KUMAR)

(a) & (b) : A statement is laid on the Table of the Sabha.
STATEMENT REFERRED TO IN REPLY TO PARTS (a) & (b) OF STARRED QUESTION NO. 166, BY DR. ABRAR AHMED AND SHRI EAJEEV SHUKLA TO BE ANSWERED IN RAJYA SABHA ON 29.11.2002 REGARDING CLEANLINESS IN RAILWAY COACHES.

(a) & (b): All railway passenger coaches are properly maintained, cleaned and attended prior to commencement of journey from the base station . Trains are also cleaned at nominated enroute ` ,. stations while traveling safaiwalas are provided on-selected trains for cleaning on the run. However, owing to intensive use and long continuous journeys, coaches become dirty on run despite enroute cleaning arrangements. Also, careless use, vandalism and lack of civic sense prevailing in certain ` regions and some-trains negate the Railway`s efforts in keeping the coaches clean and tidy
In order to meet the increasing passenger aspirations and to bring about further improvements, several new initiatives have been taken in the recent times as enumerated below:
i) Strengthening enroute cleaning arrangements by providing mechanized cleaning facilities under `Clean Train Station` scheme at identified 15 stations on major trunk routes.
ii) Introduction of environment friendly, controlled discharge toilets in order to avoid station area being polluted by toilet discharge.
iii) Development of automatic exterior washing facility for trains at busy terminals.
iv) Pest control on all coaches once a month through specialized agencies.
v) Introduction of biodegradable waste disposal bags as a part of Clean Train Station scheme. vi) Introduction of `State of the Art` modular toilets in place of conventional toilet for all classes of coaches. These toilets are user friendly, elegant, easy to clean and pilferage proof.
vii) Provision of 110 Volts electrical fittings in place of conventional 24 Volts and use of fluorescent fittings in place of bulbs. viii) Introduction of Jan Shatabdi type services in which second class coaches have upper class like feature including ergonomic chairs, noise control, modular toilets, rail mart, improved flooring etc. ix) Indigenous manufacture of modem technology LHB type coaches with advance feature including screw less fibre reinforced plastic interiors, modular toilets with control discharge system which does not dirty the station area, electronic taps and toilet fittings, environment control air-conditioning, ergonomic seats, superior ride comfort, noise insulation etc. x) Provsion of adequate maintenance time and manpower at base depot for maintenance and
cleaning for all new trains and progressive rationalization for all existing trains

records.qtitle: FINANCIAL ASSISTANCE TO MERITORIOUS SPORTS PERSONS .
records.name: Rajeev Shukla
records.qn_text:
(a) whether Government are aware of the sad state of affairs of many retired sports persons who had represented India at the national/international levels;

(b) if so, whether Government have floated any scheme to help them; if so, the details thereof;

(c) whether Government have made any provision for development of meritorious players at the national and international levels; and

(d) if so, the details thereof and the criteria being followed for providing financial assistance to such players?
records.ans_text:
THE MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF YOUTH AFFAIRS AND SPORTS (SHRI PON. RADHAKIRISHNAN)

(a) Yes, Sir. From time to time proposals are received from the outstanding sportsperson of yesteryears living in indigent conditions for financial assistance

(b) Yes, Sir. Under the following schemes, Government provides financial assistance to the outstanding/meritorious Sportspersons:-

(i) National Welfare Fund For Sportspersons: Under the scheme. Government gives monthly pensions upto Rs. 2500/- and one time lump-sum financial assistance upto Rs. 40,000/- for medical treatment to the retired sportspersor who have represented the country at national/ international levels and living in indigent circumstances, i.e. whose monthly income is less than Rs. 3,000/-from all sources.

(n) Sports Fund for Meritorious Sports Persons: Under the scheme, meritorio Sportspersons who have won medals in Olympic Games and Gold medal
World Cups/World Championships in Olympic and Asian Games disciplines are sanctioned monthly pensions @ Rs. 2500/- . Silver and Bronze medallists of World Cups/World Championships in Olympic and Asian Games disciplines and Commonwealth Games are sanctioned pension @ Rs, 2000/- per month. Pension is sanctioned from the age of 30 years for lifetime.

(c) Yes, Sir.

(d) In order to prepare the sportspersons to compete at National & International level, Government provides Financial Assistance to the various National Sports Federations and Sportspersons under the following schemes:

(i) Assistance to National Sports Federations:- Under this scheme National Sports Federations are provided financial assistance for organization of National Coaching Camps, participation of athletes in International tournaments and engagement of foreign coaches and experts for meritorious sportspersons of National and International levels.

(ii) Assistance to Promising Sports Persons and Supporting Personnel:- Under this scheme financial assistance upto Rs. 5 lakhs is sanctioned to a promising sports person, who has equaled or excelled the existing national record or is a gold medallist of last National Championship or is a medallist of Asian/Commonwealth Games/Afro-Asian Games/Olympic Games/ World Championship in different sports disciplines for undergoing training abroad, purchase of sports equipment, obtaining scientific support, and for training and participation in tournaments in the country. To get the assistance under the scheme, promising sportspersons should not be more than 25 years of age. For sports like shooting, golf, billiards and snooker, chess and yachting the age limit may be relaxed upto 35 years.

(iii) National Sports Development Fund:- Meritorious Sportspersons seeking assistance under the scheme are also provided Financial Assistance for training.

records.name: Rajeev Shukla
records.qn_text:

(b) whether it is also a fact that inspite of enhanced expenditure the visibility of publicity on small family norms has been very poor as compared to 1975-77 when all round publicity was there;

(c) if so, the reasons therefor; and

(d) the steps being taken to improve publicity on small family norms which is of paramount importance for our Nation?
records.ans_text:
THE MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF HEALTH AND FAMILY WELFARE (SHRI A. RAJA)


(a): The allocation for publicity of the entire Family Welfare Programme, including the Reproductive and Child Health Programme was Rs.160.00 Crores during 2001-02.

(b) (c) and (d): During 1975 it was Family Planning Programme focussing only on population control. There has been a paradigm shift in the Family Welfare Programme after the International Conference on Population and Development (ICPD), Cairo in 1994. The `Target Free Approach (TFA) was adopted since 1st April, 1996 all over India. This approach leaves the choice of family size to the couples themselves. Consequently the emphasis of programme has now shifted to publicity on first child birlth at proper age, adequate spacing among the issues, Immunisation and availability of both permanent and temporary methods of family planning. Thus, the goals of programmehave evolved from that earlier approach. A multi-faceted communication strategy on the above and other related issues has been opertionalised through the Electronic, print media and other forms of Mass Media together with advocacy efforts.
