records.qtitle: CUT IN CNG SUPPLY TO INDUSTRIAL UNITS .
records.name: Rajeev Shukla
records.qn_text:
(a) whether it is a fact that Compressed Natural Gas supply to many industrial houses has been cut to meet its increased demand in Delhi;

(b) if so, the loss of production of industrial units with depleted CNG supply;

(c) by when the Indraprastha Gas Ltd. (I.G.L.) will be able to meet the full requirement of Delhi; and

(d) the steps taken to increase the supply of Compressed Natural Gas to industrial units?
records.ans_text:
MINISTER OF PETROLEUM & NATURAL GAS (SHRI RAM NAIK)

(a) to (d) A statement is laid on the Table of the House. STATEMENT REFERRED TO IN REPLY OF PARTS (a) TO (d) OF THE RAJYA SABHA STARRED QUESTION NO.581 FOR ANSWER ON 07.05.2002.

(a) to (d) To meet the current compressed natural gas (CNG) requirement of public transport in Delhi, 50% of the fall back allocation to M/s Maruti Udyog Limited (MUL), which was meant for captive power generation, was reduced. Since dual fuel facilities are available with M/s MUL for captive power generation, the question of loss of production does not arise. To bridge the gap between the demand and supply of natural gas, steps such as import of liquefied natural gas and speeding up of indigenous exploration/exploitation of domestic hydrocarbon resources have been initiated. Indraprastha Gas Limited plans to meet the requirement of Delhi during the year 2003 - 04.

records.name: Rajeev Shukla
records.qn_text:
(a) whether it is a fact that the number of incidents of the vehicles run by CNG catching fire have increased over the months;

(b) if so, the details of mishaps in CNG run vehicles during the last one year;

(c) whether Government have carried out any study or evaluation on the causes for mishaps in CNG vehicles; and

(d) if so, the details thereof and the safety measures taken for CNG vehicles?
records.ans_text:
Minister of Petroleum & Natural Gas

(SHRI RAM NAIK)

(a) Yes, Sir.

(b) Details of mishaps in Delhi are as follows: 05.08.2001: Near Punjabi Bagh Flyover 20.09.2001: Minor fire in RTV at Sanjay Gandhi Transport Nagar 01.10.2001: Fire in bus at Karkardooma Court 10.10.2001: Fire in bus at Nehru Place 14.10.2001: Fire in CNG auto at Jahangeerpuri 11.11.2001: Fire in bus near Dhaula Kuan 19.12.2001: Fire in bus at G.T.K DTC Depot 27.12.2001: Fire in MOP at Delhi Mathura Highway 07.01.2002: Fire in auto-rickshaw at Okhla Morh 21.02.2002: Fire in Tata Bus at Nanglamachi Station 22.03.2002: Fire in TELCO bus near Kakrola Morh, Pappankala

(c) &(d) Informal inquiries have been carried out by Indraprastha Gas Limited (IGL). Statutory inquiry is to be done by the State Government. The inquiries by IGL reveal fault in the rupture disk of vehicles and use of spurious cylinders to be one of the causes of fire incidents.

records.name: Rajeev Shukla
records.qn_text:
(a) whether it is a fact that it has been decided to close down the Oil Coordination Committee as consequence of APM dismantling;

(b) if so, the number of officers and staff likely to become surplus and of those proposed to be absorbed;

(c) whether there will be corresponding reduction in the strength in oil companies if they are reverted back to their parent cadre public sector oil companies; and

(d) if not, the reasons for increasing the number and expenditure of public sector oil companies?
records.ans_text:
MINISTER OF PETROLEUM & NATURAL GAS

( SHRI RAM NAIK )


(a): Yes, Sir. The Oil Coordination Committee (OCC) stands dissolved from 1st April 2002.

(b) to (d): The employees of the OCC were on deputation from different organisations including public sector oil companies. Since the employees of the -oil companies in the OCC were against the sanctioned strength of these companies, their repatriation is not likely to cause any problem to the companies.

records.name: Rajeev Shukla
records.qn_text:
(a) whether Government have decided to reverse its decision on printing of five rupee notes;

(b) If so, the reasons therefor; and

(c) what will be the ratio between paper currency and metallic currency of rupees five denomination?
records.ans_text:
Minister of State in the Ministry of Finance (Shri Balasaheb Vikhe Patil)

a) No, Sir. b) Does not arise c) Notes to Coins ratio of rupee five denomination during 2001-02 is 45 : 55.

records.qtitle: TRANSFER OF ALL PSUS UNDER ONE MINISTRY .
records.name: Rajeev Shukla
records.qn_text:
(a) whether it is a fact that oil sector PSUs are diversifying into other fields like IOC into power sector and GAIL into telecom;

(b) if so, what will be the relevance of having administrative Ministry as at present;

(c) whether it will not be proper to transfer all PSUs with diversified activities under the control of one Ministry; and

(d) the Government`s views in this regard?
records.ans_text:
THE MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF HEAVY INDUSTRIES & PUBLIC ENTERPRISES (DR. VALLABHBHAI KATHIRIA)

(a) Yes Sir.

(b), (c) & (d)
Allocation of Business to various Ministries is based on the core activities of the Ministries/Departments and the PSEs under their control. Since diversification of PSEs is supplementary to core activities, there is no proposal for any change in the present arrangement.

records.qtitle: STUDY ON PUBLIC AND PRIVATE SECTOR REFINERIES .
records.name: Rajeev Shukla
records.qn_text:
(a) whether Government have carried out any study of financial performance of Public and private sector refineries for some given period;

(b) if so, the details thereof and how they compare; and

(c) if not, whether Government would carry out such a study to improve financial performance of the public sector refineries?
records.ans_text:
MINISTER OF PETROLEUM & NATURAL GAS (SHRI RAM NAIK)


(a) to (c): A statement is laid on the Table of the House.


STATEMENT REFERRED TO IN REPLY TO PARTS (a) TO (c) OF THE RAJYA SABHA STARRED QUESTION NO. 340 TO BE ANSWERED ON 16TH APRIL 2002 REGARDING STUDY ON PUBLIC AND PRIVATE SECTOR REFINERIES.

(a)&(b): No, Sir. However, the Government monitors financial performance of public sector companies, including their refining operations, through regular quarterly performance review meetings with reference to the Memorandum of Understanding (MOU) targets and previous year`s performance. Gross refining margins of public sector refineries are also reviewed at these meetings. Performance of the joint sector and the private sector refining companies is not similarly reviewed by the Government.

(c): There is no such proposal under consideration of the Government.

records.name: Rajeev Shukla
records.qn_text:
(a) the role and purpose of Oil Industry Development Board (OIDB) in the oil industry;

(b) whether after APM dismantling the OIDB will continue to exist;

(c) if so, whether OIDB benefits will cover private sector also; and

(d) if so, the changes proposed in the functioning of the OIDB and if not, the reasons therefor?
records.ans_text:
MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF PETROLUEUM & NATURAL GAS AND MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF PARLIAMENTARY AFFAIRS (SHRI SANTOSH KUMAR GANGWAR)

(a) to (d) Oil Industry Development Board (OIDB) has been established under Oil Industry Development Act, 1974 for the development of Oil Industry. The purposes for which the financial and other assistance can be given by the Board inter-alia includes all activities by way of prospecting or exploring for or production of mineral oil, refining, processing, transportation, storage, handling and marketing of mineral oil, production and marketing of all products, down-stream of oil refinery and the production of fertilizers and petro-chemicals and all activities directly or indirectly connected therewith. OIDB would continue to render the assistance for the above purpose even after dismantling of Administered Pricing Mechanism (APM). Funding towards oil sector projects are decided by OIDB on case to case basis, subject to the priorities determined by the Board from time to time.

records.name: Rajeev Shukla
records.qn_text:
(a) whether it is a fact that Bagdogra figures in the list of Category II routes under the Route Dispersal Guidelines, issued by Directorate General of Civil Aviation;

(b) if so, the reasons therefor;

(c) whether any proposal to amend this has been submitted to Government by Directorate General of Civil Aviation;

(d) if so, what action has been taken by the Ministry of Civil Aviation on this proposal so far; and

(e) what are the details of the routes being covered by all the scheduled airlines, route-wise?
records.ans_text:
MINISTER OF CIVIL AVIATION ( SHRI SYED SHAHNAWAZ HUSSAIN )
(a) and (b) :- Yes, Sir. The term `North-Eastern Region` used in the Route Dispersal Guidelines is construed to cover the entire region of `Air Defence Identification Zone (East)` which also includes Bagdogra. (c):- Directorate General of Civil Aviation (DGCA) had submitted a factual note in this regard to the Ministry of Civil Aviation. (d):- Does not arise. (e):- Routes/Services operated by Schuduled Airlines depend on customer demand, seasonal changes and other relevant factors and are published from time to time by the concerned airlines.

records.qtitle: REVIEW OF POLICY ON UNAUTHORISED COLONIES IN DELHI.
records.name: Rajeev Shukla
records.qn_text:
(a) whether it is a fact that Government have decided to review their policy on unauthorised colonies in Delhi;

(b) if so, the details thereof;

(c) whether Government are also considering regularization of unauthorised colonies set-up on public land;

(d) if so, the reasons therefor; and

(e) the novel features of the new policy?
records.ans_text:
MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF URBAN DEVELOPMENT & POVERTY ALLEVIATION

( SHRI BANDARU DATTATREYA )

(a)to(e): The Ministry has set up a Committee under the Chairmanship of Secretary (Urban Development), Government of India to examine the existing guidelines for regularisation of unauthorised colonies in Delhi and suggest modifications/amendments required, if any, to facilitate expeditious regularisation of unauthrised colonies. The other members of the Committee are VC, DDA, Pr. Secretary (UD), GNCTD, Commissioner, MCD, Chairman, NDMC, Chairman, Delhi Vidyut Board, Chief Executive Officer, Delhi Jal Board and Joint Secretary (D&L) in the Ministry. The committee is yet to submit its report.
The Government have already filed guidelines for regularisation of unauthorised colonies in existence before 31.3.1993 in the High Court of Delhi in CWP No. 4771/93 - Common Cause (Regd.) Society Vs. Union of India & Others. These guidelines provides for regularisation of unauthorised colonies on both private as well as public land.

records.qtitle: RISE IN HIV CASES IN MANIPUR .
records.name: Rajeev Shukla
records.qn_text:
(a) whether it is a fact that HIV positive cases in Manipur have increased at an alarming rate during the last couple of years;

(b) whether it was due to the fact that people in Manipur were not made aware about the causes and prevention of AIDS;

(c) if so, the reasons therefor and the responsibility fixed for the laxity; and

(d) the number of known HIV cases in Manipur at present and the action being taken to stop spreading of the dreaded disease?
records.ans_text:
THE MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF HEALTH AND FAMILY WELFARE (SHRI A. RAJA)

(a) No, Sir. The number of HIV/AIDS cases in the State of Manipur during the last three years is as below:-
1999 61 2000 364 2001 307

(b) No, Sir.

(c) Question does not arise.

(d) The cumulative number of HIV/AIDS cases in Manipur as on 31-03-2002 is 1095. Government has launched a comprehensive AIDS prevention and control programme which is a 100% centrally sponsored scheme being implemented in all States/UTs including Manipur through States/UTs. AIDS Control Societies. The main components of the programme consist of:- ú Reducing the spread of HIV in groups at high risk by identification of target populations and providing peer counselling, condom promotion, and treatment of sexually transmitted infections. ú Preventive intervention for the general population by Information, Education and Communication (IEC) and awareness campaign, provision of voluntary testing and counselling, safe blood transfusion services and prevention of occupational exposure. ú Providing financial assistance for opportunistic infections, home and community based care. ú Strengthening effectiveness and technical, managerial, financial sustainability of the intervention programmes at national, State and Community levels. ú Promoting collaboration amongst public, private and voluntary sectors.
....

records.name: Rajeev Shukla
records.qn_text:
(a) whether it is a fact that majority of train passengers in Bihar travel without ticket;

(b) if so, the reasons theerefor;

(c) what steps are being taken to ensure the entry of authorized ticket holders only in trains, and that the reserved seat passengers are not harassed by unauthorized passengers; and

(d) the annual revenue loss suffered by the Railways due to ticketless travellers and the amount collected from the defaulters, in Bihar? ANSWER MINISTER O STATE IN THE MINISTRY O PARLIAMENTARY AFFAIRS AND
records.ans_text:
MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF RAILWAYS

(SHRI O. RAJAGOPAL)
a)and(b): The exact extent of ticketless travel is not quantifiable. however, intensive checks have been done over Eastern, North Eastern, Northeast fromtier and South Eastern Railways, the portions of which are serving the State of Bihar.

(c): In addition to manning of reserved coaches by ticket checking staf, intensive drives are regularly conducted by Commercial and Vigilance departments in association with the Police against ticketless/irregular travel and also to prevent entry of unauthorized passengers in reserved compartments. Unauthorized passengers are dealt with as per the relevant provisions of law.

(d): Ticket checking on the Railways is a continuous activity. however, the loss sufered due to ticketless travellers which go undetectd cannot be assessed. State-wise figures are not maintined.

records.name: Rajeev Shukla
records.qn_text:
(a) whether it is a fact that over 88 percent of girl children engaged in hazardous domestic and small scale industries, such as match sticks, crackers, agarbatti, glass, bidi, etc., are illiterate;

(b) if so, whether Government have drawn any scheme to make them literate;

(c) if so, the details thereof; and

(d) if not, the reasons therefor and how Government propose to make them literate?
records.ans_text:
THE MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF HUMAN RESOURCE DEVELOPMENT

(PROF. RITA VERMA)

(a) Separate data is not maintained by this Ministry about the literacy status of girl children engaged in specific industries.

(b), (c) & (d) To provide education to child labour, the Ministry of Labour has been running a programme called the National Child Labour Project (NCLP). This Ministry has also launched Sarva Shiksha Abhiyan, a national level programme for Universal Elementary Education which aims to provide quality elementary education to all children in the 6-14 age group across the country by the year 2010. The Education Guarantee Scheme & Alternative and Innovative Education (EGS & AIE), a component of SSA with effect from the Tenth Plan, also provides strategies for child labour and adolescent girls to provide life oriented and gender sensitive education.

records.name: Rajeev Shukla
records.qn_text:
to answer to Unstarred Question 191, given in the Rajya Sabha on the 1st March, 2002 and state:

(a) what steps have been taken in the new consumption norms for fertilizer industry, to minimize reliance on imported fertilizers; and

(b) whether these new norms are expected to move towards self-sufficiency in fertilizers and boost their exports; if not, the reasons therefor?
records.ans_text:
THE MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF CHEMICALS AND FERTILIZERS (SHRI S. B. MOOKHERJEE)

(a) and (b): The revision of consumption norms on interim basis w.e.f. 1.4.2000 was done in order to fix the consumption norms at the realistic levels, based on the actual levels achieved in 1999-2000, or the existing level, whichever is lower. Government does not expect any significant fall in production of urea on account of interim revision of consumption norms. However, the Government is monitoring the availability vis-à-vis demand of urea and will take suitable steps to ensure that there is no significant gap between the demand and supply of urea.
If availability of urea happens to be more than the demand, then the Government can permit the export of urea.

records.name: Rajeev Shukla
records.qn_text:
(a) whether it is a fact that officers with more than 20 years of regular service as Section Officer in the Central Secretariat Service are yet to be appointed as Under Secretary on regular basis;

(b) if so, the reasons therefor;

(c) whether the Brahma Committee constituted to suggest measures for removing stagnation in CSS has taken into consideration the recommendations made by the Standing Committee of the Parliament on Home Affairs in this regard; and

(d) if so, the recommendations incorporated or being accepted by Brahma Committee and those ignored with reasons therefor?
records.ans_text:
THE MINISTER OF STATE OF THE MINISTRY OF SMALL SCALE INDUSTRIES, MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF PERSONNEL, PUBLIC GRIEVANCES AND PENSIONS, MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF PLANNING AND MINISTER OF STATE IN THE DEPARTMENTS OF ATOMIC ENERGY AND SPACE. (SMT.VASUNDHARA RAJE)

(a)&(b): Promotion of Section Officers (SOs) in the Central Secretariat Service (CSS) to the grade of Under Secretary (US) have got delayed owing, inter alia, to protracted litigation in the CAT, Principal Bench as well as in the Supreme Court over the issue of inter se seniority of direct recruits and promotee SOs. As a result, the regular Grade-I (US) panels of CSS could not be finalized after 1986. The issue was finally settled by the Supreme Court through their order dated 09.05.1997, pursuant to which a Common Seniority List (CSL) of SOs was issued on 03.12.1997. On the basis of this CSL, the Select Lists up to the year 1990 have already been issued and the proposal for the years 1991-94 has been sent to the UPSC.

(c)&(d): As per the terms of reference of the Committee of Senior Officers constituted by the Government for restructuring of CSS, the Committee was expected to go into various aspects of the cadre structure of CSS and to suggest remedial measures for removal of stagnation in the service. The Committee has since submitted its report on 28.02.2002. The various recommendations made by the Committee are currently being studied by the Government.

records.qtitle: PDS RATION TO INCOME TAX PAYEES .
records.name: Rajeev Shukla
records.min_name: CONSUMER AFFAIRS, FOOD AND PUBLIC DISTRIBUTION
records.qn_text:
(a) whether it is a fact that Government warehouses are overflowing with cereal stocks;

(b) if so, whether Government are considering to allow income-tax payees to draw ration from Public Distribution System shops;

(c) if so, the details thereof; and

(d) if not, the reasons therefor and other alternative steps taken to dispose of the surplus stock?
records.ans_text:
THE MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF CONSUMER AFFAIRS, FOOD AND PUBLIC DISTRIBUTION

( SHRI ASHOK PRADHAN )

(a): The stock of foodgrains in the Central pool as on 1st January, 2002 was 580.32 lakh tonnes (rice- 256.17 lakh tonnes and wheat - 324.15 lakh tonnes) as against the minimum Buffer Stocking norm of 168.00 lakh tonnes of foodgrains including 84 lakh tonnes of rice and 84 lakh tonnes of wheat.

(b),(c)&(d): Income-tax payers have not been debarred to draw ration from fair price shops under Public Distribution System (PDS). However, in order to target the PDS towards the poor, the levy sugar supply under the PDS has been restricted only to the families living below poverty line (BPL) in all States/UTs except the North-Eastern States. Hill States and Island Territories w.e.f. 1.2.2201.
In view of the abundant stocks of wheat and rice in the central pool, the steps taken by the Government of India to enhance food security are as under:

i) The entitlement for BPL families was raised from 10 kg per family per month to 20 kg per family per month from April, 2000 and further to 25 kg per family per month w.e.f. 12.7.2001.

ii) In November, 2000, it was decided to make foodgrains available at CIPs applicable for BPL families for all the welfare schemes including SC/ST/OBC hostels, implemented by the various Ministries of the Government of India.

iii) In November, 2000, a decision was taken to make foodgrains available at BPL rates for allotment to State Governments @ 5 kg. per head per month for covering categories of indigent people living in welfare institutions, such as beggar homes, orphanages/Nari Niketans, etc; sponsored by the State Governments and the concerned administrative Ministry of the Government of India.

iv) In November, 2000, another decision was taken to make foodgrains available at BPL rates for development schemes (where the beneficiaries belong to the BPL category) implemented by Non-Government Organisations (NGOs), sponsored by the State Governments and endorsed by the administrative Ministry in the Government of India, as also by international organizations like the World Food Programme.

v) On 1.12.2000, the allocation of foodgrains for Below the Poverty Line (BPL) families was revised on the basis of populations projections of the Registrar General as on 1.3.2000. As a result, the number of BPL families eligible for subsidized foodgrains has increased from

5.96 crores families to 6.52 crore families.

vi) The Antyodaya Anna Yojana was announced on 25.12.2000 for one crore poorest of the poor BPL families. The scheme is under implementation in all States/UTs. Each of the Antyodaya families is given 25 kg. of foodgrains @ Rs. 2 per kg for wheat and Rs. 3 per kg for rice.

vii) In January, 2001, the Food for Work Programme was introduced under which foodgrains are allocated free of cost to various States by the Ministry of Rural Development. Government of India has allocated 38.33 lakh MTs of foodgrains, from January 2001 upto 12.2.2002 for undertaking Food for Work programmes in 11 States. Government of India had allocated one lakh MTs of foodgrains for distribution in the earthquake-affected areas of Gujarat in January 2001.

viii) In May 2001, Government of India decided to give additional allocation of foodgrains at BPL rates to the drought affected States for distribution to all the drought affected families

(BPL & APL) @ 20 kg power family per month for a period of three months in the current financial year. The Government of Andhra Pradesh, Gujarat, Himachal Pradesh, Madhya Pradesh, Maharashtra and Rajasthan have already been allocated additional foodgrains. The Government of Bihar has been given additional allocation of 1.80 lakh MTs of wheat at BPL rate for flood relief.
ix) In spite of the rise in the economic cost of wheat and rice w.e.f.1.4.2001, the CIP have not been increased for the BPL category. The CIPs have been retained at Rs. 4.15 per kg for wheat and Rs. 5.65 per for rice.
x) The Central Issue Price (CIP) of wheat and rice for the APL category has been reduced w.e.f. 12.7.2001, which will be valid till 31.3.2002.
(Rs. per quintal) APL Wheat 610 Rice 830

xi) The Ministry of Rural Development has launched the Sampoorna Gramin Rozgar Yojana (SGRY) on 25th September 2001 based on the announcement made by the Prime Minister on 15th August 2001. Under the programme, it is envisaged to utilize 50 lakh MTs of foodgrains every year. The allocation of foodgrains under SGRY upto 28.2.2002 has been 30.82 lakh MTs.
xii) The Open Market Sale Scheme of wheat was continued during the current financial year 2001-2002. The quantity sold from April 2001 to 15.2.2002 was 37.87 lakh tonnes.

records.qtitle: DISAPPEARANCE OF AIRFORCE PLANE SPARES ENROUTE BANGALORE FROM NIZAMUDDIN .
records.name: Rajeev Shukla
records.qn_text:
(a) whether it is fact that a consignment containing spare parts of airforce planes have been found missing enroute Bangalore from Nizamuddin;

(b) if so, the details thereof;

(c) whether the culprits involved in the case and the officials who showed laxity in the security related consignment have been booked;

(d) if so, the details thereof; and

(e) if not, the reason therefor and present status of the investigation?
records.ans_text:
MINISTER OF DEFENCE (SHRI GEORGE FERNANDES)


(a) Yes, Sir.

(b) A consignment belonging to HAL containing spares of Air Force aircraft was despatched by HAL through M/S Elbee Ltd. by rail from Gwalior to Hazrat Nizamuddin Railway Station on 11th September 2001. This consignment contained six Packages in a box and was to be sent by Air by M/S Elbee Ltd. from Delhi to Bangalore. The consignment was reported to be missing from Hazrat Nizamuddin Railway Station when the representative of M/S Elbee Ltd. came to collect the same at 1500 hours on 12th September, 2001.

(c) to (e): The loss was reported to Nizamuddin RPF Railway Station by Railway authorities. The case is under investigation by Civil Police. It is learnt that a Departmental enquiry has also been ordered by Railway authorities and further action will be taken only after the Police investigation and Departmental enquiry are completed.

records.name: Rajeev Shukla
records.qn_text:
(a) whether it is a fact that export of Indian leather has declined at an alarming rate;

(b) if so, the reasons therefor; and

(c) the steps being taken to boost the export of leather?
records.ans_text:
THE MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF COMMERCE AND INDUSTRY

( SHRI RAJIV PRATAP RUDY )

(a) No Sir.

(b) Does not arise

(c) : Government has taken various steps and policy initiatives for export promotion of leather and leather products. These include implementation of Duty Exemption Pass Book Scheme and Duty Drawback Scheme; Tannery Modernisation Scheme; de-reservation of tanning and footwear sector from small scale industry; providing financial assistance to exporters for marketing of export products outside the country; and assisting in design and product development through Institutes like Footwear Design and Development Institute and Central Leather Research Institute.

records.qtitle: INVESTMENT BY PSUS IN OTHER PSUS .
records.name: Rajeev Shukla
records.qn_text:
(a) whether it is a fact that the Public Sector Undertakings are being allowed to investin other Public Sector Undertakings in the disinvestment process;

(b) if so, the details threof and the reasons therefor;

(c) what benefits Government will derive in such deals;

(d) whethr such decisions will affect dividends payable to Government; and

(e) if so, the details threof?
records.ans_text:
MINISTERO DISINVESTMENT AND MINISTER OF DEVELOPMENT OF NORTH EASTERN REGION

(SHRI ARUN SHOURIE)
a)&(b): On the basis of the criteria decided for the qualification of bidders for acquiring stakes in any Public Sector Undertaking slated for disinvestment, any company, in private or public sector, can take part in a competitive bidding process. Hopwever, depending on the unique features of a case, and taking into consideration all relevant factors including monopoly issues, Government can always impose reasonable restrictionsin specific cases, in public interest andin theinterest of privatisation of `non-strategic` PSUs.

(c) Depending on the case, the PSUs buying the stakes may be benefited by way o synergy between the two companies.

(d)&(e): The dividend payable by any PSU for a particular period is decided, keeping in view various factors likeprofits, availability of funds etc. As such, whether purchase o a PSU-stake by another PSU will affect th dividend paying capacity of the purchaser, in the long run, can not be precisely estimated.

records.qtitle: MENACE OF LEOPARDS IN UTTARANCHAL AND H.P .
records.name: Rajeev Shukla
records.qn_text:
(a) whether it is a fact that leopards have created menace in Uttaranchal and Himachal Pradesh by killing many people and also getting themselves killed due to lack of jungles;

(b) if so, the number of people killed by leopards and the leopards killed during the last two years; and

(c) the steps being taken to protect the lives of people and the leopards?
records.ans_text:
MINISTER OF ENVIRONMENT AND FORESTS (SHRI T.R. BAALU)

(a) & (b) Instances of depredation by leopards and the leopards being killed to prevent such depredation are reported from time to time. The details of human deaths caused by leopards and number of leopards killed to safeguard the human killings are at Annexure.

(c) The steps taken to prevent human leopard conflicts include:

1. Improvement of habitat and prey base in the Protected Areas and the buffer zones through various Centrally Sponsored Schemes including Project Tiger, Development of National Parks and Sanctuaries and Eco-development in and around Protected Areas.

2. Funds are also provided to the State Governments for purchase of communication equipments and vehicles for the field staff to reduce response time in cases of attack on human beings by wild animals.

3. Wildlife Institute of India organises courses on tranquilisation and translocation of wild animals for the field managers.

4. To mitigate the anger amongst kith and kin of a person killed by wild animal, that often leads to retaliatory killing, the Central Government has issued guidelines for ex-gratia payment of Rs. 1 lakh. The amount so paid is reimbursed under various Centrally Sponsored Schemes.

(c) if not, the reasons therefor; and

(d) the proposed grouping of Naphtha-based units and the expected benefits to the fertilizer industry and the consumers?
records.ans_text:
THE MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF CHEMICALS AND FERTILIZERS (SHRI S. B. MOOKHERJEE)

(a) : Yes, Sir.

records.qtitle: TERRITORIAL DEMARCATION BETWEEN INDIA AND BANGLADESH .
records.name: Rajeev Shukla
records.qn_text:
(a) whether it is a fact that the territorial demarcation between India and Bangladesh has not been completed and settled, so far;

(b) if so, the reasons therefor; and

(c) the steps being taken to resolve the issue and by when an amicable settlement is expected to be arrived at?
records.ans_text:
THE MINISTER OF EXTERNAL AFFAIRS

(SHRI JASWANT SINGH)


(a) to (c) A statement is placed on the Table of the House.
Statement referred to in parts (a) to (c) of the reply to Rajya Sabha Starred Question No.161 for answer on 14.03.2002


(a) to (c) While the survey authorities of the two countries have completed demarcation of over 4000 kms of the India - Bangladesh boundary, they have not been able to resolve differences in demarcation of about 6.5 kms and have referred the matter to the respective Governments. There are also outstanding issues relating to exchange of enclaves and adverse possessions.

2. The Government of India is keen on an early settlement of all boundary-related matters with Bangladesh in accordance with the terms of the India-Bangladesh Land Boundary Agreement of 1974. The Governments have agreed to constitute Joint Boundary Working Groups to address all pending matters. The first meeting of the India - Bangladesh Joint Boundary Working Groups on Border Demarcation, and on Enclaves and Adversely Possessed Territories was held in Dhaka from July 2-4, 2001. In the meeting both sides presented their respective positions on these matters in order to facilitate a clear understanding of each others` points of view and to address the issues in a pragmatic and time-bound manner. The subsequent meetings of the Joint Boundary Working Groups could not take place earlier on account of change of Government in Bangladesh viz. the handing over of power to a neutral caretaker Government on 15 July 2001 and holding of General Elections in early October 2001. The dates for the holding of the next meeting of the Joint Boundary Working Groups have been proposed to Bangladesh and their response is awaited.

3. The ratification of the Land Boundary Agreement would be completed expeditiously on completion of demarcation.

records.qtitle: PAYMENT OF SALARIES TO GOVERNMENT EMPLOYEES
records.name: Rajeev Shukla
records.qn_text:
(a) whether it is a fact that many State Governments and Central Agencies have been finding it difficult to pay salaries to their employees;

(b) if so, the details thereof and the steps taken to prevent unpaid employees from resorting to agitations;

(c) whether allowing VRS to the employees of the Central, State and Governments agencies in the wake of growing unemployment poses law and order problems in the country; and

(d) what meaningful steps are being taken to create job opportunities in the Central and State Governments?
records.ans_text:
Minister of State in the Ministry of Finance

(Shri Balasaheb Vikhe Patil)

(a) and (b): It is the responsibility of the State Governments to pay salaries to their employees and take suitable measures to improve their financial status. The Union Government through various measures helps the States to overcome temporarily cash imbalances and overdraft with the RBI to the extent possible. On the basis of the recommendations of the Eleventh Finance Commission, a Scheme for the State Fiscal Reform Facility has been drawn. Under this Scheme, the States have been encouraged to prepare a monitorable fiscal reforms programme aimed at improving their financial position in the medium term. Presuming that Central Agencies refers to Central Public Sector Undertakings, it is stated that need based budgetary support is provided to sick Central Public Sector Undertakings in order to avoid hardships to employees to pay salaries to their employees where a Govt, decision exists regarding its closure/revival in a time bound manner.

(c)and(d): Information is being collected and will be laid on the Table of the House.

records.qtitle: ESTABLISHMENT OF KUDANKULAM NUCLEAR POWER PLANT
records.name: Rajeev Shukla
records.qn_text:
(a) whether it is a fact that a nuclear power plant is proposed to be established at Kudankulam in Tamil Nadu in collaboration with Russia;

(b) if so, the details indicating the cost, capacity, power generation, date of commissioning etc.;

(c) the main features of the memorandum of understanding with Russia on this project;

(d) the rate at which power from this plant will be made available to the consumers and beneficiary States;

(e) whether the local people have raised any objection fearing that it would affect fishing industry; and

(f) if so, the assurance given by Government?
records.ans_text:
THE MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF SMALL SCALE INDUSTRIES, MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF PERSONNEL, PUBLIC GRIEVANCES AND PENSIONS, MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF PLANNING AND MINISTER OF STATE IN THE DEPARTMENTS OF ATOMIC ENERGY AND SPACE (SHRIMATI VASUNDHARA RAJE)

(a) Yes, Sir.

(b) The sanctioned cost of the project, including Indian portion of works, is Rs.13,171 crore. The capacity of each of the 2 units is 1000 MWe. The expected gross power generation per year from both the units at a capacity factor of 68.5% is about 12000 MUs (Million Units). The targeted date of completion of the Project is December 2007 for Unit-1 and December 2008 for Unit-2.

(c) The Russian organisation will carry out the design of the plant and also supply material and equipments for the entire plant. The Indian side is responsible for design and development of infrastructure, construction, erection, commissioning, operation and maintenance of the plant.

(d) The tariff of electricity from this plant will be competitive as compared to the tariff from contemporary thermal power stations in the region. The estimated tariff in the first year of operation is about 310 paise/KWh.

(e) There is no effect on the fishing activity due to the Kudankulam & project. This is also the experience at the other coastal nuclear

(f) power plant in the country viz. Madras Atomic Power Station, Tamil Nadu. The local fishermen from the surrounding villages of Kudankulam were taken on a conducted tour for meeting with the local fishermen near Madras Atomic Power Station, which is under operation for the last 20 years. It is understood that the fishermen from Kudankulam area, after discussions with the fishermen near Madras Atomic Power Station, were convinced that fishing activity is not affected by the project.

(a) (b) & (c ) : India`s exports of leather and leather products during April-August, 2001 was of US $ 845.74 million against US $ 828.21 million during the corresponding period of last year, thus recording a positive growth of 4.64%. records.qtitle: IMPACT OF CHINA S ENTRY INTO WTO ON INDIAN INDUSTRIES .
records.name: Rajeev Shukla
records.ans_text:
MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF COMMERCE AND INDUSTRY

( SHRI RAJIV PRATAP RUDY )

(a ) : Yes, Sir. The Fourth Ministerial meeting of WTO held at Doha, Qatar, decided on 10th October, 2001 to accept the accession instruments indicating the terms and conditions of Peoples Republic of China`s Membership in WTO. Subsequently, on 11th November 2001 the Government of PR China accepted the protocol done at Doha. Accordingly, PR China`s accession to WTO will enter into force on 11 December, 2001, one month after the acceptance of protocol by the Government of PR China.

(b) & ( c ) : India has been actively involved in the GATT / WTO accession process of China which started in 1986. A bilateral agreement was signed with China on 22nd February 2000 where tariff and other concessions were agreed to by China with India. There may not be any immediate impact on Indian industries on account of China`s accession to WTO as such, because India and China have already been exchanging Most Favoured Nation (MFN) Treatment and because the concessions had to be given unilaterally by China on entry to WTO and no reciprocal commitments were involved on the part of India or any other WTO Member. The effects of China`s accession to WTO should, therefore, be beneficial to Indian exports since conditions of market access including in respect of tariffs in the Chinese market will significantly improve. The main policy emphasis is to make the Indian industry globally competitive in addition to regular monitoring of imports, particularly consumer goods.

records.qtitle: PROCEDURAL DEFICIENCIES IN DISINVESTMENT OF ITDC AND HCI
records.name: Rajeev Shukla
records.qn_text:
(a) whether it is a fact that the disinvestment from ITDC and Hotel Corporation of India hotels has been held up for certain procedural deficiencies;

(b) if so, the details thereof;

(c) whether there is any difference of opinion between his Ministry and Ministry of Finance on the issue;

(d) if so, why the same could not be sorted out before approving the proposal for disinvestment in hotels; and

(e) by when, notices inviting tenders for disinvestment in hotels are likely to be issued?
records.ans_text:
MINISTER OF LAW, JUSTICE AND COMPANY AFFAIRS

(SHRI ARUN JAITLEY)

(a) to (e) A statement is laid on the Table on the House.
STATEMENT REFERRED TO IN REPLY TO PARTS (a) TO (e) OF RAJYA SABHA STARRED QUESTION NO. 295 FOR ANSWER ON 10.12.2001 REGARDING PROCEDURAL DEFICIENCIES IN DISINVESTMENT OF ITDC AND HCI.

Sir, there are no procedural deficiencies in the disinvestment of ITDC and Hotel Corporation of India hotels. There is also no difference of opinion between the Ministry of Finance and Ministry of Disinvestment. The position about inviting tenders for disinvestment in hotels of ITDC and Hotel Corporation of India is given as under:
India Tourism Development Corporation (ITDC)
Expressions of Interest were invited for 17 hotels (8 in the 1st tranche & 9 in the 2nd tranche). After due diligence by the qualified parties and finalization of transaction documents, financial bids were invited for the 8 hotels advertised in the 1st tranche. No bids/compliant bids were received for two hotels and in respect of the remaining 6 hotels, 8 bids in all were received and the respective highest bids in each of the 6 hotels have been accepted by Government. The bids in respect of the 9 hotels advertised in the 2nd tranche are yet to be invited. In respect of the remaining hotels, the advertisement inviting Expression of Interest is yet to be issued.
Hotel Corporation of India
A sub-committee was constituted by the Ministry of Civil Aviation to oversee the process of disinvestment of HCI and a Global Advisor was appointed by Air India for the purpose. The Government later decided to have the process of disinvestment in HCI completed by the Ministry of Disinvestment. Financial bids were invited from the bidders for HCI properties (other than Centaur Lake View, Srinagar) and after scrutiny & examination, the Government has accepted the bids in respect of two hotels. The other properties (except Srinagar) for which either the bids were below reserve price or no bid was received, further action to re-invite bids would be taken in due course. Regarding Hotel Centaur Lake View, Srinagar, some issues are yet to be resolved with Government of Jammu & Kashmir.

records.qtitle: NATIONAL DRIVE FOR ERADICATION OF CANCER .
records.name: Rajeev Shukla
records.qn_text:
(a) whether it is a fact that cancer cases in the country are continuously increasing;

(b) if so, the details thereof, State-wise;

(c) whether Government propose to launch a national drive against this dreaded ailment like T.B., leprosy etc. to eradicate it; and

(d) if so, by when and if not, the reasons therefor?
records.ans_text:
MINISTER OF HEALTH AND FAMILY WELFARE

(DR. C.P. THAKUR)

(a): Time trend analysis of the data from population-based cancer registries over the last decade shows a small but significant increase in the overall incidence of cancer in the urban cancer registries, among both men and women.
Though there are year-to-year variations, available data suggest that incidence of certain cancers like cancer of oesophagus, gall bladder, lung, stomach and rectum has shown increase in some registries, while incidence of cancer of mouth, pharynx and cervix has shown a downward trend in certain registries.

(b): The State-wise distribution of cancer cases in India is not available.

(c)&(d): This Ministry is already implementing the National Cancer Control Programme, the Revised National T.B. Control Programme (widely known as DOTS) and the National Leprosy Eradication Programme with the objective of eliminating/controlling these dreaded diseases.

records.qtitle: ACTION AGAINST THOSE FAVOURING OSAMA BIN LADEN .
records.name: Rajeev Shukla
records.qn_text:
(a) whether it is a fact that many Muslim organizations and clerics in India have raised their voice in favour of Osama Bin Laden after US attack on Afghanistan;

(b) if so, the details thereof; and

(c) the steps taken to counter them; and what political and social steps have been taken to bring them in line with the Government stand to support American efforts to root out terrorism from the globe?
records.ans_text:
THE MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF HOME AFFAIRS

(I.D. SWAMI)

(a)to(c): As per available information some Muslim leaders and organisations have raised their voice in favour of Osama Bin Laden and condemned the US-led air-strikes in Afghanistan and expressed the anguish of the Muslim community over these developments. At the same time some eminent moderate Muslim opinion leaders have supported the efforts to root out terrorism in the name of jehad, or otherwise.
`Public Order` and `Police` are State subjects as per the Constitution of India and hence maintenance of law and order as well as communal harmony are the primary concern of the State Governments. In so far as the Union Government are concerned, the Government have been providing assistance to the State Governments in a variety of ways to tackle the issues causing communal cleavage - both administrative and promotional - in a sustained manner i.e. assistance in improving their policing infrastructure, sending alert messages periodically, sharing intelligence with them, providing Central Para-military Forces including the composite Rapid Action Force on specific request and issuing guidelines from time to time to promote communal harmony.
The activities of all organisations having a bearing on maintenance of communal harmony are under constant watch of law enforcement agencies and requisite legal action is taken, wherever necessary.

records.name: Rajeev Shukla
records.qn_text:
(a) whether Government are apprehensive about the relations between Nepal and India after the situation created by massacre in Royal Palace, Nepal followed by the resignation of their Prime Minister; and

(b) what diplomatic action has been taken to ensure that the existing relations between the two countries improve further?
records.ans_text:
THE MINISTER OF STATE FOR EXTERNAL AFFAIRS

(SHRI OMAR ABDULLAH)

(a) and (b) A Statement is placed on the Table of the House.
STATEMENT REFERRED TO IN PARTS (A) AND (B) OF THE ANSWER TO RAJYA SABHA UNSTARRED QUESTION NO. 3428 TO BE ANSWERED ON 23.08.2001 ON `INDO-NEPAL RELATIONS IN THE WAKE OF ROYAL MASSACRE`

In an unfortunate tragic incident, King Birendra and Queen Aishwarya along with some other members of the Royal Family of Nepal were shot dead on June 1, 2001. Crown Prince Dipendra, who was involved in the shoot out, also succumbed to his injuries and died on June 4, 2001. Gyanendra Bir Bikram Shah Dev, younger brother of Late King Biendra, was pronounced the new King by the Royal Council of Nepal and was enthroned on June 4, 2001.

2.. Immediately after the tragic incident, Government of India released a statement which was read out by the External Affairs Minister on June 2. It stated that as a close neighbour and friend, India conveyed its heartfelt condolences to the mourning nation of the Kingdom of Nepal. A three day State mourning was declared by Government of India as a mark of respect. On the same day, the Indian Cabinet passed a Resolution at a specially convened emergency meeting. Rashtrapatiji conveyed his condolences to the new King. PM sent letters of condolence to the Queen Mother and the then PM Girija Prasad Koirala. While expressing condolences, confidence was expressed that friendship and co-operation would continue between our two countries in pursuit of peace and progress and mutually beneficial development.

3. Soon after assumption of office by Hon`ble Sher Bahadur Deuba as the Prime Minister of Nepal, PM spoke to him over the telephone and a congratulatory message was sent thereafter.

4. The enduring bonds of friendship between India and Nepal are strong and are based on mutual understanding and trust. Our relations have withstood the test of time and Internal developments in one country will not be allowed by either side to adversely affect the other and relations between the two.


5. The existing bilateral mechanisms between the two countries continue to be in operation. Agencies of the two governments are meeting regularly. Some of the Meetings held recently include the Fourth Meeting of the Joint Working Group on Border Management in June, 2001 and the Inter-Governmental Meeting to discuss matters relating to Trade and Transit in August, 2001.
6. The External Affairs Minister, Shri Jaswant Singh, also paid a goodwill visit to Kathmandu from August 17 to 19, 2001. This was the first high level contact between the two governments since the enthronement of King Gyanendra on Jule 4, 2001.

records.qtitle: COLLAPSE OF CIVIL AND CRIMINAL JUSTICE SYSTEM .
records.name: Rajeev Shukla
records.qn_text:
(a) whether it is a fact that there is a total collapse in civil and criminal justice system and the conviction rate is hardly 7 per cent whereas 93 per cent of those charged with various crimes go scot-free;

(b) whether Government have studied and analysed the reasons for collapse in justice which encouraged crime becoming a low risk job;

(c) the steps Government propose to take to ensure speedy conviction of criminals and justice to aggrieved parties;

(d) whether any comprehensive judicial reforms are under consideration; and

(e) if so, the details thereof?
records.ans_text:
MINISTER OF LAW, JUSTICE AND COMPANY AFFAIRS AND SHIPPING (SHRI ARUN JAITLEY) (a): No, Sir. As per information made available by the National Crime Records Bureau, Ministry of Home Affairs, the average conviction rate of crimes under the Indian Penal Code from the year 1995 to 1999 has been 39.02%.

(b): The reasons for poor conviction rate, inter alia, can be attributed to the nature of the procedural laws, practices and procedures followed by criminal courts and the inadequencies of the investigating and prosecuting agencies.

(c) to (e) :Various steps have been taken by the Government for the speedy disposal of both civil and criminal cases. These include amendment of the Civil Procedure Code and the Code of Criminal Procedure, increase in the number of posts of Judges/Judicial Officers, establishment of Special Courts/tribunals, computerisation of courts and adoption of alternative modes of dispute resolution, such as, arbitration and conciliation. Lok Adalats have been given a statutory base as supplementary forum for resolution of disputes. As regards Criminal Procedure Code, the Law Commission of India has comprehensively reviewed the Code of Criminal Procedure, 1973. The Government has recently appointed a Committee under the chairmanship of Shri Justice V.S.Malimath, to suggest measures for revamping the Criminal Justice System. Government has sanctioned a scheme involving an amount of Rs.502.90 crore for creation of 1734 Fast Track Courts for expeditious disposal of long pending sessions cases and cases involving undertrials in jails, on priority. The scheme is in operation with effect from April, 2001.

(b) whether they have been found operating in connivance with the authorised outlets of the various public undertakings under the Ministry of Petroleum and Natural Gas;

(c) if so, the details thereof and the action taken against the outlets; and

(d) the steps taken to prevent sale of spurious diesel?
records.ans_text:
MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF PETROLEUM & NATURAL GAS (SHRI SANTOSH KUMAR GANGWAR)

(a) : No, Sir.

(b) & (c) : Do not arise.

(c) : The oil marketing companies carry out regular/surprise checks of retail outlets, to prevent various malpractices including adulteration. In addition, special drives are launched by the oil companies both on their own and also under direction of Government from time to time to check malpractices. Further, Anti Adulteration Cell, headed by a Director General, has been set up and empowered for search & seizure under various control orders.

records.qtitle: PAUCITY OF SPACE IN THE VAULTS OF NATIONALISED BANKS IN JAIPUR
records.name: Rajeev Shukla
records.qn_text:
(a) whether it is a fact that nationalised banks in Jaipur are finding it difficult to accept currency deposits owing to paucity of space in their vaults; and

(b) if so, what steps are being taken to transfer the accumulated currency to Reserve Bank of India or other sources to facilitate the depositors for their deposits in the banks?
records.ans_text:
THE MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF FINANCE

(SHRI BALASAHEB VIKHE PATIL)

(a):- Yes, Sir.

(b) :- The Reserve Bank of India (RBI) has taken following steps in this regard :
a) Short Term Measures

i) Notes are regularly lifted from the currency chests in Jaipur.
ii) Diversion orders have been issued from Jaipur to Bhopal, Mumbai and Nagpur to ease the pressure on Jaipur Office.
iii) In order to dispose of soiled notes at RBI expeditiously, RBI has opened one New Note Examination Hall (Revised Procedure) which disposes of the soiled ntes 150% of the Normal Procedure. RBI has also introduced 2 Modified Procedure Section to dispose of lower denominations notes at fast track which disposes of soiled notes 200% the Normal Procedure.
b) Long Term Measures RBI is introducing Currency Verification and Processing Systems at Jaipur Office shortly which will dispose of soiled notes at 50,000 pieces per hour. Thus, the soiled notes from nationalized banks are periodically taken over by RBI, Jaipur for processing and disposal.

records.qtitle: FORCEFUL ACQUISITION OF AGRICULTURAL LAND FOR RELOCATION OF INDUSTRIES IN DELHI
records.name: Rajeev Shukla
records.qn_text:
(a) whether it is a fact that Government have forcefully acquired agricultural land with standing crop in Delhi for relocation of indusries without paying the promised cost;

(b) whether the cost of crop, fertilizers and pesticides have also been taken into account while deciding the compensation to be paid;

(c) whether the farmers are agitating on these issues; and

(d) by when the compensation is likely to be paid to all whose land has been acquired?
records.ans_text:
MINISTER OF URBAN DEVELOPMENT & POVERTY ALLEVIATION

(  SHRI JAGMOHAN )

(a):   The  Government of NCT of Delhi has informed that it  has
acquired agricultural land for relocation of Industries pursuant
to the direction of Hon`ble Supreme Court of India.

(b):  Yes, Sir.

(c):   Farmers had demanded enhancement of the compensation rate
for the acquired land.

(d):   Where  award has been announced by the  Land  Acquisition
Collector,  payment has been offered in all the cases.  Most  of
the  persons  have also collected the payment.  In  cases  where
award  is yet to be announced, 80% of the compensation has  been
offered  to the affected persons as per section 17(3-A) of  Land
Acquisition  Act,  1894  and  most of them  have  collected  the
compensation.

records.qtitle: FAILURE OF PULSE POLIO PROGRAMME IN U.P. .
records.name: Rajeev Shukla
records.qn_text:
(a) whether it is a fact that the Pulse Polio Programme in U.P. has failed miserably during the last five years;

(b) if so, the reasons therefor;

(c) whether Government have constituted any probe panel to go deep into the matter; and

(d) if so, the results thereof?
records.ans_text:
THE MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF HEALTH AND FAMILY WELFARE (SHRI A. RAJA)

(a) & (b) There has been significant decline in the number of polio cases in Uttar Pradesh due to implementation of intensified polio eradication activities. These have declined from 881 in 1998 to 773 in 1999, 179 in 2000 and 23 during 2001 reported till 8th August, 2001.

(c) & (d) The polio eradication implementation strategy is reviewed/recommended every year by a committee of national and international experts, keeping in view the progress and the epidemiological situation in each State. The strategy recommended by the experts for 2001-2002 provides for
(i) two national immunization rounds
(ii) one sub-national round in high risk States of U.P., Bihar, West Bengal and Delhi,
(iii) pre-emptive vaccination rounds in areas with continued polio circulation, even during low transmission season and
(iv) mop-up rounds following detection of confirmed polio cases in the concerned district as also in surrounding districts. .......

records.name: Rajeev Shukla
records.qn_text:
(a) whether it is a fact that the quantity of RSPM, Nitrogen Dioxide and Sulphur in the atmosphere over Delhi has been over the safe level for the last many days;

(b) if so, the reasons therefor; and

(c) the steps being taken to reduce their level which otherwise may tell upon the health of people living in the National Capital? ANSWER MINISTER OF ENVIRONMENT AND FORESTS (SHRI T.R. BAALU)

(a),

(b) &

(c) A statement is laid on the Table of the House. STATEMENT IN RESPECT OF PARTS

(a),

(b) &

(c) OF RAJYA SABHA STARRED QUESTION NO. 288 FOR 10.8.2001 REGARDING `POLLUTANTS LEVEL IN DELHI` RAISED BY SHRI RAJEEV SHUKLA: ________________________________________________________________

(a) &

(b) The ambient air quality is being monitored at seven locations in Delhi. During July-August, 2001, the average levels of Respirable Suspended Particulate Matter (RSPM), Oxides of Nitrogen and Sulphur dioxide in Delhi have been reported by Central Pollution Control Board to be below their safe limits. However, the prescribed limits of Respirable Suspended Particulate Matter (RSPM) and Oxides of Nitrogen were exceeded on a few days at a few locations mainly due to vehicular emissions.

(c) The steps taken to control pollution include the following:- (i) Action Plan to control pollution in Delhi has been prepared and is being implemented. (ii) Emission standards for on-road vehicles and mass emission standards for new vehicles have been notified under the Motor Vehicles Act, 1988 and are enforced by Transport Departments of the State Governments including Delhi. (iii) A comprehensive Policy for Abatement of Pollution that lays stress on both the control and preventive aspects of pollution has been formulated. (iv) Unleaded petrol is supplied in the entire country from 1.2.2000 and diesel with 0.25% sulphur maximum content is supplied from 1.1.2000 in the entire country. Ultra low sulphur (0.05%) fuel (petrol and diesel) has also been introduced in major cities. (v) Compressed Natural Gas (CNG) is supplied for automobiles through a number of retail outlets in Delhi to cater to the CNG vehicles. (vi) Benzene concentration in petrol has been reduced. (vii) A network of 290 Ambient Air Quality Monitoring Stations has been set up throughout the country. (viii) Emission standards for industries have been notified under the Environment (Protection) Act, 1986 to check pollution. (ix) Industries are also required to install necessary pollution control equipments before commissioning of their plants. (x) Industries are required to take consent from the respective State Pollution Control Board under the Air (Prevention and Control of Pollution) Act, 1981. **** GOVERNMENT OF INDIA MINISTRY OF ENVIRONMENT AND FORESTS RAJYA SABHA UNSTARRED QUESTION NO. 2159 TO BE ANSWERED ON 10.08.2001 CONFERENCE ON POLLUTION 2159. SHRI PREM CHAND GUPTA: Will
records.ans_text:
the Minister of Environment and Forests be pleased to state:

(a) whether it is a fact that at a three-day conference on pollution recently, the World Bank representative suggested that not less than 20 per cent of deaths in India are due to pollution;

(b) whether it was also stated that there is considerable scope for improvement in the regulatory and fiscal regimes for industrial pollution check and the laws don`t have any economic incentive or disincentive for pollution abatement; and

(c) if so, what action Government are taking in this regard?
ANSWER
MINISTER OF ENVIRONMENT AND FORESTS

(SHRI T.R. BAALU)

(a) The World Bank representative had conjectured that atleast 20 per cent of deaths in India is attributable to pollution.

(b) & (c) Yes Sir. The conference recommended various options for further improvement in the regulatory and fiscal regimes for consideration of the Ministry.

records.qtitle: RELIEF MATERIALS TO FLOOD VICTIMS OF ORISSA .
records.name: Rajeev Shukla
records.qn_text:
(a) whether it is a fact that the relief material and food supply could not reach the marooned people affected by floods in Orissa, in time;

(b) whether it is also a fact that the rescue operations started with the help of army could provide relief only to 40 per cent of the flood victims;

(c) what are the reasons for the civil authorities not acting in alacrity to provide timely relief to the flood affected people; and

(d) whether any probe is proposed to be undertaken in this regard?
records.ans_text:
MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF AGRICULTURE

(SHRI SHRIPAD Y. NAIK)


(a) to (d): Distribution of relief at the ground level is the responsibility of the State Government. The Government of Orissa had reportedly taken all necessary steps from the beginning including issuing timely warnings, instructions to the District Collectors for evacuation of people and arranging relief supplies to the affected people. The State Government have informed that food stocks were available and that the sarpanches were authorised to administer relief in most cases. According to the State Government, the marooned people were rescued by the civilian authorities and the army and about 7 lakh people were evacuated during different stages of flood.
The State Government have also informed that the civil authorities have provided relief in time and that no probe is being undertaken.

records.qtitle: LOSS OF PROPERTIES AND LIVES INFLICTED BY ULFA .
records.name: Rajeev Shukla
records.qn_text:
(a) the loss of properties and lives inflicted by ULFA activist in May, 2001 assembly polls related violence in Assam and neighbouring States;

(b) how many ULFA activists were nabbed or killed by the security forces during the poll process in Assam;

(c) the reasons for the failure of intelligence and security forces to contain ULFA violence in Assam; and

(d) the steps taken to protect lives and properties from terrorist outfits in Assam?
records.ans_text:
THE MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF HOME AFFAIRS

( I.D. SWAMI )

(a): According to available information, United Liberation Front of Assam (ULFA) militants had killed 37 persons between 11.4.2001 to 17.5.2001. The exact loss of property is yet to be estimated. Information from the neighbouring States is being collected and will be laid on the Table of the House.

(b): Between 11.4.2001 to 17.5.2001, 75 ULFA militants were nabbed by the security forces. 19 ULFA militants died in various encounters with the security forces in the said period.

(c)&(d): There has been no failure of intelligence and security forces in Assam in containing the violence unleashed by the militants. The Government has taken various steps to protect lives and properties from terrorist outfits in Assam. This include, inter-alia, deployment of Para-military Forces and Army in the State, coordinated action by Army, Para-military Forces and State Police for counter insurgency operations, declaration of major insurgent groups as unlawful associations under the Unlawful Activities (Prevention) Act, 1967; declaration of the entire State of Assam as `disturbed area` under the Armed Forces (Special Powers) Act, 1958; reimbursement of security related expenditure to the State Government and modernization/up-gradation of State Police Force. Regular review of the situation both at State and Central Government level is being made.
Following effective security arrangements, 74.38% voters were able to cast their vote in the General Assembly Elections held in May, 2001 in Assam.

records.qtitle: RELOCATION OF INDUSTRIAL UNITS IN DELHI.
records.name: Rajeev Shukla
records.qn_text:
(a) the number of polluting industrial units in the non-conforming areas in Delhi to be relocated and the number of such units which have been relocated, so far;

(b) whether Government have developed sufficient plots with power and water supply to accommodate the remaining polluting units;

(c) whether any deadline has been fixed to relocate all the polluting units from the non-conforming areas;

(d) if not, the reasons therefor;

(e) whether any authority has been specified to oversee the operations of relocations of industrial units and made accountable for any lapses; and

(f) if so, the details thereof and if not, the reasons therefor?
records.ans_text:
MINISTER OF STATE FOR URBAN DEVELOPMENT & POVERTY ALLEVIATION

( SHRI BANDARU DATTATREYA )

(a): The Govt. of N.C.T. of Delhi has reported that polluting industrial units functioning in the residential/non-conforming areas of Delhi and who had applied for allotment of alternate industrial accommodation under the `Relocation Scheme` are considered for allotment of plots. 6563 `F` category and water polluting units which had applied and were found eligible for allotment of plots under the Relocation Scheme have been given allotments on priority basis in industrial areas at Jhilmil, Patparganj, Badli, Narela and Bawana Industrial Areas.

(b): Industrial plots have been allotted to all the polluting and `F` category industries which had applied under the Relocation Scheme and were found eligible under the Scheme.

(c)&(d): The development work under the Relocation Scheme is reported to be progressing as per schedule and the work is expected to be completed by September,2002.

(e)&(f): Delhi State Industrial Development Corporation Ltd.

(DSIDC) has been entrusted with the task of development of industrial areas and allotment of industrial plots/flats to the units found eligible under the Relocation Scheme.

records.name: Rajeev Shukla
records.qn_text:
(a) whether it is a fact that fake medicines have been detected in Delhi and other parts of the country;

(b) if so, the details thereof; and

(c) the steps proposed to be taken to unearth entire fake medicines and initiate positive action against the illicit manufacturers and traders of fake drugs?
records.ans_text:
THE MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF HEALTH AND FAMILY WELFARE (SHRI A. RAJA)

(a) : Yes Sir. Spurious/Fake medicines have been detected by the State Licensing Authorities in Delhi and other parts of the country.

(b) : As per the feedback available from State Licensing Authorities 93 samples of spurious drugs have been detected during the period 1999-2000, state-wise details of which are at Annexure I. In Delhi four more cases were detected during the period 2000-2001. During July, 2001, an interstate spurious drug racket has been uncovered in Bhagirath Place in Delhi who were clandestinely manufacturing, selling and distributing fake medicines. Arrested persons are being proceeded against as per the provision of law.

(c) : Enforcement of Drugs and Cosmetics Act, 1940 and Rules thereof is done by State Drugs Control Authorities. The Drugs Controller General

(India) has advised the State Drugs Controllers to take the following measures for curbing the incidence of spurious drugs;
i) Constitution/reactivation of State Drug Advisory Committees in which various trade and industry associations as well as consumer associations should find representation.
ii) Establishment of separate intelligence- cum-legal machinery with police assistance.
iii) Training should be provided to selected Officials of Drug Control Administration in the modalities of intelligence work, prosecution etc. in respect of Spurious/Counterfeit drugs.
iv) To ensure speedy analysis of drugs samples by establishing own state level drug testing facilities.
v) State Drugs Licensing Authorities to be cautious while approving licences for drug products to ensure that `lookalike` products are not encouraged.
vi) To develop efficient communication facilities and recall procedures.
vii) To undertake surveillance of suspected dealers.
viii) To engage experienced counsel for fighting spurious drug cases. ix) To obtain cooperation of Pharmaceutical Industry by regular interaction with them. x) To collect survey samples under National Survey Quality Evaluation of Drug(NSQED) programme. To ensure manufacture of qualitative drugs/medicines in the country Good Manufacturing Practices is a statutory requirement under the Drugs and Cosmetics Act. These provisions are being upgraded.
The All India Organisation of Chemist and Druggist Association (AIOCD) holds National Pharmacy Weeks from time to time to create awareness among the public. Do`s and Don`t`s for consumers are also published.
The Union Ministry of Health & Family Welfare has constituted a Committee under the Chairmanship of Director General of Health Services (DGHS) on July 18., 2001 to go into all aspects of the menace of spurious drugs and suggest remedial measures.
