records.name: Rajeev Shukla
records.qn_text:
(a) whether the Project Tiger has succeeded in protecting and increasing the number of tigers in India;

(b) what is the present number of living tigers in India, as compared to that in 1973;

(c) how many tigers have died or were killed during the last two years and the causes of their death;

(d) how many poachers have been arrested and brought to book for killing tigers; and

(e) what steps are being taken to protect the tigers and facilitate their further breeding?
records.ans_text:
MINISTER FOR ENVIRONMENT AND FORESTS (SHRI T.R.BAALU)

(a) & (b) As against 1827 tigers in 1972, India now has about 3800 tigers.

(c) The number of deaths of tigers during last two years is as follows:
1999 2000 Natural death 16 15 Death due to poaching 38 39 Total 54 54

(d) Action against the poachers is invariably taken by the State Governments. As such the list of poachers is not compiled and collated by the Government of India. However the list of important cases and poachers arrested is given in Annexure 1.

(e) The details are given in Annexure II. 





ANNEXURE I




ANNEXURE   IN RESPECT OF PART (d) OF THE RAJYA SABHA UNSTARRED 
QUESTION NO. 1422  TO BE ANSWERED ON 03-08-2001 REGARDING 
`PROTECTION OF TIGERS`




Details of offenders arrested and action taken 




i. On  18.12.99, 3 tiger skins, 50 leopard skins and 5 otter skins were seized at Sahibabad, 
Uttar Pradesh border. 8 nos. of offenders were arrested. The investigation has been 
completed and the complaint has been filed in the court.


ii. On 12.1.2000, 4 nos. of tiger skins, 70nos. of leopard skins,18000nos. of leopard claws, 
132 nos. of tiger claws and 221 nos. of black buck skins were seized at Khaga. 6 nos. 
offenders were arrested. The investigation has been completed and the complaint 
has been filed in the court.


iii. On 15.1.2001, the Special Task Force, Uttar Pradesh arrested 2 persons for 
possessing 1 tiger and 1 leopard skin at Atariya Railway Station, Sitapur. Investigation is 
in progress.


iv. On 6.2.2001 one tiger carcass was found in Nallamala forests in Andhra Pradesh. 5 
offenders were arrested. Investigation is under progress.


v. On 25.2.2001, the Special Task Force, Uttar Pradesh arrested 4 persons for illegal possession 
of 1 tiger skin, 41 kgs of bones including 7 tiger skulls at Kheri (Palia). Investigation is i
n progress.


vi. On 21.3.2001, 1 tiger skin, 5 tiger skulls, 1.9 kgs antler horns, 10 nos. of tiger claws, 23 kgs 
of tiger bones, 3 nos. of tiger teeth and 4 nos. of leopard skins were seized by Central 
Bureau of Investigation in  Nagpur. 6 nos. of offenders were arrested. The investigation 
is in progress.


vii. On 7.4.2001, the Special Task Force, Uttar Pradesh arrested 3 persons for illegal possession 
of 1 tiger skin and 1 leopard skin at Palia, Kheri. Investigation in progress.


viii. On 27.4.2001, the Special Task Force, ttar Pradesh arrested 5 persons for possessing 1 tiger 
and 19 leopard skin at Kanpur and 5 leopard skin and 10 claws in Lucknow. Investigation is 
in progress.


ix. On 14.5.2001, the Special Task Force, Uttar Pradesh arrested 2 persons for possessing 2 
suspected tiger skin at Allahabad. Investigation is in progress.




ANNEXURE II


ANNEXURE   IN RESPECT OF PART (e) OF THE RAJYA SABHA UNSTARRED QUESTION
NO. 1422  TO BE ANSWERED ON 03-08-2001 REGARDING  `PROTECTION OF TIGERS`. 


STEPS TAKEN BY THE GOVERNMENT OF INDIA


NATIONAL LEVEL


1. Setting up of a National Coordination Committee to control poaching and illegal 
trade in wildlife with enforcement agencies like customs, Revenue Intelligence, 
Indo-Tibetan Border Police, Border Security Force, Central Reserves Police, Coast Guards,
 State Police, Deputy Director, Wildlife Preservation & Scientific Organisation like 
Zoological and Botanical Survey of India. 


2. Training  Programs and Workshops have been organised to sensitize the above departments
to be proactive in control of trade and smuggling of wildlife products. 


3. A special co-ordination committee with Secretary (E&F), Special Secretary (Home),
 Director, CBI and representative of the Chairman, central Board of Excise & Customs has 
been created to ensure better co-ordination in the efforts to curb smuggling of wildlife products. 


4. Central assistance is being provided to State Governments to strengthen the protection  
infrastructure including armed squads, vehicles, communication network and co-ordination 
between the Park Managers.  


5. Schemes for awards and rewards for outstanding performance and acts of valor has been 
introduced to encourage detection and reporting.
6. The State Government have been advised to strengthen vigilance and intensify patrolling. 


7 Launching of public awareness programme to involve Non-Governmental Organisations and 
others for supporting the Government in its efforts towards wildlife conservation. 


8. Supporting programmers of Institutions and NGOs in exploring tiger-trade routes and developing a forensic identification reference Manual for tiger parts and products. 


9. Funds are being provided to the States Governments for eco-development of the areas to 
reduce the biotic pressure thereon.10. Site specific special force in Project Tiger Areas.
11. Special Strike Force all over the Country to control Trade.
12. Creation of wildlife trade control bureau.


INTERNATIONAL LEVEL :


1. Initiated creation of  a Forum of Tiger Range Countries, i.e Global Forum for 
addressing international issues related of tiger conservation. 


2. To control transboundary trade and effect mutual cooperation in tiger conservation:-


(i) A protocol has been signed with People`s Republic of China. 


(ii) An MOU with his Majesty`s Government of Nepal has been signed. 


(iii) Dialogue with Bangladesh has been initiated.


3. Several resolutions at CITES to check illegal trade in Tiger parts and products 
have been adopted at India`s initiative. 


4. The Millennium Tiger Conference was held in March, 1999. The conference declaration 
suggested several action for conservation of tiger both at national and International level.

records.qtitle: WORK PERMIT TO MIGRANTS FROM BANGLADESH
records.name: Rajeev Shukla
records.qn_text:
(a) whether it is a fact that Government are considering/have decided to give work permit to the migrants from Bangladesh;

(b) if so, the reasons therefor, particularly, when the local public is facing unemployment; and

(c) the steps taken to enhance employment opportunities in the country with particular reference to the North-Eastern States?
records.ans_text:
MINISTER OF LABOUR


(DR. SATYA NARAYAN JATIYA) a) to c): A statement is laid on the table of the House.
STATEMENT REFERRED TO IN REPLY TO THE RAJYA SABHA STARRED QUESTION NO. 178 BY SHRI RAJEEV SHUKLA REGARDING WORK PERMIT TO MIGRANTS FROM BANGLADESH, FOR ANSWER ON 2.8.2001.



(a) No sir. There is no proposal for the grant of work permit to the migrants from Bangladesh.


(b) Does not arise.


(c) Ninth Plan has accorded priority to agriculture and rural development with a view to generating adequate productive employment and eradication of poverty. The plan has focused on sectors, sub-sectors and technologies which are labour intensive, in regions characterised by higher rates of unemployment and underemployment.
Government have also been implementing special programmes for eradication of poverty and generation of employment. The major poverty alleviation programmes, which provide employment in the rural areas, are Swarna Jayanti Gram Swarozgar Yojana, Jawahar Gram Samriddhi Yojana and Employment Assurance Scheme. In the urban areas, Swarna Jayanti Shahari Rozgar Yojana (SJSRY) is in operation since 1.12.97, which also seeks to provide gainful employment to the poor. Prime Minister`s Rozgar Yojana is being implemented to provide employment opportunities to educated unemployed youth in both rural and urban areas. 10% of the total Plan allocation of the Central Government is earmarked for the development in North Eastern States. An allocation of Rs 100 crores have been made to strengthen and modernise vocational skill training in North Eastern States.
These measures would provide supplementary impetus for generation of employment opportunities in North Eastern States in addition to the employment generation efforts of the State Governments through various plan schemes.

records.name: Rajeev Shukla
records.qn_text:
(a) whether Government have decided to construct new roads and widen the existing highways;

(b) if so, the details for the current year and for the next Five Year Plan period;

(c) the amount likely to be spent during the current year and the next Five Year Plan, separately; and

(d) the steps taken to ensure timely completion of the work?
records.ans_text:
MINISTER OF STATE FOR ROAD TRANSPORT AND HIGHWAYS

(INDEPENDENT CHARGE)

(MAJOR GENERAL (RETD.) B.C.KHANDURI, AVSM)

(a) This Ministry is mainly responsible for the Development and maintenance of National Highways. The development of National Highways including widening is a continuous process and improvement works are taken up in phases depending upon the availability of funds.

(b) Government has taken up National Highway development Project (NHDP) for laning of 13252 Km length comprising of Golden Quadilateral and North-South and East -West corridor. This project is targetted for completion by December, 2007. In addition, the annual plan for 2001-2002 provides for widening to 2 lane of about 1100 km of National Highways. The programme for National Highways other than NHDP for the next 5 year plan period is yet to be finalized.

(c) During the current year an amount of Rs.6500 crore is proposed to be spent on development of National Highways including NHDP. An amount of Rs. 50,000 crores is proposed to be spent on NHDP during the next five years. Since the tenth five year plan is yet to be finalized it is not possible to indicate the amount to be spent in next five years on non NHDP sections of National Highway.

(d) The step taken include standardization of bidding procedure, pre-qualification of contractors, supervision by independent engineer, provision for liquidated damages for delay and bonus for early completion, close monitoring of projects etc.

records.qtitle: ONE DAY STRIKE BY GOVERNMENT EMPLOYEES .
records.name: Rajeev Shukla
records.qn_text:
(a) whether about 95 lacs Central and State Government employees have observed a day`s country-wide strike on July 25th 2001, to protest against the privatisation of Government work and corporatisation of Government departments; and

(b) if so, Government`s reaction thereto and the steps taken to allay fears of the Government employees over the issue?
records.ans_text:
THE MINISTER OF STATE OF THE MINISTRY OF SMALL SCALE INDUSTRIES, AGRO AND RURAL INDUSTRIES, MINISTER OF STATE IN THE DEPARTMENT OF PERSONNEL AND TRAINING, DEPARTMENT OF PENSIONS AND PENSIONERS WELFARE OF THE MINISTRY OF PERSONNEL, PUBLIC GRIEVANCES AND PENSIONS AND MINISTER OF STATE IN THE DEPARTMENTS OF ATOMIC ENERGY AND SPACE. (SMT.VASUNDHARA RAJE)

(a): Some sections of the employees from Central Government and various State Governments had observed a strike on July 25, 2001 to protest inter-alia against the privatization of Government functions and corporatisation of Government departments; and

(b): With the object of promoting harmonious relations and of securing the greatest measures of cooperation between the Government, in its capacity as employer, and the general body of its employees, Government had, in consultation with the Staff Side, established in 1966 the scheme for Joint Consultative Machinery and Compulsory Arbitration for Central Government employees. Under this Scheme, a well-defined machinery already exists to settle matters of common concern, including service conditions of employees and other related issues, through the process of negotiation and arbitration. The staff side have already given an agenda item on these issues for the next meeting.

records.qtitle: BIFURCATION OF CHANDIGARH AS CAPITAL FOR PUNJAB OR HARYANA .
records.name: Rajeev Shukla
records.qn_text:
(a) whether any decision has been taken to give Chandigarh as State Capital either to Punjab or Haryana;

(b) if not, whether both the States are required to build their own Capitals; if so, the details thereof; and

records.qtitle: CLEARANCE TO PAK TABLE TENNIS TEAM .
records.name: Rajeev Shukla
records.qn_text:
(a) whether it is a fact that delay in clearance has discouraged the Pakistan table-tennis team to participate in the 15th Commonwealth Table-Tennis Championship;

(b) if so, the reasons for delay in conveying the clearance; and

(c) what steps have been taken to counter Pakistan media`s contention of linking the delay to India`s pulling out of Sharjah cricket tournament?
records.ans_text:
THE MINISTER OF YOUTH AFFAIRS AND SPORTS

(SUSHREE UMA BHARTI)



(a) to (c): A Statement is laid on the Table of the House.

STATEMENT REFERRED TO IN REPLY TO PARTS (a) to (c) OF RAJYA SABHA STARRED QUESTION NO.95 FOR 27.7.2001 REGARDING CLEARANCE TO PAK TABLE-TENNIS TEAM


(a) to (c): The Table Tennis Federation of India (TTFI) submitted an application on 31.1.2001 seeking approval and financial assistance of Government for holding the 15th Commonwealth Table Tennis Championship at New Delhi from 14th to 20th April, 2001. Thereafter, on 13.2.2001, the Federation indicated that Pakistan and Fiji are not participating in this Championship. Accordingly, after obtaining the clearance of Ministry of External Affairs and Ministry of Home Affairs, permission was given to TTFI for holding the event from 14th to 20th April, 2001. Later on, the Table Tennis Federation informed on 22.3.2001 that Pakistan has confirmed its participation. As such after obtaining the clearance of Ministry of External Affairs, the approval for inviting the Table Tennis Team of Pakistan was conveyed on 11th April, 2001. As such, it will be seen that there has been no delay on the part of the Government of India in giving clearance to the participation of Pakistan Table Tennis Team in the 15th Com monwealth Table Tennis Championship. There is no basis for linking Pakistan`s non-participation in the 15th Commonwealth Table Tennis Championship with India`s decision not to play in Sharjah. India`s decision for not playing in Sharjah Cricket tournament is based on a policy decision taken by the Government of India not to play any cricket matches at non-regular Cricket venues at least for a period of three years.

records.qtitle: DEPICTING SIKKIM AS A NATION ON CHINESE WEBSITE .
records.name: Rajeev Shukla
records.qn_text:
(a) whether Government`s attention has been drawn to the news-item under the caption `China lists Sikkim as Asian Nation on website` which appeared in the Asian Age on 14th April, 2001;

(b) if so, Government`s reaction thereto; and

(c) the action proposed to be taken at diplomatic channels to keep the record straight?
records.ans_text:
THE MINISTER OF STATE FOR EXTERNAL AFFAIRS

(SHRI OMAR ABDULLAH)

(a): Yes, Sir.

(b)-(c): We have taken up with the Chinese side the issue of their incorrect depiction of Sikkim. We have pointed out that their position on Sikkim, an issue related to India`s sovereignty and territorial integrity, is not in conformity with their own stated objective of seeking goodwill and friendship with India, and is not in keeping with the principles of Panchsheel. It gives rise to misgivings in the minds of the Indian people, Parliament and Government and adversely affects the process of building trust and confidence. We have also conveyed to the Chinese side that we expect them to acknowledge the reality of Sikkim as an integral part of India. This would help promote development of friendly, cooperative, good neighbourly and mutually beneficial relations between our two countries.

(SHRIMATI VASUNDHARA RAJE)

(b) The suspension of operation of the demonstration plant for radiation processing of spices at Vashi was due to some procedural lapses observed by the inspection team of Atomic Energy Regulatory Board (AERB) during their visit to the Facility on 26 June 2001.

records.name: Rajeev Shukla
records.qn_text:
(a) the number of suspected ISI agents and their local contacts arrested during the last two years;

(b) whether it is a fact that U.P., Delhi, Maharashtra and Bihar have become convenient haven for ISI activities; and

(c) how Central Government is helping these States/Union Territories to flush out suspected ISI agents and nab their local contacts?
records.ans_text:
THE MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF HOME AFFAIRS

(CH. VIDYASAGAR RAO)

(a)&(b): The Government is aware that ISI of Pakistan is involved in aiding, abetting and supporting terrorism in various parts of the country. Activities of Pak ISI have been noticed in various parts of the country including U.P., Delhi, Maharashtra and Bihar. However, information with reference to arrest of suspected ISI agents and their local contacts is not maintained by the Central Government.

(c): In order to deal with the situation, Government have adopted a well-coordinated and multi-pronged approach for tackling the activities of ISI which includes strengthening the border management, galvanizing the intelligence machinery, neutralizing plans of ISI by well coordinated intelligence based operations and modernization and upgradation of police and security forces with advanced sophisticated weapons and communication system etc.
Central Government has also been sensitizing the State Governments about the threat perception and activities of ISI in the country. Periodic coordination meetings are also held with the State Governments for sharing the inputs from various quarters as well as for devising strategies to counter such activities. Various security agencies belonging to Union and States have been working together to check the activities of ISI. Central Government also reimburses the security related expenditure to the State Governments. As a result of coordinated action, a number of Pakistan backed modules have been neutralized.

records.qtitle: LAW AND ORDER SITUATION IN MANIPUR .
records.name: Rajeev Shukla
records.qn_text:
(a) whether it is a fact that the law and order situation has deteriorated to the extent in Manipur that militants barge into DC`s office and force him to sign cheques at gun point;

(b) if so, the steps that are being taken to improve law and order situation in Manipur; and

(c) whether Central Government have formed any special task force to help State Government to contain activities of ultras there?
records.ans_text:
THE MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF HOME AFFAIRS

(I.D. SWAMI)

(a): In one incident in November, 2000, NSCN(I/M) cadres snatched an amount of Rs.44,78,031/- at gun point from Deputy Commissioner, Chandel out of DRDA funds.

(b) & (c): Law & Order situation in Manipur is a cause of concern. An action plan has been prepared to deal with militancy situation and improvement of administration in Manipur. Central Government has formulated a special scheme for modernisation of police forces in North Eastern States. Under the Scheme, vehicles, communication equipments, arms and ammunition and other security related items are provided in kind. Under the scheme of reimbursement of `Security Related Expenditure`, expenditure incurred by State Government on security is reimbursed by the Central Government. Other steps taken by Government, inter alia includes deployment of Central Para Military Forces and Army, improved coordination and sharing of intelligence between the security forces, declaration major militant organisations as `Unlawful Association` and declaration of most seriously affected areas as `Disturbed Areas`.

records.name: Rajeev Shukla
records.qn_text:
(a) whether it is a fact that Taliban Militia in Afghanistan has fully demolished historic Buddha statues disregarding appeals from world leaders;

(b) what steps government have taken at diplomatic channels to prevent these demolition and the reasons for their ineffectiveness;

(c) whether Government apprehends similar treatment to Hindu temples and Sikh Gurudwaras in Afghanistan; and

(d) if so, what steps are being taken or proposed to be taken for protection of these religious places?
records.ans_text:
THE MINISTER OF STATE FOR EXTERNAL AFFAIRS

(SHRI U. V. KRISHNAM RAJU)

(a)-(b) Following the issue of a decree on 26th February, 2001 ordering the destruction of all statues in Afghanistan, appeals were addressed internationally to the Taliban not to destroy historical works of art, being the heritage of all mankind. The Buddha Statues at Bamiyan were specifically mentioned. The Taliban militia completely disregarded international opinion and appeals and carried out this act of cultural vandalism over a period of time.
In a statement issued on 27th February, 2001, the Government condemned the Taliban decree and called upon them to ensure full protection of Bamiyan Buddhas and all other relics. On 2nd March, 2001, the External Affairs Minister made a statement in both Houses of Parliament in which he, inter-alia, offered to bring these artifacts to India for safekeeping for the Afghan people. On the same day both Houses of Parliament adopted unanimous resolutions condemning this barbarism.
The Government also raised this issue internationally. Prime Minister wrote to several Heads of Governments, including the permanent members of the UN Security Council, the UN Secretary General and to Heads of Governments of countries with Buddhist populations (Bhutan, Japan, Sri Lanka, Lao People`s Democratic Republic, Mongolia, Thialand, Cambodia, Myanmar, Republic of Korea) urging that the collective voice of humanity be raised against this outrage and that the Taliban be made to see reason. India co-sponsored a UNGA resolution adopted on 9th March, 2001 on the destruction of Bamiyan Buddhas and other manifestations of Afghanistan`s pre-Islamic art. The Resolution called upon the Taliban to abide by their previous commitments to protect Afghanistan`s cultural heritage from all acts of vandalism damage and theft.
There was widespread international condemnation of the Taliban militia`s actions. The UN Secretary General, Director General of UNESCO, European Union and several Muslim countries were severely critical of the Taliban militia. During Prime Minister`s recent visit to Iran, the President of the Islamic Republic of Iran while condemning the Taliban actions said that they had brought a bad name to Islam.

(c)-(d) The Government is aware of harsh discriminatory policies of the Taliban against the minorities and their places of worship in Afghanistan. Government has brought this to the attention of its foreign interlocutors.

records.name: Rajeev Shukla
records.qn_text:
(a) whether it is a fact that after consecutive droughts, the country is likely to face acute water scarcity during coming summer;

(b) if so, what steps are proposed to be taken to overcome the situation through proper water management; and

(c) what special efforts are being made to harvest rain and store water?
records.ans_text:
THE MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF WATER RESOURCES

(SMT. BIJOYA CHAKRAVARTY)

(a) During the Summer 2001, parts of some States such as Gujarat, Rajasthan, Madhya Pradesh, Chhatisgarh and Himachal Pradesh are experiencing drought like situation due to deficient and inadequate rainfall in these areas during the South-West monsoon in Year 2000 A.D. The rainfall during post-monsoon period has also been scanty in these states.

(b) & (c) The Department of Drinking Supply have relaxed the provisions in the guidelines relating to Accelerated Rural Water Supply Programme (ARWSP) and Prime Minister’s Gramodaya Yojna (PMGY) for the drought affected States. A Minimum Need Programme (MNP) is also being implemented by Department of Drinking Water Supply. Water resources development including construction of storages for utilization of water is taken up by the State Governments as per their own priorities. Upto 1995, a live storage capacity of 177 BCM has been created by construction of large dams in the country. Besides, projects to add an additional storage capacity of about 75 BCM are under construction and for 132 BCM are under planning. The replenishable ground water

………..2/- -2-
is of the order of 432 BCM, out of which about 154 BCM has been developed for use. With the help of these storages and other minor irrigation schemes an irrigation potential of 90 Million hectare (Mha) has been created upto the end of the Eighth Plan against the ultimate irrigation potential of 139.9 Mha in the country. Government of India is promoting rainwater harvesting through Watershed Management Programme, artificial recharge of ground water and roof-top rainwater harvesting under the sector reform project of Accelerated Rural Water Supply Programme under the Ministry of Rural Development, for which technical and financial assistance is provided to the State Governments and other implementing agencies. The Central Ground Water Board under Ministry of Water Resources is implementing a Central Sector pilot scheme of artificial recharge to ground water through rain water harvesting in different parts of the country. Ministry of Agriculture is implementing a scheme entitled ‘Macro-Management’ in all States and Union Territories. This includes watershed management in the catchments of River Valley Projects and Flood Prone Rivers and National Watershed Development Project for Rainfed Areas. Under the above two programmes for conserving the rainwater, farm ponds and water harvesting structures are being constructed. Water collected in these structures is being utilized for life saving irrigation to the crops at the time of scarcity of rains.

records.qtitle: HIGHEST NUMBER OF TB CASES IN DELHI .
records.name: Rajeev Shukla
records.qn_text:
(a) whether it is a fact that Delhi has the highest number of TB cases in the world as 40-50 per cent of the total population is estimated to be infected with TB bacilli and 2.5 per cent suffering from the dreaded disease;

(b) if so, what steps are being taken to tackle TB menace and check its further spread;

(c) whether sufficient funds, medical personnel, preventive and curative medicines, injections etc. are available with Government; and

(d) if not, what is being done in this regard?
records.ans_text:
THE MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF HEALTH AND FAMILY WELFARE (SHRI A. RAJA)

(a) It is estimated that prevalence of infection in respect of Tuberculosis in India is about 30-40%. Since the disease spreads by air, the incidence of TB in the country is by and large similar. Whole of Delhi is covered by RNTCP under which total cases detected in 138 lakhs population during the year 2000 was 23907 which is approximately 173 /lac, on an annualised basis.

(b) To tackle the problem of Tuberculosis, RNTCP is being implemented since 1997-98 in the whole of Delhi. This aims at curing 85% of new sputum positive cases and to detect 70% of such cases. The implementation of RNTCP in Delhi has shown good results with a new smear positive case detection rate of 68/lac and a treatment rate of about 80%.

(c) Yes, Sir.

(d) Does not arise.

records.qtitle: PLAINTS FROM A NRI LADY DOCTOR .
records.name: Rajeev Shukla
records.qn_text:
(a) Whether the High Level Committee for NRIs or NRI Grievance Cell or any other division of his Ministry received complaint from a NRI lady doctor, convenor of the Indian Medical Association about the harassment and discrimination by Australian Government and its High Commission at Delhi, and

(b) if so the details thereof and the action taken by Government?
records.ans_text:
BY THE MINISTER OF EXTERNAL AFFAIRS

(SHRI JASWANT SINGH)

(a) and (b) One Indian doctor, Dr. Mona Verma, who was practising in the State of Queensland, Australia during the period from September 1998 to December 1999 has alleged harassment and acts of racism. The complaints centered around (1) alleged pressure on her by her Australian employer to commit unethical practices such as administering psychotropic substances and false certification of insanity (2) denial by the Medical Board of Queensland of registration despite her possessing the requisite sponsorship from another employer; and (3) refusal by the Australian High Commission of a `bridging visa` to return to Australia. MEA had pressed her case with the Australian High Commission in Delhi who regretted that rules do not permit bridging visa to be issued outside Australia. Our High Commission in Canberra had contacted the Queensland Medical Board regarding her complaint of harassment and was asked for an authorisation letter from the doctor. Accordingly we requested Dr. Verma to send us an authorisation letter to enable the High Commission to pursue the enquiries on her behalf with the Queensland Medical Board, but she has not until now sent it.

records.name: Rajeev Shukla
records.qn_text:
(a) whether Government propose to disinvest a part of stocks of Hindustan Zinc Ltd;

(b) if so, what per cent of its investment is planned to be off-loaded and when;

(c) whether Government will consider adopting the same pattern as was adopted for BALCO; and

(d) whether Government have evaluated the advantage and disadvantages of off-loading a layer part as was done in BALCO?
records.ans_text:
MINISTER OF STATE (INDEPENDENT CHARGE) OF THE DEPARTMENT OF DISINVESTMENT, MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRIES OF PLANNING, STATISTICS & PROGRAMME IMPLEMENTATION AND MINISTER OF STATE IN THE DEPARTMENT OF ADMINISTRATIVE REFORMS AND PUBLIC GRIEVANCES (SHRI ARUN SHOURIE)

(a) Yes, Sir.

(b) Government has decided for disinvestment of 26% equity in Hindustan Zinc Ltd. through strategic sale with giving appropriate role in management to the strategic partner.

(c) & (d) Although the general procedure of sale of equity through strategic sale remains broadly the same, the pattern followed for disinvestment in BALCO can not be replicated in case of disinvestment in Hindustan Zinc Ltd. for various reasons like the following:-
· BALCO was a 100% Government held company and therefore 51% equity could be sold to the strategic partner while retaining 49%. In case of HZL Government holds only 75.92% of the paid-up capital of the company while balance is held by the financial institutions and public.
· BALCO was not a public listed company but HZL is a public listed company and the shares of the company are traded on Bombay Stock Exchange. The acquirer of the strategic stake offered by the Government would be required to make an open offer for acquiring further shares from other shareholders in accordance with the SEBI take over code. Such a stipulation was not required in case of BALCO since it was not listed on stock exchanges.
Therefore, different transactions can not be completed in identical manner since the facts and circumstances of every transaction like percentage of equity offered, the quality and number of interested parties, terms and conditions of sale, financial performance of the concerned companies, future prospects of the business of the company are different. The process of disinvestment and the policy of disinvestment are improved / streamlined with the experience gained over time. The experience of disinvestment in BALCO will be useful in the disinvestment of HZL.

(c) what steps are being taken to ensure punctuality and adherence to working norms in Government offices; and

(d) whether Government would designate some authority to conduct surprise checks to identify defaulters in order to imbide discipline? @@ AAAAAA
records.ans_text:
MINISTER OF STATE OF DEPARTMENT OF PERSONNEL AND TRAINING AND DEPARTMENT OF PENSIONS AND PENSIONERS WELFARE IN THE MINISTRY OF PERSONNEL, PUBLIC GRIEVANCES AND PENSIONS (SMT. VASUNDHARA RAJE)

(a) :It is a fact that salaries of Government employees have increased as a result of the implementation of the recommendations of the Fifth Central Pay Commission.

(b)&(c):Improvement in work culture and efficiency is an ongoing process. Several measures have been taken by the Central Government to improve efficiency, transparency in decision making and training of employees. Several sector specific measures have also been taken by the concerned Ministries/Departments.
In so far as enforcement of punctuality and order is concerned, the existing instructions envisage, inter-alia, the following measures to ensure punctuality of Government servants:-

(i) Daily surprise checks under the direct supervision of a senior officer,

(ii) Debiting of half a day`s casual leave from the causal leave account of the Government servant for each late attendance.

(d) :No, Sir. The instructions on punctuality envisage that necessary measures for enforcement of punctuality be evolved by the Head of Offices and Departments in the light of the broad objective and general instructions laid down in the matter.

records.qtitle: LOSS OF LIVES IN MISHAPS IN BCCL .
records.name: Rajeev Shukla
records.qn_text:
(a) how many miners lost their lives in the collieries of Bharat Coking Coal Limited (BCCL) during 1998-1999, 1999- 2000 and 2000-2001;

(b) the details of each mishap with causes thereof and the cases where management have been held responsible;

(c) the steps taken to prevent recurrence of such mishap; and

(d) the amount of compensation paid to families of each deceased miner?
records.ans_text:
THE MINISTER OF STATE FOR COAL SHRI SYED SHAHNAWAZ HUSSAIN

(a) to (d): A statement is laid on the table of the House. ferred to in parts (a) to (d) of the Rajya Sabha Starred Question No. 279 for 14.03.2001 regarding Loss of lives in mishaps in BCCL

(a) to (d): The details of accident is furnished as under:- 


1998-99       1999-2000     2000-01(upto
Feb.)
No. of               26             26              9
Accidents
No. of               26             29             12
Fatalities


N.B.  Excluding Bagdigi Disaster on 2-2-2001 in which  29
persons lost their lives.


The  details  of  each mishap with  particulars  of
deceased,  causes, management officials held  responsible
and  compensation paid are given as Annexure-1.  However,
the details of Bagdigi Disaster, which took place on 2-2-
2001, are given below.



On 2-2-2001 at about 12.30 P.M. 30 miners including
Manager  & One Asstt. Manager were trapped due to  sudden
inrush of water in the workings of Bagdigi Colliery.  Out
of  30  persons,  29 bodies have been recovered  and  one
person  Shri Salim Ansari was rescued alive from Bagdigi.
While the development of 7 seam in Bagdigi Colliery under
Lodna  Area was in progress within the leasehold area  of
Bagdigi towards Joyrampur Colliery, Level-III heading  of
7   seam  of  Bagdigi  Colliery  joined  with  15   level
waterlogged  old working of Joyrampur Colliery  resulting
in inundation of developed galleries of 7 seam of Bagdigi
Colliery.   Consequently 30 workers were  trapped  inside
the  mine.  The reasons of the mishap will be known after
the  statutory enquiry by DGMS and the Court  of  Enquiry
are submitted.



Pending detailed investigation, the Agent of Bagdigi
Colliery,  Shri A.K. Sengupta, the former Surveyor,  Shri
R.N.  Kundu, and the present Surveyor, Shri R.C. Das  had
been  put  under suspension. General Manager of the  mine
has  also  been transferred.  The details of compensation
paid to the families is at Annexure—II.



Steps taken to prevent such mishap


1.    Instructions  have been issued in  writing  to  all
CGM/GM  of  the  areas that in case  of  coal  extraction
within  60 meters from water logged working in same  seam
or  in  overlying or underlying seams with  the  approval
DGMS,  the  conditions stipulated by DGMS to be  followed
strictly.


2.    A  committee consisting of senior officers has been
constituted in each area who will inspect the mines of other
area to ascertain the danger to the working districts and
other workings of the mines due to inundation from surface
as well as underground waters from the different areas of
the  same  mine or of the neighboring mines and  also  to
ascertain the danger of influx of


2


noxious/  toxic  gasses as well as  fire  damp  into  the
working  districts  or  other workings  either  from  the
sealed off area of the same mine or of the other mines.


3.   Old workings, isolations and fire stopping are being
inspected as per CMR.


4.   Great emphasis has been given for quality inspection
of the mines.

  

5.   Safety Committee meeting at mine level has been made
more effective.



6.    To inculcate safety consciousness among workers  by
organizing  safety  week, safety  drives,  publicity  and
propaganda on safety.


7    Extensive training programme has been  arranged  to
train workers, supervisory staff and executives.


8.    Each  Area  General Manager holds a special  safety
meeting  on  last Friday of the month where they  discuss
only about the safety matters.


9.    Three outside experts had been appointed to conduct
3rd  Round  of  Safety Audit to examine  all  aspects  of
safety   in  depth  including  existing  provisions   and
recommend  precautions and had submitted  their  reports,
which  have been circulated to all collieries  and  areas
for implementation.



10.   Safety  First Report of all mines are  examined  in
every  month  and suitable measures are taken  to  secure
safety.

records.name: NANA DESHMUKH
records.qn_text:
(a) whether India and Vietnam have entered into defence collaboration especially in training of their military personnel in each other’s country;

(b) whether Indian forces are being trained in jungle warfare in Vietnam; and

(c) if so, what are the details thereof?
records.ans_text:
MINISTER OF DEFENCE (SHRI GEORGE FERNANDES)

(a) The bilateral relations in the area of Defence between India and Vietnam include training for members of armed forces of the two countries. Vietnamese officers have attended training courses in India.

records.qtitle: IMPACT ON IMPORT AND EXPORT OF AGRICULTURAL PRODUCTS .
records.name: Rajeev Shukla
records.qn_text:
(a) whether Government have analysed the impact on import and export of agricultural products in the light of six years experience of WTO treaty keeping in view the welfare of 70 crore people engaged in agriculture in India;

(b) if so, the conclusions arrived at; and

(c) the steps taken to protect the Indian agriculture industry from the unfavourable foreign competition?
records.ans_text:
THE MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF COMMERCE AND INDUSTRY

( SHRI OMAR ABDULLAH)

(a) & (b) : From time to time Government have been analysing the data on import and export of agricultural commodities. It has been observed that though there had been an increase in the agricultural imports during the period 1995-96 to 1998-99, the imports have shown a declining trend in the year 1999-2000 and during the current year. The analysis of the data on agricultural exports indicates that after an initial jump in the first year after the coming into existence of the WTO agreement, the exports recorded growth upto the financial year 1996-97, and thereafter have shown a slight decline.

(c) : However, keeping in view the sensitivity of certain agricultural items particularly in the wake of removal of quantitative restrictions, Government are determined to ensure through the appropriate calibration of applied tariffs within the bound levels that imports do not cause any injury to domestic producers. Towards this end, Government have from time to time increased duties on a number of agricultural items where any significant increase in imports was noticed or apprehended. Besides Government can take other actions such as anti-dumping or safeguard action or impose countervailing duties under certain specified circumstances as provided under WTO Agreements.

records.name: Rajeev Shukla
records.qn_text:
(a) the agreements signed during the visit of Chinese leader Li Peng;

(b) whether these agreements are based on the policy of liberalisation; and

(c) what provisions have been made to protect the domestic industries?
records.ans_text:
THE MINISTER OF EXTERNAL AFFAIRS

(SHRI JASWANT SINGH)

(a)-(c): A Statement is laid on the Table of the House. STATEMENT TO BE PLACED ON THE TABLE OF THE HOUSE WITH REFERENCE TO RAJYA SABHA STARRED QUESTION NO.183 FOR ANSWER ON MARCH 8, 2001


Agreements signed with China

Mr. Li Peng, a senior Chinese leader and Chairman of the National Peoples` Congress(NPC) paid an eight-day official visit to India from 9-17 January, 2001 at the joint invitation of the Hon`ble Chairman, Rajya Sabha and the Hon`ble Speaker, Lok Sabha. The visit took place at Chinese request. Mr. Li Peng is the seniormost Chinese leader to visit India since the visit of President Jiang Zemin in November, 1996. This is his second visit. He had visited India in December, 1991 as the Premier of the State Council of China.

2. During this visit he called on the President, Vice President and Prime Minister. He also held discussions with the Hon`ble Speaker, Deputy Chairperson Rajya Sabha, EAM, Leader of the Opposition, leaders of Parliamentary Groups and Indian Industry. In addition to New Delhi, Mr. Li Peng visited Mumbai, Agra, Bangalore and Hyderabad.

3. Mr. Li Peng had frank and cordial discussions with our leadership on bilateral relations. He described the primary objective of his visit as the promotion of friendship and cooperation with India. He also said that:
- China places emphasis on maintaining good-neighbourly relations with India.
- China does not pose a threat to its neighbours.
- China does not view India as a threat.
- China wishes to see a prosperous, developed and strong India and welcomes a more active role by India in regional and international affairs.
- China desires to expand trade and economic cooperation with India.
- there was need to enhance mutual trust and understanding so that the relationship is based on strong foundations.
- that the common ground between our two countries far outweighs the differences, and that unresolved problems in our relations should not become impediments to the expansion of our relationship.

4. Prime Minister and other leaders reiterated Government`s commitment to developing friendly and good-neighbourly relations with China on the basis of Panchsheel and mutual sensitivity to each other`s concerns. We welcomed the progress in our bilateral relations and conveyed that interaction should increase and be accelerated. Government believes that as neighbours, India and China have to solve all problems in a reasonable manner to the satisfaction of both countries. This was conveyed to Mr. Li Peng.


5. The boundary question was discussed in broad terms. In November, 2000 India and China exchanged maps depicting each other`s perceptions of the Line of Actual Control in the Middle Sector of the India-China boundary. This was the first step in the process of clarifying and confirming the LAC along the entire border. During discussions with Mr. Li Peng, it was agreed that the recent development represented progress and marked a good beginning. We have proposed that this process of LAC clarification should be expedited. It has been agreed that the modalities will be discussed in the mechanisms already set up for this purpose.
6. Our concerns regarding international and cross border terrorism were conveyed to Mr. Li Peng. He said that China condemns international terrorism in all forms.

7 We exchanged views on the international situation in general. There was agreement on the need to develop the international situation towards its natural trend of multi-polarity.

8. Mr. Li Peng said that cooperation between India and China will benefit peace and stability in the region and the world.

9. It has been agreed to establish Parliamentary Friendship Groups in both Parliaments.
10. No specific bilateral agreement was signed during the visit.
11. Both sides expressed the desire to enhance trade and economic cooperation. (During the year 2000, bilateral trade, according to Chinese statistics, increased to US$ 2.92 billion, an increase of approximately 47%. India`s exports grew by over 63% and China`s exports by 35%.)
12. Government has already invited Chinese Premier Mr. Zhu Rongji to visit India at a mutually convenient date. Mr. Li Peng extended invitations to Vice President, Prime Minister and Hon`ble Speaker Lok Sabha to visit China.
13. Government have consistently viewed bilateral relations with China in a positive spirit. Our approach has been principled and based on the premise that good-neighbourly relations are to mutual benefit. The high-level dialogue with China has led to an overall improvement in our bilateral relationship. We believe that our two countries must solve all problems through dialogue in a fair and reasonable manner to the satisfaction of both countries, and with due sensitivity to each other`s concerns.

records.qtitle: TREATING SEA WATER FOR IRRIGATION OR DRINKING PURPOSES
records.name: Rajeev Shukla
records.qn_text:
(a) whether any scientific study has been carried out to treat sea water for irrigation or drinking purposes in the coastal areas ;

(b) if so, the detailed results thereof; and

(c) if not, whether Government would undertake such a study ?
records.ans_text:
THE MINISTER OF STATE IN THE DEPARTMENT OF ATOMIC ENERGY (SMT. VASUNDHARA RAJE)

(a) Yes, Sir.

(b) Two processes viz. Multi Stage Flash (MSF) and Reverse Osmosis (RO) have been developed by the Bhabha Atomic Research Centre(BARC) for desalination of water from the Ocean. A demonstration plant is being set up at Kalpakkam, Tamil Nadu which will produce 6300 m3/day of desalinated water from sea water out of which 4500m3/day will be produced by MSF technology while the balance of 1800 m3/day will be by RO technology. This demonstration plant is linked to the Madras Atomic Power Station for supply of steam and electricity and is scheduled to be commissioned by March 2002.

(c) Does not arise.

records.qtitle: TERRORIST NABBED KILLED DURING RAMZAN CEASEFIRE .
records.name: Rajeev Shukla
records.qn_text:
(a) the number of terrorist nabbed and killed during the Ramzan ceasefire declared by the Prime Minister;

(b) the number of security personnel targeted and killed by terrorist outfits during the ceasefire; and

(c) the steps taken by Government to minimize the casualties?
records.ans_text:
THE MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF HOME AFFAIRS

(CH. VIDYASAGAR RAO)

(a): 227 and 82 terrorists were killed and apprehended respectively during the period of Ramzan Peace Initiative from 28.11.2000 to 25.2.2001.

(b): 91 Security Force personnel were killed during the same period.

(c): Strategies being followed by the Security forces and intelligence agencies are regularly reviewed and refined at various levels including in the Unified Headquarters keeping in view the ground situation and available intelligence inputs.

records.name: Rajeev Shukla
records.qn_text:
(a) whether it is a fact that Delhi is one of the most air polluted cities in the world;

(b) whether there is any proposal to restrict registration of motor vehicles to check air pollution; and

(c) what active steps are being taken to reduce air pollution in the city?
records.ans_text:
MINISTER OF ENVIRONMENT AND FORESTS

(SHRI T.R. BAALU)

(a) Delhi is one of the most polluted cities in the world in respect of the prevailing ambient concentration of particulate matter.

(b) No, Sir.

(c) Steps taken/ being taken to reduce air pollution in the city include progressive tightening of emission norms for motor vehicles, supply of better quality of fuel having low sulphur content, adoption of Compressed Natural Gas (CNG) and Liquified Petroleum Gas (LPG) as auto fuel, augmentation of public transport system, optimisation of traffic flow and development of road infrastructure, shifting of industrial units located in non-conforming areas, closing of hazardous industrial units, strengthening of air quality monitoring and surveillance system.

records.qtitle: IMPACT OF WTO TREATY ON EMPLOYMENT PROSPECTS
records.name: Rajeev Shukla
records.min_name: SMALL SCALE INDUSTRIES AND RURAL AND AGRO INDUSTR
records.qn_text:
(a) whether it is a fact that WTO Treaty has seriously affected the employment prospects in Indian agriculture industries;

(b) how many units of agriculture industries have closed down during the last six years, year-wise and the number of employees rendered unemployed during that period; and

(c) the steps taken to revive these units?
records.ans_text:
THE MINISTER OF STATE (INDEPENDENT CHARGE) IN THE MINISTRY OF SMALL SCALE INDUSTRIES AND AGRO AND RURAL INDUSTRIES

(SMT. VASUNDHARA RAJE)



(a) to (c): A statement is laid on the Table of the House.

STATEMENT REFERRED TO IN REPLY TO PART (a) TO (c) RAJYA SABHA STARRED QUESTION NO. 111 BY SHRI RAJEEV SHUKLA FOR ANSWER IN RAJYA SABHA ON 1.3.2001


(a) No instance has been brought to the notice of this Ministry that employment prospects have been seriously affected in Indian agriculture industries because of the WTO treaty.

(b) & (c): While no such data is maintained, the Government is fully aware of the likely impact of the WTO environment and has taken a number of measures for preparing Indian industries including the Small Scale Sector to meet the challenges of liberalisation and globalisation. An Inter-Ministerial Group has been constituted to assess the impact of removal of Quantitative Restrictions on domestic producers and to suggest corrective measures. The Government has in place a suitable mechanism for monitoring the import of sensitive items and to provide adequate protection to the domestic producers through various WTO compatible measures, these include appropriate calibration of applied tariffs within the bound tariffs, anti-dumping measures and other safeguard action such as imposition of countervailing duties where necessary. Other measures that have already been taken include, increase in the excise exemption limit from Rs. 50 lakhs to Rs. 1 crore, a scheme of Capital Subsidy @ 12% for investment in technology upgradation in selected sectors, raising the eligibility limit for coverage under the Credit Guarantee Scheme from Rs. 10 lakhs to Rs. 25 lakhs, continuation of financial support (upto Rs. 75,000/-) for obtaining ISO 9000 certification.

records.qtitle: LOOTING OF RELIEF MATERIALS MEANT FOR QUAKE VICTIMS .
records.name: Rajeev Shukla
records.qn_text:

(b) as the authorities have failed to transport these materials to the needy and targeted people in villages in far off areas, the same is being collected or looted by unscrupulous people near the dumping grounds; and

records.ans_text:
MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF AGRICULTURE

(SHRI SHRIPAD Y. NAIK)


(a) to (c): The responsibility for distribution of relief material is that of the Government of Gujarat. No reports have been received from the State Government regarding dumping of relief material in big cities and either not reaching the targeted people or being looted by unscrupulous elements. The State Government has deputed Senior Officers to supervise distribution and management of relief.

records.qtitle: FAILURE TO RECOVER INCOME TAX DUES THROUGH AUCTION OF PROPERTIES. .

MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF FINANCE____________________

(SHRI GINGEE N. RAMACHANDRAN)

records.qtitle: BASIC FACILITIES IN SPECIAL TRAINS FOR AHMEDABAD .
records.name: Rajeev Shukla
records.qn_text:
(a) whether it is a fact that no water and food was made available in special trains introduced from Ahmedabad for earthquake affected people;

(b) whether any enquiry has been conducted in this regard and if so, the findings thereof; and

(c) how it is proposed to be ensured that all long route special and fee trains have minimum basic facilities of water and food ?
records.ans_text:
MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF RAILWAYS

(SHRI DIGVIJAY SINGH)

(a) to (c) The railways have made adequate arrangements of water and food for the passengers of trains carrying earthquake victims and their relatives. Catering stalls, trolleys and refreshment rooms were kept open round the clock on platforms. Apart from this, food packets were also distributed by different Non-Government Organisations and local bodies free of cost at various stations enroute.

records.qtitle: MEDICAL TEAMS OF FOREIGN COUNTRIES FOR GUJARAT .
records.name: Rajeev Shukla
records.qn_text:
(a) whether it is a fact that many foreign countries rushed medical teams for the service of earthquake victims in Gujarat;

(b) if so, the details thereof;

(c) whether it is also a fact that many teams had to wait for many days in the absence of guidance and co-ordinator from the Ministry of Health and Family Welfare for their deployment; and

(d) the steps taken for optimum utilization of their services?
records.ans_text:
THE MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF HEALTH AND FAMILY WELFARE (SHRI A. RAJA)

(a) Yes, Sir.

(b) As per the information available till date Medical teams from Germany (36 members), France (60 members), Hungary (I5 members), Israel (160 members), Korea (23 members), Japan (9 members), Malaysia (7 members), Omen (14 members), Austria (19 members), South Korea (6 members), Mexico (12 members), reached Gujarat for providing medical relief to the earthquake victims.

(c) No, Sir.

(d) The Crisis Management Group under the Ministry of Agriculture took appropriate steps for coordination with various relief agenceis (International & National) for providing medical relief. State Control rooms were alerted to respond immediately to provide guidance to the medical teams from abroad for their deployment; placements were made according to requirement of services of the victims. A special coordination committee was formed to keep close contact, liaison and coordinate with foreign teams arriving at the Airport. Accommodation for their stay, transport was made, Escorts were provided to accompany them. .....

records.name: KRISHNA KUMAR BIRLA

(b) if so, the details thereof stating the nature of the stolen documents;

(SHRI AJIT KUMAR PANJA)

records.ans_text:

(SHRI DIGVIJAY SINGH)

trains which are well patronised by full fare paying

passengers. Therefore, as a matter of policy,

records.name: Rajeev Shukla

(a) whether Government are considering to bring all State Service Commissions under the purview of UPSC to ensure uniform standard of examination/selection for similar posts throughout the country;

(b) if not, whether Government would give a thought to this; and

(c) if not, the reasons therefor?
records.ans_text:
MINISTER OF STATE OF DEPARTMENT OF PERSONNEL AND TRAINING AND DEPARTMENT OF PENSION AND PENSIONERS` WELFARE IN THE MINISTRY OF PERSONNEL, PUBLIC GRIEVANCES AND PENSIONS (SMT. VASUNDHARA RAJE)

(a) & (b) : No, Sir.

(c) : The Union Public Service Commission (UPSC) is a constitutional body entrusted with the duties of conducting examinations for recruitment to services of the Union under Article 320 of the Constitution. Under the same Article of the Constitution, the State Public Service Commissions have been constituted for conducting examinations for recruitment to services of the respective States. As the State public services and the State Public Service Commissions are included in the State List in the Seventh Schedule to the Constitution of India and Union Public services and the Union Public Service Commission finds place in the Union List of the said Schedule, it is neither possible nor desirable to bring the State Public Service Commissions under the purview of UPSC.

records.qtitle: USE OF NON CONVENTIONAL SOURCES OF ENERGY IN INDUSTRIAL UNITS .
records.name: Rajeev Shukla
records.qn_text:
(a) whether it is a fact that requirement of power of industrial units both big and small in metropolitan cities is not being met; (

(b) whether Government have identified or propose to identify such units which can compulsorily be fed by non-conventional sources of energy, if not, the reason therefor;

(c) what steps have been taken to maximise the use of non-conventional source of energy in metropolitan cities; and

(d) the achievements made during the last three years and the targets set for the next three years?
records.ans_text:
MINISTER OF STATE FOR NON-CONVENTIONAL ENERGY SOURCES

(INDEPENDENT CHARGE) (SHRI M. KANNAPPAN)

(a): All the thirteen States, which have metropolitan cities, except the State of West Bengal, have reported shortage of power supply ranging from 1.6% to 13.3%.

(b): No, Sir. The total installed capacity of projects for generation of power from non-conventional sources at present is less than 3% of the overall installed capacity of power generation in our country. It is, therefore, not considered appropriate to compulsorily substitute the conventional power for any industrial units with power from non-conventional sources.

(c): The Ministry is implementing a wide range of centrally sponsored schemes / programmes to maximise the use of non-conventional energy sources by providing various fiscal, financial and promotional incentives to promoters, entrepreneurs, beneficiaries, implementing agencies / organizations, State Electricity Boards, etc. In

addition, higher subsidies / incentives are provided under major programmes to special category of people such as Schedule Castes and Schedule Tribes as well as in specific areas such as North-East States, Hilly areas, Islands, etc. Programmes, which are especially suited for metropolitan cities include: solar photovoltaic and solar thermal applications, recovery of energy from urban wastes and solar passive architecture.

(d): The achievements made during the last three years in the country in respect of non-conventional source of energy are given in the Annexure. As regards the targets for the next three years, these are fixed on year to year basis and are in accordance with approved Annual Plans and Five Year Plan.

records.name: Rajeev Shukla
records.qn_text:
(a) whether the spurt in ULFA atrocities in North-East is due to intelligence failure;

(b) whether Government are aware that other militant outfits have also joined hands with ULFA;

(c) how many persons have been killed in the North-East during the last year by militant outfits and how many militants have been nabbed and killed during the same period; and

(d) what steps Government are taking to normalise the situation there?
records.ans_text:
THE MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF HOME AFFAIRS

(I.D. SWAMI)

(a) & (b): The recent killings of innocent civilians in Assam are mainly due to the desperation of ULFA as it has been losing support from the public in Assam and its cadres are demoralized.
There are reports of collaboration between ULFA and other militant groups.

(c): During 1999, 800 persons including 203 Security Forces personnel have been killed in the North East by militant outfits. During the said period 1447 militants have been arrested and 442 militants killed.

(d): The Government has taken various steps to bring the law and order situation in North Eastern States under control. These include, inter alia, deployment of Para-military forces and army in the State, coordinated action by army, Para-military forces and State Police for counter insurgency operations, declaration of major insurgent groups as unlawful association under the Unlawful Activities(Prevention) Act, 1967; declaration of insurgency affected State as `disturbed area` under the Armed Forces (Special Powers) Act, 1958; reimbursement of security related expenditure to the State Governments and modernisation/upgradation of State Police Force. Regular review of the situation both at State and Central Government level is being made.

records.qtitle: DISTURBANCE IN KASHMIR BY PAK PRISONERS .
records.name: Rajeev Shukla
records.qn_text:
(a) whether Government are aware that the Pakistan Government is reported to have assured freedom to its prisoners on contract for killing and creating disturbances in Kashmir; and

(b) if so, the steps proposed to be undertaken to counter such a move?
records.ans_text:
THE MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF HOME AFFAIRS

(CH. VIDYASAGAR RAO)

(a): Yes Sir. Pakistan and Pakistan sponsored terrorist groups have been continuously attempting to induct foreign mercenaries from across the border/LoC into J&K for continuing the ongoing terrorism. Such mercenaries have also included criminals, smugglers and ex-servicemen as well as impressionable youth.

(b): With a view to deal with the cross border terrorism the Government has adopted a multi pronged approach which includes, inter-alia, strengthening the border management, neutralising plans of the militants by appropriate action against them in the hinterland, gearing up intelligence machinery, greater functional framework of operation Groups and Intelligence Groups of the UHQ at all levels, improved technology, weapons and equipments for Security Forces, closer vigil on the border, establishment of more naka parties in depth areas to check infiltration/exfiltration, more police pickets, intensive patrolling etc.

records.name: Rajeev Shukla
records.qn_text:
(a) the present annual production of crude oil in the country and planned production during the year 2004-2005;

(b) the estimated annual demand of crude oil for the year 2004-2005;

(c) whether any special plan has been drawn to increase the production of crude oil; and

(d) by when the country is likely to achieve self-sufficiency in crude production?
records.ans_text:
MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRYOF PETROLEUM AND NATURAL GAS

(SHRI E. PONNUSWAMY) -

(a): & (b): The target set for the crude oil production during 2000-01 is 32.46 Million Metric Tonne (MMT) including additional 0.5 MMT production planned by ONGC and the actual production in the first seven month (April-Oct., 2000) has been 18.94 MMT (Provisional). The indigenous production during 2001-02 is estimated to be about 32.30 MMT. The production for the subsequent 2-3 years would have been of a similar magnitude; however various measures taken by the Government as given in reply to part (c) are expected to increase the production. The demand for crude oil for the year 2004-05 would be worked out as a part of the Xth Plan preparation, the exercise of which is yet to commence.

(c): Government has taken several steps to increase crude oil production in the country, which include:-
i) To improve the recovery factor from existing major fields by implementing Enhanced Oil Recovery (EOR)/Improved Oil Recovery (IOR) schemes. These would also help in accelerating oil production from the fields.
ii) To add reserves by exploring in the deeper layers in the producing areas. Contd...2/- -: 2 :-

iii) To explore in the new areas specially in deep water and difficult frontier areas.
iv) To develop faster the newly discovered oil fields.
v) To increase workover and stimulation operations.
vi) To increase exploration efforts through the New Exploration Licensing Policy (NELP).
vii) To increase use of 3-D seismic surveys in new and producing areas.

(d): Self-sufficiency may be possible only in the event of few major discoveries of oil fields, as the demand for oil has been increasing at a faster pace, whereas indigenous production is almost stagnant and there have been no major oil discoveries during the past few years.

records.qtitle: DELAYED OPERATIONS OF AI S FLIGHTS .
records.name: Rajeev Shukla
records.qn_text:
(a) the number of Air India flights in India which could not fly on scheduled time during the last one year;

(b) the reasons for delayed take off in each case; and

(c) the steps taken to ensure their operation as per schedule?
records.ans_text:
MINISTER OF CIVIL AVIATION (SHRI SHARAD YADAV)

(a) : During the period November, 1999 to October, 2000, 2448 Air India flights were delayed at Indian stations.

(b): These flights are delayed mostly due to adversfe weather airport restrictions, technical snags, and miscellaneous and consequential reasons.

(c): Air India has taken several steps to ensure their operation as per schedule such as
(i) all delays are investigated to pinpoint the cause and remedial action is taken wherever necessary;
(ii) flight schedule integrity is continuously monitored and the processes/procedures/systems are constantly evaluated, reviewed and upgraded;
(iii) Air India`s Delay Monitoring Committee meets every day and fortnightly meeting is also conducted with the officers of DGCA to analyse every delay and take preventive actions;

(iv) Air India`s Technical Cell plans for repair action on aircraft which are know to be coming with a snag. This Cell also looks into the snag which occurs at outstations;
(v) periodic refresher training is conducted for Air India`s engineers and technicians.

records.qtitle: EMPLOYMENT OF PERSONNEL IN PRIVATE SECTOR
records.name: Rajeev Shukla
records.qn_text:
(a) whether there exists a mechanism to ascertain employment of personnel in private sector;

(b) if so, how many cases of violation of minimum wages have to come to light; and

(c) the action taken against the defaulters?
records.ans_text:
MINISTER OF STATE FOR LABOUR AND EMPLOYMENT ( SHRI MUNI LALL ) - -


(a): The National Sample Survey Organisation (NSSO) collects data on employment through comprehensive surveys on quinquennial basis. In addition to the quinquennial surveys, NSSO also conducts annual surveys with a smaller sample size. Besides, the Directorate General of Employment & Training also collects data on employment in the organised sector under its Employment Market Information (EMI) Programme.


(b) & (c): As regards violation of minimum wages, the enforcement of the provisions of Minimum Wages Act, 1948 is secured through the officers of Central Industrial Relations Machinery in the Central sphere. In the State sphere, the enforcement is secured through the State Enforcement Machinery. The officers who conduct regular inspections, take appropriate action whenever any case of non-payment or less payment of minimum wages is detected.
In the Central sphere, most of the mines covered as scheduled employment under the Minimum Wages Act are in private sector. As per the latest available information pertaining to violations of the provisions of the Minimum Wages Act in mines in Central sphere during 1998-99 as many as 3671 inspections were carried out in which 44806 irregularities were detected, 1547 employers convicted, 394 claim cases disposed of and an amount of Rs. 38.45 lakhs awarded.

THE MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF CONSUMER AFFAIRS, FOOD AND PUBLIC DISTRIBUTION

( SHRI SRIRAM CHAUHAN )

(a), (b) & (c) : The Government has not debarred the Income Tax payers from the purview of the Public distribution System (PDS) for supply of foodgrains, edible oils and kerosene. The Government of India have decided to exclude Income Tax Assesses and their family members from the purview of PDS sugar from July, 2000 onwards. Accordingly pending finalisation of the list of income tax assesses and their family members with the help of income tax authorities, ad-hoc reduction in the monthly levy sugar quota of States/UTs has been made.
The State Governments have been advised to obtain a simple declaration from the ration card holders as to whether or not he/she and his/her family members is/are income tax assesses. Such declaration has a provision that in the event the declaration made is found, on verification, to be false, the cardholder is liable for cancellation of his/her card or such other penalty as the State Government may decide to impose.

records.name: Rajeev Shukla
records.qn_text:
(a) the number of Bangladeshis who have migrated to India till now and what is the number of such persons coming daily to India after crossing Bangladesh border;

(b) the States/Union Territories which have been bearing the brunt of their influx and the number of such persons in Assam and other North-Eastern States, separately;

(c) what is the action plan to repatriate them and issue identity cards to them as long as they are on this soil; and

(d) whether there is any proposal to seal our border with Bangladesh and if not, what are the other options under contemplation?
records.ans_text:
THE MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF HOME AFFAIRS

( I.D. SWAMY)

(a) & (b) : In view of the long and porous border with Bangladesh and also on account of various push and pull factors, many Bangladeshis have managed to sneak into various parts of the country. It is difficult to make a realistic estimate of the number of illegal immigrants from Bangladesh because they enter surreptitiously and are able to mingle easily with the local population due to ethnic and linguistic similarities.

( c) The powers of detection and deportation of foreigners have been delegated to the State Governments/ Union Territory Administrations, under Section 3 (2) ( c) of the Foreigners Act, 1946. Instructions have been issued to the State Governments/ Union Territory Administrations to intensify efforts to identity and deport illegal foreign nationals and also to sensitise the local population about the magnitude and seriousness of the problem. There is no proposal at present to issue identity cards to Bangladeshi nationals. 2/-
-2-

(d) A series of measures have been taken by the Government to curb the problem of infiltration of Bangladeshi nationals into India. These include raising of additional Battalions of Border Security Force. Reduction of gaps between the border outposts, intensification of patrolling both on the land and the riverine border, accelerated programme of construction of border roads and fencing, increase in the number of outpost towers, provision of surveillance equipments etc . The matter has also been taken up with the Government of Bangladesh on various occasions. The progress of these measures is reviewed regularly. State Governments and Union Territory Administrations have also been directed to enforce the provisions of the Foreigners Act, 1946 (IMDT Act 1983 in case of Assam) strictly.

records.qtitle: TERM LOAN TO MNCS FOR ACQUISITION OF ASSETS
records.name: Rajeev Shukla
records.qn_text:
(a) whether the acquisition of cement plants by Foreign Multi-Nationals in India is through funds received from abroad;

(b) whether Indian Financial Institutions and Banks are extending funds as Term Loan or Working Capital for such acquisition; and

(c) what is the policy of Government in respect of encouraging Indian Financial Institutions and Banks to extend Term loan to Multi-Nationals for acquisition of existing Indian assets?
records.ans_text:
THE MINISTER OF STATE IN THE SHRI V. DHANANJAY KUMAR MINISTRY OF FINANCE

(a),(b)&(c): Foreign investors, including foreign companies, are allowed to establish companies in India after obtaining requisite approvals and clearances under the Foreign Direct Investment Policy approved by Government of India. Such companies/entities are permitted to raise fund for meeting their equity and debt requirements from domestic or offshore sources in accordance with the terms and conditions stipulated by concerned authorities at the time of their establishment in India. The decision regarding financing of a particular economic activity or granting loans to individual entities however, is taken by FIs themselves based on their commercial judgement and the lending policy laid down by their respective boards within the framework of prudential regulations and exposure norms prescribed by RBI from time to time. In accordance with the practices and usages customary amongst the banks and financial institution and in conformity with the provisions of statues governing the financial institutions and the provisions of the Public Financial Institutions (Obligation as to fidelity and secrecy) Act, 1983, the information relating to individual company/unit cannot be divulged.

records.name: Rajeev Shukla
records.qn_text:
(a) whether it is a fact that Rohini MIG Scheme for allotment of 90 square meters plots in Rohini, Delhi, was launched in 1981 but the scheme was not fully subscribed then;

(b) whether it is also a fact that the land earmarked for allotment of plots under the scheme has been diverted to other subsequent schemes, such as commercial complexes, flats, group housing etc; causing delay in allotment to original applicants;

(c) if so, the reasons therefor; and

(d) by when all original applicants are likely to get plots?
records.ans_text:
MINISTER OF URBAN DEVELOPMENT & POVERTY ALLEVIATION

( SHRI JAGMOHAN )


(a): DDA in the year 1981 launched Rohini Residential Scheme for allotment of MIG, LIG and Janta plots. As per the Scheme, the registrants of MIG Category were to be allotted plots of the size of 90 and 60 square metres. Under this scheme, 82,384 persons got themselves registered for allotment of plots including 9,669 persons for allotment of plots of 90 square metres under MIG category.

(b)&(c): No, Sir.

(d): No definite time-frame can be given for allotment of plots to the remaining registrants at this stage. The process of acquisition of land has since been initiated by the Govt. of NCT of Delhi. As soon as the possession of the land so acquired is handed over to the DDA, further action for allotment of plots to the registrants will be taken after completing the process of development.

records.subject: Overhauling of justice delivery system
records.extent: It was inter alia stated that the Government has taken up the work of preparing a roadmap for judicial reforms in the country which aims, inter-alia, at reducing pendency in the courts. In this context, the Government organized a `National Consultation for strengthening the judiciary towards reducing pendency and delays` on 24th-25th October, 2009 at Vigyan Bhawan, New Delhi. In the National Consultation, it was, inter-alia, resolved that the efforts will be made by all concerned to reduce the time taken for disposal of cases from 15 years to 3 years and to work together to implement the various steps including formation of a National Arrears Grid; required to ensure provision of expeditious, quality and inclusive justice. These are under consideration of the Government.
